Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP)**  
*Partial‑segment blockage disruption – bidirectional track sharing*  

---

## 1.  Sets, Indices and Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | Set of trains, indexed by *t* (|T| = N). |
| **S** | Set of stations (including origin / destination), indexed by *s*. |
| **L** | Set of line‑segments (track sections) between two consecutive stations, indexed by *ℓ*. Each segment ℓ belongs to a *direction* d∈{+ , –}. |
| **B** ⊆ L | Sub‑set of **blocked segments** (partial blockage). |
| **Wℓ** | Disruption time‑window on blocked segment ℓ = \([w^{\text{start}}_{\ell},w^{\text{end}}_{\ell}]\). |
| **Δt** | Discretisation interval for time (e.g. 1 min). |
| **τmax** | Upper bound on travel time on any segment (in Δt‑units). |
| **τmin** | Lower bound on travel time on any segment (in Δt‑units). |
| **c^E_t** | Energy consumption coefficient for train *t* (kWh per Δt when moving). |
| **c^D_t** | Penalty cost for delaying train *t* (€/min). |
| **c^C_t** | Penalty cost for canceling train *t* (€/cancellation). |
| **M** | Large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints. |
| **α_t** | Maximum acceleration (Δt‑units per Δt). |
| **β_t** | Maximum deceleration (Δt‑units per Δt). |
| **v^{\max}_t** | Maximum admissible speed for train *t* (Δt‑units per Δt). |
| **v^{\min}_t** | Minimum admissible speed (normally 0). |
| **d_{st}** | Scheduled (pre‑disruption) departure time of train *t* from station *s* (in Δt‑units). |
| **a_{st}** | Scheduled arrival time of train *t* at station *s* (in Δt‑units). |
| **R_t** | Set of admissible routes for train *t*. For a normal line a train has two possible routes on a blocked segment: **original** (stay on its own direction) or **reroute** (use opposite direction). |
| **π_{t,r}** | Binary indicator: 1 if train *t* uses route *r∈R_t*, 0 otherwise. |
| **γ_{t,s}** | Binary indicator: 1 if train *t* is cancelled, 0 otherwise. |

---

## 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| **x_{t,s}** | integer (≥0) | Actual departure time of train *t* from station *s* (Δt‑units). |
| **y_{t,s}** | integer (≥0) | Actual arrival time of train *t* at station *s* (Δt‑units). |
| **τ_{t,ℓ}** | integer (≥0) | Travel time of train *t* on segment ℓ (Δt‑units). |
| **v_{t,ℓ}** | continuous ≥0 | Average speed of train *t* on segment ℓ (Δt‑units per Δt). |
| **e_{t,ℓ}** | continuous ≥0 | Energy consumed by train *t* while traversing ℓ. |
| **π_{t,r}** | binary | Route choice (original vs rerouted) for train *t*. |
| **γ_{t}** | binary | Cancellation decision for train *t*. |
| **z_{t,ℓ}** | binary | 1 if train *t* occupies segment ℓ during its travel (used for conflict avoidance). |
| **δ_{t,t',ℓ}** | binary | 1 if trains *t* and *t'* conflict on segment ℓ (i.e. overlap in time). Used only in linearisation (see constraints). |

*All time variables are measured in multiples of Δt (e.g. minutes).*

---

## 3. Objective Function  

The integrated model simultaneously minimises **total delay**, **cancellation cost**, and **energy consumption**:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & 
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} c^{D}_{t}\,\bigl(x_{t,s}-d_{st}\bigr)^{+}}_{\text{Delay penalty}} \\
&+ \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} c^{C}_{t}\,\gamma_{t}}_{\text{Cancellation penalty}} \\
&+ \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L} c^{E}_{t}\,e_{t,\ell}}_{\text{Energy consumption}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

`(·)^{+}` denotes the positive part; it can be linearised by introducing auxiliary variables  
\( \Delta_{t,s}\ge 0\) with constraints \( \Delta_{t,s}\ge x_{t,s}-d_{st}\) and \( \Delta_{t,s}\ge 0\). Then the delay term becomes \(\sum_{t,s}c^{D}_t\Delta_{t,s}\).

---

## 4. Core Constraints  

### 4.1 Cancellation logic  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& x_{t,s}\le M\,(1-\gamma_{t}) \qquad \forall t,s,\\
& y_{t,s}\le M\,(1-\gamma_{t}) \qquad \forall t,s,\\
& \pi_{t,r}\le 1-\gamma_{t} \qquad \forall t,r .
\end{aligned}
\]

If a train is cancelled (\(\gamma_t=1\)) all timing variables are forced to 0 (or a dummy large value) and no route is selected.

### 4.2 Route‑selection (original / reroute)  

Each train must choose exactly one admissible route (or be cancelled):

\[
\sum_{r\in R_t}\pi_{t,r}=1-\gamma_{t}\qquad\forall t .
\]

The route choice determines which direction the train uses on a blocked segment ℓ∈B:

\[
z_{t,\ell}= 
\begin{cases}
\pi_{t,r^{\text{orig}}} & \text{if } \ell\in B \text{ and original direction is allowed},\\
\pi_{t,r^{\text{reroute}}}& \text{if } \ell\in B \text{ and train uses opposite direction},\\
1 & \text{if } \ell\notin B .
\end{cases}
\]

In a linear model we introduce binary parameters  
\( \rho_{t,\ell}^{r}\in\{0,1\}\) ( =1 if route *r* uses segment ℓ). Then

\[
z_{t,\ell}= \sum_{r\in R_t}\rho_{t,\ell}^{r}\,\pi_{t,r}\qquad\forall t,\ell .
\]

### 4.3 Temporal consistency (arrival–departure)  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& y_{t,s}=x_{t,s-1}+ \tau_{t,\ell_{s-1}} \qquad \forall t,\; s\in S\setminus\{ \text{origin}\},\\
& x_{t,s}=y_{t,s}+ d^{\text{dw}}_{t,s}\;(1-\gamma_{t}) \qquad \forall t,\; s\in S\setminus\{ \text{destination}\},
\end{aligned}
\]

where \(d^{\text{dw}}_{t,s}\) is the (minimum) dwell time at station *s* (given data).

### 4.4 Travel‑time bounds (speed limits)  

For every train‑segment pair:

\[
\tau^{\min}_{t,\ell}\;z_{t,\ell}\ \le\ \tau_{t,\ell}\ \le\ \tau^{\max}_{t,\ell}\;z_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t,\ell .
\]

The bounds are derived from speed limits:

\[
\tau^{\min}_{t,\ell}= \Big\lceil \frac{L_{\ell}}{v^{\max}_{t}} \Big\rceil ,\qquad
\tau^{\max}_{t,\ell}= \Big\lfloor \frac{L_{\ell}}{v^{\min}_{t}} \Big\rfloor .
\]

\(L_{\ell}\) is the length of segment ℓ (in Δt‑units of distance).

### 4.5 Speed‑energy relationship  

Assume a linear energy model: energy per segment equals a constant times speed (or travel time). A common approximation for high‑speed trains is:

\[
e_{t,\ell}=c^{E}_t \, v_{t,\ell}\, \tau_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t,\ell .
\]

Because \(v_{t,\ell}=L_{\ell}/\tau_{t,\ell}\), the above can be linearised by introducing a new continuous variable \(q_{t,\ell}=1/\tau_{t,\ell}\) and using a piece‑wise linear approximation, or simply use the travel‑time bounds to approximate energy:

\[
e_{t,\ell}=c^{E}_t\left( \alpha^{\text{acc}}_t\,\tau_{t,\ell}+ \alpha^{\text{cruise}}_t\right)z_{t,\ell},
\]

where \(\alpha^{\text{acc}}_t,\alpha^{\text{cruise}}_t\) are calibrated coefficients (assumption). This expression is linear in τ.

### 4.6 Acceleration / deceleration limits (within a segment)  

If a train changes speed between two consecutive segments ℓ and ℓ′, the difference in average speeds must respect limits:

\[
v_{t,\ell'}-v_{t,\ell}\le \alpha_t \qquad\forall t,\; (\ell,\ell')\text{ consecutive},\\
v_{t,\ell}-v_{t,\ell'}\le \beta_t \qquad\forall t,\; (\ell,\ell')\text{ consecutive}.
\]

Using \(v_{t,\ell}=L_{\ell}/\tau_{t,\ell}\) we obtain a non‑linear term; we linearise by a *big‑M* formulation with binary variables that indicate whether the speed is increased/decreased, or by piece‑wise linear approximations (assumption).

### 4.7 Conflict‑avoidance on shared (bidirectional) segments  

Only one train may occupy a segment ℓ at a given time. Using the discretised time horizon **H** = {1,…,Hmax} we introduce binary occupancy variables:

\[
u_{t,\ell,h}= 
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if train }t\text{ is on segment }\ell\text{ during time slot }h,\\
0 & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad \forall t,\ell,h .
\]

Linking τ to occupancy:

\[
\sum_{h= x_{t,s-1}+1}^{x_{t,s-1}+ \tau_{t,\ell}} u_{t,\ell,h}= \tau_{t,\ell}\;z_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t,\ell .
\]

Conflict‑free condition (binary linear):

\[
\sum_{t\in T} u_{t,\ell,h}\le 1\qquad\forall \ell\in L,\; h\in H .
\]

When the time horizon is large, the model can be tightened by *interval‑based* conflict variables (see Section 5). For the purpose of this MILP we keep the simple time‑slot formulation.

### 4.8 Disruption‑window feasibility  

A train that uses a blocked segment ℓ must **avoid** the disruption window unless it is rerouted (i.e. uses opposite direction). This is expressed by forcing its occupancy to be outside \([w^{\text{start}}_{\ell},w^{\text{end}}_{\ell}]\) when the original direction is chosen:

\[
\sum_{h=w^{\text{start}}_{\ell}}^{w^{\text{end}}_{\ell}} u_{t,\ell,h}\le M\,(1-\pi_{t,r^{\text{orig}}})\qquad\forall t,\ell\in B .
\]

If the train is rerouted (\(\pi_{t,r^{\text{reroute}}}=1\)) the constraint is relaxed because the train travels on the opposite track (which is assumed to be free).

---

## 5.  Linearisation & Modeling Remarks  

1. **Positive‑part of delay** – Introduce auxiliary \(\Delta_{t,s}\ge0\) with  
   \(\Delta_{t,s}\ge x_{t,s}-d_{st}\) and \(\Delta_{t,s}\ge0\). The objective uses \(\Delta_{t,s}\).

2. **Energy‑speed linearisation** – Use a piece‑wise linear approximation of the function \(e(v)=a\,v^{2}+b\,v+c\) over the admissible speed interval. Introduce break‑points \(\{v^{k}\}\) and binary variables \(w_{t,\ell}^{k}\) to select the segment of the piece‑wise line.

3. **Acceleration constraints** – Replace the non‑linear term \(v_{t,\ell}=L_{\ell}/\tau_{t,\ell}\) by a set of *SOS‑2* variables or by a discretised speed‑level set \(\mathcal{V}_t\). Let \(s_{t,\ell}^{p}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate speed level *p* (with speed value \(v^{p}\) and corresponding travel time \(\tau^{p}=L_{\ell}/v^{p}\)). Then  

   \[
   \sum_{p}s_{t,\ell}^{p}=z_{t,\ell},\qquad
   \tau_{t,\ell}= \sum_{p}\tau^{p}s_{t,\ell}^{p},\qquad
   v_{t,\ell}= \sum_{p}v^{p}s_{t,\ell}^{p}.
   \]

   Acceleration limits become linear differences between successive speed‑level binaries.

4. **Big‑M values** – Choose \(M\) slightly larger than the planning horizon (e.g. total number of time slots).  

5. **Time‑slot granularity** – Δt can be set to 1 min for high‑resolution schedules; a coarser Δt (e.g., 5 min) reduces model size.

---

## 6.  Complete MILP Formulation  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} c^{D}_{t}\,\Delta_{t,s}
      + \sum_{t\in T} c^{C}_{t}\,\gamma_{t}
      + \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L} c^{E}_{t}\,e_{t,\ell} \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } 
&\Delta_{t,s}\ge x_{t,s}-d_{st} &&\forall t,s,\\
&\Delta_{t,s}\ge 0 &&\forall t,s,\\[4pt]
&\sum_{r\in R_t}\pi_{t,r}=1-\gamma_{t} &&\forall t,\\
&z_{t,\ell}= \sum_{r\in R_t}\rho_{t,\ell}^{r}\,\pi_{t,r} &&\forall t,\ell,\\
&x_{t,s}\le M(1-\gamma_{t}) &&\forall t,s,\\
&y_{t,s}\le M(1-\gamma_{t}) &&\forall t,s,\\[4pt]
&y_{t,s}=x_{t,s-1}+ \tau_{t,\ell_{s-1}} &&\forall t,\; s\neq \text{origin},\\
&x_{t,s}=y_{t,s}+ d^{\text{dw}}_{t,s}(1-\gamma_{t}) &&\forall t,\; s\neq \text{destination},\\[4pt]
&\tau^{\min}_{t,\ell}\,z_{t,\ell}\le \tau_{t,\ell}\le \tau^{\max}_{t,\ell}\,z_{t,\ell} &&\forall t,\ell,\\
&e_{t,\ell}=c^{E}_t\Big(\alpha^{\text{acc}}_t\,\tau_{t,\ell}+ \alpha^{\text{cruise}}_t\Big)z_{t,\ell} &&\forall t,\ell,\\[4pt]
&\sum_{h= x_{t,s-1}+1}^{x_{t,s-1}+ \tau_{t,\ell}} u_{t,\ell,h}= \tau_{t,\ell}\,z_{t,\ell} &&\forall t,\ell,\\
&\sum_{t\in T} u_{t,\ell,h}\le 1 &&\forall \ell\in L,\; h\in H,\\[4pt]
&\sum_{h=w^{\text{start}}_{\ell}}^{w^{\text{end}}_{\ell}} u_{t,\ell,h}\le M\,(1-\pi_{t,r^{\text{orig}}}) &&\forall t,\ell\in B,\\[4pt]
&\text{(Acceleration / deceleration linearised constraints)}\\
&u_{t,\ell,h}\in\{0,1\},\; \pi_{t,r}\in\{0,1\},\; \gamma_{t}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{t,\ell}\in\{0,1\},\\
&x_{t,s},y_{t,s},\tau_{t,\ell},e_{t,\ell}\ge 0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

All remaining non‑linear terms (speed‑energy, acceleration) are replaced by the linearisation techniques described in Section 5.

---

## 7.  Key Modeling Assumptions (explicitly stated)

| # | Assumption |
|---|------------|
| A1 | Time is discretised into equal intervals Δt (e.g., 1 min). |
| A2 | Each train has at most **two** admissible routes on a blocked segment: the original direction and the opposite‑track reroute. |
| A3 | Blocked segments are unavailable **only** during the given disruption window; after the window they are free. |
| A4 | Energy consumption on a segment is approximated linearly by travel time (or by a piece‑wise linear function of speed). |
| A5 | Dwell times at stations are known, deterministic, and must be respected in the rescheduled timetable. |
| A6 | Maximum/minimum speeds are constant for a given train on all segments (no speed‑limit variation along the line). |
| A7 | Acceleration and deceleration limits are enforced between consecutive segments via linearised speed‑level variables. |
| A8 | Cancellation is allowed for any train; cancelled trains incur a fixed penalty and generate no further constraints. |
| A9 | Conflict‑avoidance is modelled at the granularity of the chosen Δt; only one train may occupy a segment in any time slot. |
| A10| Big‑M values are set sufficiently large (≥ planning horizon) but not excessively large to avoid numerical instability. |

---

## 8.  Remarks on Solving the Model  

* The MILP can become large for realistic networks because of the time‑slot occupancy variables \(u_{t,\ell,h}\).  
* A **decomposition** approach (as suggested in the source text) is often employed:  
  1. **Master IP** – decides route choices \(\pi_{t,r}\), cancellations \(\gamma_t\) and a coarse “plan” (set of feasible travel‑time intervals) for each train.  
  2. **Sub‑problems** – for each train, given a selected plan, solve a small LP that yields a feasible speed‑profile (the “train plan”).  
  3. **Iterative refinement** – add missing conflict‑avoidance cuts (e.g., via Benders or local branching) until a feasible global timetable is obtained.  

* The formulation above provides the **complete** MILP that can be handed to a commercial solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress). The linearisation tricks in Section 5 keep the model within the MILP class.

--- 

**End of model description**.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP) under a partial‑segment blockage**

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \( \mathcal{T}=\{1,\dots ,T\} \) | Trains to be scheduled |
| \( \mathcal{S}=\{1,\dots ,S\} \) | Elementary track‑segments (ordered along the line) |
| \( \mathcal{K}=\{1,\dots ,K\} \) | admissible speed‑levels (e.g. low, medium, high) |
| \( \mathcal{H}= \{0,\Delta t ,2\Delta t ,\dots ,H_{\max}\} \) | Discrete time‑points for block‑occupancy checks |
| \( \mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{S} \) | Segments that are **blocked** during the disruption |
| \( \mathcal{O}\subseteq\mathcal{S} \) | Segments that have an opposite‑track usable for rerouting |
| \( \mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{S} \) | Segments that contain stations (possible dwell) |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical value / comment |
|--------|-------------|------------------------|
| \( \hat a_t \) | Planned arrival time of train \(t\) at its final destination | timetable |
| \( L_s \) | Length of segment \(s\) (km) | – |
| \( v^{k}_s \) | Speed (km/h) associated with speed‑level \(k\) on segment \(s\) | – |
| \( \tau^{k}_s = \dfrac{L_s}{v^{k}_s} \) | Travel time (h) on segment \(s\) if level \(k\) is used | pre‑computed |
| \( e^{k}_s \) | Energy consumption (kWh) on segment \(s\) with level \(k\) | from train‑power model |
| \( v^{\min}_s , v^{\max}_s \) | Minimum / maximum admissible speed on segment \(s\) | speed limits |
| \( \omega^{\text{delay}}_t \) | Weight of delay for train \(t\) (passenger importance) | usually 1 |
| \( \omega^{\text{energy}} \) | Global weight for energy consumption | chosen by planner |
| \( \Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{\min},\;\Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{\max} \) | Minimum / maximum dwell time at any station (h) | e.g. 0.5–2 min |
| \( B^{\text{start}}_s , B^{\text{end}}_s \) | Beginning / ending time of the blockage on segment \(s\in\mathcal{D}\) | known from the disruption |
| \( M \) | Large constant (big‑M) for linearisation | > planning horizon |
| \( \beta_s\in\{0,1\} \) | 1 if segment \(s\) possesses an opposite track, 0 otherwise | 1 for \(s\in\mathcal{O}\) |

---

### 3. Decision variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \( x^{\text{orig}}_{t,s}\in\{0,1\} \) | binary | 1 → train \(t\) uses the **original** track on segment \(s\) |
| \( x^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}\in\{0,1\} \) | binary | 1 → train \(t\) uses the **opposite** track on segment \(s\) (only if \(s\in\mathcal{O}\)) |
| \( y^{k}_{t,s}\in\{0,1\} \) | binary | 1 → speed‑level \(k\) is selected for train \(t\) on segment \(s\) |
| \( d_{t,s}\ge 0 \) | continuous | Departure time of train \(t\) from the upstream node of segment \(s\) |
| \( a_{t,s}\ge 0 \) | continuous | Arrival time of train \(t\) at the downstream node of segment \(s\) |
| \( \theta_{t,s,\tau}\in\{0,1\} \) | binary | 1 → train \(t\) occupies segment \(s\) during time slot \([\tau,\tau+\Delta t)\) |
| \( \eta_{t,s}\ge 0 \) | continuous | Dwell time of train \(t\) at station segment \(s\in\mathcal{P}\) |
| \( \xi_{t,s}\in\{0,1\} \) | binary | 1 → train \(t\) actually stops at station \(s\) |
| \( \delta_t\ge 0 \) | continuous | Total delay of train \(t\) (difference between actual and planned final arrival) |

---

### 4. Objective function  

\[
\boxed{
\min \;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} \omega^{\text{delay}}_{t}\,\delta_t}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\omega^{\text{energy}}\,
\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} e^{k}_s\, y^{k}_{t,s}}_{\text{total weighted energy}}
}
\]

The first term penalises passenger delay, the second term accounts for the energy consumption of the chosen speed profiles.

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Routing choice on blocked segments  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& x^{\text{orig}}_{t,s}+x^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}=1 &&\forall t\in\mathcal{T},\; \forall s\in\mathcal{D}\\
& x^{\text{orig}}_{t,s}=1 &&\forall t\in\mathcal{T},\; \forall s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\mathcal{D}\\
& x^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}\le \beta_s &&\forall t\in\mathcal{T},\; \forall s\in\mathcal{D}
\end{aligned}
\]

#### 5.2 Exactly one speed level per traversed segment  

\[
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} y^{k}_{t,s}=x^{\text{orig}}_{t,s}+x^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}
\qquad\forall t\in\mathcal{T},\; \forall s\in\mathcal{S}
\]

#### 5.3 Travel‑time linking  

\[
a_{t,s}= d_{t,s}+ \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \tau^{k}_s\, y^{k}_{t,s}
\qquad\forall t\in\mathcal{T},\; \forall s\in\mathcal{S}
\]

#### 5.4 Schedule continuity along the line  

\[
d_{t,s+1}= a_{t,s}+ \eta_{t,s}\qquad\forall t\in\mathcal{T},\; s=1,\dots ,S-1
\]

where \(\eta_{t,s}=0\) if \(s\notin\mathcal{P}\).

#### 5.5 Dwell‑time limits at stations  

\[
\Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{\min}\,\xi_{t,s}\le \eta_{t,s}\le \Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}\,\xi_{t,s}
\qquad\forall t\in\mathcal{T},\; s\in\mathcal{P}
\]

If a train does not stop (\(\xi_{t,s}=0\)) the dwell time is forced to zero.

#### 5.6 Speed‑limit feasibility (pre‑filter)  

Only speed levels whose speed lies inside \([v^{\min}_s , v^{\max}_s]\) are kept in \(\mathcal{K}\). The constraint is therefore implicit; alternatively  

\[
y^{k}_{t,s}=0\quad\text{if }v^{k}_s\notin [v^{\min}_s , v^{\max}_s].
\]

#### 5.7 Block‑occupancy linking (big‑M)  

\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{t,s} &\le \tau + M\,(1-\theta_{t,s,\tau}) &&\forall t,s,\tau\\
a_{t,s} &\ge \tau+\Delta t - M\,(1-\theta_{t,s,\tau}) &&\forall t,s,\tau
\end{aligned}
\]

If \(\theta_{t,s,\tau}=1\) the two inequalities force the interval \([d_{t,s},a_{t,s})\) to cover the whole slot \([\tau,\tau+\Delta t)\).

#### 5.8 Capacity (conflict‑avoidance)  

\[
\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} \theta_{t,s,\tau}\le 1
\qquad\forall s\in\mathcal{S},\; \forall \tau\in\mathcal{H}
\]

(If a dedicated opposite track allows simultaneous opposite‑direction trains, the RHS can be set to 2 for segments with \(\beta_s=1\).)

#### 5.9 Disruption‑window restriction  

\[
\theta_{t,s,\tau}\le x^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}
\;+\;
\mathbf{1}_{\{\tau\notin [B^{\text{start}}_s ,\,B^{\text{end}}_s)\}}
\qquad\forall t,\; s\in\mathcal{D},\; \tau\in\mathcal{H}
\]

During the blockage a train may occupy the segment only if it has been rerouted to the opposite track.

#### 5.10 Delay definition  

Let \(s^{\text{last}}_t\) be the last segment of train \(t\).  

\[
\delta_t \ge a_{t,s^{\text{last}}_t} - \hat a_t \qquad\forall t\in\mathcal{T},
\qquad
\delta_t \ge 0.
\]

(If early arrival should be penalised, an analogous variable can be added.)

#### 5.11 Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x^{\text{orig}}_{t,s},\;x^{\text{opp}}_{t,s},\;y^{k}_{t,s},
\;\theta_{t,s,\tau},\;\xi_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\\
&d_{t,s},\;a_{t,s},\;\eta_{t,s},\;\delta_t\ge 0
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 6. Complete MILP  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ll}
\displaystyle\min\limits_{x,y,d,a,\theta,\delta}
& \displaystyle\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} \omega^{\text{delay}}_{t}\,\delta_t
   + \omega^{\text{energy}}\,
   \sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} e^{k}_s\, y^{k}_{t,s} \\[4mm]
\text{s.t.} & \text{Routing constraints (5.1)}\\
            & \text{Exactly‑one‑speed (5.2)}\\
            & \text{Travel‑time linking (5.3)}\\
            & \text{Schedule continuity (5.4)}\\
            & \text{Dwell‑time limits (5.5)}\\
            & \text{Occupancy linking (5.7a)}\\
            & \text{Capacity (5.7b)}\\
            & \text{Disruption window (5.8)}\\
            & \text{Delay definition (5.10)}\\
            & \text{Variable domains (5.11)}.
\end{array}
}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only products involve a binary variable and a continuous one, which are handled by the big‑M linearisation shown in (5.7a) and (5.8). The model can be solved with any state‑of‑the‑art MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, SCIP, …).  

**Interpretation of the solution**

* \(x^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}=1\) indicates that train \(t\) is rerouted onto the opposite track on the blocked segment \(s\).  
* \(y^{k}_{t,s}=1\) gives the optimal speed level (hence travel time \(\tau^{k}_s\) and energy \(e^{k}_s\)).  
* \(d_{t,s},a_{t,s}\) provide a conflict‑free timetable that respects dwell‑time limits and the disruption window.  
* The objective value quantifies the trade‑off between passenger delay and energy consumption.

This formulation fulfills the requested integrated TRSMP model, explicitly handling bidirectional conflicts, rerouting decisions, speed‑profile selection, and the coupling between rescheduling and speed management.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
**Variables**

| Symbol | Meaning | Type | Index set |
|--------|---------|------|-----------|
| \(x_{i,r}\) | 1 if train \(i\) uses route \(r\) (otherwise 0) | binary | \(i\in I,\; r\in R_i\) |
| \(y_{i,s,t}\) | 1 if train \(i\) occupies segment \(s\) at time period \(t\) | binary | \(i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T\) |
| \(v_{i,s,t}\) | Speed of train \(i\) on segment \(s\) during period \(t\) (km/h) | continuous | \(i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T\) |
| \(a_{i,s,t}\) | 1 if train \(i\) accelerates on segment \(s\) at time \(t\) | binary | \(i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T\) |
| \(d_{i,s,t}\) | 1 if train \(i\) decelerates on segment \(s\) at time \(t\) | binary | \(i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T\) |
| \(A_i\) | Arrival time of train \(i\) at its destination (minutes) | continuous | \(i\in I\) |
| \(D_i\) | Departure time of train \(i\) from its origin (minutes) | continuous | \(i\in I\) |
| \(\delta_i\) | Delay of train \(i\) (minutes) | continuous | \(i\in I\) |
| \(z_{i,s,t,k}\) | 1 if speed of train \(i\) on segment \(s\) at time \(t\) lies in piece‑wise interval \(k\) | binary | \(i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T,\; k\in K\) |
| \(v^{2}_{i,s,t}\) | Linearised value of \(v_{i,s,t}^{2}\) | continuous | \(i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T\) |

**Parameters (illustrative values, replace with real data)**  

* Sets: \(I\) – trains, \(S\) – track segments, \(T=\{0,\dots,T_{\max}\}\) – discrete time periods, \(R_i\) – feasible routes for train \(i\), \(K\) – piece‑wise intervals.  
* \(\Delta\) – length of a time period (minutes).  
* \(L_{\min},L_{\max}\) – minimum/maximum admissible speed.  
* \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) – energy‑cost coefficients.  
* \(w_{\text{delay}}\) – weight of total delay in the objective.  
* \(\hat A_i\) – scheduled arrival time of train \(i\).  
* \(\underline{d}_i\) – minimum dwell time for train \(i\).  
* \(B\) – blocked segment (e.g. \(s^{*}\)).  
* \([T^{\text{start}},T^{\text{end}}]\) – disruption time window.  
* \(\ell_s\) – physical length of segment \(s\) (km).  
* Piece‑wise break‑points \(\{b_k\}_{k\in K\cup\{K+1\}}\) with slopes \(\sigma_k\) and intercepts \(\eta_k\) such that  
  \[
  v^{2}\approx \sigma_k v + \eta_k \quad\text{for } b_k\le v\le b_{k+1}.
  \]

**Objective function**

\[
\min\;
w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{i\in I}\delta_i
\;+\;
\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{t\in T}
\Bigl(
\alpha\,v^{2}_{i,s,t}
+\beta\,a_{i,s,t}
+\gamma\,d_{i,s,t}
\Bigr)
\]

The first term penalises total passenger delay, the second term represents the energy consumption of all trains (quadratic speed term linearised, plus penalties for acceleration/deceleration).

**Constraints**

1. **Route selection** – each train chooses exactly one feasible route  
   \[
   \sum_{r\in R_i} x_{i,r}=1 \qquad\forall i\in I .
   \]

2. **Link occupancy to chosen route** – a segment can be occupied only if it belongs to the selected route  
   \[
   y_{i,s,t}\le \sum_{r\in R_i:\; s\in r} x_{i,r} \qquad\forall i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T .
   \]

3. **Flow continuity** – if a train occupies segment \(s\) at time \(t\) it must occupy the next segment of its route at time \(t+1\) (or leave the network after the last segment)  
   \[
   y_{i,s,t}=y_{i,s',t+1}\qquad
   \forall i\in I,\; t\in T,\; (s,s')\text{ consecutive on the selected route of }i .
   \]

4. **Blocked segment** – no train may occupy the disrupted segment during the blockage window  
   \[
   y_{i,B,t}=0 \qquad\forall i\in I,\; t\in[T^{\text{start}},T^{\text{end}}] .
   \]

5. **Bidirectional conflict** – at most one train on a segment at any time (single‑track or shared opposite direction)  
   \[
   \sum_{i\in I} y_{i,s,t}\le 1 \qquad\forall s\in S,\; t\in T .
   \]

6. **Speed dynamics** – speed evolves according to acceleration/deceleration decisions  
   \[
   v_{i,s,t+1}=v_{i,s,t}+ \Delta\,a_{i,s,t}-\Delta\,d_{i,s,t}
   \qquad\forall i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T\setminus\{T_{\max}\}.
   \]

7. **Speed limits** – admissible speed range (already enforced by variable bounds)  
   \[
   L_{\min}\le v_{i,s,t}\le L_{\max}\qquad\forall i,s,t .
   \]

8. **Dwell time at stations** – departure must follow arrival by at least the minimum dwell time  
   \[
   D_i - A_i \ge \underline{d}_i \qquad\forall i\in I .
   \]

9. **Arrival‑departure consistency with travel times** – the arrival time equals the sum of travel times over occupied segments (linearised by assuming a worst‑case speed \(L_{\max}\) or by a tighter piece‑wise formulation)  
   \[
   A_i \ge \sum_{s\in S}\sum_{t\in T}\frac{\ell_s}{L_{\max}}\;\Delta\; y_{i,s,t}
   \qquad\forall i\in I .
   \]

   (A more accurate linearisation can replace the denominator by a convex combination of speed‑interval slopes.)

10. **Delay definition**  
    \[
    \delta_i = A_i - \hat A_i \qquad\forall i\in I,\qquad
    \delta_i \ge 0 .
    \]

11. **Piece‑wise linearisation of \(v^{2}\)**  

    *Exactly one interval active*  
    \[
    \sum_{k\in K} z_{i,s,t,k}=1 \qquad\forall i,s,t .
    \]

    *Link speed to interval bounds*  
    \[
    b_k\,z_{i,s,t,k}\le v_{i,s,t}\le b_{k+1}\,z_{i,s,t,k}+M\bigl(1-z_{i,s,t,k}\bigr)
    \qquad\forall i,s,t,k .
    \]

    *Linearised square*  
    \[
    v^{2}_{i,s,t}= \sum_{k\in K}\bigl(\sigma_k v_{i,s,t}+\eta_k\bigr)z_{i,s,t,k}
    \qquad\forall i,s,t .
    \]

12. **Acceleration/Deceleration exclusivity (optional)** – a train cannot accelerate and decelerate simultaneously on the same segment and period  
    \[
    a_{i,s,t}+d_{i,s,t}\le 1 \qquad\forall i,s,t .
    \]

**Assumptions / Remarks**

* All time is discretised into equal periods of length \(\Delta\).  
* Segment lengths are taken as unit length for the simplified travel‑time constraint; replace by actual \(\ell_s\) for realism.  
* The piece‑wise linear approximation of \(v^{2}\) uses break‑points \(\{0,20,40,60,80,100\}\) km/h (example) and coefficients \(\sigma_k,\eta_k\) that reproduce the quadratic curve within each interval.  
* Big‑M \(M\) is set to \(L_{\max}\) (or a larger safe value) to deactivate bounds when the interval is not selected.  
* The model is a pure MILP; all non‑linearities (quadratic speed term, travel‑time \( \ell_s/v\)) are linearised as described.  

The formulation above constitutes a complete mixed‑integer linear programming model for the **integrated train rescheduling and speed management problem (TRSMP)** under a partial‑segment blockage, capturing route choice, bidirectional conflict resolution, speed dynamics, and energy‑aware objective.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling & Speed‑Management MILP (Partial Segment Blockage)**  

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\). |
| \(S\) | Set of track segments, indexed by \(s\). |
| \(L\) | Set of admissible speed‑levels, indexed by \(\ell\) (each \(\ell\) has a constant speed \(v_\ell\)). |
| \(B\subseteq S\) | Segments that are **partially blocked**. |
| \(R\) | Set of feasible **routes** for a train (normally two: normal route and detour). |
| \(\text{Succ}_t\) | Ordered list of successive segment pairs \((s,s')\) for the route selected by train \(t\). |
| \(C\) | Set of conflict pairs \((t,s,d,t',s',d')\) – two trains in opposite directions that cannot occupy the same physical track simultaneously. |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(L_s\) | Length of segment \(s\) (km). |
| \(v_\ell\) | Speed of level \(\ell\) (km h\(^{-1}\)). |
| \(e_\ell\) | Energy consumption rate of level \(\ell\) (kWh km\(^{-1}\)). |
| \(U_{t,s}\) | Mandatory dwell time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) (min). |
| \(a_t\) | Planned departure time of train \(t\) from its origin (min). |
| \(d_t\) | Planned arrival time of train \(t\) at its destination (min). |
| \(B^{\text{start}}_s,\,B^{\text{end}}_s\) | Start / end of the blockage window on \(s\in B\) (min). |
| \(W^{\text{delay}}\) | Weight of total delay in the objective. |
| \(W^{\text{energy}}\) | Weight of total energy consumption in the objective. |
| \(M\) | Large constant (e.g., 10 000 min). |
| \(T_{\max}\) | Planning horizon (max time). |

---

### 3. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| \(x_{t,r}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) uses route \(r\). |
| \(z_{t,s,\ell}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses segment \(s\) with speed level \(\ell\). |
| \(s_{t,s}\ge0\) | continuous | **Start time** of train \(t\) on segment \(s\). |
| \(c_{t,s}\ge0\) | continuous | **Exit time** of train \(t\) from segment \(s\). |
| \(y_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | Auxiliary for blockage: 1 if train finishes segment \(s\) **before** the blockage, 0 otherwise. |
| \(\delta_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | Ordering on a conflict pair (which train passes first). |
| \(d_t\ge0\) | continuous | Total delay of train \(t\). |
| \(E\ge0\) | continuous | Total energy consumption of all trains. |

---

### 4. Model  

#### Objective  

\[
\min\; W^{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in T} d_t \;+\; W^{\text{energy}}\,E
\tag{OBJ}
\]

#### Route choice  

\[
\sum_{r\in R} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T \tag{R1}
\]

If segment \(s\) does **not** belong to the selected route, the corresponding speed variables are forced to 0  

\[
z_{t,s,\ell}\le \sum_{r:\,s\in r} x_{t,r}\qquad\forall t,s,\ell \tag{R2}
\]

#### Exactly one speed level per traversed segment  

\[
\sum_{\ell\in L} z_{t,s,\ell}= \sum_{r:\,s\in r} x_{t,r}\qquad\forall t,s \tag{S1}
\]

#### Temporal relation on a segment  

\[
c_{t,s}= s_{t,s}+ \sum_{\ell\in L}\frac{L_s}{v_\ell}\,z_{t,s,\ell}+U_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,s \tag{T1}
\]

#### Continuity along the route  

\[
s_{t,s'}\ge c_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,\;(s,s')\in\text{Succ}_t \tag{T2}
\]

#### Blockage‑avoidance (big‑M)  

\[
\begin{aligned}
c_{t,s}&\le B^{\text{start}}_s + M\,y_{t,s}\\
s_{t,s}&\ge B^{\text{end}}_s - M\,(1-y_{t,s})
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t,\;s\in B \tag{B1}
\]

\(y_{t,s}=1\) ⇒ train finishes before the blockage; \(y_{t,s}=0\) ⇒ train starts after it.

#### Bidirectional conflict (pairwise ordering)  

For every \((t,s,d,t',s',d')\in C\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
s_{t',s'} &\ge c_{t,s} - M\,\delta_{t,t',s}\\
s_{t,s}   &\ge c_{t',s'} - M\,(1-\delta_{t,t',s})\\
\delta_{t,t',s}&\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall (t,s,d,t',s',d')\in C \tag{C1}
\]

#### Delay definition  

\[
d_t \ge c_{t,\text{last}(t)} - d_t^{\text{plan}}\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{D1}
\]

where \(\text{last}(t)\) denotes the final segment of train \(t\).

#### Energy consumption  

\[
E = \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{\ell\in L} e_\ell\,L_s\,z_{t,s,\ell} \tag{E1}
\]

#### Horizon and non‑negativity  

\[
0\le s_{t,s},c_{t,s}\le T_{\max},\quad d_t\ge0,\quad E\ge0 \qquad\forall t,s \tag{H1}
\]

---

### 5. Remarks & Assumptions  

* **Route set** \(R\) contains at most two alternatives (normal line vs. opposite‑track detour).  
* **Speed levels** are pre‑defined; acceleration/deceleration phases are embedded in the chosen level (linearised travel time).  
* **Blockage** is a hard time window – a train may either finish the blocked segment before it opens or start after it closes (big‑M formulation).  
* **Conflict pairs** \(C\) are generated from all trains that share a physical track in opposite directions; the binary \(\delta\) linearises the “either‑or’’ ordering.  
* The model is a **pure MILP** (all products involve a binary variable and a constant).  

---

### 6. How to use  

1. **Data preparation** – enumerate for each train the feasible routes, the segment list for each route, segment lengths, speed‑level data, blockage windows, and conflict pairs.  
2. **Parameter setting** – choose reasonable weights \(W^{\text{delay}},W^{\text{energy}}\) to reflect the decision maker’s priority.  
3. **Solver** – feed the above formulation to any MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP). The optimal solution provides for every train: selected route, speed level on each segment, exact entry/exit times, incurred delay, and the total energy used.  

The model simultaneously guarantees **conflict‑free operation**, **respect of the blockage window**, **feasible speed‑derived travel times**, while **optimising the trade‑off between punctuality and energy consumption** – precisely the requirements described in the introductory text.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockages**

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\). |
| \(S\) | Set of directed track segments (arcs), indexed by \(s\). |
| \(K\) | Set of admissible speed levels, indexed by \(k\) (e.g. low, medium, high). |
| \(\mathcal{I}=\{1,\dots ,I_{\max}\}\) | Discrete time horizon (time‑slots of length \(\Delta\) minutes). |
| \(\mathcal{B}\subseteq S\times\mathcal{I}\) | Blocked segment–time pairs (segment \(s\) cannot be occupied at slot \(i\)). |
| \(\mathcal{C}\subseteq S\times S\) | Set of bidirectional conflict pairs \((s,s')\) that share the same physical track. |
| \(P_t\subseteq S\) | Ordered list of segments that train \(t\) must traverse (its planned route). |
| \(\text{pred}_t(s)\) | Predecessor segment of \(s\) on train \(t\)’s route (empty for the first segment). |
| \(\text{succ}_t(s)\) | Successor segment of \(s\) on train \(t\)’s route (empty for the last segment). |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning | Typical units |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| \(d_s\) | Length of segment \(s\) (km). |
| \(v_k\) | Speed associated with level \(k\) (km/h). |
| \(\tau_{s,k}= \big\lceil \frac{d_s}{v_k}\frac{60}{\Delta}\big\rceil\) | Travel‑time of segment \(s\) when speed level \(k\) is used (in slots). |
| \(e_{s,k}\) | Energy consumption for traversing segment \(s\) with speed level \(k\) (kWh). |
| \(a_t\) | Original planned arrival time of train \(t\) at its final destination (slot). |
| \(w^{\text{delay}}\) | Weight of total delay in the objective (€/slot). |
| \(w^{\text{energy}}\) | Weight of total energy consumption in the objective (€/kWh). |
| \(M\) | Large constant (>\(I_{\max}\)). |
| \(\underline{t}_{t,s},\;\overline{t}_{t,s}\) | Earliest / latest feasible start time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) (slots). |

---

### 3. Decision variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,s,i}\in\{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) **starts** segment \(s\) at the beginning of slot \(i\). |
| \(y_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses segment \(s\) with speed level \(k\). |
| \(z_{t,s,i}\in\{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) **occupies** segment \(s\) during slot \(i\). |
| \(\delta_t\ge 0\) | Continuous | Total delay of train \(t\) (slots). |

Auxiliary binary for linking (used in the linearization of the product \(x_{t,s,i}y_{t,s,k}\))  

\[
w_{t,s,i,k}\in\{0,1\}\quad\forall t,s,i,k .
\]

---

### 4. Model constraints  

#### 4.1 Speed‑level selection  
Exactly one speed level is chosen for every traversed segment  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} y_{t,s,k}= \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} x_{t,s,i}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in P_t . \tag{C1}
\]

#### 4.2 Linking start‑time, speed level and occupancy  

\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{t,s,i,k} &\le x_{t,s,i},\\
w_{t,s,i,k} &\le y_{t,s,k},\\
w_{t,s,i,k} &\ge x_{t,s,i}+y_{t,s,k}-1,\\[2pt]
z_{t,s,i'} &= \sum_{i,k:\; i\le i' \le i+\tau_{s,k}-1} w_{t,s,i,k}
\qquad\forall t,s,i'.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C2}
\]

Thus \(z_{t,s,i'}=1\) iff the train started the segment earlier and, with the chosen speed level, still occupies it at slot \(i'\).

#### 4.3 Temporal feasibility (precedence)  

\[
\sum_{i} i\,x_{t,\text{succ}_t(s),i}
\;\ge\;
\sum_{i} i\,x_{t,s,i}
\;+\;
\sum_{k}\tau_{s,k}\,y_{t,s,k}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in P_t\setminus\{\text{last}\}. \tag{C3}
\]

For the first segment of each train  

\[
\underline{t}_{t,s}\le\sum_{i} i\,x_{t,s,i}\le\overline{t}_{t,s}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\; s=\text{first}(P_t). \tag{C4}
\]

#### 4.4 Blockage constraints  

\[
z_{t,s,i}=0 \qquad\forall (s,i)\in\mathcal{B},\;\forall t\in T . \tag{C5}
\]

#### 4.5 Track‑capacity / bidirectional conflict  

For each conflict pair \((s,s')\in\mathcal{C}\) and each slot  

\[
z_{t,s,i}+z_{t',s',i}\le 1
\qquad\forall i\in\mathcal{I},\;\forall t,t'\in T . \tag{C6}
\]

(If the physical capacity of a segment is larger than 1, replace “1’’ by that capacity.)

#### 4.6 Delay definition  

Arrival time of train \(t\) at its final destination (last segment of \(P_t\))  

\[
\text{arr}_t=
\sum_{i} i\,x_{t,\text{last}(t),i}
\;+\;
\sum_{k}\tau_{\text{last}(t),k}\,y_{t,\text{last}(t),k}.
\tag{C7}
\]

Delay is the excess over the original schedule  

\[
\delta_t \ge \text{arr}_t - a_t ,\qquad \delta_t\ge 0
\qquad\forall t\in T . \tag{C8}
\]

#### 4.7 Variable domains  

\[
x_{t,s,i},\,y_{t,s,k},\,z_{t,s,i},\,w_{t,s,i,k}\in\{0,1\},
\qquad
\delta_t\ge 0 .
\tag{C9}
\]

---

### 5. Objective function  

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay and total energy consumption  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
w^{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in T}\delta_t
\;+\;
w^{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in P_t}\sum_{k\in K} e_{s,k}\,y_{t,s,k}
}
\tag{OBJ}
\]

The first term penalises passenger‑or system‑related lateness, the second term penalises the energy used by the chosen speed levels.  By adjusting \(w^{\text{delay}}\) and \(w^{\text{energy}}\) the decision maker can give priority to punctuality or sustainability.

---

### 6. Complete MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&
w^{\text{delay}}\sum_{t}\delta_t
+ w^{\text{energy}}\sum_{t}\sum_{s\in P_t}\sum_{k} e_{s,k}\,y_{t,s,k} \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(C1)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&\text{(C2)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&\text{(C3)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&\text{(C4)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&\text{(C5)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&\text{(C6)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&\text{(C7)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&\text{(C8)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&\text{(C9)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints and the objective are linear; the only integer variables are the binaries \(x,y,z,w\).  The model can be solved with any state‑of‑the‑art MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP, …).

---

### 7. Remarks & practical use  

* **Data preparation** – discretise the planning horizon (e.g., 5 min slots), choose a small speed‑level set \(K\), compute \(\tau_{s,k}\) and \(e_{s,k}\) from physical formulas, build the blockage set \(\mathcal{B}\) from the known partial segment outage, and build the conflict set \(\mathcal{C}\) for opposite‑direction arcs sharing the same track.  

* **Model size** – the number of binary variables is \(|T|\times|S|\times| \mathcal{I}|\) for \(x\) plus \(|T|\times|S|\times|K|\) for \(y\).  For large networks a decomposition (e.g., column generation, Benders) can be applied; the presented MILP is the *master* formulation.  

* **Interpretation of the solution** – the optimal \(x_{t,s,i}=1\) gives the exact timetable (departure from each segment), while the corresponding \(y_{t,s,k}=1\) provides the speed level (hence the speed profile) to be executed by the train‑control system.  The computed delays \(\delta_t\) and total energy allow a post‑hoc assessment of service quality and sustainability.  

---

**In summary**, the MILP above integrates **train rescheduling** (routing, timing, conflict avoidance) with **speed management** (choice of admissible speed levels) while explicitly handling **partial segment blockages** and **bidirectional track conflicts**.  The objective balances punctuality and energy efficiency, delivering a conflict‑free, executable timetable for high‑speed rail operations under disruption.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for Conflict‑Detection‑and‑Resolution (CDR) under Distance‑to‑Go (DTG) signalling**  
The formulation below is a complete, linear model that can be used directly in a commercial MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, …).  All symbols are defined, the objective is to minimise the total delay of all trains, and every constraint is written in a linear fashion.  Where data are not supplied in the description, reasonable assumptions are explicitly stated.

---

## 1.   Sets, Indices and Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning (indices) | Typical size |
|--------|-------------------|--------------|
| **T**   | Set of trains,  `t ∈ T` | ≤ 500 |
| **S**   | Set of track sections (blocks or TTD sections), `s ∈ S` | ≤ 2000 |
| **V**   | Set of possible speed‑profile choices, `v ∈ V` (e.g. “cruise‑speed”, “slow‑approach”) | 3‑5 |
| **N(s)**| Set of neighbour sections of *s* (immediate predecessor/successor) | ≤ 2 |
| **τ**   | Set of discrete time instants used for the planning horizon, `τ ∈ {0,…,H}` (minutes) | H ≈ 1200 |
| **π(t)**| Planned (original) departure time of train *t* from its first section (given) | – |
| **L_s**| Physical length of section *s* (km) | – |
| **Vmax_t**| Maximum allowable speed of train *t* (km/h) | – |
| **a_brk**| Uniform deceleration used for braking curves (km/h²) – assumed constant for all trains (typical 1.0 km/h²) | – |
| **Δ**   | Minimum safety time gap (seconds) imposed by signalling (e.g. 30 s) | – |
| **M**   | Large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints (e.g. 10⁶) | – |
| **c_t**| Cost coefficient for delaying train *t* (normally 1, can be weighted) | – |

### 1.1   Speed‑dependent braking distance  

For a train *t* travelling at speed *v* (km/h) the **braking distance** (km) is

\[
b_{t}(v)=\frac{v^{2}}{2\,a_{\text{brk}}}\qquad\text{(derived from }v^{2}=2 a s\text{)} .
\]

Because the model must stay linear, we pre‑compute the braking distance for every admissible speed‑profile *v* and store it as a parameter  

\[
B_{t,v}=b_{t}(v)\quad \forall t\in T,\;v\in V .
\]

---

## 2.   Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Definition |
|----------|------|------------|
| **x\_{t,s,τ}** | binary | 1 if train *t* **enters** section *s* at the beginning of time instant τ, 0 otherwise |
| **y\_{t,s,τ}** | binary | 1 if train *t* **leaves** section *s* at the end of time instant τ, 0 otherwise |
| **z\_{t,v}**   | binary | 1 if train *t* uses speed‑profile *v* (i.e., its cruising speed on free sections), 0 otherwise |
| **d\_t**       | continuous, ≥0 | Total delay (minutes) of train *t* with respect to its original schedule π(t) |
| **p\_{t,s,τ}** | binary | 1 if the **brake‑indication point** of train *t* lies inside section *s* at time τ (used for DTG safety) |
| **q\_{t,s,τ}** | binary | 1 if the **end‑of‑authority (EoA)** of train *t* lies inside section *s* at time τ (always the last occupied section) |

---

## 3.   Objective Function  

\[
\boxed{\min \; \sum_{t\in T} c_{t}\; d_{t}}
\]

The model minimises the total weighted delay of all trains.  If all \(c_t=1\) the objective is simply the sum of delays.

---

## 4.   Core Constraints  

### 4.1   Flow of a train through sections  

For every train *t* and every section *s*  

\[
\sum_{\tau=0}^{H} x_{t,s,\tau}= \sum_{\tau=0}^{H} y_{t,s,\tau}\qquad\forall t,s
\]

The train must leave a section as many times as it enters it (0 or 1 for each section).  

**Section‑entry/exit linking** (a train can leave a section only after it has entered it):

\[
\sum_{\tau'=0}^{\tau} x_{t,s,\tau'} \ge y_{t,s,\tau}\qquad\forall t,s,\tau
\tag{4.1}
\]

### 4.2   Single speed‑profile selection  

\[
\sum_{v\in V} z_{t,v}=1\qquad\forall t\in T
\tag{4.2}
\]

### 4.3   Travel‑time consistency  

If a train enters a section at time τ and leaves it at τ′, the travelling time must be at least the **minimum travel time** dictated by the chosen speed‑profile *v* and the section length.

Minimum travel time (minutes) for train *t*, speed‑profile *v* on section *s* :

\[
\theta_{t,s,v}= \frac{L_s}{\displaystyle \frac{V_{\max,t}\,z_{t,v}}{60}} \;=\; \frac{60\,L_s}{V_{\max,t}} \; \text{ (independent of v because Vmax is a bound)} .
\]

To keep the model linear we use a pre‑computed lower bound \(\underline{\theta}_{t,s}\) (e.g. the fastest feasible travel time). Then for every τ,τ′ :

\[
y_{t,s,\tau'} \le x_{t,s,\tau}\;+\;M\bigl(1-\delta_{t,s,\tau,\tau'}\bigr)
\]

with binary auxiliary \(\delta_{t,s,\tau,\tau'}\) that forces  

\[
\delta_{t,s,\tau,\tau'}=1 \;\Longrightarrow\; \tau'-\tau \ge \underline{\theta}_{t,s}
\]

Linearisation (big‑M) yields:

\[
\tau'-\tau + M(1-\delta_{t,s,\tau,\tau'}) \ge \underline{\theta}_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,s,\tau,\tau'
\tag{4.3}
\]

\[
\sum_{\tau'} \delta_{t,s,\tau,\tau'} = y_{t,s,\tau'}\qquad\forall t,s,\tau
\tag{4.4}
\]

(In practice the model is written with a *time‑indexed* flow, so (4.3) is replaced by a simple “minimum dwell” constraint: if a train enters at τ it cannot leave before τ+⌈\underline{\theta}_{t,s}⌉.)

### 4.4   Delay definition  

The **arrival time** at the last section of train *t* is the latest τ for which the train leaves that section:

\[
\text{Arr}_t = \sum_{\tau=0}^{H} \tau \; y_{t,s^{\text{last}}_{t},\tau}
\]

The scheduled arrival (without disturbances) is \(\pi(t)+\text{scheduled\_travel}_t\).  We capture the deviation as delay:

\[
d_t \ge \text{Arr}_t - \bigl(\pi(t)+\text{scheduled\_travel}_t\bigr)\qquad\forall t
\tag{4.5}
\]

\(d_t\) is forced to be non‑negative.

### 4.5   DTG safety – speed‑dependent separation  

Consider two distinct trains *t* and *t′* that travel on the **same** section *s* (or on neighbouring sections).  Under DTG the **brake‑indication point (IP)** of the following train must be placed at least the braking distance *behind* the rear of the leading train.  This is modelled by the **minimum headway** (in minutes) that depends on the speed of the leading train.

For a pair (t,t′) with *t* ahead of *t′* on section *s* we enforce:

\[
\sum_{\tau=0}^{H}\tau\, y_{t,s,\tau} \;+\; \underbrace{\frac{B_{t,v}}{V_{\max,t}}\,60}_{\text{braking‑time}} \;+\; \Delta \;\le\; \sum_{\tau=0}^{H}\tau\, x_{t′,s,\tau}
\qquad\forall t,t′,s,\;v\in V
\tag{4.6}
\]

The term \(\frac{B_{t,v}}{V_{\max,t}}\,60\) converts the braking distance (km) into a **time** (minutes) at the maximum speed of the leading train.  The binary variable \(z_{t,v}\) selects the correct *v*:

\[
\sum_{v\in V} \bigl( B_{t,v}\,z_{t,v}\bigr) \;=\; \text{effective braking distance for }t .
\]

Because (4.6) is non‑linear (product of binary \(z_{t,v}\) and continuous sums), we linearise it with auxiliary binaries \(w_{t,t′,s,v}\) :

\[
w_{t,t′,s,v} \le z_{t,v},\qquad
\sum_{v\in V} w_{t,t′,s,v}=1\qquad\forall t,t′,s
\]

and replace (4.6) by

\[
\sum_{\tau} \tau\, y_{t,s,\tau} \;+\; \frac{B_{t,v}}{V_{\max,t}}\,60\; w_{t,t′,s,v} \;+\; \Delta \;\le\; \sum_{\tau} \tau\, x_{t′,s,\tau}
\qquad\forall t\neq t′,\,s,\,v
\tag{4.7}
\]

Only the *active* speed‑profile of the leading train contributes to the headway.

### 4.6   End‑of‑Authority (EoA) consistency  

The **EoA** of a train is always the last occupied section.  We force the binary variable \(q_{t,s,\tau}\) to be 1 exactly when the train leaves *s* at τ and does **not** occupy any later section afterwards:

\[
q_{t,s,\tau} \le y_{t,s,\tau}\qquad\forall t,s,\tau
\tag{4.8}
\]

\[
q_{t,s,\tau} \le 1-\sum_{s'\succ s}\sum_{\tau'>\tau} y_{t,s',\tau'}\qquad\forall t,s,\tau
\tag{4.9}
\]

(Here “\(s'\succ s\)” denotes sections downstream of *s* on the route of *t*.)

The EoA is used only for reporting; it does not affect feasibility beyond (4.7) because the braking curve is already captured by the speed‑dependent headway.

### 4.7   Switch (junction) handling  

For sections that are **switches** (denoted by the subset \(S^{\text{sw}}\subseteq S\)) we must guarantee that at most one train occupies the switch at a time, regardless of speed:

\[
\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\tau=0}^{H} x_{t,s,\tau}\le 1\qquad\forall s\in S^{\text{sw}}
\tag{4.10}
\]

If a train traverses a switch, it must respect the same headway (4.7) as on normal sections.

### 4.8   Capacity of ordinary sections  

Ordinary sections are **single‑track** (one train at a time).  The classic fixed‑block capacity constraint is retained, but the DTG model relaxes it because a following train may enter earlier if the braking distance allows.  We therefore enforce only the **speed‑dependent headway** (4.7).  For completeness we can add an optional hard capacity:

\[
\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\tau=0}^{H} x_{t,s,\tau}\le 1\qquad\forall s\in S\setminus S^{\text{sw}}
\tag{4.11}
\]

If the railway is double‑track, (4.11) can be omitted.

### 4.9   Logical linking of brake‑indication point  

The brake‑indication point of a train must be placed **exactly** the braking distance before the EoA.  Using the pre‑computed distance \(B_{t,v}\) we write:

\[
\sum_{\tau} \tau\, p_{t,s,\tau}
\;=\;
\sum_{\tau} \tau\, q_{t,s',\tau}
\;-\;
\frac{B_{t,v}}{V_{\max,t}}\,60\;z_{t,v}
\qquad\forall t,\; \text{where } s\text{ is the section containing the IP and } s' \text{ the EoA}
\tag{4.12}
\]

In practice (4.12) is enforced only for the section pair that are *adjacent* on the route; the model therefore uses auxiliary binaries to select the correct pair.

---

## 5.   Summary of the Linear Model  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{t\in T} c_t d_t \\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(4.1)–(4.12)} && \text{(linear constraints)}\\
& x_{t,s,\tau},y_{t,s,\tau},z_{t,v},p_{t,s,\tau},q_{t,s,\tau},w_{t,t',s,v}\in\{0,1\}\\
& d_t\ge 0 &&\forall t\in T
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only non‑obvious part (the product of a binary speed‑profile selection with a continuous headway term) has been linearised via the auxiliary binaries \(w_{t,t',s,v}\).  The model therefore belongs to the class of **Mixed‑Integer Linear Programs (MILP)** and can be solved to optimality for realistic instances (tens to a few hundreds of trains, a few thousand sections) with modern branch‑and‑bound solvers.

---

## 6.   Key Modelling Assumptions (explicit)

| # | Assumption | Rationale |
|---|------------|-----------|
| A1 | Braking deceleration \(a_{\text{brk}}\) is constant for all trains. | Simplifies the braking‑distance formula; realistic values (≈ 1 km/h²) are widely used in ETCS‑L2 simulations. |
| A2 | Trains travel at their **maximum allowed speed** on free sections; speed‑profile choice *v* only modifies the braking distance (e.g., “slow‑approach” adds a safety margin). | Keeps the model linear; speed‑profile selection is captured by binary variables \(z_{t,v}\). |
| A3 | Time is discretised in 1‑minute intervals (Δτ = 1 min).  The planning horizon H is long enough to cover the whole day (e.g., 20 h = 1200 min). | Enables a classic time‑indexed MILP while preserving sufficient resolution for headway calculations. |
| A4 | Minimum safety time gap Δ (seconds) is added to the headway (converted to minutes). | Guarantees a non‑zero buffer even when braking distance is very small. |
| A5 | All sections are **single‑track** unless they belong to a predefined set of double‑track sections; capacity constraint (4.11) can be omitted for double‑track. | Mirrors typical main‑line railway topology. |
| A6 | Switches are modelled as special sections \(S^{\text{sw}}\) that cannot be occupied simultaneously (4.10). | Reflects the physical limitation of a point where routes diverge. |
| A7 | The end‑of‑authority (EoA) is always placed at the *down‑stream* end of the last occupied section (as required by ETCS‑L2 with TTD). | Matches the description of DTG signalling where the MA ends at a block/TTD boundary. |
| A8 | Pre‑computed parameters \(\underline{\theta}_{t,s}\) (minimum travel time) and \(B_{t,v}\) (braking distance) are exact, i.e., no further rounding is needed. | Guarantees linearity; any rounding error is negligible compared with the planning horizon. |

---

### How to use the model  

1. **Data preparation** – Build the sets *T*, *S*, *V*, the adjacency lists *N(s)*, the lengths *L_s*, the maximum speeds *Vmax_t*, the original timetable (π(t) and scheduled travel times).  
2. **Parameter computation** – Compute \(\underline{\theta}_{t,s}\) from \(L_s/V_{\max,t}\) (rounded up to the nearest minute) and the braking distances \(B_{t,v}\) for every speed‑profile.  
3. **Model building** – Insert the data into a MILP modelling language (e.g., Gurobi/Python, AMPL, JuMP).  
4. **Solve** – Run the solver; the optimal solution provides the revised entry/exit times (the \(x\) and \(y\) variables) and the selected speed‑profiles (\(z\)).  
5. **Interpretation** – From the solution extract the new timetable, total delay \(d_t\) for each train, and the locations of brake‑indication points (\(p\)) and EoAs (\(q\)).  

The resulting schedule respects **speed‑dependent separation** inherent to DTG signalling, while minimising the total delay, thus delivering a mathematically‑sound decision support tool for real‑time railway traffic management.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRS‑MP)**  
*Partial‑segment‑blockage disruption – bidirectional conflict resolution*  

---

## 1. Sets, Indices and Parameters  *(assumptions are explicitly marked)*  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** = {1,…,|T|} | Set of trains (indexed by *t*). |
| **S** = {1,…,|S|} | Set of stations (including the two terminals). |
| **E** = { (i,j) | i,j∈S, i<j } | Set of track‑segments (directed arcs) between consecutive stations. |
| **B** ⊆ **E** | Set of *blocked* segments (partial‑blockage area). |
| **D** = { (t,i) | t∈T, i∈S } | Train‑station pairs (arrival/departure events). |
| **K** = {1,…,Kmax} | Set of *speed‑profile* plans that can be assigned to a train on a given segment (see §2). |
| **Δt** | Length of the planning horizon discretisation (e.g. 1 min). |
| **H** | Set of discrete time‑instants 0,Δt,2Δt,…,Hmax (Hmax = planning horizon). |
| **τ⁰_{t,i}** | Original (pre‑disruption) scheduled arrival time of train *t* at station *i*. |
| **σ⁰_{t,i}** | Original scheduled departure time of train *t* from station *i*. |
| **L_{i,j}** | Physical length of segment (i,j) (km). |
| **v^{max}_{i,j}**, **v^{min}_{i,j}** | Upper / lower admissible speed on segment (i,j) (km/h). |
| **a^{max}_{i,j}**, **a^{min}_{i,j}** | Max acceleration / deceleration on segment (i,j) (km/h²). |
| **c^{E}_{t,i,j,k}** | Energy consumption (kWh) of train *t* when travelling on (i,j) with plan *k*. |
| **c^{D}_{t,i}** | Penalty cost for deviating from the original departure time at station *i* (e.g. passenger dissatisfaction). |
| **M** | “Big‑M’’ constant (larger than any feasible time value, e.g. 10⁶). |
| **ε** | Small positive number used for strict ordering (e.g. 1 s). |

**Assumptions (explicitly stated):**  

1. *Deterministic* disruption: the blockage of each segment **b∈B** is known a priori and lasts from time **τ^{b, start}** to **τ^{b, end}**.  
2. Trains are *bidirectional* on a single track; only one train may occupy a segment at a given instant (conflict‑avoidance).  
3. Each train may *reroute* around a blocked segment by using the opposite track (modeled as an alternative arc (j,i) with the same length).  
4. Speed on a segment is represented by a *finite* set of pre‑computed admissible speed‑profiles **k∈K** (piece‑wise constant acceleration/velocity).  
5. Dwell time at a station is a *decision variable* bounded between a minimum and a maximum (passenger boarding/alighting time).  
6. All trains are identical with respect to dynamic limits (a^{max}, a^{min}, v^{max}, v^{min}); heterogeneity can be introduced by indexing parameters with *t* if needed.  

---

## 2. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| **a_{t,i}** | Continuous ≥0 | Actual *arrival* time of train *t* at station *i*. |
| **d_{t,i}** | Continuous ≥0 | Actual *departure* time of train *t* from station *i*. |
| **w_{t,i}** | Continuous ≥0 | Dwell time at station *i* for train *t* ( w_{t,i}= d_{t,i} – a_{t,i} ). |
| **x_{t,i,j}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if train *t* traverses segment (i,j) in the forward direction; 0 otherwise. |
| **y_{t,i,j}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if train *t* traverses segment (i,j) in the *reverse* direction (i.e., uses opposite track for rerouting). |
| **z_{t,i,j,k}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if plan *k* is selected for train *t* on segment (i,j). |
| **u_{t,i,j,τ}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if train *t* occupies segment (i,j) at discrete instant τ∈H. |
| **π_{t,i}** ∈ {1,…,|T|} | Integer | *Position* (order) of train *t* on a shared segment (used for conflict‑avoidance). |

Additional auxiliary variables (linearisation):  

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| **Δ_{t,i,j}** | Continuous ≥0 | Travel time of train *t* on segment (i,j). |
| **β_{t,i,j}** | Continuous ≥0 | “Slack’’ variable for energy‑efficiency objective (optional). |

---

## 3. Objective Function  

The integrated model simultaneously minimises **(i)** total passenger‑related delay cost, **(ii)** total energy consumption, and **(iii)** a small penalty for the number of reroutings (to avoid unnecessary use of opposite track). A weighted linear combination is used:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \;  & \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in S} c^{D}_{t,i}\,\bigl|\,d_{t,i}-\sigma^{0}_{t,i}\,\bigr|}_{\text{Delay penalty}} \\
& + \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in E}\sum_{k\in K} c^{E}_{t,i,j,k}\,z_{t,i,j,k}}_{\text{Energy consumption}} \\
& + \underbrace{\lambda \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in B}\bigl(y_{t,i,j}\bigr)}_{\text{Rerouting penalty}} .
\end{aligned}
\tag{OBJ}
\]

*The absolute value in the first term can be linearised by introducing two non‑negative variables* \(p^{+}_{t,i},p^{-}_{t,i}\) *with* \(d_{t,i}-\sigma^{0}_{t,i}=p^{+}_{t,i}-p^{-}_{t,i}\) *and* \(c^{D}_{t,i}\bigl|d_{t,i}-\sigma^{0}_{t,i}\bigr| = c^{D}_{t,i}(p^{+}_{t,i}+p^{-}_{t,i})\).

\(\lambda>0\) is a small weight that discourages unnecessary rerouting.

---

## 4. Constraints  

### 4.1 Logical consistency of routing  

1. **Exactly one direction per segment** (forward, reverse or not used)  

\[
x_{t,i,j}+y_{t,i,j}= \begin{cases}
1 & \text{if train }t\text{ must travel from }i\text{ to }j\;(i,j)\in\text{its route}\\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in E .
\tag{R1}
\]

2. **Plan selection** – exactly one speed‑profile per traversed segment  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} z_{t,i,j,k}= x_{t,i,j}+y_{t,i,j}\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in E .
\tag{R2}
\]

### 4.2 Time‑flow (timetable) constraints  

3. **Dwell time definition**  

\[
d_{t,i}=a_{t,i}+w_{t,i}\qquad\forall t,\;i\in S .
\tag{T1}
\]

4. **Minimum/maximum dwell**  

\[
w^{\min }_{t,i}\le w_{t,i}\le w^{\max }_{t,i}\qquad\forall t,i .
\tag{T2}
\]

5. **Travel‑time linking with selected plan**  

\[
\Delta_{t,i,j}= \sum_{k\in K}\frac{L_{i,j}}{v_{k}}\,z_{t,i,j,k}
\qquad\forall t,(i,j)\in E .
\tag{T3}
\]

*(Here \(v_{k}\) is the average speed of plan *k*; if a plan includes acceleration/deceleration phases, the corresponding travel time can be pre‑computed.)*

6. **Temporal precedence along the route**  

\[
a_{t,j}\;\ge\; d_{t,i} + \Delta_{t,i,j} \qquad \forall t,\;(i,j)\in E \text{ with } x_{t,i,j}=1 .
\tag{T4}
\]

If the train uses the reverse direction (rerouting) the same constraint holds with \(y_{t,i,j}=1\).

### 4.3 Blockage feasibility  

7. **No occupation of blocked segment during its closure**  

\[
u_{t,i,j,\tau}\le 1- \mathbf{1}_{\{\tau^{b,start}\le \tau\le \tau^{b,end}\}}\qquad 
\forall t,\;(i,j)\in B,\;\forall \tau\in H .
\tag{B1}
\]

(If a train traverses the blocked segment, the binary occupancy variable must be 0 during the blockage; otherwise the model will be infeasible.)

8. **Link occupancy to travel times** (big‑M linearisation)  

\[
u_{t,i,j,\tau}\ge 
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if } a_{t,i}\le \tau\Delta t \le a_{t,i}+ \Delta_{t,i,j} \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\]

Implemented with:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau\Delta t - a_{t,i} &\le M\,u_{t,i,j,\tau} ,\\
a_{t,i}+ \Delta_{t,i,j} - \tau\Delta t &\le M\,(1-u_{t,i,j,\tau}) .
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t,(i,j),\tau .
\tag{B2}
\]

### 4.4 Bidirectional conflict‑avoidance on a single track  

9. **At most one train on a segment at any instant**  

\[
\sum_{t\in T} u_{t,i,j,\tau} \le 1 \qquad\forall (i,j)\in E\setminus B,\;\forall \tau\in H .
\tag{C1}
\]

(For blocked segments the constraint is automatically satisfied because of (B1).)

10. **Ordering variables to break symmetry (optional, improves MILP strength)**  

If two trains occupy the same segment at different times, the ordering variable \(\pi_{t,i,j}\) ensures a linear precedence:

\[
a_{t',i} \ge d_{t,i} + \epsilon - M\,(1-\theta_{t,t',i,j})\qquad\forall t\neq t',\;(i,j)\in E .
\tag{C2}
\]

where \(\theta_{t,t',i,j}\in\{0,1\}\) indicates that train *t* precedes train *t'* on segment (i,j).  
Additionally:

\[
\theta_{t,t',i,j} + \theta_{t',t,i,j}=1 \qquad\forall t\neq t',\;(i,j)\in E .
\tag{C3}
\]

### 4.5 Rerouting feasibility  

11. **Rerouting only allowed on blocked segments**  

\[
y_{t,i,j}\le \mathbf{1}_{\{(i,j)\in B\}}\qquad\forall t,(i,j)\in E .
\tag{R3}
\]

12. **Maximum number of simultaneous reroutings (capacity of opposite track)**  

\[
\sum_{t\in T} y_{t,i,j}\le C^{opp}_{i,j}\qquad\forall (i,j)\in B .
\tag{R4}
\]

\(C^{opp}_{i,j}\) is the capacity of the opposite track (normally 1, but can be larger if signalling permits).  

### 4.6 Physical speed limits  

13. **Speed‑profile respects segment limits** (already embedded in the pre‑computed set **K**, but we can enforce)**  

\[
v^{min}_{i,j}\le v_{k}\le v^{max}_{i,j}\qquad\forall k\in K,\;(i,j)\in E .
\tag{S1}
\]

If a plan includes acceleration/deceleration phases, the corresponding **a^{max}**, **a^{min}** are already satisfied by construction.  

### 4.7 Domain restrictions  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& a_{t,i}, d_{t,i}, w_{t,i}, \Delta_{t,i,j}\ge 0 &&\forall t,i,(i,j)\\
& x_{t,i,j},y_{t,i,j},z_{t,i,j,k},u_{t,i,j,\tau},\theta_{t,t',i,j}\in\{0,1\} &&\forall\text{indices}\\
& \pi_{t,i,j}\in\{1,\dots,|T|\} &&\forall t,i,j .
\end{aligned}
\tag{D}
\]

---

## 5. Full MILP Statement  

Putting everything together, the **TRS‑MP** is:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in S} c^{D}_{t,i}\,(p^{+}_{t,i}+p^{-}_{t,i})
        + \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in E}\sum_{k\in K} c^{E}_{t,i,j,k}\,z_{t,i,j,k}
        + \lambda \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in B} y_{t,i,j} \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\begin{cases}
d_{t,i}=a_{t,i}+w_{t,i} &\forall t,i \\
w^{\min }_{t,i}\le w_{t,i}\le w^{\max }_{t,i} &\forall t,i \\
\Delta_{t,i,j}= \displaystyle\sum_{k\in K}\frac{L_{i,j}}{v_{k}}\,z_{t,i,j,k} &\forall t,(i,j)\\
a_{t,j}\ge d_{t,i}+ \Delta_{t,i,j} - M(1-x_{t,i,j}) &\forall t,(i,j)\\
a_{t,j}\ge d_{t,i}+ \Delta_{t,i,j} - M(1-y_{t,i,j}) &\forall t,(i,j)\\
x_{t,i,j}+y_{t,i,j}= \begin{cases}1 &\text{if }(i,j)\text{ belongs to }t\text{'s route}\\0&\text{otherwise}\end{cases}&\forall t,(i,j)\\
\sum_{k\in K}z_{t,i,j,k}=x_{t,i,j}+y_{t,i,j} &\forall t,(i,j)\\
u_{t,i,j,\tau}\le 1-\mathbf{1}_{\{\tau^{b,start}\le \tau\le \tau^{b,end}\}} &\forall t,(i,j)\in B,\;\tau\\
\tau\Delta t - a_{t,i}\le M\,u_{t,i,j,\tau} &\forall t,(i,j),\tau\\
a_{t,i}+ \Delta_{t,i,j} - \tau\Delta t \le M\,(1-u_{t,i,j,\tau}) &\forall t,(i,j),\tau\\
\sum_{t\in T} u_{t,i,j,\tau}\le 1 &\forall (i,j)\in E\setminus B,\;\tau\\
a_{t',i}\ge d_{t,i}+ \epsilon - M(1-\theta_{t,t',i,j}) &\forall t\neq t', (i,j)\\
\theta_{t,t',i,j}+ \theta_{t',t,i,j}=1 &\forall t\neq t', (i,j)\\
y_{t,i,j}\le \mathbf{1}_{\{(i,j)\in B\}} &\forall t,(i,j)\\
\sum_{t\in T} y_{t,i,j}\le C^{opp}_{i,j} &\forall (i,j)\in B\\
d_{t,i}-\sigma^{0}_{t,i}=p^{+}_{t,i}-p^{-}_{t,i} &\forall t,i\\
p^{+}_{t,i},p^{-}_{t,i}\ge 0 &\forall t,i\\
\text{Domain restrictions } (D) .
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 6. Remarks on Model Use  

1. **Linearisation** – All non‑linearities (absolute value, “if‑then’’ logical relations, travel‑time linking) are linearised through binary variables and big‑M constraints, yielding a pure MILP.  
2. **Scalability** – For large networks the number of occupancy binaries \(u_{t,i,j,\tau}\) can be reduced by *time‑window aggregation* (e.g., using interval‑based variables) – this is the basis of the decomposition described in the source paper.  
3. **Energy data** – The coefficients \(c^{E}_{t,i,j,k}\) are obtained from a separate train‑dynamics sub‑model (e.g., a convex energy‑consumption approximation) and are treated as parameters in the MILP.  
4. **Extension** – Passenger‑connection penalties, crew‑scheduling, or stochastic disruption durations can be added by introducing extra sets and variables while preserving linearity.  

---

**Thus the formulation above constitutes a complete mixed‑integer linear programming model for the *Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem* (TRS‑MP) under partial‑segment blockages, capturing (i) conflict‑free routing on a single bidirectional track, (ii) integrated selection of speed‑profile plans, and (iii) a bi‑objective (delay + energy) optimisation.**
