Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP)**  
The model below captures (i) the choice of departure/arrival times, (ii) possible rerouting on the opposite track during a partial‑segment blockage, (iii) the order of trains that share a track segment, and (iv) a linearised representation of the speed profile that determines the running time on each elementary track‑section.  

All indices, parameters, decision variables and constraints are listed first, followed by the complete mathematical formulation.  Where information is not supplied in the description, reasonable assumptions are made and explicitly flagged (**Assumption**).

---

## 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** = {1,…, |T|} | Set of trains that have to be scheduled (including those that may be cancelled). |
| **S** = {1,…, |S|} | Set of stations (including the origin and terminal of every train). |
| **L** = {1,…, |L|} | Set of *track‑sections* (elementary line segments) between two consecutive stations. |
| **B** ⊆ **L** | Subset of sections that are *blocked* (partial‑segment blockage) during the disruption window. |
| **K** = {1,…, |K|} | Set of *time‑intervals* used to discretise the disruption window for linearisation of speed‑energy relations (see Assumption A3). |
| **D** = {1,2} | Direction index: 1 = “normal” (track side that is normally used by the train), 2 = “opposite” (rerouting on the other side of the double‑track). |

*Auxiliary index:*  
\( (i,j) \in \mathcal{P}_t\) denotes the ordered pair of consecutive stations visited by train \(t\) (i.e. the *path* of train \(t\)).  

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical Value / Source |
|--------|-------------|------------------------|
| \(a_{t,s}\) | Scheduled (original) arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\). | From the pre‑disruption timetable. |
| \(d_{t,s}\) | Scheduled departure time of train \(t\) from station \(s\). | From the pre‑disruption timetable. |
| \(L_{i,j}\) | Physical length (km) of the track‑section between stations \(i\) and \(j\). | Infrastructure data. |
| \(\underline{v}_{i,j}\) , \(\overline{v}_{i,j}\) | Minimum / maximum admissible speed (km/h) on section \((i,j)\). | Safety / line‑capacity limits. |
| \(\alpha_{i,j}\) , \(\beta_{i,j}\) | Linear coefficients that approximate the **energy consumption** on section \((i,j)\) as a function of the *average speed* \(v_{t,i,j}\) (see Assumption A4).  Energy = \(\alpha_{i,j} v + \beta_{i,j}\). |
| \(T^{\text{start}} , T^{\text{end}}\) | Beginning and end of the disruption time window (minutes from midnight). | Given by the disruption scenario. |
| \(M\) | A large positive constant (big‑M) used for logical constraints. | E.g. 10 000 min. |
| \(\gamma\) | Weight of the energy‑minimisation term in the objective (0 ≤ γ ≤ 1). | Decision‑maker preference. |
| \(\rho\) | Penalty cost for cancelling a train (large enough to discourage unnecessary cancellations). | E.g. 10 000 € per cancelled train. |
| \(\psi\) | Penalty for violating the original order of two trains on a shared section (used to keep the solution close to the original schedule). | Small positive value. |
| \(\delta_{t}^{\text{max}}\) | Maximum allowable delay (minutes) for train \(t\) (service‑level requirement). | Typically 30 min. |
| \(\theta_{i,j}\) | Binary indicator: 1 if section \((i,j)\) belongs to the blocked set **B**, 0 otherwise. | From disruption description. |
| \(p_{i,j}^{\text{min}}\) , \(p_{i,j}^{\text{max}}\) | Minimum / maximum *travel time* on section \((i,j)\) when travelling at \(\underline{v}_{i,j}\) / \(\overline{v}_{i,j}\).  \(p_{i,j}^{\text{min}} = \frac{L_{i,j}}{\overline{v}_{i,j}}\), \(p_{i,j}^{\text{max}} = \frac{L_{i,j}}{\underline{v}_{i,j}}\). | Derived from speed limits. |
| \(c_{i,j}\) | Minimum head‑way (minutes) required between two successive trains travelling in the same direction on section \((i,j)\). | Safety rule (e.g., 3 min). |
| \(c_{i,j}^{\text{opp}}\) | Minimum head‑way for opposite‑direction trains sharing the *same* physical track (when one uses the opposite side). | Usually larger than \(c_{i,j}\) (e.g., 5 min). |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} \ge 0\) | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\). |
| \(x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} \ge 0\) | Continuous | Actual departure time of train \(t\) from station \(s\). |
| \(y_{t,i,j} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses section \((i,j)\) on its *normal* side, 0 otherwise. |
| \(z_{t,i,j} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses section \((i,j)\) on the *opposite* side (rerouting). |
| \(u_{t,i,j} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) **uses** section \((i,j)\) (i.e. either normal or opposite).  \(u_{t,i,j}=y_{t,i,j}+z_{t,i,j}\). |
| \(v_{t,i,j} \ge 0\) | Continuous | *Average speed* of train \(t\) on section \((i,j)\) (km/h). |
| \(\tau_{t,i,j} \ge 0\) | Continuous | Travel time of train \(t\) on section \((i,j)\) (minutes). |
| \(\eta_{t}\in\{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) is **cancelled**; 0 otherwise. |
| \(\sigma_{t,i,j}^{\text{ord}} \in\{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) is scheduled **before** train \(i\) on shared section \((i,j)\) (see ordering constraints). |
| \(\lambda_{i,j}^{\text{conf}} \ge 0\) | Continuous | Slack variable that measures violation of head‑way constraints (penalised in the objective to keep solution feasible). |

*Additional auxiliary variables for linearisation (Assumption A3):*  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(w_{t,i,j}^{k} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if travel time \(\tau_{t,i,j}\) falls into discretised interval \(k\) (used to linearise the energy function). |
| \(\tau_{i,j}^{k,\min},\tau_{i,j}^{k,\max}\) | Parameters | Lower/upper bound of travel‑time interval \(k\) on section \((i,j)\). |

---

## 4. Assumptions  

| # | Statement |
|---|-----------|
| **A1** | Each train follows a *fixed* station sequence (no intermediate stops are added/removed). |
| **A2** | The disruption only blocks one side of a double‑track line; the opposite side remains physically usable after a short safety‑check delay. |
| **A3** | Energy consumption on a section is approximated by a piece‑wise linear function of the average speed; the piecewise representation is captured by the binary variables \(w_{t,i,j}^{k}\). |
| **A4** | The relationship between speed and travel time on a section is linearised by the constraints \(\tau_{t,i,j}=L_{i,j}/v_{t,i,j}\) and bounded by \([p_{i,j}^{\text{min}},p_{i,j}^{\text{max}}]\). The exact non‑linear term is replaced by the McCormick envelope (see constraints). |
| **A5** | Dwell time at a station is assumed to be a *minimum* value \(h_{s}^{\text{min}}\) (e.g., 2 min) and can be increased arbitrarily to absorb delays; the model does not penalise longer dwell times except through the delay‑penalty term. |
| **A6** | Cancellation of a train removes all its constraints except the cancellation penalty; cancelled trains do not occupy any track sections. |
| **A7** | All times are measured in minutes from a common reference (e.g., midnight). |

---

## 5. Model Formulation  

### 5.1 Objective Function  

The decision maker wants to (i) **minimise total delay**, (ii) **minimise energy consumption**, (iii) **avoid unnecessary cancellations**, and (iv) **respect the original train ordering**. A weighted linear objective is used:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \underbrace{(1-\gamma)\Bigg[ \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} \bigl( x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}}-a_{t,s}\bigr) \Bigg]}_{\text{Total delay (weighted)}} \\
& + \underbrace{\gamma \Bigg[ \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in L} \bigl(\alpha_{i,j} v_{t,i,j} + \beta_{i,j}\bigr) u_{t,i,j}\Bigg]}_{\text{Total energy (weighted)}} \\
& + \underbrace{\rho \sum_{t\in T} \eta_{t}}_{\text{Cancellation penalty}} \\
& + \underbrace{\psi \sum_{(i,j)\in L}\sum_{t\neq t'} \bigl| \sigma_{t,i,j}^{\text{ord}} - \sigma_{t',i,j}^{\text{ord}} \bigr|}_{\text{Order‑preservation penalty}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

*Explanation:*  
- The first term sums the **arrival‑time deviations** from the original schedule (delay).  
- The second term aggregates the **linearised energy** on every travelled section.  
- The third term heavily penalises cancelled trains.  
- The fourth term penalises changes in the relative order of two trains that share a section (keeps the solution close to the original timetable).

### 5.2 Core Constraints  

#### 5.2.1 Time‑flow on each train  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} \; \ge \; x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} + h_{s}^{\text{min}} \quad &&\forall t\in T,\; s\in S \tag{C1}\\
& x_{t,j}^{\text{arr}} \; = \; x_{t,i}^{\text{dep}} + \tau_{t,i,j} \quad &&\forall t\in T,\; (i,j)\in \mathcal{P}_t \tag{C2}
\end{aligned}
\]

\(h_{s}^{\text{min}}\) is the minimum dwell time (Assumption A5).  

#### 5.2.2 Travel‑time – speed coupling (linearisation of \(\tau = L/v\))

Using McCormick envelopes for the bilinear term \(L_{i,j}=v_{t,i,j}\tau_{t,i,j}\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
& \tau_{t,i,j} \ge \frac{L_{i,j}}{\overline{v}_{i,j}} \quad &&\forall t,i,j \tag{C3a}\\
& \tau_{t,i,j} \le \frac{L_{i,j}}{\underline{v}_{i,j}} \quad &&\forall t,i,j \tag{C3b}\\
& v_{t,i,j} \ge \underline{v}_{i,j} u_{t,i,j} \quad &&\forall t,i,j \tag{C3c}\\
& v_{t,i,j} \le \overline{v}_{i,j} u_{t,i,j} \quad &&\forall t,i,j \tag{C3d}
\end{aligned}
\]

If a train does **not** use the section (\(u_{t,i,j}=0\)) the bounds force \(v_{t,i,j}=0\) and \(\tau_{t,i,j}=0\).

#### 5.2.3 Blockage‑avoidance (routing decision)

A train may traverse a blocked section only on the opposite side *and* only **outside** the disruption window:

\[
\begin{aligned}
& y_{t,i,j} \le 1-\theta_{i,j} \quad &&\forall t,i,j \tag{C4a}\\
& z_{t,i,j} \le \theta_{i,j} \quad &&\forall t,i,j \tag{C4b}\\
& \text{If } \theta_{i,j}=1 \text{ (blocked)}:\;
   \begin{cases}
      x_{t,i}^{\text{dep}} \ge T^{\text{end}} \quad \text{or} \\
      x_{t,i}^{\text{arr}} \le T^{\text{start}}
   \end{cases}
   \;\; \text{whenever } y_{t,i,j}=1 . \tag{C4c}
\end{aligned}
\]

Constraint (C4c) forces a train that would use the **normal** side of a blocked section to either finish traversing the section **before** the disruption starts or start **after** it ends.  

#### 5.2.4 Binary routing consistency  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& u_{t,i,j}= y_{t,i,j}+z_{t,i,j} \quad &&\forall t,i,j \tag{C5}\\
& y_{t,i,j},\,z_{t,i,j}\in\{0,1\},\; u_{t,i,j}\in\{0,1\}. 
\end{aligned}
\]

#### 5.2.5 Head‑way (conflict‑avoidance)  

For any two distinct trains \(t\) and \(t'\) that **both** use the same physical track (i.e. same direction on the same side) on section \((i,j)\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
& x_{t',i}^{\text{dep}} \; \ge \; x_{t,i}^{\text{dep}} + c_{i,j}\;-\; M\,(1-\sigma_{t,i,j}^{\text{ord}}) \quad &&\forall t\neq t',\;(i,j)\in L \tag{C6a}\\
& x_{t,i}^{\text{dep}} \; \ge \; x_{t',i}^{\text{dep}} + c_{i,j}\;-\; M\,\sigma_{t,i,j}^{\text{ord}} \quad &&\forall t\neq t',\;(i,j)\in L \tag{C6b}\\
& \sigma_{t,i,j}^{\text{ord}} \in \{0,1\}. 
\end{aligned}
\]

If both trains travel on **opposite** sides (i.e. one uses \(y\), the other uses \(z\) on the same physical segment), the required head‑way is larger:

\[
x_{t',i}^{\text{dep}} \ge x_{t,i}^{\text{dep}} + c_{i,j}^{\text{opp}} - M\bigl(1-\sigma_{t,i,j}^{\text{ord}}\bigr) .
\]

The binary variable \(\sigma_{t,i,j}^{\text{ord}}\) decides which train is scheduled first; the objective penalises changes in this ordering (see the last term of the objective).

#### 5.2.6 Delay limits  

\[
x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} \le a_{t,s} + \delta_{t}^{\text{max}} \;+\; M \eta_{t}\quad \forall t,s \tag{C7}
\]

If train \(t\) is cancelled (\(\eta_{t}=1\)), the constraint is relaxed.

#### 5.2.7 Cancellation logic  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} = a_{t,s}\;,\; x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} = d_{t,s}\quad &&\forall t,s\text{ if } \eta_{t}=1 \tag{C8a}\\
& u_{t,i,j}=0 \quad &&\forall i,j \text{ if } \eta_{t}=1 \tag{C8b}\\
& \eta_{t}\in\{0,1\}. 
\end{aligned}
\]

#### 5.2.8 Piece‑wise linear energy approximation  

For each section \((i,j)\) we pre‑define \(K\) travel‑time intervals \([\tau_{i,j}^{k,\min},\tau_{i,j}^{k,\max}]\). Exactly one interval is selected for each travelled section:

\[
\begin{aligned}
& \sum_{k=1}^{K} w_{t,i,j}^{k}= u_{t,i,j} \quad &&\forall t,i,j \tag{C9a}\\
& \tau_{i,j}^{k,\min} w_{t,i,j}^{k} \le \tau_{t,i,j} \le \tau_{i,j}^{k,\max} w_{t,i,j}^{k} + M(1-w_{t,i,j}^{k}) \quad &&\forall t,i,j,k \tag{C9b}\\
& w_{t,i,j}^{k}\in\{0,1\}. 
\end{aligned}
\]

The **energy** contribution of train \(t\) on section \((i,j)\) is then expressed linearly as:

\[
E_{t,i,j}= \sum_{k=1}^{K}\bigl(\alpha_{i,j}^{k} v_{t,i,j}+ \beta_{i,j}^{k}\bigr) w_{t,i,j}^{k},
\]

where \(\alpha_{i,j}^{k},\beta_{i,j}^{k}\) are the coefficients of the linear segment that corresponds to interval \(k\). In the objective we simply use \(\alpha_{i,j} v_{t,i,j}+ \beta_{i,j}\) because the binary \(w\) variables already enforce the correct segment.

---

## 6. Complete MILP  

Putting everything together, the **TRSMP MILP** reads:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & (1-\gamma)\!\!\sum_{t\in T}\!\sum_{s\in S}\!\bigl(x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}}-a_{t,s}\bigr) 
        + \gamma\!\!\sum_{t\in T}\!\sum_{(i,j)\in L}\!\bigl(\alpha_{i,j} v_{t,i,j}+ \beta_{i,j}\bigr)u_{t,i,j}\\
        &\;+\; \rho\!\sum_{t\in T}\!\eta_{t}
        +\; \psi\!\sum_{(i,j)\in L}\!\sum_{t\neq t'}\!\bigl| \sigma_{t,i,j}^{\text{ord}}-\sigma_{t',i,j}^{\text{ord}}\bigr| \\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } 
        & \text{(C1)–(C9)} \\
        & x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}},x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}},\tau_{t,i,j},v_{t,i,j}\ge 0\\
        & y_{t,i,j},z_{t,i,j},u_{t,i,j},w_{t,i,j}^{k},\sigma_{t,i,j}^{\text{ord}}\in\{0,1\}\\
        & \eta_{t}\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear (or linearised) and all integer variables are binary, therefore the model is a **mixed‑integer linear program (MILP)**.

---

## 7. Remarks on the Model  

1. **Bidirectional conflict handling** – By distinguishing normal (\(y\)) and opposite (\(z\)) side usage, the model can schedule a train to *reroute* onto the opposite track during the blockage while still respecting a larger head‑way \(c_{i,j}^{\text{opp}}\).  

2. **Coupling of rescheduling and speed** – Variables \(\tau_{t,i,j}\) and \(v_{t,i,j}\) link the timetable (arrival/departure times) with the speed profile. The McCormick envelope (C3) guarantees that the travel time corresponds to the chosen speed, while the piece‑wise linear energy term captures the energy‑delay trade‑off.  

3. **Cancellation** – The binary \(\eta_t\) allows the model to drop a train completely when the disruption makes it impossible to serve it within the allowed delay bound. The large penalty \(\rho\) ensures that cancellations are used only as a last resort.  

4. **Decomposition potential** – The model naturally separates into (i) a *master* integer program that decides the binary routing/order variables \((y,z,\sigma,\eta)\) and (ii) a set of *sub‑problems* (one per train) that, given a routing, solve a small linear program for the speed‑time variables \((v,\tau)\). This structure matches the decomposition approach described in the paper.  

5. **Scalability** – The number of binary variables grows with \(|T|\times|L|\) (routing) plus \(|T|^2\times|L|\) (ordering). In practice, ordering variables are introduced only for pairs of trains that share a section (sparsity can be exploited).  

---

**End of formulation**.

**Variables**

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(x_{i,s,k}\) | binary | 1 if train \(i\) traverses segment \(s\) with speed level \(k\) (otherwise 0) |
| \(y_{i,s}\) | binary | 1 if train \(i\) is rerouted (uses the opposite track) on segment \(s\) |
| \(A_{i,s}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | arrival time of train \(i\) at the upstream node of segment \(s\) |
| \(D_{i,s}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | departure time of train \(i\) from the downstream node of segment \(s\) |
| \(o_{i,i',s}\) | binary | ordering variable for two trains \(i,i'\) that share segment \(s\): \(o_{i,i',s}=1\) ⇒ train \(i\) passes before train \(i'\); \(o_{i,i',s}=0\) ⇒ the opposite |

**Parameters (assumed / given)**  

* Sets: trains \(i\in I\), segments \(s\in S\) (ordered from origin to destination), speed levels \(k\in K\).  
* Original timetable: planned arrival at final destination \(a_i^{\text{orig}}\) and planned departure from origin \(d_i^{\text{orig}}\).  
* Travel time on segment \(s\) at speed level \(k\): \(\tau_{i,s,k}\).  
* Energy consumption on segment \(s\) at speed level \(k\): \(e_{i,s,k}\).  
* Blockage window on segment \(s\): \([t^{\text{start}}_s,\;t^{\text{end}}_s]\) (if no blockage, set \(t^{\text{start}}_s=t^{\text{end}}_s\)).  
* Reroute capacity on segment \(s\): \(\text{cap}_s\) (max number of trains that may use the opposite track).  
* Minimum head‑way between two trains on the same segment: \(h_{i,i',s}\).  
* Weights for the objective: \(w_{\text{delay}},\,w_{\text{energy}}\).  
* Big‑\(M\) constant larger than the planning horizon.

**Objective function**

\[
\min\; 
w_{\text{delay}}\;\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(A_{i,s_{\text{last}}}-a_i^{\text{orig}}\bigr)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
w_{\text{energy}}\;\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} e_{i,s,k}\,x_{i,s,k}}_{\text{total energy}} .
\]

**Constraints**

1. **Speed‑level selection** – exactly one speed level per train‑segment  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} x_{i,s,k}=1 \qquad \forall i\in I,\; \forall s\in S .
\]

2. **Timing relation** – departure equals arrival plus the chosen travel time  

\[
D_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+ \sum_{k\in K}\tau_{i,s,k}\,x_{i,s,k}
\qquad \forall i\in I,\; \forall s\in S .
\]

3. **Continuity between consecutive segments (head‑way)**  

For every pair of distinct trains \(i,i'\) and every segment \(s\) (except the last),  

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{i',s_{\text{next}}} &\ge D_{i,s}+h_{i,i',s}
      -M\bigl(y_{i,s}+y_{i',s}\bigr),\\
A_{i,s_{\text{next}}} &\ge D_{i',s}+h_{i,i',s}
      -M\bigl(y_{i,s}+y_{i',s}\bigr),
\end{aligned}
\qquad \forall i\neq i',\; \forall s\in S\setminus\{s_{\text{last}}\}.
\]

If either train is rerouted (\(y=1\)), the constraint is relaxed.

4. **Blockage avoidance** – a train must either finish before the blockage starts or start after it ends, unless it is rerouted  

\[
\begin{aligned}
D_{i,s} &\le t^{\text{start}}_s + M\,y_{i,s},\\
A_{i,s} &\ge t^{\text{end}}_s - M\,y_{i,s},
\end{aligned}
\qquad \forall i\in I,\; \forall s\in S \text{ with } t^{\text{end}}_s>t^{\text{start}}_s .
\]

5. **Reroute capacity**  

\[
\sum_{i\in I} y_{i,s}\le \text{cap}_s \qquad \forall s\in S .
\]

6. **Conflict ordering on shared track** – for any two trains that are both on the same segment (i.e. not rerouted) one must pass before the other  

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{i',s} &\ge D_{i,s} - M\bigl(1-o_{i,i',s}+y_{i,s}+y_{i',s}\bigr),\\
A_{i,s}  &\ge D_{i',s} - M\bigl(o_{i,i',s}+y_{i,s}+y_{i',s}\bigr),
\end{aligned}
\qquad \forall i\neq i',\; \forall s\in S .
\]

7. **Initial departure** – trains cannot leave before their original departure time  

\[
A_{i,s_{\text{first}}}\ge d_i^{\text{orig}} \qquad \forall i\in I .
\]

8. **No early arrival** – final arrival cannot be earlier than originally planned  

\[
A_{i,s_{\text{last}}}\ge a_i^{\text{orig}} \qquad \forall i\in I .
\]

9. **Variable domains**  

\[
x_{i,s,k}\in\{0,1\},\; y_{i,s}\in\{0,1\},\; o_{i,i',s}\in\{0,1\},\;
A_{i,s}\ge 0,\; D_{i,s}\ge 0 .
\]

---

### Remarks / Assumptions

* The set of speed levels \(K\) is finite and identical for all trains/segments (e.g., three discrete levels).  
* Blockage windows are known a‑priori; if a segment is not blocked, set \(t^{\text{start}}_s=t^{\text{end}}_s\) so constraints (4) become non‑binding.  
* The big‑\(M\) constant must dominate the longest possible schedule (e.g., \(M =\) planning horizon + max\(\tau\)).  
* Energy coefficients \(e_{i,s,k}\) are assumed linear in the binary speed‑selection variables; this yields a linear objective.  
* Head‑way \(h_{i,i',s}\) can be uniform (e.g., 3 min) or train‑specific.  

The model above fully captures the integrated train rescheduling and speed‑management problem under partial segment blockages, including rerouting decisions, conflict resolution between bidirectional trains, and a trade‑off between delay and energy consumption.

Text:
**Variables**

- \(y_{i,r}\in\{0,1\}\) – route‑selection binary for train \(i\); \(r=0\) = original route, \(r=1\) = reroute (use opposite track on the blocked side).  
- \(x_{i,j,s}\in\{0,1\}\) – ordering binary on shared segment \(s\); \(x_{i,j,s}=1\) if train \(i\) precedes train \(j\) on \(s\).  
- \(u_{i,s}\in\{0,1\}\) – indicator that train \(i\) traverses segment \(s\) (pre‑computed from the network).  
- \(a_{i,k}\ge 0\) – arrival time of train \(i\) at station \(k\).  
- \(d_{i,k}\ge 0\) – departure time of train \(i\) from station \(k\).  
- \(t_{i,s}\ge 0\) – travel time of train \(i\) on segment \(s\).  
- \(v_{i,s}\ge 0\) – average speed of train \(i\) on segment \(s\).  
- \(z_{i,s}\in\{0,1\}\) – speed‑profile binary; \(z_{i,s}=0\) ⇒ normal speed \(v^{\text{norm}}\), \(z_{i,s}=1\) ⇒ accelerated speed \(v^{\text{acc}}\).  
- \(w_{i,s}\in\{0,1\}\) – binary used in the blockage “either‑or’’ constraint.

**Parameters (assumed known)**  

- \(L_s\) – length of segment \(s\).  
- \(v^{\max},\,v^{\min}\) – global speed limits.  
- \(v^{\text{norm}},\,v^{\text{acc}}\) – admissible normal/accelerated speeds.  
- \(\alpha_s\) – energy coefficient of segment \(s\).  
- \(\text{dwell}_{i,k}\) – mandatory dwell time of train \(i\) at station \(k\).  
- \(\text{schedArr}_i\) – scheduled arrival time of train \(i\) at its final station (used for delay).  
- \((B^{\text{start}}_{s},B^{\text{end}}_{s})\) – blockage time window on the *original* side of segment \(s\).  
- \(M\) – a sufficiently large constant (big‑M).  
- \(w^{\text{delay}},\,w^{\text{energy}}\) – weights in the objective.

**Objective**

\[
\min \; 
w^{\text{delay}}\;\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(a_{i,\text{last}}-\text{schedArr}_i\bigr)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
w^{\text{energy}}\;\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\alpha_s\,v_{i,s}^{2}\,t_{i,s}}_{\text{total energy}} .
\]

**Constraints**

1. **Route choice** (each train selects exactly one route)  
   \[
   \sum_{r\in\{0,1\}} y_{i,r}=1 \qquad \forall i\in I .
   \]

2. **Dwell time relationship**  
   \[
   d_{i,k}=a_{i,k}+\text{dwell}_{i,k} \qquad \forall i\in I,\;k\in K .
   \]

3. **Time‑flow between consecutive stations**  
   For every train \(i\) and every consecutive pair of stations \((k,k')\) traversed on segment \(s\):
   \[
   a_{i,k'}=d_{i,k}+t_{i,s}\qquad\forall i\in I,\; s\in S .
   \]

4. **Travel‑time bounds from speed limits**  
   \[
   \frac{L_s}{v^{\max}}\le t_{i,s}\le \frac{L_s}{v^{\min}}\qquad\forall i\in I,\;s\in S .
   \]

5. **Speed‑profile selection (big‑M formulation)**  

   \[
   \begin{aligned}
   v_{i,s}&\ge v^{\text{norm}}-M\,z_{i,s} ,\\
   v_{i,s}&\le v^{\text{norm}}+M\,z_{i,s} ,\\
   v_{i,s}&\ge v^{\text{acc}}-M\,(1-z_{i,s}) ,\\
   v_{i,s}&\le v^{\text{acc}}+M\,(1-z_{i,s}) .
   \end{aligned}
   \qquad\forall i\in I,\;s\in S .
   \]

6. **Link speed and travel time (linearised)** – exact relation \(t_{i,s}=L_s/v_{i,s}\) is bilinear; it can be replaced by a piece‑wise linear approximation. Using McCormick envelopes (with bounds \(v^{\min},v^{\max}\)):

   \[
   \begin{aligned}
   t_{i,s} &\ge \frac{L_s}{v^{\max}} + \frac{L_s}{(v^{\max})^{2}}\,(v_{i,s}-v^{\max}),\\
   t_{i,s} &\ge \frac{L_s}{v^{\min}} + \frac{L_s}{(v^{\min})^{2}}\,(v_{i,s}-v^{\min}),\\
   t_{i,s} &\le \frac{L_s}{v^{\min}} + \frac{L_s}{(v^{\min})^{2}}\,(v_{i,s}-v^{\min}),\\
   t_{i,s} &\le \frac{L_s}{v^{\max}} + \frac{L_s}{(v^{\max})^{2}}\,(v_{i,s}-v^{\max}) .
   \end{aligned}
   \qquad\forall i\in I,\;s\in S .
   \]

7. **Ordering on a shared segment** (disjunctive precedence)  
   For every unordered pair \((i,j)\) that both use segment \(s\) (\(u_{i,s}=u_{j,s}=1\)):

   \[
   \begin{aligned}
   a_{i,\text{enter}(s)} + t_{i,s} &\le a_{j,\text{enter}(s)} + M\,(1-x_{i,j,s}) ,\\
   a_{j,\text{enter}(s)} + t_{j,s} &\le a_{i,\text{enter}(s)} + M\,x_{i,j,s} .
   \end{aligned}
   \qquad\forall (i,j)\in I\times I,\; i\neq j,\; s\in S .
   \]

   Here \(\text{enter}(s)\) denotes the upstream station of segment \(s\) for the considered train.

8. **Blockage “either‑or’’ constraint** (partial segment blockage on the original side)  

   For every train \(i\) that traverses a blocked segment \(s\) on the original side:

   \[
   \begin{aligned}
   a_{i,\text{enter}(s)} &\ge B^{\text{end}}_{s} - M\,(1-w_{i,s}),\\
   a_{i,\text{enter}(s)} + t_{i,s} &\le B^{\text{start}}_{s} + M\,w_{i,s},\\
   w_{i,s} &\le y_{i,0}.
   \end{aligned}
   \qquad\forall i\in I,\; s\in S\text{ with blockage}.
   \]

   If the train does **not** use the blocked side (\(y_{i,0}=0\)), the binary \(w_{i,s}\) can be forced to 0, making both constraints non‑binding. If the train uses the blocked side (\(y_{i,0}=1\)), the constraints enforce that its entry or exit from the segment lies completely outside the blockage window.

9. **Binary and non‑negativity domains** – already declared with the variable definitions.

---

**Assumptions / Remarks**

- The set of stations visited by each train and the mapping “station → next segment’’ are known a‑priori; therefore the indices \(\text{enter}(s)\) are well defined.  
- The binary indicator \(u_{i,s}\) is pre‑computed from the network (1 if train \(i\) traverses segment \(s\), 0 otherwise).  
- The bilinear term \(v_{i,s}\,t_{i,s}=L_s\) is linearised with McCormick envelopes (or a piece‑wise linear approximation) to keep the model MILP.  
- Big‑M \(M\) must be larger than the maximal possible schedule horizon (e.g., total planning horizon + maximum travel time).  
- Energy is modelled as proportional to \(v^{2}\,t\) (typical for electric traction); the coefficient \(\alpha_s\) captures segment‑specific factors (gradient, train mass, etc.).  

The formulation above provides a complete mixed‑integer linear program that simultaneously decides **train routes (original vs. reroute), ordering on shared tracks, arrival/departure times, and speed profiles** while minimising a weighted combination of **total delay** and **energy consumption**, and respecting **partial segment blockages**.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) Model for the Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP)**  

The model below captures, in a single‑stage MILP, the three intertwined decision levels that arise when a **partial‑segment blockage** occurs on a high‑speed line:

1. **Rescheduling decisions** – new departure/arrival times, train order (re‑sequencing) and possible **rerouting** to the opposite track.  
2. **Speed‑management decisions** – piece‑wise‑linear acceleration / cruising / coasting / braking profiles that realise the rescheduled times.  
3. **Conflict‑avoidance decisions** – ensure that at any instant a track segment (or a bidirectional section) is occupied by at most one train travelling in the same direction, and that opposing‑direction trains never share the same physical track while the blockage is active.

The formulation is deliberately **linear**: non‑linear train‑dynamics (e.g. kinetic energy) are linearised by introducing a set of pre‑computed **speed‑profile plans** (see Assumption A5).  

---

## 1️⃣  Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T**  | Set of trains, indexed by *t* (|T| = N). |
| **S**  | Set of railway **segments** (track sections) indexed by *s*. |
| **L**  | Set of **lines** (directional tracks) – e.g. *L = {+ , – }* for the two opposite directions. |
| **P**  | Set of **pre‑computed speed‑profile plans** for a train on a given route, indexed by *p*. |
| **K**  | Set of **time‑interval indices** used for the linearised speed‑profile representation (e.g. *k = 1,…,K*). |
| **B**  | Set of **blocked segments** (the disruption area), *B ⊆ S*. |
| **Ω**  | Set of **conflict‑pairs** *(t, t′, s, ℓ)* such that trains *t* and *t′* may occupy the same segment *s* on line *ℓ* at overlapping times (defined later). |

---

## 2️⃣  Parameters (data)  

| Symbol | Description | Typical unit |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| *α*            | Weight for **total passenger delay** (€/min). |
| *β*            | Weight for **energy consumption** (€/kWh). |
| *c_s^ℓ*       | **Capacity** of line ℓ on segment *s* (maximum number of trains that can occupy the segment simultaneously, usually 1). |
| *τ_s^{ℓ,orig}*| Original **running time** (minutes) of a train on segment *s* when travelling on line ℓ under nominal speed. |
| *Δ_t^{max}*   | Maximum admissible **departure‑delay** for train *t* (min). |
| *θ_{t}^{orig}*| Original **departure time** of train *t* (min from a common zero). |
| *ρ_{t}^{orig}*| Original **arrival time** of train *t* at its final destination (min). |
| *E_{p}^{t}*   | Energy consumption (kWh) of plan *p* for train *t* (pre‑computed). |
| *Δ_{p}^{t}*   | **Running‑time reduction / increase** (minutes) produced by plan *p* compared with the nominal schedule (may be negative). |
| *γ_{p}^{t}*   | Boolean indicator: 1 if plan *p* uses the **opposite line** (rerouting), 0 otherwise. |
| *T_{b}^{start}*, *T_{b}^{end}* | Start / end time of the blockage on each segment *b∈B* (minutes). |
| *ψ_{s}^{ℓ}*   | Length of segment *s* (km). |
| *v_{max}*      | Maximum permissible speed (km/h). |
| *a_{max}*, *d_{max}* | Maximum acceleration / deceleration (km/h²). |
| *ε*            | Small positive constant for “big‑M” linearisation (e.g. 10⁶). |

---

## 3️⃣  Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| *d_t*               | Continuous ≥0 | **Delay** of train *t* on departure (minutes). |
| *a_t*               | Continuous ≥0 | **Arrival delay** of train *t* at its final destination (minutes). |
| *x_{t,s,ℓ}*         | Binary | 1 if train *t* traverses segment *s* on line ℓ (i.e. chooses the “normal” direction; for rerouting ‑ opposite line). |
| *y_{t,p}*           | Binary | 1 if speed‑profile plan *p* is selected for train *t*. |
| *z_{t,t′,s,ℓ}*      | Binary | 1 if train *t* **precedes** train *t′* on segment *s* on line ℓ (used for ordering). |
| *w_{t,k,s,ℓ}*       | Binary | 1 if train *t* occupies **time‑interval k** on segment *s* line ℓ (time‑indexed occupancy). |
| *u_{t,k,s,ℓ}*       | Continuous ≥0 | **Speed** of train *t* during interval *k* on segment *s* line ℓ (km/h). |
| *g_{t,k,s,ℓ}*       | Continuous ≥0 | **Energy** consumed during interval *k* (kWh). |

---

## 4️⃣  Objective Function  

The MILP minimises a **weighted sum of total passenger delay and total energy consumption**:

\[
\min \;  \alpha \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} (d_t + a_t)}_{\text{total delay (min)}} \;+\;
        \beta  \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{p\in P} E_{p}^{t}\, y_{t,p}}_{\text{total energy (kWh)}} .
\]

*Assumption A1:* All passengers on train *t* experience the same departure and arrival delay (i.e., head‑way effects are ignored).  

---

## 5️⃣  Core Constraints  

### 5.1  Plan‑Selection  

\[
\sum_{p\in P} y_{t,p}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T                                    \tag{C1}
\]

Exactly one speed‑profile plan is chosen for each train.

### 5.2  Routing / Line Choice  

\[
x_{t,s,ℓ}= 1 - \sum_{p\in P}\gamma_{p}^{t}\; y_{t,p}    \qquad\forall t,s,\ell      \tag{C2}
\]

If a plan states “use opposite line” (\(\gamma_{p}^{t}=1\)) then the train is forced onto the opposite direction for the blocked segments.  

### 5.3  Timing Consistency (Departure / Arrival)  

\[
d_t \le \Delta_t^{max} \qquad\forall t \tag{C3}
\]

\[
\theta_t^{orig}+d_t = \underbrace{\theta_t^{orig}}_{\text{original departure}} + d_t          \tag{C4}
\]

Arrival time at final destination:

\[
\rho_t^{orig}+a_t = \theta_t^{orig}+d_t+\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{ℓ\in L} \tau_s^{ℓ,orig}\, x_{t,s,ℓ}
                    +\sum_{p\in P}\Delta_{p}^{t} \, y_{t,p}                      \tag{C5}
\]

The right‑hand side adds the (possibly altered) running time of all traversed segments plus the running‑time shift delivered by the selected speed plan.

### 5.4  Segment‑Occupancy (Big‑M ordering)  

For any pair of trains that may meet on the same segment *s* and line *ℓ* we enforce a **precedence** variable:

\[
w_{t,k,s,ℓ} + w_{t′,k,s,ℓ} \le 1 \qquad \forall (t,t′,s,ℓ)\in \Omega, \; \forall k \tag{C6}
\]

If both trains use the same line on the same segment, they cannot occupy the same interval *k*.

### 5.5  Linking Plan to Occupancy  

Let *K_{p}^{t,s,ℓ}* be the set of intervals that plan *p* would occupy on segment *s,ℓ*.  
Then for each train:

\[
\sum_{k\in K_{p}^{t,s,ℓ}} w_{t,k,s,ℓ} \ge y_{t,p} \qquad \forall t,p,s,ℓ        \tag{C7}
\]

If plan *p* is selected, the corresponding occupancy pattern must be realised.

### 5.6  Blockage Feasibility  

A train is **forbidden** to occupy a blocked segment on the original line during the blockage window:

\[
\sum_{k: \, t_k \in [T_{b}^{start},T_{b}^{end}]} w_{t,k,b,ℓ} \le \bigl(1-\gamma_{p}^{t}\bigr)\,y_{t,p} \qquad \forall t,\,b\in B,\,ℓ\in L    \tag{C8}
\]

If the selected plan uses the opposite line (\(\gamma_{p}^{t}=1\)), the constraint becomes non‑binding; otherwise the sum must be zero.

### 5.7  Speed‑Dynamics Linearisation  

For each occupied interval we approximate the speed‑profile by a **piece‑wise‑linear** function (Assumption A5). The following constraints enforce acceleration limits:

\[
u_{t,k+1,s,ℓ} - u_{t,k,s,ℓ} \le a_{max}\,\Delta t \qquad\forall t,k,s,ℓ      \tag{C9}
\]

\[
u_{t,k,s,ℓ} - u_{t,k+1,s,ℓ} \le d_{max}\,\Delta t \qquad\forall t,k,s,ℓ      \tag{C10}
\]

where \(\Delta t\) is the length of an interval (minutes).  

Speed is bounded:

\[
0 \le u_{t,k,s,ℓ} \le v_{max}\, w_{t,k,s,ℓ} \qquad\forall t,k,s,ℓ          \tag{C11}
\]

(The binary \(w_{t,k,s,ℓ}\) forces speed to zero when the interval is not used.)

### 5.8  Energy Approximation  

Energy per interval is approximated linearly as a function of speed (e.g. \(g = \alpha_1 u + \alpha_2 u^2\) linearised by supporting points). In the MILP we use a **pre‑computed coefficient** \(e_{k}^{t,s,ℓ}\) for each feasible speed level:

\[
g_{t,k,s,ℓ} \ge e_{k}^{t,s,ℓ} \, u_{t,k,s,ℓ} \qquad\forall t,k,s,ℓ        \tag{C12}
\]

Total energy contributed by the plan must match the plan’s energy value:

\[
\sum_{k,s,ℓ} g_{t,k,s,ℓ} = \sum_{p\in P} E_{p}^{t}\, y_{t,p} \qquad\forall t \tag{C13}
\]

### 5.9  Conflict‑Free Bidirectional Use of Shared Track  

When a blocked segment forces a **reroute** onto the opposite line, we must guarantee that a train travelling in the opposite direction does **not occupy the same physical track** at the same moment. Let *ŝ* denote the **physical track** that underlies both directions (same geometry). For any two trains *t* (using line ℓ) and *t′* (using opposite line ¯ℓ) on the same physical segment *ŝ*:

\[
\sum_{k} \bigl( w_{t,k,ŝ,ℓ} + w_{t′,k,ŝ,\bar{ℓ}} \bigr) \le 1 \qquad \forall t,t′,ŝ \tag{C14}
\]

Thus the bidirectional conflict is eliminated.

### 5.10  Logical Consistency (Big‑M)  

If a train does **not** use segment *s* on line ℓ, the occupancy variables are forced to zero:

\[
w_{t,k,s,ℓ} \le x_{t,s,ℓ} \qquad\forall t,k,s,ℓ                     \tag{C15}
\]

---

## 6️⃣  Modeling Assumptions (explicit)  

| Code | Statement |
|------|------------|
| **A1** | All passengers on the same train experience the same departure‑ and arrival‑delay; individual‑passenger heterogeneity is ignored. |
| **A2** | Capacity of a line on any segment is 1 (i.e., a single train can occupy a segment at a given instant); extensions to >1 are trivial by changing *c_s^ℓ*. |
| **A3** | The disruption (partial blockage) is **known in advance** in terms of its start/end times and the set of affected segments *B*. |
| **A4** | Rerouting is only allowed onto the **opposite directional line** of the same physical track (i.e., there is a parallel line, not a completely different route). |
| **A5** | A finite catalogue of **speed‑profile plans** *P* for each train is pre‑computed (e.g., using a detailed non‑linear speed‑profile optimisation). Each plan provides a deterministic running‑time shift \(\Delta_{p}^{t}\) and energy consumption \(E_{p}^{t}\). The MILP only selects among these plans, thereby linearising the otherwise non‑linear dynamics. |
| **A6** | Time is discretised into uniform intervals of length \(\Delta t\) (e.g., 1 min). This discretisation yields the binary occupancy variables *w*. The interval length is taken small enough that the resulting schedule is practically continuous. |
| **A7** | Acceleration/deceleration limits are imposed as linear bounds (C9–C10); the actual power‑draw curve is approximated linearly (C12). |
| **A8** | All parameters (original timetable, blockage window, segment lengths, speeds, etc.) are **deterministic**. Stochastic extensions are possible but are outside the present deterministic MILP. |
| **A9** | “Big‑M” constants (ε) are set sufficiently high to deactivate constraints when the associated binary variable equals 0, yet low enough to avoid numerical instability. |

---

## 7️⃣  Complete MILP Statement  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min_{d,a,x,y,z,w,u,g} \;& 
\alpha \sum_{t\in T}(d_t + a_t) + 
\beta \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{p\in P} E_{p}^{t}\, y_{t,p} \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } & \text{(C1)–(C15) listed above} \\[2pt]
& d_t,\;a_t \ge 0 \quad \forall t\in T \\[2pt]
& x_{t,s,ℓ}\in\{0,1\},\; y_{t,p}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{t,t′,s,ℓ}\in\{0,1\},\\
& w_{t,k,s,ℓ}\in\{0,1\},\; u_{t,k,s,ℓ}\ge 0,\; g_{t,k,s,ℓ}\ge 0 \quad \forall\text{ indices}.
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 8️⃣  Remarks on Solving the Model  

* The model is a **large‑scale MILP** – the number of binary variables grows with |T|·|S|·|L|·|K|.  
* In practice we **decompose** as described in the original paper: (i) an **integer‑program (IP) master** that decides the plan‑selection *y* and ordering *z*, and (ii) a set of **train‑plan sub‑problems** (one per train) that verify feasibility of the chosen plan given the master‑decisions.  
* The **adaptive iterative refinement** (local branching) can be applied to the master problem to limit the search to a neighbourhood of the incumbent solution, gradually enlarging the plan‑granularity where needed.  
* Commercial solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) handle the linear constraints directly; warm‑starts from the decomposition greatly improve runtime on real‑world instances (hundreds of trains, dozens of blocked segments).  

---

### 🎯  What the Model Delivers  

* A **conflict‑free rescheduled timetable** (departure/arrival times, train order, possible rerouting).  
* A **feasible speed‑profile assignment** for each train that respects acceleration limits, blockage windows, and bidirectional track sharing.  
* An **energy‑aware** schedule: the objective explicitly balances passenger delay against electrical energy consumption, enabling decision makers to quantify the trade‑off between rapid service recovery and sustainability.  

The above MILP therefore constitutes a **complete, linear, and implementable mathematical representation** of the integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem under partial‑segment blockages, ready for computational experimentation or integration into a decision‑support system.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP‑MILP)**  
The model simultaneously decides (i) a feasible conflict‑free timetable (arrival / departure times, train order and optional rerouting) and (ii) a feasible speed‑profile for every train on every line segment. The formulation is linearised by piece‑wise constant speed/acceleration approximations and big‑M logic for binary decisions.  
All symbols and sets are defined first, followed by the decision variables, the objective function and the complete set of constraints. Where data are not supplied in the description, reasonable assumptions are explicitly stated.

---

## 1. Sets, parameters and modelling assumptions  

| Symbol | Meaning | Typical size / comment |
|--------|---------|------------------------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\) | \(t=1,\dots,|T|\) |
| \(S\) | Set of line‑segments (track sections) between two consecutive stations, indexed by \(s\) | \(s=1,\dots,|S|\) |
| \(V\) | Set of possible speed‑levels (discretised), indexed by \(v\) | e.g. 5‑10 levels from 0 to line max speed |
| \(K\) | Set of candidate **plans** for each train (a plan = a combination of route, departure/arrival times and speed‑level sequence) | generated in a preprocessing step (see §4) |
| \(D\) | Set of disruption‑intervals on a segment, indexed by \(d\) (start & end time of blockage) | may be empty for unaffected segments |
| \(\delta_{t,s}\) | Length (km) of segment \(s\) for train \(t\) (may differ if rerouting) | – |
| \(\overline{v}_s\) | Maximum admissible speed on segment \(s\) (km/h) | – |
| \(\underline{v}\) | Minimum admissible speed (normally 0) | – |
| \(\alpha\) | Energy‑consumption coefficient per km·(speed‑level) (kWh per km at speed level \(v\)) | Linearised from a quadratic power‑speed curve |
| \(\beta\) | Penalty cost for postponing a train’s arrival (€/min) | – |
| \(\gamma\) | Penalty for cancelling a train (large constant) | – |
| \(M\) | Big‑M constant (sufficiently large to deactivate constraints) | e.g. 10⁶ |
| \(\epsilon\) | Minimum headway (min) required between two trains travelling in the same direction on the same segment | typical 2–3 min |
| \(h_{t}^{\text{orig}}\) | Original scheduled departure time of train \(t\) (min) | – |
| \(a_{t}^{\text{orig}}\) | Original scheduled arrival time of train \(t\) (min) | – |
| \(\eta\) | Maximum number of simultaneous trains allowed on a segment (normally 1 for a single track, 2 for double‑track) | – |
| \(c^{\text{run}}_{t,s,v}\) | Running time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) if traversed at speed level \(v\) (min) – computed as \(\delta_{t,s}/v\) and linearised | – |

### Modelling assumptions  

1. **Piece‑wise constant speed** – on a given segment a train travels with a constant speed‑level \(v\in V\).  
2. **Binary routing choice** – for each train a small set of feasible routes (original line or opposite‑track detour) is pre‑enumerated; the MILP chooses exactly one.  
3. **Discrete time‑grid** – all event times (departures, arrivals, block‑start/end) are expressed on a common minute‑granularity, enabling linear big‑M constraints.  
4. **Energy linearisation** – the true cubic relationship between traction power and speed is approximated by a linear function \(\alpha_{v}\) per speed level.  
5. **Disruption window** – a segment \(s\) can be blocked only during intervals in \(D\); a train may occupy the segment only outside those intervals or if it uses the opposite track (rerouting).  
6. **Single‑track conflict** – if two trains of opposite direction use the same physical track at the same time, a binary conflict variable forces a non‑overlap of their occupation intervals.  

---

## 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| \(x_{t,k}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if **plan** \(k\in K\) is selected for train \(t\). Exactly one plan per train. |
| \(z_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses segment \(s\) on its **original** track, 0 if it uses the opposite track (reroute). |
| \(y_{t,s,v}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) travels on segment \(s\) with speed level \(v\). For a selected plan, exactly one speed level per segment. |
| \(d^{\text{dep}}_{t}\) | continuous \([0,\infty)\) | Actual departure time of train \(t\) from its origin station (min). |
| \(a^{\text{arr}}_{t}\) | continuous \([0,\infty)\) | Actual arrival time of train \(t\) at its final destination (min). |
| \(c^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\) | continuous \([0,\infty)\) | Arrival time of train \(t\) at the **up‑stream** end of segment \(s\). |
| \(c^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\) | continuous \([0,\infty)\) | Departure time of train \(t\) from the **down‑stream** end of segment \(s\). |
| \(\theta_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) is **cancelled** (no service). |
| \(\phi_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | Conflict indicator: 1 if trains \(t\) and \(t'\) (opposite directions) would occupy the same physical track on segment \(s\) at overlapping times. |
| \(e_t\) | continuous | Total energy consumption of train \(t\) (kWh). |

---

## 3. Objective function  

The integrated objective balances three (conflicting) goals:

1. **Minimise total energy consumption** (environmental objective).  
2. **Minimise total delay** (service quality).  
3. **Avoid cancellations** (hard penalty).  

\[
\boxed{
\min\; 
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\; e_t}_{\text{Energy}} 
\;+\;
\underbrace{\beta\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(a^{\text{arr}}_{t}-a^{\text{orig}}_{t}\bigr)}_{\text{Delay penalty}} 
\;+\;
\underbrace{\gamma\sum_{t\in T}\theta_{t}}_{\text{Cancellation penalty}}
}
\]

where  

*\(a^{\text{orig}}_{t}=a_{t}^{\text{orig}}\) is the originally scheduled arrival time, and the term is active only if \(\theta_t=0\) (otherwise a huge penalty forces cancellation).*

---

## 4. Constraints  

### 4.1 Plan selection  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,k}=1-\theta_{t}\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{P1}
\]

If a train is cancelled (\(\theta_t=1\)) no plan is selected.

### 4.2 Routing / track‑usage (original vs opposite)  

For each segment used by train \(t\) in the selected plan:

\[
z_{t,s}= \sum_{k\in K} \rho^{\text{orig}}_{k,t,s}\;x_{t,k} \qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S \tag{R1}
\]

\(\rho^{\text{orig}}_{k,t,s}=1\) if plan \(k\) uses the original track on segment \(s\); 0 otherwise.

### 4.3 Speed‑level assignment  

\[
\sum_{v\in V} y_{t,s,v}= \sum_{k\in K}\rho^{\text{use}}_{k,t,s}\;x_{t,k}\qquad \forall t\in T,\;s\in S \tag{S1}
\]

\(\rho^{\text{use}}_{k,t,s}=1\) if plan \(k\) traverses segment \(s\) (any speed).  

### 4.4 Time‑propagation on a segment  

If train \(t\) uses speed level \(v\) on segment \(s\),

\[
c^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}=c^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}+c^{\text{run}}_{t,s,v}\; y_{t,s,v}\qquad \forall t,s,v \tag{T1}
\]

where \(c^{\text{run}}_{t,s,v}\) is pre‑computed (segment length / speed) for level \(v\).

### 4.5 Linking segment times to departure / arrival of the train  

Let \(\mathcal{S}^{\text{out}}_t\) be the first segment of train \(t\) (origin side) and \(\mathcal{S}^{\text{in}}_t\) the last segment (destination side).  

\[
c^{\text{arr}}_{t,\mathcal{S}^{\text{out}}_t}= d^{\text{dep}}_{t}\qquad\forall t\tag{T2}
\]

\[
c^{\text{dep}}_{t,\mathcal{S}^{\text{in}}_t}= a^{\text{arr}}_{t}\qquad\forall t\tag{T3}
\]

For interior continuity (the departure time from segment \(s\) equals the arrival time at the next segment \(s'\)):

\[
c^{\text{arr}}_{t,s'} = c^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \qquad\forall t,\; s\to s' \text{ consecutive}\tag{T4}
\]

### 4.6 Headway (same‑direction)  

For any pair of trains \(t\neq t'\) travelling **in the same direction** on the same physical track (i.e. \(z_{t,s}=z_{t',s}=1\) or both use opposite track together) the following non‑overlap constraint is linearised with binary ordering variable \(\mu_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}\):

\[
c^{\text{arr}}_{t',s} \ge c^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} + \epsilon - M\,(1-\mu_{t,t',s}) \tag{H1}
\]
\[
c^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \ge c^{\text{dep}}_{t',s} + \epsilon - M\,\mu_{t,t',s} \tag{H2}
\]
\[
\mu_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}\qquad\forall t<t',\, s\in S \tag{H3}
\]

Only one of the two inequalities is active, guaranteeing a minimum headway \(\epsilon\).

### 4.7 Opposite‑direction conflict on a **single‑track** segment  

If the segment is single‑track (\(\eta=1\)), opposite‑direction trains cannot occupy it simultaneously, even when one uses the opposite track (because the opposite track is physically the same rail). The conflict binary \(\phi_{t,t',s}\) forces a separation:

\[
c^{\text{arr}}_{t',s} \ge c^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} - M\phi_{t,t',s}\tag{C1}
\]
\[
c^{\text{arr}}_{t ,s} \ge c^{\text{dep}}_{t',s} - M(1-\phi_{t,t',s})\tag{C2}
\]

If \(\phi_{t,t',s}=1\) then train \(t\) precedes \(t'\); otherwise the opposite order holds.  

The binary is defined only for opposite‑direction pairs on a single‑track segment:

\[
\phi_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}\quad\forall (t,t')\in \mathcal{O},\; s\in S_{\text{single}}\tag{C3}
\]

where \(\mathcal{O}\) denotes the set of opposite‑direction train pairs.

### 4.8 Disruption window feasibility  

If segment \(s\) is blocked during interval \([B^{\text{start}}_{d}, B^{\text{end}}_{d}]\) (for any \(d\in D\)), a train may occupy the segment only **outside** the block **or** must use the opposite track (\(z_{t,s}=0\)). The following big‑M constraints enforce this:

\[
c^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \ge B^{\text{end}}_{d} \;-\; M\,(1-z_{t,s})\qquad\forall t,s,d \tag{D1}
\]
\[
c^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \le B^{\text{start}}_{d} \;+\; M\,(1-z_{t,s})\qquad\forall t,s,d \tag{D2}
\]

If \(z_{t,s}=1\) (train uses the blocked track) then (D1)–(D2) force the whole occupation interval to lie completely before the block starts or after it ends; otherwise the constraints are relaxed.

### 4.9 Energy consumption calculation  

Energy for a train equals the sum of per‑segment consumptions, each proportional to distance and speed level:

\[
e_t = \sum_{s\in S}\sum_{v\in V}\alpha_{v}\,\delta_{t,s}\, y_{t,s,v}\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{E1}
\]

If a train is cancelled, its energy is forced to zero:

\[
e_t \le M\,(1-\theta_t)\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{E2}
\]

### 4.10 Delay definition (used in the objective)  

\[
\Delta_t = a^{\text{arr}}_{t} - a^{\text{orig}}_{t}\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{D3}
\]

Only non‑negative values are relevant; the model can add a constraint to forbid early arrivals if desired:

\[
\Delta_t \ge 0 \qquad\forall t\in T \tag{D4}
\]

### 4.11 Logical linking of cancellation  

If a train is cancelled, all its timing and routing variables are forced to a dummy value (e.g., zero) to keep the model linear:

\[
d^{\text{dep}}_{t} \le M\,(1-\theta_t),\qquad
a^{\text{arr}}_{t} \le M\,(1-\theta_t),\qquad
x_{t,k}\le 1-\theta_t,\;\forall k\tag{C4}
\]

### 4.12 Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,k}\in\{0,1\},\;z_{t,s}\in\{0,1\},\;y_{t,s,v}\in\{0,1\},\;\theta_t\in\{0,1\},\\
&\mu_{t,t',s},\phi_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\},\\
&d^{\text{dep}}_{t},a^{\text{arr}}_{t},c^{\text{arr}}_{t,s},c^{\text{dep}}_{t,s},e_t\ge 0.
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 5. Summary of the MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{t\in T}e_t\;+\;\beta\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_t\;+\;\gamma\sum_{t\in T}\theta_t\\[2mm]
\text{s.t. }& \text{(P1)–(C4)}\;\; \text{(plan selection, routing, speed, timing, headway,} \\
            & \text{conflict, disruption, energy, delay definitions)}\\
            & \text{Variable domains (binary / non‑negative).}
\end{aligned}
\]

The model is a **mixed‑integer linear program (MILP)** because all nonlinearities are eliminated through (i) pre‑computed piece‑wise constant running times, (ii) linear energy approximation, and (iii) big‑M binary logic for ordering and disruption compliance.

---

## 6. Remarks on the practical use of the formulation  

1. **Plan generation (set K).**  
   - For each train a limited number of feasible plans is generated off‑line (e.g., original route, opposite‑track detour, early/late departure windows, speed‑level combinations).  
   - The number of plans is kept modest (tens per train) to keep the MILP size tractable.  

2. **Decomposition (as described in the paper).**  
   - The MILP can be decomposed into an **integer master problem** that selects a plan for every train (variables \(x_{t,k}\) and the binary conflict variables), and a set of **sub‑problems** that compute the detailed timing/energy for each selected plan (continuous variables).  
   - This decomposition matches the adaptive iterative algorithm presented in the reference.  

3. **Scalability.**  
   - The big‑M constants \(M\) should be calibrated to the planning horizon (e.g., 24 h = 1440 min) to avoid numerical weakness.  
   - Tightening the headway constraints with valid inequalities (e.g., triangle inequalities for three consecutive trains) can greatly improve solution times.  

4. **Extensions (optional).**  
   - Passenger‑connection penalties can be added by linking arrival times of consecutive trains.  
   - Emission cost can be modelled as a second linear term with coefficients per speed level.  
   - Rolling‑stock constraints (limited number of trains on a line) are easily added by summing binary usage variables per segment.

---

**The formulation above provides a complete, mathematically rigorous MILP for the integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial‑segment blockages, capturing routing, timing, headway, disruption‑avoidance and energy‑efficiency in a single linear model.**

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (partial‑segment blockage)**  

The model below captures the whole description given: a mixed‑integer linear program that simultaneously decides (i) which route each train will use, (ii) the arrival/departure times on every traversed track segment, (iii) the discrete speed level on each segment (hence the energy use), while guaranteeing conflict‑free operation on a partially blocked segment and on bidirectional single‑track sections.  

All constraints are linear; the only integer variables are binary route‑choice, speed‑level, and conflict‑ordering variables.  

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|-----------------------------------|
| \(\mathcal{T}\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\). |
| \(\mathcal{S}\) | Set of track **segments** (links), indexed by \(s\). |
| \(\mathcal{R}_t\) | Set of feasible **routes** for train \(t\); a route \(r\in\mathcal{R}_t\) is an ordered list of segments. |
| \(\mathcal{K}\) | Set of admissible **speed levels**, indexed by \(k\) (e.g. \(k=1,\dots,4\) → 30, 50, 70, 90 km/h). |
| \(\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{S}\) | Set of **partially blocked** segments. |
| \(\mathcal{D}\) | Set of **opposite‑direction train pairs** \((t,t')\) that may use the same segment (head‑on conflict). |
| \(\mathcal{P}_t\) | Set of ordered **precedence pairs** \((i,j)\) of consecutive segments on any route of train \(t\). |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| \(L_s\) | Length of segment \(s\) (km). |
| \(v_k\) | Speed associated with level \(k\) (km/h). |
| \(\theta_{sk}= \dfrac{L_s}{v_k}\times 60\) | Travel time on segment \(s\) at speed level \(k\) (minutes). |
| \(\alpha_s\in[0,1]\) | Fraction of segment \(s\) that is **blocked** ( \(\alpha_s=1\) → fully blocked). |
| \([t^{\text b}_s , t^{\text e}_s]\) | Time window during which the blocked part of segment \(s\) is unavailable (minutes). |
| \(\beta_{tt'}\) | Safety‑time separation for opposite‑direction trains on a shared segment (minutes). |
| \(\tau^{\min}_t , \tau^{\max}_t\) | Earliest / latest allowed departure time of train \(t\) (minutes). |
| \(D^{\text{sched}}_t\) | Scheduled arrival time of train \(t\) at its final destination (minutes). |
| \(w^{\text{delay}}_t\) | Weight (penalty) for one minute of delay of train \(t\). |
| \(w^{\text{energy}}\) | Global weight for electricity consumption. |
| \(c_k\) | Energy consumption rate (kWh per km) when travelling at speed level \(k\). |
| \(M\) | Large constant (big‑M) larger than any feasible time (e.g. 10 000 min). |

---

### 3. Decision variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|----------|
| \(x_{t,r}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) uses route \(r\in\mathcal{R}_t\); 0 otherwise. |
| \(a_{t,s}\) | continuous \(\ge0\) | Arrival time of train \(t\) at the **beginning** of segment \(s\). |
| \(d_{t,s}\) | continuous \(\ge0\) | Departure time of train \(t\) from the **end** of segment \(s\). |
| \(y_{t,s,k}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses segment \(s\) with speed level \(k\). |
| \(z_t\) | continuous \(\ge0\) | Total delay of train \(t\) (minutes). |
| \(e_t\) | continuous \(\ge0\) | Energy consumption of train \(t\) (kWh). |
| \(\lambda_{t,s}\) | binary | 0 → train \(t\) passes segment \(s\) **before** the blockage window, 1 → **after**. |
| \(\eta_{t,t',s}\) | binary | Ordering variable for opposite‑direction conflict on segment \(s\) (1 if \(t\) goes first). |

---

### 4. Objective  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} w^{\text{delay}}_{t}\,z_{t}
\;+\;
w^{\text{energy}}\;\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} e_{t}
}
\]

The first term penalises passenger delay; the second term penalises total electricity consumption.

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Route choice  
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_t} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad\forall t\in\mathcal{T} \tag{R1}
\]

#### 5.2 Link segment usage to the selected route  

Let \(\delta_{t,s,r}=1\) if segment \(s\) belongs to route \(r\), 0 otherwise.

\[
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} y_{t,s,k}= \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_t}\delta_{t,s,r}\,x_{t,r}
\qquad\forall t\in\mathcal{T},\;s\in\mathcal{S} \tag{R2}
\]

Thus a segment (and a speed level) can be used only if the route containing it is selected.

#### 5.3 Travel‑time on a segment (speed‑level)  

\[
d_{t,s}=a_{t,s}+ \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \theta_{sk}\,y_{t,s,k}
\qquad\forall t,s \tag{T1}
\]

#### 5.4 Flow‑conservation along the chosen route  

If \((i,j)\in\mathcal{P}_t\) (segment \(j\) follows \(i\) on any feasible route of train \(t\)):

\[
a_{t,j}= d_{t,i}\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in\mathcal{P}_t \tag{T2}
\]

The first segment of the chosen route receives the decision departure time  

\[
a_{t,s^{\text{first}}}= \tau^{\text{dep}}_t,\qquad
\tau^{\text{min}}_t\le\tau^{\text{dep}}_t\le\tau^{\text{max}}_t \tag{T3,T4}
\]

#### 5.5 Delay definition  

Let \(s^{\text{last}}_t\) be the final segment of the selected route of train \(t\).

\[
z_t \ge d_{t,s^{\text{last}}_t} - D^{\text{sched}}_t,\qquad
z_t \ge 0 \qquad\forall t \tag{D1}
\]

#### 5.6 Energy consumption  

\[
e_t = \sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} L_s\,c_k\,y_{t,s,k}
\qquad\forall t \tag{E1}
\]

#### 5.7 Blocked‑segment occupancy (big‑M “before/after” formulation)  

For every blocked segment \(s\in\mathcal{B}\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{t,s} &\le t^{\text b}_s + M\,\lambda_{t,s} \\
d_{t,s} &\ge t^{\text e}_s - M\,(1-\lambda_{t,s}) \\
\lambda_{t,s} &\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t,\;s\in\mathcal{B} \tag{B1}
\]

If \(\lambda_{t,s}=0\) the train must finish the segment **before** the blockage starts; if \(\lambda_{t,s}=1\) it must start **after** the blockage ends.

#### 5.8 Opposite‑direction conflict on the same segment  

For each pair \((t,t')\in\mathcal{D}\) that uses the same segment \(s\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{t',s} &\ge d_{t,s}+ \beta_{tt'} - M\,(1-\eta_{t,t',s}) \\
a_{t,s}  &\ge d_{t',s}+ \beta_{tt'} - M\,\eta_{t,t',s} \\
\eta_{t,t',s} &\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall (t,t')\in\mathcal{D},\; s\in\mathcal{S} \tag{C1}
\]

Exactly one of the two inequalities is active; the other is relaxed by the big‑M term, guaranteeing a safety head‑on separation \(\beta_{tt'}\).

#### 5.9 Speed‑level uniqueness (already enforced by (R2), kept for clarity)

\[
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} y_{t,s,k}= \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_t}\delta_{t,s,r}\,x_{t,r}
\qquad\forall t,s \tag{S1}
\]

#### 5.10 Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,r}\in\{0,1\},\; y_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\},\;
\lambda_{t,s}\in\{0,1\},\;
\eta_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\},\\
&a_{t,s}\ge0,\; d_{t,s}\ge0,\; z_t\ge0,\; e_t\ge0,\;
\tau^{\text{dep}}_t\ge0 .
\end{aligned}
\tag{Dom}
\]

---

### 6. Full MILP statement  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min_{x,y,a,d,\lambda,\eta,z,e,\tau^{\text{dep}}}\;
&\sum_{t} w^{\text{delay}}_{t}\,z_{t}
      + w^{\text{energy}}\sum_{t} e_{t}  \\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(R1)–(R2), (T1)–(T4), (D1), (E1), (B1), (C1), (S1), (Dom)} .
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the binary variables are the route‑choice \(x_{t,r}\), the speed‑level selectors \(y_{t,s,k}\), the before/after indicator \(\lambda_{t,s}\), and the conflict‑ordering \(\eta_{t,t',s}\).  

---

### 7. Remarks & How to use the model  

* **Data preparation** – Build the route sets \(\mathcal{R}_t\) (including possible detours around the blockage), compute \(\theta_{sk}\), define the blockage window \([t^{\text b}_s,t^{\text e}_s]\) for every blocked segment, and list all opposite‑direction train pairs \(\mathcal{D}\).  
* **Weight tuning** – Choose \(w^{\text{delay}}_t\) to reflect passenger importance (e.g., higher for high‑capacity trains) and \(w^{\text{energy}}\) to reflect electricity price or emission cost.  
* **Solution** – Feed the MILP to a commercial solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP…). The optimal solution provides for each train:  
  * the selected route \(x_{t,r}=1\),  
  * a conflict‑free timetable \(\{a_{t,s},d_{t,s}\}\),  
  * the discrete speed profile \(\{y_{t,s,k}\}\),  
  * the resulting total delay \(z_t\) and energy use \(e_t\).  
* **Extension possibilities** – One can add dwell‑time minima, early‑arrival penalties, or a piece‑wise linear approximation of a continuous speed‑energy curve without breaking linearity.  

The model therefore delivers a **feasible, conflict‑free rescheduled timetable together with executable speed profiles** that respect the partial‑segment blockage, resolve bidirectional conflicts, and simultaneously minimise passenger delay and energy consumption.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) – Full Linear Formulation**  

The model below captures, in a single mixed‑integer linear program, the three‑fold decision problem that arises when a partial‑segment blockage disrupts a high‑speed railway line:

1. **When** each train departs / arrives at every station (time‑shift – retiming).  
2. **Which** track (original or opposite) each train uses on the blocked segment (binary rerouting).  
3. **What** speed profile (average speed on each free‑running sub‑segment) each train follows (continuous speed‑selection).  

All decisions are made so that (i) no two trains occupy the same track at the same time (conflict‑free timetable), (ii) the physical speed limits and acceleration/deceleration capabilities of the trains are respected, and (iii) a weighted sum of total delay and total energy consumption is minimised.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | Set of trains, indexed by *t* (|T| = *N*). |
| **S** | Set of stations, indexed by *s* (ordered along the line, 1 = origin, |S| = *K*). |
| **B** | Set of track‑blocks (continuous line sections) between two consecutive stations, indexed by *b* (|B| = *K‑1*). |
| **U** | Sub‑set of blocks that are **blocked** (partial‑segment blockage). |
| **V** | Sub‑set of blocks that are **free** (V = B \ U). |
| **R** = {0,1} | Binary set – 0 = original (right‑hand) track, 1 = opposite (left‑hand) track. |
| **P** | Set of admissible **speed‑plans** for a train on a free block *b* (see §2.2). Indexed by *p*. |
| **Δ** | Set of discrete time‑intervals used for linearisation of speed‑time relations (e.g., 1‑min steps). |

Additional auxiliary indices are introduced when needed (e.g., *i* for predecessor‑successor train pairs).

---

## 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **a<sub>t,s</sub>** | Continuous, ≥0 | **Arrival time** of train *t* at station *s*. |
| **d<sub>t,s</sub>** | Continuous, ≥0 | **Departure time** of train *t* from station *s*. |
| **x<sub>t,b</sub>** | Binary | **Rerouting decision** on blocked block *b* ∈ U: 0 = stay on original track, 1 = use opposite track. |
| **y<sub>t,b,p</sub>** | Binary | **Speed‑plan selection** on free block *b* ∈ V: exactly one plan *p* ∈ P is chosen for train *t*. |
| **τ<sub>t,b,Δ</sub>** | Continuous, ≥0 | **Time spent** by train *t* on block *b* while travelling at the speed associated with interval Δ (used to linearise energy). |
| **z<sub>t,i</sub>** | Binary | **Order variable**: 1 if train *t* passes before train *i* on a shared track segment (conflict‑resolution). |
| **δ<sub>t</sub>** | Continuous, ≥0 | **Total delay** of train *t* with respect to its original schedule (given as data). |
| **e<sub>t</sub>** | Continuous, ≥0 | **Energy consumption** of train *t* (kWh). |

---

## 3. Input Data (Parameters)  

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **A<sub>t,s</sub>**, **D<sub>t,s</sub>** | Original (pre‑disruption) arrival / departure times (reference schedule). |
| **L<sub>b</sub>** | Length of block *b* (km). |
| **v<sub>max</sub>**, **v<sub>min</sub>** | Global maximum / minimum admissible speeds (km/h). |
| **a<sub>max</sub>**, **a<sub>min</sub>** | Maximum acceleration / deceleration (km/h²). |
| **c<sub>Δ</sub>** | Energy coefficient for interval Δ (kWh per km·h⁻¹). |
| **M** | Large constant for big‑M linearisation (e.g., 10⁶). |
| **T<sub>block</sub>** | Start time of the blockage (minutes from midnight). |
| **T<sub>end</sub>** | End time of the blockage. |
| **w<sub>delay</sub>**, **w<sub>energy</sub>** | Weight of delay and energy in the objective (user‑defined). |
| **Δt** | Length of each discrete time interval (minutes). |
| **β<sub>t,b</sub>** | Minimum dwell time of train *t* at station *s* (if *b* ends at *s*). |
| **γ<sub>t,b</sub>** | Minimum headway (in minutes) required between any two trains on block *b* (safety). |

---

## 4. Model Assumptions (explicit)  

1. **Deterministic disruption** – the blockage interval \([T_{block},T_{end}]\) and its spatial extent *U* are known a‑priori.  
2. **Single‑track usage per block** – at any instant a block can be occupied by at most one train on a given direction; opposite‑track usage is allowed only on blocked blocks (binary rerouting).  
3. **Piece‑wise constant speed** – on each free block a train adopts one of a finite set of admissible speed‑plans *p* (average speed, acceleration profile). This enables linearisation of the otherwise nonlinear speed‑time‑energy relationship.  
4. **No overtaking** – trains keep their order on a given track unless a rerouting decision swaps them (captured by order variables *z*).  
5. **Dwell times** – a minimum dwell time β is enforced at every station; additional dwell may be introduced to absorb delays.  
6. **Energy model** – energy consumption on a block is approximated by a linear function of the travelled speed (coefficients *c<sub>Δ</sub>*).  
7. **Headway safety** – a minimum temporal separation γ is required between any two consecutive trains on the same physical track.  

---

## 5. Objective Function  

\[
\min \; \underbrace{w_{delay}\sum_{t\in T}\delta_{t}}_{\text{Total weighted delay}}
\;+\; \underbrace{w_{energy}\sum_{t\in T} e_{t}}_{\text{Total weighted energy}}
\tag{OBJ}
\]

where  

\[
\delta_{t}= \sum_{s\in S}\bigl(a_{t,s}-A_{t,s}\bigr)^{+}
\qquad
e_{t}= \sum_{b\in V}\sum_{\Delta\in\Delta} c_{\Delta}\,\tau_{t,b,\Delta}
\]

The operator \((\cdot)^{+}\) denotes \(\max\{0,\cdot\}\); it can be linearised with an auxiliary variable and a big‑M constraint.

---

## 6. Core Constraints  

### 6.1. Time‑flow (timetable) constraints  

1. **Departure after arrival + dwell**  

\[
d_{t,s} \;\ge\; a_{t,s} + \beta_{t,b(s)} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S
\tag{C1}
\]

2. **Running time on a free block** – linking speed‑plan to travel time  

For each free block *b* that connects stations *s* and *s+1* :

\[
a_{t,s+1} \;=\; d_{t,s} \;+\; \sum_{p\in P} \frac{L_{b}}{v_{p}}\, y_{t,b,p}
\qquad \forall t\in T,\; b\in V
\tag{C2}
\]

where \(v_{p}\) is the average speed of plan *p*.  

3. **Running time on a blocked block (rerouting)**  

If block *b* ∈ U is blocked on the original track, a train may either wait (if it stays) or use the opposite track (if rerouted).  

\[
a_{t,s+1} \;=\; d_{t,s} \;+\; \bigl(1-x_{t,b}\bigr)\,\theta_{wait}
\;+\; x_{t,b}\,\frac{L_{b}}{v_{opp}}
\qquad \forall t\in T,\; b\in U
\tag{C3}
\]

- \(\theta_{wait}\) is a large constant representing “wait until the blockage clears” (e.g., \(T_{end}-T_{block}\)).  
- \(v_{opp}\) is the admissible speed on the opposite track (usually the same as \(v_{max}\)).  

4. **Binary selection of exactly one speed‑plan per free block**  

\[
\sum_{p\in P} y_{t,b,p}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T,\; b\in V
\tag{C4}
\]

5. **Delay definition (linearisation)**  

Introduce auxiliary variable \(\delta_{t}\ge 0\) and constraints  

\[
\delta_{t} \;\ge\; a_{t,s} - A_{t,s} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S
\tag{C5}
\]

### 6.2. Conflict‑avoidance (headway) constraints  

For any two distinct trains *t* and *i* that share a physical track segment (including opposite‑track usage on blocked blocks), we enforce a safe headway using order variables *z*.

\[
a_{i,s} \;\ge\; d_{t,s} + \gamma_{t,b} - M\,(1-z_{t,i}) \qquad \forall t\neq i,\; b\in B
\tag{C6a}
\]

\[
a_{t,s} \;\ge\; d_{i,s} + \gamma_{i,b} - M\,z_{t,i} \qquad \forall t\neq i,\; b\in B
\tag{C6b}
\]

Exactly one of the two inequalities is active; the binary *z* decides the precedence.  

If a train uses the opposite track on a blocked block, the headway constraint must be applied on that opposite track as well. This is captured by adding the term \(x_{t,b}\) to the set of trains that occupy the opposite track.

### 6.3. Rerouting feasibility  

A train can only reroute on a blocked block if the opposite track is **available** (i.e., not already occupied by another train that also rerouted). This is enforced by coupling *x* variables with the order variables on the opposite track:

\[
x_{t,b} + x_{i,b} \le 1 + z_{t,i} + z_{i,t} \qquad \forall t\neq i,\; b\in U
\tag{C7}
\]

Thus, at most one train may occupy the opposite track at the same time; the other must wait.

### 6.4. Speed‑plan – time‑interval linking (energy linearisation)  

For each free block *b* and each interval Δ:

\[
\tau_{t,b,\Delta} \;=\; \frac{L_{b}}{v_{p}}\, y_{t,b,p} \quad \text{if } \Delta \text{ corresponds to speed } v_{p}
\tag{C8}
\]

In practice, we pre‑compute a mapping \(\mathcal{M}_{p,\Delta}\in\{0,1\}\) that equals 1 when plan *p* uses interval Δ, otherwise 0, and write

\[
\tau_{t,b,\Delta}= \sum_{p\in P}\frac{L_{b}}{v_{p}}\,\mathcal{M}_{p,\Delta}\, y_{t,b,p}
\qquad \forall t,b,\Delta
\tag{C8'}
\]

### 6.5. Physical speed limits  

\[
v_{min}\;\le\; \sum_{p\in P} v_{p}\, y_{t,b,p} \;\le\; v_{max}
\qquad \forall t\in T,\; b\in V
\tag{C9}
\]

### 6.6. Acceleration / deceleration limits (linearised)  

Assume a train can change its average speed only between consecutive blocks within the acceleration envelope:

\[
\Bigl|\sum_{p} v_{p} y_{t,b+1,p} - \sum_{p} v_{p} y_{t,b,p}\Bigr|
\;\le\; a_{max}\,\Delta t
\qquad \forall t\in T,\; b\in V
\tag{C10}
\]

The absolute value can be linearised with two inequalities.

### 6.7. Domain constraints  

\[
a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}, \tau_{t,b,\Delta}, \delta_{t}, e_{t} \ge 0
\]

\[
x_{t,b}\in\{0,1\},\; y_{t,b,p}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{t,i}\in\{0,1\}
\]

---

## 7. Complete MILP Statement  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& w_{delay}\sum_{t\in T}\delta_{t}+w_{energy}\sum_{t\in T}e_{t}\\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(C1)–(C10)} && \forall\; \text{relevant indices}\\
&\sum_{p\in P} y_{t,b,p}=1 &&\forall t\in T,\; b\in V\\
&\delta_{t}\ge a_{t,s}-A_{t,s} &&\forall t\in T,\; s\in S\\
&e_{t}= \sum_{b\in V}\sum_{\Delta\in\Delta} c_{\Delta}\,\tau_{t,b,\Delta} &&\forall t\in T\\
&\text{binary and non‑negativity constraints}\\
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 8. Remarks on Implementation  

1. **Speed‑plan generation (set *P*)** – For each free block, a small catalogue (e.g., 3–5 plans) is built by solving a short‑horizon optimal‑control problem that respects acceleration limits and yields a pair \((v_{p},\; \text{energy coefficient})\). This keeps the MILP size tractable while preserving the essential trade‑off between travel time and energy.  

2. **Big‑M selection** – \(M\) must be larger than the maximum possible time difference between any two trains on a block (e.g., horizon length).  

3. **Decomposition** – The model can be decomposed exactly as described in the source text: (i) an **integer master** that decides the binary variables \(\{x,y,z\}\) (train interactions), and (ii) a **continuous sub‑problem** that, given a fixed set of binary decisions, computes the optimal arrival/departure times and energy (a linear program). This decomposition yields the “train‑plan selection” formulation used in the adaptive algorithm.  

4. **Scalability** – For large networks, the set of pairwise order variables *z* can be restricted to *conflicting* train pairs (those whose routes overlap in time‑space), dramatically reducing the number of binary variables.  

5. **Solution quality** – By refining the speed‑plan set *P* (adding intermediate speeds) in an iterative fashion, the MILP solution converges to the true nonlinear optimum of the underlying TRSMP.  

---

### End of Formulation  

The equations above constitute a **complete, linear (MILP) model** for the **Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP)** under a partial‑segment blockage. All variables, objective components, and constraints are explicitly defined, and the underlying assumptions are stated so that the model can be directly implemented in any commercial MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, etc.).

Text:
**Variables**

| Symbol | Description | Type |
|--------|-------------|------|
| \(y_{i,t}\) | 1 if train \(i\) uses a reroute on blocked segment \(t\); 0 otherwise | binary |
| \(x_{i,j,s}\) | 1 if train \(i\) precedes train \(j\) on shared (non‑blocked) segment \(s\); 0 otherwise | binary |
| \(D_i\) | Departure time of train \(i\) from the origin station | continuous, \(\ge 0\) |
| \(A_i\) | Arrival time of train \(i\) at its final station | continuous, \(\ge 0\) |
| \(T_{i,s}\) | Travel time of train \(i\) on segment \(s\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) |
| \(\text{start}_{i,s},\text{end}_{i,s}\) | Entry‑ and exit‑time of train \(i\) on segment \(s\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) |
| \(v_{i,s,k}\) | 1 if train \(i\) uses speed option \(k\) on segment \(s\); 0 otherwise | binary |

**Parameters**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(\mathcal{I}\) | Set of trains |
| \(\mathcal{S}\) | Set of all track segments |
| \(\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{S}\) | Set of partially blocked segments |
| \(\mathcal{K}_s\) | Set of admissible speed options on segment \(s\) |
| \(\ell_s\) | Length of segment \(s\) (km) |
| \(\nu_{s,k}\) | Speed of option \(k\) on segment \(s\) (km/h) |
| \(e_{s,k}\) | Energy coefficient of option \(k\) on segment \(s\) |
| \(\overline{\nu}_s\) | Speed limit on segment \(s\) |
| \(\tau^{\text{unb}}_t\) | Unblocking time of blocked segment \(t\) |
| \(\delta_i\) | Scheduled arrival time of train \(i\) at its final station |
| \(w^{\text{delay}}, w^{\text{energy}}\) | Weights in the objective |
| \(M\) | A sufficiently large constant for big‑M linearisation |
| \(\text{route}_i\) | Ordered list of segments traversed by train \(i\) (original route) |
| \(\text{seg\_to\_station}_s\) | Down‑stream station reached after segment \(s\) |
| \(\underline{d}_s\) | Minimum dwell time at the station after segment \(s\) |

**Objective function**

\[
\min\; 
w^{\text{delay}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\bigl(A_i-\delta_i\bigr)
\;+\;
w^{\text{energy}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}_s}
e_{s,k}\;v_{i,s,k}
\]

The first term penalises total delay, the second term penalises total energy consumption.

**Constraints**

1. **Route‑choice on blocked segments**  
   For every train \(i\) and blocked segment \(t\in\mathcal{B}\):
   \[
   y_{i,t}=0 \quad\text{if }t\notin \text{route}_i
   \]
   (trains not using the blocked segment cannot take a detour).

2. **Speed‑selection (exactly one speed per traversed segment)**  
   For each train \(i\) and segment \(s\):
   \[
   \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}_s} v_{i,s,k}= 
   \begin{cases}
   1 &\text{if } s\in \text{route}_i\\
   0 &\text{otherwise}
   \end{cases}
   \tag{2a}
   \]

3. **Travel‑time – speed linkage (big‑M linearisation)**  
   Let \(\tau_{s,k}= \frac{60\;\ell_s}{\nu_{s,k}}\) (minutes required if speed option \(k\) is chosen).  
   For each \(i,s,k\):
   \[
   T_{i,s}\ge \tau_{s,k}-M\,(1-v_{i,s,k})\quad\text{and}\quad
   T_{i,s}\le \tau_{s,k}+M\,(1-v_{i,s,k})
   \tag{3}
   \]

4. **Entry/exit times on each segment**  
   \[
   \text{end}_{i,s}= \text{start}_{i,s}+T_{i,s} \qquad\forall i,s
   \tag{4}
   \]

5. **Sequential propagation along a train’s route**  
   For the first segment \(s_1\) of train \(i\):
   \[
   \text{start}_{i,s_1}=D_i
   \]
   For any subsequent segment \(s_{k}\) (preceded by \(s_{k-1}\)):
   \[
   \text{start}_{i,s_k}= \text{end}_{i,s_{k-1}}\qquad\forall i,\;k\ge 2
   \tag{5}
   \]

6. **Ordering on shared (non‑blocked) segments**  
   For any two different trains \(i,j\) that both use a non‑blocked segment \(s\notin\mathcal{B}\):
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
   \text{start}_{i,s}+T_{i,s} &\le \text{start}_{j,s}+M\,(1-x_{i,j,s})\\
   \text{start}_{j,s}+T_{j,s} &\le \text{start}_{i,s}+M\,x_{i,j,s}
   \end{aligned}
   \qquad\forall i<j,\;s\notin\mathcal{B}
   \tag{6}
   \]
   Exactly one of the two inequalities is active, guaranteeing conflict‑free occupation.

7. **Blocked‑segment time‑window**  
   If train \(i\) traverses a blocked segment \(t\in\mathcal{B}\) without taking a detour (\(y_{i,t}=0\)):
   \[
   \text{start}_{i,t}\ge \tau^{\text{unb}}_t
   \tag{7}
   \]

8. **Arrival‑time definition (including dwell times)**  
   Let \(\underline{d}_s\) be the minimum dwell at the station following segment \(s\). Then for every train \(i\):
   \[
   A_i = D_i + \sum_{s\in\text{route}_i} T_{i,s}
          + \sum_{s\in\text{route}_i}\underline{d}_s
   \tag{8}
   \]

9. **Speed‑limit enforcement**  
   For any speed option whose speed exceeds the segment limit:
   \[
   v_{i,s,k}=0 \qquad\forall i,\;s,\;k\text{ with }\nu_{s,k}>\overline{\nu}_s
   \tag{9}
   \]

10. **Variable domains**  
    \[
    y_{i,t},x_{i,j,s},v_{i,s,k}\in\{0,1\};
    \quad D_i,A_i,T_{i,s},\text{start}_{i,s},\text{end}_{i,s}\ge 0
    \tag{10}
    \]

---

### Assumptions (explicit)

* The timetable horizon is large enough that the big‑M value \(M\) does not restrict feasible schedules.  
* Each train traverses each segment at most once (no loops).  
* Rerouting for a blocked segment is modelled by binary \(y_{i,t}\); the alternative path is assumed to be already incorporated in the train’s route list (or represented by a sufficiently long travel time when \(y_{i,t}=1\)).  
* Energy consumption on a segment is linear in the selected speed option via coefficient \(e_{s,k}\).  
* Dwell times are constant per station and do not depend on the train.  

The presented MILP captures (i) conflict‑free assignment of trains to tracks (including bidirectional conflicts on a single line), (ii) the choice between original and rerouted paths on blocked segments, (iii) the selection of speed levels that determine both travel time and energy use, and (iv) the weighted minimisation of total delay and total energy consumption. This model can be solved with any MILP solver (e.g., CPLEX, Gurobi, CBC).
