Text:
**Passenger‑oriented Real‑time Train‑Scheduling MILP (MPC‑style)**  
The formulation below follows the description in the prompt. It combines (i) a piece‑wise‑constant approximation of time‑varying passenger demand, (ii) flexible train composition (choice of the number of cars per train), and (iii) rolling‑stock circulation (assignment of physical train units to service trips). The model is written for a single planning horizon (the MPC prediction window) that is later shifted forward in a receding‑horizon fashion.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Sets, Indices and Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | Set of service trips (planned departures)  \(t=1,\dots ,|T|\) |
| **S** | Set of stations on the line  \(s=1,\dots ,|S|\) (ordered from origin to terminal) |
| **K** | Set of train‑type (composition) alternatives  \(k=1,\dots ,|K|\) (e.g., 2‑car, 4‑car, 6‑car) |
| **U** | Set of rolling‑stock units (physical trainsets)  \(u=1,\dots ,|U|\) |
| **I** | Set of demand intervals (piece‑wise constant)  \(i=1,\dots ,|I|\) |
| **P** | Set of passenger‑flow arcs \((s,s')\) with \(s<s'\) (origin‑destination pairs) |

**Parameters (assumed known / estimated)**  

* \(L_k\) – passenger capacity of composition \(k\) (seats).  
* \(c_k\) – operating cost per service trip when using composition \(k\) (fuel, crew, etc.).  
* \(c^{\text{turn}}_u\) – cost of turning (re‑positioning) unit \(u\) between two trips (e.g., dead‑head).  
* \(\Delta^{\text{run}}_{s,s'}\) – nominal running time (travel time) between consecutive stations \(s\) and \(s'\).  
* \(\Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}\) – maximum admissible dwell time at a station (seconds).  
* \(\Delta^{\text{head}}_{\min}\) – minimum headway between two consecutive departures from the same station (seconds).  
* \(\Delta^{\text{head}}_{\max}\) – maximum headway allowed (service‑frequency bound).  
* \(d_{p,i}\) – forecast passenger demand for OD‑pair \(p\in P\) during interval \(i\) (persons).  
* \(\tau_i\) – start time of interval \(i\) (seconds from the beginning of the MPC horizon).  
* \(M\) – a big‑M constant (larger than any feasible time value, e.g. 10⁶ s).  

*Assumptions* (explicitly stated):  

1. Passenger demand is piece‑wise constant on each interval \(i\).  
2. Trains may skip stations (stop‑skipping) – modelled by binary stop‑variables.  
3. Rolling‑stock units are homogeneous except for their current location; any unit can be assigned to any composition \(k\).  
4. All trips start and finish within the prediction horizon (no carry‑over of unfinished trips).  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| \(x_{t,k}\) | binary | 1 if trip \(t\) uses composition \(k\). |
| \(y_{t,u}\) | binary | 1 if rolling‑stock unit \(u\) is assigned to trip \(t\). |
| \(z_{t,s}\) | binary | 1 if trip \(t\) stops at station \(s\) (otherwise it skips). |
| \(a_{t,s}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Arrival time of trip \(t\) at station \(s\). |
| \(d_{t,s}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Departure time of trip \(t\) from station \(s\). |
| \(\theta_{p,i}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Number of passengers of OD‑pair \(p\) that board during interval \(i\). |
| \(w_{p,i}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Number of passengers of OD‑pair \(p\) that wait (unserved) at the end of interval \(i\). |
| \(e_{t}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Energy consumption (or any other linear cost proxy) of trip \(t\). (optional, can be omitted). |

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Objective Function  

The goal is a **weighted sum** of three components:

1. **Operating cost** (fixed cost per composition + turning cost).  
2. **Passenger waiting penalty** (unserved demand).  
3. **Schedule deviation penalty** (to keep the solution close to a nominal timetable, if desired).  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in K} c_k \, x_{t,k}}_{\text{composition cost}} 
      + \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{u\in U} c^{\text{turn}}_u \, y_{t,u}}_{\text{rolling‑stock turning cost}} \\[2mm]
    & + \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{p\in P}\sum_{i\in I} w_{p,i}}_{\text{passenger waiting penalty}} 
      + \underbrace{\beta \sum_{t\in T}\bigl|a_{t,s^{\text{orig}}}-\hat a_{t}\bigr|}_{\text{timetable deviation}} 
\end{aligned}
\]

* \(\alpha,\beta\) are user‑defined weighting coefficients.  
* \(\hat a_{t}\) denotes the nominal (planned) departure time of trip \(t\) from its origin station \(s^{\text{orig}}\).  
* The absolute value can be linearised with auxiliary variables if required.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Constraints  

#### 4.1. Composition‑selection constraints  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,k}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T \tag{C1}
\]

Each trip uses exactly one composition.

#### 4.2. Rolling‑stock assignment  

\[
\sum_{u\in U} y_{t,u}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T \tag{C2}
\]

Each trip is performed by exactly one physical unit.

\[
\sum_{t\in T} y_{t,u}\le 1 \qquad\forall u\in U \tag{C3}
\]

A unit cannot be assigned to two trips that overlap in time (see later temporal feasibility constraints).  

#### 4.3. Stop‑skipping (service plan)  

If a train does not stop at a station, its dwell time is forced to zero:

\[
d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \le \Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}\, z_{t,s} \qquad\forall t,s \tag{C4}
\]

\[
d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \ge 0 \qquad\forall t,s \tag{C5}
\]

If \(z_{t,s}=0\) then the dwell time is forced to 0.

#### 4.4. Travel‑time propagation  

For consecutive stations \(s\) and \(s+1\):

\[
a_{t,s+1} \ge d_{t,s} + \Delta^{\text{run}}_{s,s+1} \qquad\forall t,\; s=1,\dots,|S|-1 \tag{C6}
\]

If a train skips a station, the dwell time term disappears automatically because of (C4).

#### 4.5. Headway (service‑frequency) constraints  

For any two trips \(t\) and \(t'\) that depart from the same origin station:

\[
a_{t',s^{\text{orig}}} - a_{t,s^{\text{orig}} \ge \Delta^{\text{head}}_{\min} - M\,(1-\delta_{t,t'}) \tag{C7}
\]

\[
a_{t',s^{\text{orig}}} - a_{t,s^{\text{orig}}} \le \Delta^{\text{head}}_{\max} + M\,(1-\delta_{t,t'}) \tag{C8}
\]

where \(\delta_{t,t'}\) is a binary variable equal to 1 if \(t'\) follows \(t\) in the schedule (can be introduced by ordering the trips a priori; for simplicity we assume trips are indexed in chronological order, thus \(\delta_{t,t'}=1\) for \(t'<t\)).  

#### 4.6. Capacity – passenger boarding  

The number of passengers that board a train cannot exceed its capacity (sum over all OD‑pairs whose origin is the current station and whose boarding interval overlaps the train’s dwell time).

Define a binary indicator  

\[
b_{t,p,i}= 
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if trip }t\text{ stops at the origin station of }p\text{ and } a_{t,s^{\text{orig}(p)}}\in[\tau_i,\tau_{i+1})\\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\]

(Linearised with big‑M if needed.)

Then capacity constraint for each trip:

\[
\sum_{p\in P}\sum_{i\in I} \theta_{p,i}\, b_{t,p,i} \le \sum_{k\in K} L_k \, x_{t,k} \qquad\forall t\in T \tag{C9}
\]

#### 4.7. Demand balance (flow conservation)  

For each OD‑pair \(p\) and interval \(i\):

\[
\theta_{p,i} + w_{p,i-1}= d_{p,i}+ w_{p,i} \qquad\forall p\in P,\; i\in I \tag{C10}
\]

where  

* \(d_{p,i}\) is the number of passengers of OD‑pair \(p\) that actually board during interval \(i\).  
* \(w_{p,0}=0\) (no waiting before the horizon starts).  

The boarding variable \(d_{p,i}\) can be expressed through the capacity constraints:

\[
d_{p,i}= \sum_{t\in T} \theta_{p,i}\, b_{t,p,i} \qquad\forall p,i \tag{C11}
\]

(If the sum exceeds capacity, the excess is automatically transferred to waiting variable \(w_{p,i}\) via (C10).)

#### 4.8. Rolling‑stock temporal feasibility  

If unit \(u\) performs trip \(t\) and then trip \(t'\), the departure of the second must be after the arrival of the first plus a turnaround time \(\Delta^{\text{turn}}_u\). Introduce binary linking variable \(\lambda_{t,t',u}\) that equals 1 when \(u\) serves \(t\) and then \(t'\). A compact linearisation is:

\[
a_{t',s^{\text{orig}}} \ge d_{t,s^{\text{term}}}+ \Delta^{\text{turn}}_u - M\,(2-y_{t,u}-y_{t',u}) \qquad\forall t,t',u \tag{C12}
\]

If both \(y_{t,u}=y_{t',u}=1\) the constraint is active; otherwise the big‑M term deactivates it.

#### 4.9. Non‑negativity / binary definitions  

\[
x_{t,k}\in\{0,1\},\; y_{t,u}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{t,s}\in\{0,1\},\;
a_{t,s}\ge0,\; d_{t,s}\ge0,\;
\theta_{p,i}\ge0,\; w_{p,i}\ge0 \tag{C13}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Full MILP Statement  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \sum_{t}\sum_{k}c_k x_{t,k}
      +\sum_{t}\sum_{u}c^{\text{turn}}_u y_{t,u}
      +\alpha\sum_{p,i} w_{p,i}
      +\beta\sum_{t}\bigl|a_{t,s^{\text{orig}}}-\hat a_{t}\bigr| \\[1mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(C1)–(C13)} \\
\end{aligned}}
\]

All constraints are linear (big‑M linearisation is used where necessary), therefore the model is a **Mixed‑Integer Linear Program (MILP)**.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 6. Model‑Predictive‑Control (MPC) Embedding  

1. **Prediction horizon**: Divide the future planning period \([0,T_{\text{hor}}]\) into \(N_I\) equal intervals \(\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{N_I}\).  
2. **Data update**: At each control step \(k\) (every \(\Delta t_{\text{MPC}}\) seconds) refresh the demand forecasts \(d_{p,i}\) for the remaining intervals.  
3. **Solve the MILP** (or the reduced MILP after presolve + LSTM‑predicted integer vars).  
4. **Implement** only the first control actions (e.g., the departure times and composition of the first few trips).  
5. **Shift horizon** forward, repeat.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 7. Remarks on Presolve & Learning‑Based Acceleration  

* **Presolve techniques** (as mentioned in the prompt) can be applied before solving:  
  * Eliminate compositions \(k\) that cannot satisfy the maximal demand in any interval.  
  * Fix \(z_{t,s}=0\) for stations with zero expected boarding in the entire horizon.  
  * Remove rolling‑stock units that are unavailable (maintenance).  

* After presolve, the remaining binary variables \(\{x_{t,k}, y_{t,u}, z_{t,s}\}\) are fed to an **LSTM** that predicts a feasible (or near‑feasible) binary pattern. Those predictions are then **fixed** in the MILP, turning the problem into a pure **LP** for the continuous timing variables \(\{a_{t,s},d_{t,s},\theta_{p,i},w_{p,i}\}\). This two‑stage scheme preserves feasibility (the LP respects all linear constraints) while dramatically reducing the online computational burden.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
**In summary**, the equations above constitute a complete linear (MILP) model for passenger‑oriented real‑time train scheduling that captures time‑varying demand, flexible train composition, and rolling‑stock circulation, and is ready to be embedded in an MPC loop or combined with a learning‑based predictor for fast online operation.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for Conflict‑Detection‑and‑Resolution (CDR) under Distance‑to‑Go (DTG) signalling**  

The formulation below is a complete, linear model that can be used directly in a commercial MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, …).  All symbols are defined explicitly; where data are not given in the description, reasonable assumptions are stated and marked **(Assumption)**.

---

## 1.  Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\). |
| \(N\) | Set of network nodes (stations, switch‑points, block ends, TTD‑sections). |
| \(A\subseteq N\times N\) | Set of directed track arcs (track‑segments) \((i,j)\). |
| \(S\subseteq A\) | Sub‑set of arcs that are **switches** (turnouts). |
| \(K\) | Set of discrete **speed‑profile options** (e.g. “full speed”, “reduced speed”). |
| \(P_t\) | Ordered list of planned path nodes for train \(t\) (derived from the timetable). |
| \(\mathcal{P}_t\) | Set of consecutive node‑pairs \((i,j)\) that appear in \(P_t\). |

---

## 2.  Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning | Typical unit |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| \(L_{ij}\) | Length of arc \((i,j)\). | [km] |
| \(\bar v_{k}\) | Nominal speed for speed‑profile \(k\). | [km/h] |
| \(a^{\text{br}}_{t}\) | Braking deceleration of train \(t\) (absolute value). | [km/h²] |
| \(\tau^{\text{dw}}_{t,i}\) | **Dwell time** required at node \(i\) for train \(t\) (if \(i\) is a station). | [s] |
| \(\tau^{\text{run}}_{t,ij,k}\) | Running time of train \(t\) on arc \((i,j)\) when using speed‑profile \(k\). Computed as  

\[
\tau^{\text{run}}_{t,ij,k}= \frac{L_{ij}}{\bar v_{k}} \times 3600 \qquad\text{(Assumption: constant speed on the arc).}
\] | [s] |
| \(\beta_{t,ij}\) | **Braking distance** of train \(t\) when travelling on arc \((i,j)\) at the speed used on that arc (depends on the chosen profile).  

\[
\beta_{t,ij}= \frac{\bar v_{k}^{2}}{2\,a^{\text{br}}_{t}} \quad\text{if profile }k\text{ is selected on }(i,j). 
\] | [km] |
| \(\Delta^{\text{sep}}_{t,t'}\) | Minimum **speed‑dependent separation distance** required between the *front* of the following train \(t\) and the *rear* of the leading train \(t'\).  

\[
\Delta^{\text{sep}}_{t,t'} = \beta_{t',\text{last}} + \epsilon \qquad\text{with }\epsilon=0.05\text{ km (safety margin).}
\] | [km] |
| \(M\) | Large constant for Big‑M linearisation (e.g. \(M = 10^{6}\)). |
| \(\text{EOT}_{t}\) | Original **expected time of arrival** at the final node of train \(t\) (from the given timetable). | [s] |
| \(\text{EOT}^{\text{orig}}_{t,i}\) | Original expected time of passage of node \(i\) by train \(t\) (from the timetable). | [s] |
| \(\text{Cap}_{ij}\) | Maximum number of trains that can simultaneously occupy arc \((i,j)\) (normally 1, but may be 2 on double‑track). | – |
| \(\text{Cap}^{\text{switch}}_{s}\) | Maximum number of trains that may occupy a switch \(s\) at the same time (normally 1). | – |

---

## 3.  Decision variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|--------|
| \(x_{t,ij}^{k} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses arc \((i,j)\) with speed‑profile \(k\); 0 otherwise. |
| \(a_{t,i} \ge 0\) | Continuous | **Actual arrival time** of train \(t\) at node \(i\). |
| \(d_{t,i} \ge 0\) | Continuous | **Actual departure time** of train \(t\) from node \(i\). |
| \(\delta_{t,t'}^{i} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | Ordering variable: 1 if train \(t\) passes node \(i\) **after** train \(t'\); 0 otherwise. |
| \(z_{t} \ge 0\) | Continuous | **Total delay** of train \(t\) (difference between actual final arrival and original expected arrival). |
| \(y_{t,s} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) occupies switch \(s\) (any of its incoming/outgoing arcs). |
| \(b_{t,i} \ge 0\) | Continuous | **Brake‑indication point** (distance measured from node \(i\) backwards along the train’s route) for train \(t\) when the MA ends at node \(i\). (Only needed for reporting; not used in constraints). |

---

## 4.  Objective  

Minimise the weighted sum of total delays (weights can be set to 1 for a pure delay minimisation):

\[
\boxed{\min \; \sum_{t\in T} w_{t}\, z_{t}}
\]

where \(w_{t}=1\) for all trains unless a priority weighting is required (e.g., passenger vs. freight).

---

## 5.  Constraints  

### 5.1 Path feasibility  

1. **Exactly one speed‑profile per traversed arc**  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,ij}^{k}= 
\begin{cases}
1 & \forall (i,j)\in \mathcal{P}_t\\
0 & \forall (i,j)\notin \mathcal{P}_t
\end{cases}
\qquad\forall t\in T
\tag{1}
\]

2. **Flow conservation on the path** – ensures that the train follows its ordered node list  

\[
\sum_{j:(i,j)\in \mathcal{P}_t} \sum_{k} x_{t,ij}^{k}
\;-\;
\sum_{j:(j,i)\in \mathcal{P}_t} \sum_{k} x_{t,ji}^{k}
=
\begin{cases}
1 & i = \text{origin of }t\\
-1 & i = \text{destination of }t\\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\; i\in N
\tag{2}
\]

### 5.2 Timing relations  

3. **Departure after arrival + dwell (if any)**  

\[
d_{t,i} \;\ge\; a_{t,i} + \tau^{\text{dw}}_{t,i}\qquad\forall t\in T,\; i\in N
\tag{3}
\]

4. **Travel time on an arc** – link arrival at the next node to departure from the current node  

\[
a_{t,j} \;\ge\; d_{t,i} + \sum_{k\in K}\tau^{\text{run}}_{t,ij,k}\,x_{t,ij}^{k}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in \mathcal{P}_t
\tag{4}
\]

5. **Initial condition (original timetable)**  

\[
a_{t,\text{origin}} \;=\; \text{EOT}^{\text{orig}}_{t,\text{origin}} \qquad\forall t\in T
\tag{5}
\]

6. **Delay definition**  

\[
z_{t} \; \ge\; a_{t,\text{destination}} - \text{EOT}^{\text{orig}}_{t,\text{destination}}
\qquad\forall t\in T
\tag{6}
\]

### 5.3 Capacity / occupancy constraints  

7. **At most one train in a block/TD‑section** (fixed‑block analogue, but we keep it for safety; the DTG separation will dominate in most cases)  

\[
\sum_{t\in T}\Bigl[\, a_{t,i} \le \theta \le d_{t,i} \,\Bigr] \;\le\; \text{Cap}_{ij}
\qquad\forall (i,j)\in A,\; \forall \theta\in\{a_{t,i},d_{t,i}\}
\tag{7}
\]

In a linear model this is expressed with ordering binaries (see next constraint).

8. **Ordering of two trains on the same arc**  

For every unordered pair \((t,t')\) with \(t\neq t'\) and every arc \((i,j)\) that both may use (i.e. \((i,j)\in\mathcal{P}_t\cap\mathcal{P}_{t'}\)):

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{t',i} &\ge d_{t,i} - M\,(1-\delta_{t,t'}^{i}) \\
a_{t,i}   &\ge d_{t',i} - M\,\delta_{t,t'}^{i}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall (i,j)\in A
\tag{8}
\]

The binary \(\delta_{t,t'}^{i}\) chooses which train is first on the arc.

### 5.4 Speed‑dependent separation (core DTG feature)  

9. **Minimum distance between successive trains** – expressed in time using the braking distance of the leading train.  
For each pair \((t,t')\) that share a common **conflict node** \(i\) (the point where the MA of the following train ends, i.e. the entry of the occupied block/section), we enforce:

\[
a_{t,i} \;\ge\; a_{t',i} + \frac{\Delta^{\text{sep}}_{t',t}}{\bar v_{k}}\times 3600 - M\,(1-\delta_{t,t'}^{i})
\qquad\forall t\neq t',\; i\in N
\tag{9}
\]

Explanation:  
*If train \(t\) follows train \(t'\) at node \(i\) (\(\delta_{t,t'}^{i}=1\)), the arrival time of \(t\) must be later than the arrival of \(t'\) by at least the time needed to cover the speed‑dependent separation distance \(\Delta^{\text{sep}}_{t',t}\) at the speed used on the preceding arc. The speed \(\bar v_{k}\) is the one selected for the arc that brings train \(t\) to node \(i\) (the model can use a big‑M linearisation to pick the appropriate speed; for clarity we write it directly).*

If the pair does **not** share the same block/section (i.e., they are on different tracks), the binary can be forced to 0, making the constraint inactive.

### 5.5 Switch occupation  

10. **Only one train may occupy a switch at a time**  

\[
\sum_{t\in T} y_{t,s} \;\le\; \text{Cap}^{\text{switch}}_{s} \qquad\forall s\in S
\tag{10}
\]

Linking \(y_{t,s}\) to the arc variables:

\[
y_{t,s} \;\ge\; \sum_{k\in K}\bigl(x_{t,ij}^{k}+x_{t,ji}^{k}\bigr) \qquad\forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in S
\tag{11}
\]

### 5.6 Brake‑indication point (optional reporting)  

12. **Compute the distance from node \(i\) where the brake must be applied** (used only for output, not for feasibility).  

\[
b_{t,i}= \beta_{t,\text{prev}} \quad\text{where }\text{prev}\text{ is the arc preceding }i\text{ on }t\text{'s path.}
\tag{12}
\]

Because \(\beta_{t,\text{prev}}\) is known once the speed‑profile on that arc is fixed, we can linearise it by:

\[
b_{t,i}= \sum_{k\in K}\beta_{t,\,\text{prev},k}\,x_{t,\text{prev}}^{k}
\qquad\forall t,i
\tag{13}
\]

---

## 6.  Summary of the model  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{t\in T} w_{t}\,z_{t} \\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(1)–(13)} \\
&x_{t,ij}^{k}\in\{0,1\},\;
\delta_{t,t'}^{i}\in\{0,1\},\;
y_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\\
&a_{t,i},d_{t,i},z_{t},b_{t,i}\ge 0\qquad\forall t,i.
\end{aligned}
\]

The model simultaneously decides:

* **Which speed‑profile** each train uses on every arc (binary \(x\)).  
* **When** each train arrives/departs from every node (continuous \(a,d\)).  
* **The ordering** of trains on shared resources (binary \(\delta\), \(y\)).  
* **The resulting total delay** (continuous \(z\)).  

The **speed‑dependent separation constraint (9)** captures the essence of DTG signalling: the required headway between two trains is a function of the leading train’s braking distance, which itself depends on its speed and deceleration capability. By selecting different speed‑profiles, the optimisation can deliberately reduce braking distances (e.g., by slowing a train before a bottleneck) and thereby increase line capacity while keeping total delay minimal.

---

### 7.  Remarks & modelling choices (Assumptions)

| # | Assumption | Reason |
|---|------------|--------|
| A1 | Running time on an arc is computed with a **constant speed** equal to the chosen profile speed \(\bar v_k\). | Keeps the model linear; more detailed speed‑profile (piece‑wise) can be added at the cost of extra variables. |
| A2 | Braking distance uses the simple physics formula \(\beta = v^{2}/(2a)\). | Adequate for high‑speed mainline trains; safety margin \(\epsilon\) added. |
| A3 | The **end of authority (EoA)** is always at the **end of a block/TD‑section**; the brake‑indication point may lie anywhere inside the preceding arc. | Matches the ETCS‑L2 with Trackside Train Detection (TTD) description. |
| A4 | Capacity of a block is 1 (single‑track). For double‑track lines the parameter \(\text{Cap}_{ij}\) can be set to 2. | Allows the same formulation for both cases. |
| A5 | Large‑M value \(M=10^{6}\) is sufficient to deactivate constraints when the associated binary is 0. | Standard practice; can be tightened for numerical stability. |
| A6 | All trains start at their original timetable origin time (constraint 5). Re‑dispatching the origin time would require an additional decision variable. | Reflects the typical real‑time CDR situation where the delay originates downstream of the origin. |

---

**End of MILP formulation** – this model can be directly implemented, solved, and the optimal values of the binary variables give the rescheduling actions (speed reductions, re‑ordering at switches, etc.) that resolve all conflicts under DTG signalling while minimising total delay.

Text:
**Passenger‑oriented Real‑time Train‑Scheduling MILP (MPC‑style)**  

The model below is a *complete* mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) formulation that can be embedded in a Model‑Predictive‑Control (MPC) horizon.  
All symbols are defined in the **Notation** table; missing data are indicated as **Assumption A‑x** and can be replaced by the planner’s actual numbers.

---

## 1. Notation  

| Symbol | Meaning | Type / Set |
|--------|---------|------------|
| **\(T\)** | Set of trains that may be dispatched in the horizon  | \(t=1,\dots,|T|\) |
| **\(S\)** | Set of stations (ordered along the line) | \(s=1,\dots,|S|\) |
| **\(K\)** | Set of admissible train‑composition types (e.g. 2‑car, 4‑car, 6‑car) | \(k\in K\) |
| **\(I\)** | Set of time intervals that discretise the prediction horizon (piece‑wise‑constant demand) | \(i=1,\dots,|I|\) |
| **\(c_k\)** | Capacity (passenger seats) of composition type \(k\) | (Assumption A‑1) |
| **\(c^{\text{stock}}_k\)** | Number of train‑sets of type \(k\) available in the depot at the start of the horizon | (Assumption A‑2) |
| **\(d_{s,i}\)** | Expected passenger arrivals at station \(s\) during interval \(i\) (origin‑only demand) | (Assumption A‑3) |
| **\(\Delta_i\)** | Length (minutes) of interval \(i\) | (Assumption A‑4) |
| **\(\tau^{\text{run}}_{s,s+1}\)** | Minimum running time (minutes) between consecutive stations \(s\) and \(s+1\) (track‑speed limit) | (Assumption A‑5) |
| **\(\tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}\)** | Upper bound on dwell time at any station (minutes) | (Assumption A‑6) |
| **\(M\)** | Large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints | (Assumption A‑7) |

### Decision variables  

| Variable | Definition | Domain |
|----------|------------|--------|
| \(x_{t,k}\) | **Binary** – train \(t\) uses composition type \(k\) | \(\{0,1\}\) |
| \(y_{t,s}\) | **Binary** – train \(t\) stops at station \(s\) (1 = stop, 0 = pass‑through) | \(\{0,1\}\) |
| \(a_{t,i}\) | **Binary** – train \(t\) departs the first station *in* interval \(i\) (i.e. its departure time belongs to interval \(i\)) | \(\{0,1\}\) |
| \(p_{t,s,i}\) | **Continuous** – number of passengers on board train \(t\) just after leaving station \(s\) during interval \(i\) | \(\ge 0\) |
| \(w_{s,i}\) | **Continuous** – passengers **waiting** at station \(s\) at the end of interval \(i\) | \(\ge 0\) |
| \(\theta_{t,s}\) | **Continuous** – departure time (minutes from horizon start) of train \(t\) from station \(s\) | \(\ge 0\) |
| \(\delta_{t,s}\) | **Continuous** – dwell time of train \(t\) at station \(s\) | \(\ge 0\) |
| \(z_{t,s,i}\) | **Binary** – train \(t\) is present at station \(s\) during interval \(i\) (used for linking demand to the correct interval) | \(\{0,1\}\) |

---

## 2. Model Overview  

The MPC solves the MILP over a *rolling* horizon of length \(H = \sum_{i\in I}\Delta_i\) minutes.  
At each control step the first interval’s decisions are implemented, the horizon is shifted, and the problem is resolved with updated demand forecasts.

The objective simultaneously (i) minimises passenger waiting time, (ii) limits timetable deviation from a nominal schedule, and (iii) reduces the number of deployed train‑sets (operational cost).

---

## 3. Objective Function  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; 
& \underbrace{\alpha_1 \sum_{s\in S}\sum_{i\in I} w_{s,i}}_{\text{Passenger waiting time}} \\
& + \underbrace{\alpha_2 \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} \bigl| \theta_{t,s} - \theta^{\text{nom}}_{t,s}\bigr|}_{\text{Timetable deviation}} \\
& + \underbrace{\alpha_3 \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,k}}_{\text{Number of active trains (cost)}}
\end{aligned}
\]

where  

* \(\theta^{\text{nom}}_{t,s}\) is a given nominal departure time (e.g., from the day‑time schedule).  
* \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3\) are weighting coefficients chosen by the planner (Assumption A‑8).  
* The absolute value can be linearised with auxiliary variables \(u_{t,s}^{+},u_{t,s}^{-}\) and constraints  
  \[
  \theta_{t,s} - \theta^{\text{nom}}_{t,s}= u_{t,s}^{+} - u_{t,s}^{-},\qquad 
  u_{t,s}^{+},u_{t,s}^{-}\ge 0 .
  \]

---

## 4. Constraints  

### 4.1 Train‑composition selection  
\[
\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,k}= \sum_{i\in I} a_{t,i}\qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{C1}
\]
Every train that is dispatched (appears in exactly one interval) must be assigned **one** composition type.

### 4.2 Rolling‑stock availability (fleet balance)  
\[
\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in I} a_{t,i}\,x_{t,k}\le c^{\text{stock}}_k \qquad \forall k\in K
\tag{C2}
\]

### 4.3 Stop‑plan linking  
If a train does not stop at a station, its dwell time is forced to zero and no passenger exchange occurs.  
\[
\delta_{t,s}\le \tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}\, y_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,s
\tag{C3}
\]

### 4.4 Temporal feasibility – running‑time constraints  

For any two consecutive stations \(s\) and \(s+1\) that a train actually visits (i.e. both \(y_{t,s}=y_{t,s+1}=1\)):

\[
\theta_{t,s+1}\;\ge\; \theta_{t,s} + \tau^{\text{run}}_{s,s+1} + \delta_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,\; s=1,\dots,|S|-1
\tag{C4}
\]

If the train skips a station, the constraint is relaxed by a big‑M term:

\[
\theta_{t,s+1}\;\ge\; \theta_{t,s} + \tau^{\text{run}}_{s,s+1} + \delta_{t,s}
      - M\,(2-y_{t,s}-y_{t,s+1})\qquad\forall t,s
\tag{C4b}
\]

### 4.5 Interval‑assignment consistency  

A train that departs in interval \(i\) must have its first departure time inside that interval:

\[
\theta_{t,1} \;\ge\; \Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\Delta_j\Bigr) a_{t,i}
\qquad\forall t,i
\tag{C5a}
\]
\[
\theta_{t,1} \;\le\; \Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{i}\Delta_j\Bigr) a_{t,i} + M\,(1-a_{t,i})
\qquad\forall t,i
\tag{C5b}
\]

### 4.6 Passenger‑flow balance  

For each train \(t\), station \(s\) and interval \(i\) where the train is present (\(z_{t,s,i}=1\)):

\[
p_{t,s,i}= p_{t,s-1,i} + \underbrace{\beta_{t,s,i}}_{\text{boardings}} - \underbrace{\gamma_{t,s,i}}_{\text{alightings}}
\qquad\forall t,s,i
\tag{C6}
\]

Boardings and alightings are expressed linearly using the binary stop decision and the waiting‑passenger stock:

* **Boardings** (only if the train stops):
  \[
  \beta_{t,s,i}= \min\!\bigl\{ w_{s,i}^{\text{in}},\; c_k - p_{t,s-1,i}\bigr\}\; y_{t,s}
  \]
  Linearisation uses auxiliary variables \(b_{t,s,i}\) and constraints:
  \[
  b_{t,s,i}\le w_{s,i},\quad
  b_{t,s,i}\le c_k - p_{t,s-1,i},\quad
  b_{t,s,i}\le M y_{t,s},\quad
  b_{t,s,i}\ge 0.
  \]

* **Alightings** are taken as the number of passengers whose destination is station \(s\).  
  For the purpose of this model we assume a *known* destination distribution \(q_{s,s'}\) (fraction of passengers boarding at \(s\) whose destination is \(s'\)). Then
  \[
  \gamma_{t,s,i}= \sum_{s'>s} q_{s,s'}\,\beta_{t,s,i}
  \]
  (linear because \(q\) is a parameter).

### 4.7 Capacity limits  

\[
p_{t,s,i}\;\le\; \sum_{k\in K} c_k\,x_{t,k}\qquad\forall t,s,i
\tag{C7}
\]

### 4.8 Waiting‑passenger dynamics  

For every station \(s\) and interval \(i\) (except the first interval \(i=1\)):

\[
w_{s,i}= w_{s,i-1}+ d_{s,i} - \sum_{t\in T} b_{t,s,i} \qquad\forall s,i\ge 2
\tag{C8}
\]

Initial waiting passengers are assumed zero (or given as parameter \(w_{s,0}\)).  

All waiting variables must be non‑negative:

\[
w_{s,i}\ge 0\qquad\forall s,i
\tag{C8b}
\]

### 4.9 Logical linking of train presence to interval  

A train is present at station \(s\) during interval \(i\) iff its departure time from the first station lies before the end of interval \(i\) **and** the train has not yet left station \(s\):

\[
z_{t,s,i}\ge a_{t,i'}\quad\forall t,s,i,\; i'\le i\; \text{with}\; \theta_{t,s}\le \sum_{j=1}^{i}\Delta_j
\]
(Implemented with big‑M and ordering constraints; omitted for brevity – **Assumption A‑9**).

---

## 5. Summary of the MILP  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \alpha_1\sum_{s,i} w_{s,i}
      + \alpha_2\sum_{t,s}\bigl(u_{t,s}^{+}+u_{t,s}^{-}\bigr)
      + \alpha_3\sum_{t,k} x_{t,k}\\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(C1)}\;-\text{(C9)} \;\;\text{as listed above}\\
& x_{t,k},y_{t,s},a_{t,i},z_{t,s,i}\in\{0,1\}\\
& p_{t,s,i},w_{s,i},\theta_{t,s},\delta_{t,s},b_{t,s,i},u_{t,s}^{\pm}\ge 0 .
\end{aligned}
}
\]

---

## 6. Remarks & Assumptions  

| # | Description |
|---|--------------|
| **A‑1** | Capacity of each composition type (e.g., \(c_{2\text{‑car}}=200\) pax, \(c_{4\text{‑car}}=400\) pax). |
| **A‑2** | Fleet availability for each type at the start of the horizon (e.g., 5 two‑car, 3 four‑car). |
| **A‑3** | Passenger arrival forecasts per station per interval (derived from historical data or short‑term prediction). |
| **A‑4** | All intervals have equal length (e.g., \(\Delta_i=5\) min) – can be relaxed. |
| **A‑5** | Minimum travel times between stations, derived from line speed limits and distance. |
| **A‑6** | Maximum dwell time (e.g., 30 s) to guarantee service regularity. |
| **A‑7** | Big‑M value set larger than the horizon length (e.g., \(M=10^4\) min). |
| **A‑8** | Decision‑maker chooses weighting coefficients to reflect service policy. |
| **A‑9** | The presence‑linking constraints are linearised using standard “interval‑cover” big‑M formulations; they do not affect model size significantly after presolve pruning (see Section 7 of the original paper). |
| **A‑10** (Optional) – **Rolling‑horizon update**: after solving, only the decisions for the first interval \(i=1\) are executed; the horizon is shifted by \(\Delta_1\) and the MILP is resolved with updated \(d_{s,i}\) and \(w_{s,i}\). |

---

## 7. How the Model Fits an MPC Loop  

1. **Forecast** the piece‑wise‑constant demand \(d_{s,i}\) for the next \(H\) minutes.  
2. **Build** the MILP with the data above.  
3. **Solve** (commercial MILP solver or a learning‑augmented heuristic).  
4. **Implement** the first interval’s control actions:  
   * dispatch the trains whose \(a_{t,i}=1\) for the current interval,  
   * set the dwell times \(\delta_{t,s}\) and stop decisions \(y_{t,s}\).  
5. **Update** waiting‑passenger stocks \(w_{s,i}\) using the realised boardings.  
6. **Shift** the horizon, repeat from step 1.

Because the integer variables \(x_{t,k},y_{t,s},a_{t,i}\) are the *most* computationally demanding part, the original paper proposes a **presolve‑+‑LSTM** scheme that first removes obviously infeasible combinations (e.g., a 6‑car train at a station with platform length < 6‑car) and then predicts the remaining binary decisions with a trained LSTM. The MILP is then solved **only for the continuous variables** (\(\theta,\delta,p,w\)), guaranteeing feasibility while achieving real‑time performance.

--- 

**End of MILP description**. This formulation can be directly coded in any algebraic modelling language (AMPL, GAMS, Pyomo, JuMP) and embedded inside an MPC controller for passenger‑oriented real‑time train scheduling.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the real‑time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)**  
The model is built on the description given in the introduction and related work. It follows the three‑stage decomposition (rerouting → reordering → rescheduling) and is presented as a *single* MILP that can be solved either in a sub‑optimal “pair‑wise‑delay” mode or in a full‑propagation mode (the latter guarantees global optimality).  

---

## 1. Sets, parameters and assumptions  

| Symbol | Meaning | Remarks / Assumptions |
|--------|---------|------------------------|
| **T** = {1,…,|T|} | Set of trains that have to be dispatched in the planning horizon. | All trains are known a‑priori (arrival time, origin/destination). |
| **N** = {1,…,|N|} | Set of *nodes* (stations, junctions, signal blocks) of the railway network. | Nodes are topologically ordered along each line (index k). |
| **A** ⊆ N×N | Set of directed *arcs* (track sections) linking nodes. | Each arc a = (i,j) has a physical length ℓₐ and a maximum speed vₐ. |
| **Rᵢ** ⊆ 𝒫ᵢ | Set of admissible *routes* for train i. 𝒫ᵢ is the set of all simple paths from origin oᵢ to destination dᵢ. | A pre‑processing step (e.g. k‑shortest‑paths) limits |Rᵢ| to a manageable number (≤ 5–10). |
| **Kₐ** | Set of *track‑segments* (or signal blocks) that belong to arc a. | Used for capacity constraints. |
| **H** | Set of *time‑points* (discretisation of the planning horizon). | Horizon H = {0,…,H‑1} with Δt = 1 min (or any convenient granularity). |
| **Δ₀ᵢ** | Planned (timetable) departure time of train i from its origin. | Primary delay = deviation from Δ₀ᵢ. |
| **cₐ** | Capacity of track‑segment a (maximum number of trains that can occupy it simultaneously). | Usually cₐ = 1 for a single‑track block; cₐ > 1 for double‑track, passing loops, etc. |
| **βₐ** | Energy consumption factor (kWh per km) for arc a. | Used only in the *energy‑aware* variant (optional). |
| **M** | A “big‑M’’ constant larger than any feasible time (e.g. 10 000 min). | Used to linearise logical relations. |
| **ε** | Small positive constant (e.g. 0.001) to break ties in FIFO‑type ordering. | |

**Assumptions** (explicitly stated in the model)

1. **Deterministic travel times** – The travel time on arc a for train i is fixed and equal to τₐ = ℓₐ / vₐ (rounded up to the nearest time‑step).  
2. **No overtaking on a single‑track block** – If two trains use the same block they must respect a safe headway of at least one time‑step.  
3. **Safety overlap** – After a train stops at a signal, a fixed clearance margin σ (in minutes) must be kept free behind it (modeled by additional capacity constraints).  
4. **Primary vs secondary delay** – Primary delay is the deviation from the original timetable at the origin; secondary delay is the waiting time caused by conflicts with other trains.  
5. **Pair‑wise interpretation (sub‑optimal mode)** – Secondary delay of train i is attributed to a *single* predecessor train j (binary variable yᵢⱼ). In the full‑propagation mode the model uses cumulative delay variables dᵢʰ that automatically propagate.  

---

## 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Definition |
|----------|------|------------|
| **xᵢʳ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *i* is assigned to route *r* ∈ Rᵢ, 0 otherwise. |
| **sᵢʰ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *i* **starts** (leaves its origin) at time‑point *h* ∈ H. |
| **aᵢₐʰ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *i* occupies arc *a* during time‑point *h*. |
| **yᵢⱼ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | Pair‑wise waiting: 1 if train *i* is forced to wait for train *j* (j ≠ i). Used only in the sub‑optimal formulation. |
| **dᵢʰ** ≥ 0 | continuous | Cumulative delay of train *i* measured at the beginning of time‑point *h* (full‑propagation mode). |
| **zᵢʰ** ≥ 0 | continuous | Optional: energy consumption of train *i* up to time‑point *h* (used only in the energy‑aware variant). |

Auxiliary variables (derived in constraints)

* **pᵢₐ** = Σ₍ʳ∈Rᵢ₎ xᵢʳ·δ₍ʳ,ₐ₎ , where δ₍ʳ,ₐ₎ = 1 if route *r* contains arc *a*, 0 otherwise.  (binary, but linearised via big‑M).  

---

## 3. Objective functions  

Two alternative objective functions are provided; the user may select one or a weighted combination.

### 3.1. Primary‑delay minimisation (sub‑optimal mode)

\[
\min \; \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{h\in H} h \; s_{i h}
\]

Because each train starts exactly once, the term **h·sᵢʰ** equals the actual departure time; minimizing the sum therefore minimises total primary delay (relative to the timetable Δ₀ᵢ, which can be added as a constant if needed).

### 3.2. Total delay (including secondary) – full‑propagation mode  

\[
\min \; \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{h\in H} d_{i h}
\]

The cumulative delay variables dᵢʰ capture both primary and secondary delays; the objective directly minimises the total delay experienced by all trains.

### 3.3. Energy‑aware extension (optional)

\[
\min \; \alpha \underbrace{\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{h\in H} d_{i h}}_{\text{delay}} \;+\; \beta \underbrace{\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{h\in H} \beta_{a}\; a_{i a h}}_{\text{energy}}
\]

with weighting coefficients α,β > 0.

---

## 4. Model constraints  

### 4.1. Route selection  

1. **Exactly one route per train**  

\[
\sum_{r\in R_i} x_{i r}=1 \qquad \forall i\in T
\]

2. **Link route choice to arc usage** (big‑M linearisation)  

\[
a_{i a h} \le \sum_{r\in R_i} \delta_{r a}\,x_{i r} \qquad \forall i\in T,\; a\in A,\; h\in H
\]

If route *r* does not contain arc *a*, δ_{ra}=0, forcing aᵢₐʰ = 0.

### 4.2. Train movement (time‑expanded network)

3. **Departure time definition**  

\[
\sum_{h\in H} s_{i h}=1 \qquad \forall i\in T
\]

4. **Flow conservation on arcs** – a train can occupy an arc only after it has started and must stay on it for the deterministic travel time τₐ.  

For each train *i* and arc *a* with travel time τₐ:

\[
\sum_{h' = h}^{h+\tau_a-1} a_{i a h'} \; \ge\; \tau_a \; s_{i h} \qquad \forall i\in T,\; a\in A,\; h\in H
\]

(This forces a block of τₐ consecutive time‑steps to be set to 1 when the train starts on that arc.)

5. **Successor‑predecessor linking** – after leaving arc a the train must immediately enter the next arc on its chosen route. Let **Succ(a)** be the set of arcs that can follow a (according to the network topology). For each *i*, *a*, *h*:

\[
a_{i a h} \le \sum_{a'\in Succ(a)} a_{i a' (h+1)} + M\,(1-\sum_{r\in R_i}\delta_{r a}x_{i r})
\]

If arc a is not part of the selected route, the RHS is relaxed by big‑M.

### 4.3. Capacity (conflict) constraints  

6. **Block capacity** – at any time‑point the number of trains occupying a block cannot exceed its capacity cₐ (including safety overlap σ).  

\[
\sum_{i\in T} a_{i a h} \le c_a \qquad \forall a\in A,\; h\in H
\]

If a safety overlap σ is required, we can enlarge the effective occupation interval by σ (i.e., shift the aᵢₐʰ variable forward by σ time‑steps).

### 4.4. Pair‑wise waiting (sub‑optimal mode)  

7. **Each train waits for at most one predecessor**  

\[
\sum_{j\in T\setminus\{i\}} y_{i j} \le 1 \qquad \forall i\in T
\]

8. **Waiting time equals the start time of the predecessor plus its travel on the shared block**  

For any pair (i,j) that share at least one common block a, define **Shared(i,j)** = {a ∈ A | a belongs to both selected routes of i and j}. Using big‑M:

\[
s_{i h} \le \sum_{j\neq i}\sum_{h'} (h' + \tau_a) \, y_{i j} \;+\; M\,(1-y_{i j}) \qquad \forall i\in T,\; h\in H
\]

In practice the model linearises the “wait‑until‑j‑clears‑a” condition by coupling yᵢⱼ with the occupancy variables aⱼₐʰ.

9. **FIFO (optional) – enforce first‑in‑first‑out on a block**  

If train i precedes train j on block a, then

\[
\sum_{h} h\, a_{i a h} \le \sum_{h} h\, a_{j a h} \qquad \forall a\in A,\; i,j\in T \text{ with } o_i < o_j \text{ on the same line}
\]

(Only needed when a deterministic ordering is required.)

### 4.5. Delay propagation (full‑propagation mode)  

If the model is solved in the *global‑optimum* mode, the pair‑wise variables yᵢⱼ are omitted and the cumulative delay variables dᵢʰ are used.

10. **Definition of cumulative delay** – the delay at the beginning of a time‑step equals the previous delay plus any waiting caused by capacity conflicts. For each train i and time h:

\[
d_{i, h+1} \ge d_{i h} + \underbrace{\Big( \sum_{a\in A}\big( a_{i a h} - a_{i a (h-1)}\big) \Big)}_{\text{waiting indicator}} \qquad \forall i\in T,\; h\in H\setminus\{0\}
\]

A more compact formulation uses a *conflict‑penalty* variable wᵢʰ:

\[
w_{i h} \ge a_{i a h} + \sum_{j\neq i} a_{j a h} - c_a \qquad \forall a\in A,\; i\in T,\; h\in H
\]

\[
d_{i, h+1} \ge d_{i h} + \max_{a\in A} w_{i h}
\]

(Linearised with big‑M and auxiliary binaries.)

11. **Link start time to primary delay**  

Let Δ₀ᵢ be the scheduled departure time. Then

\[
\sum_{h\in H} h\, s_{i h} = \Delta_{0i} + d_{i0} \qquad \forall i\in T
\]

where dᵢ₀ is the primary delay (non‑negative).  

### 4.6. Reordering (optional)  

If the dispatcher wants to allow a different train order on a shared block, introduce binary ordering variables **oᵢⱼₐ** ∈ {0,1} meaning “train i passes before train j on block a”.  

12. **Mutual exclusivity**  

\[
o_{i j a} + o_{j i a} = 1 \qquad \forall a\in A,\; i<j,\; i,j\in T \text{ using } a
\]

13. **Consistency with occupancy**  

\[
\sum_{h} h\, a_{i a h} \le \sum_{h} h\, a_{j a h} + M\,(1-o_{i j a}) \qquad \forall a,i,j
\]

These constraints replace the FIFO rule when reordering is permitted.

### 4.7. Energy‑aware extension (optional)  

14. **Energy consumption on arc a**  

\[
z_{i h} \ge z_{i, h-1} + \beta_a\, a_{i a h} \qquad \forall i\in T,\; a\in A,\; h\in H
\]

The total energy term in the objective (see 3.3) aggregates zᵢᴴ.

---

## 5. Complete MILP formulation  

Putting everything together, the **sub‑optimal pair‑wise model** (fast, used for the first stage) is:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{h\in H} h\, s_{i h} \\
\text{s.t. } & \sum_{r\in R_i} x_{i r}=1 &&\forall i\\
& \sum_{h\in H} s_{i h}=1 &&\forall i\\
& a_{i a h} \le \sum_{r\in R_i}\delta_{r a}x_{i r} &&\forall i,a,h\\
& \sum_{h'=h}^{h+\tau_a-1} a_{i a h'} \ge \tau_a\, s_{i h} &&\forall i,a,h\\
& \sum_{i\in T} a_{i a h} \le c_a &&\forall a,h\\
& \sum_{j\neq i} y_{i j}\le 1 &&\forall i\\
& s_{i h} \le \sum_{j\neq i}\sum_{h'} (h'+\tau_a) y_{i j} + M(1-y_{i j}) &&\forall i,h\\
& \text{(optional FIFO / reordering constraints)}\\
& x_{i r},\, s_{i h},\, a_{i a h},\, y_{i j}\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
\]

The **global‑optimum model** (full propagation) replaces the y‑variables by the cumulative delay variables dᵢʰ and adds constraints (10)–(13). Its objective is:

\[
\min\; \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{h\in H} d_{i h}
\]

subject to the same route‑selection, capacity, flow‑conservation constraints plus the delay‑propagation constraints (10)–(13).  

If the energy‑aware objective (3.3) is selected, the term \(\sum_{i,a,h}\beta_a a_{i a h}\) is added and the auxiliary energy variables zᵢʰ are introduced with (14).

---

## 6. Remarks on model size and solution strategy  

* **Variable count** – O(|T|·|R| + |T|·|H| + |T|·|A|·|H|). The pre‑selection of a small set of routes (|Rᵢ| ≤ 5) and a modest time‑granularity (Δt = 1 min) keep the model tractable for medium‑size networks (≈ 50 trains, 100 blocks).  
* **Decomposition** – The first stage (sub‑optimal) can be solved in seconds and provides a feasible routing and ordering that serves as a warm‑start for the second stage (full‑propagation).  
* **Benders‑free** – Because the routing variables xᵢʳ are fixed after the first stage, the second stage becomes a pure rescheduling MILP with far fewer binary variables, which explains the low runtime reported in the paper.  
* **Optimality condition** – The model is globally optimal when the pair‑wise waiting variables yᵢⱼ correctly capture all conflict chains, i.e., when **no train experiences a waiting chain of length > 1**. This condition is verified a‑posteriori; if violated, the second stage is invoked.  

---

### End of MILP description  

The formulation above can be directly implemented in any MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP). By toggling the objective and the set of constraints (pair‑wise vs. cumulative delay, energy term, reordering), the same codebase can be used for the three contributions described in the paper:  

1. **Fast sub‑optimal rerouting + reordering** (pair‑wise model).  
2. **Exact rescheduling with fixed routes** (full‑propagation model).  
3. **Global‑optimum model with delay propagation** (full‑propagation + optional energy term).  

All required assumptions have been stated explicitly, and missing data (e.g., travel times, capacities) have been introduced as reasonable parameters.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling & Speed‑Management MILP  
(Partial‑Segment‑Blockage Scenario)**  

---

### 1️⃣ Sets, Indices & Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | set of trains, *t* ∈ T |
| **S** | set of track segments, *s* ∈ S |
| **D** = {↑,↓} | travel directions, *d* ∈ D |
| **P** | admissible speed‑levels, *p* ∈ P (break‑points of the speed‑vs‑energy curve) |
| **B** | set of discrete time periods that belong to the blockage window on the affected segment *ŝ* |
| **δₜ** | scheduled (original) departure time of train *t* |
| **τ̂ₜ** | scheduled arrival time of train *t* at its final destination |
| **Lₛ** | length of segment *s* (km) |
| **vₚ** | speed value associated with level *p* (km·h⁻¹) – constants |
| **Eₚ** | energy coefficient (kWh · km⁻¹) for level *p* (linearised from the true power‑vs‑speed curve) |
| **a_max**, **a_min** | maximal acceleration / deceleration (km·h⁻²) allowed between two consecutive speed‑levels |
| **Capₛ,₍d₎** | capacity of segment *s* in direction *d* (normally 1, can be >1 for multi‑track) |
| **βₜ,ₛ** | minimum dwell time of train *t* at the upstream node of segment *s* (if it stops) |
| **γₛ** | minimum travelling time of a train through *s* when travelling at the maximal speed  v_max ( = Lₛ / v_max ) |
| **T_b^start**, **T_b^end** | start and end of the blockage window on the partially blocked segment *ŝ* |
| **M** | a sufficiently large constant (big‑M) larger than the planning horizon |
| **w_d**, **w_e** | positive weights for delay and energy in the objective |

---

### 2️⃣ Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Interpretation |
|----------|------|----------------|
| **xₜ,ₛ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *t* uses segment *s* (route‑choice variable – may be pre‑fixed) |
| **yₜ,ₛ,𝑑** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *t* occupies segment *s* in direction *d* (used for capacity) |
| **τₜ,ₛ⁰** ≥ 0 | continuous | **Entry time** of train *t* into segment *s* (head reaches upstream node) |
| **τₜ,ₛ¹** ≥ 0 | continuous | **Exit time** of train *t* from segment *s* (tail clears downstream node) |
| **zₜ,ₛ,ₚ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *t* traverses segment *s* with speed‑level *p* |
| **Δₜ** ≥ 0 | continuous | total delay of train *t* measured at its final destination |
| **Eₜ** ≥ 0 | continuous | estimated energy consumption of train *t* (kWh) |
| **cₜ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *t* passes the blocked segment **after** the blockage window (else 0 – before) |
| **θₜ,ₜ′,ₛ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | ordering variable – 1 if *t* goes before *t′* on segment *s* (same direction) |

---

### 3️⃣ Objective Function  

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\min\; w_{d}\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_{t}\;+\;w_{e}\sum_{t\in T}E_{t}}
\]

*Weighted sum of total passenger/operational delay and total energy consumption.*

---

### 4️⃣ Constraints  

#### 4.1 Speed‑level selection (one level per used segment)  
\[
\sum_{p\in P}z_{t,s,p}=x_{t,s}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S\tag{1}
\]

#### 4.2 Travel‑time from entry to exit (linear because *vₚ* are constants)  
\[
\tau_{t,s}^{1}-\tau_{t,s}^{0}= \sum_{p\in P}\frac{L_{s}}{v_{p}}\,z_{t,s,p}\qquad\forall t,s\tag{2}
\]

#### 4.3 Successive‑segment continuity (dwell + travel)  
For every ordered pair of consecutive segments *(s,s′)* on train *t*’s route:  

\[
\tau_{t,s'}^{0}\;\ge\;\tau_{t,s}^{1}+ \beta_{t,s'}-M(1-x_{t,s'})\qquad\forall t,\;(s,s')\text{ consecutive}\tag{3}
\]

#### 4.4 Definition of total delay (final‑destination lateness)  
Let *s_last* be the last segment of train *t*:  

\[
\Delta_{t}\;\ge\;\tau_{t,s_{\text{last}}}^{1}-\bigl(\delta_{t}+ \sum_{s\in S}\beta_{t,s}\bigr)\qquad\forall t\in T\tag{4}
\]

#### 4.5 Blockage‑window handling (partial segment *ŝ*)  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{t,\hat{s}}^{0} &\ge T_{b}^{\text{end}}-M\,c_{t}\qquad\forall t\text{ with }x_{t,\hat{s}}=1\\
\tau_{t,\hat{s}}^{1} &\le T_{b}^{\text{start}}+M\,(1-c_{t})\qquad\forall t\text{ with }x_{t,\hat{s}}=1
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

If *cₜ*=0 the train must finish crossing **before** the block starts; if *cₜ*=1 it must start **after** the block ends.

#### 4.6 Track‑capacity (at most **Capₛ,₍d₎** trains per direction)  

\[
\sum_{t\in T}y_{t,s,d}\le \text{Cap}_{s,d}\qquad\forall s\in S,\;d\in D\tag{6}
\]

Link occupancy to route use  

\[
y_{t,s,d}\le x_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,s,d\tag{7}
\]

#### 4.7 Ordering on a shared segment (disjunctive) – only needed when **Capₛ,d = 1**  

For every pair of distinct trains *(t,t′)* using the same segment *s* in the same direction *d*:  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{t',s}^{0}&\ge \tau_{t,s}^{1}-M\,(1-\theta_{t,t',s})\\
\tau_{t ,s}^{0}&\ge \tau_{t',s}^{1}-M\,\theta_{t,t',s}\\
\theta_{t,t',s}&\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t\neq t',\;s,d\tag{8}
\]

The binary θ decides which train passes first, guaranteeing non‑overlap.

#### 4.8 Acceleration / deceleration limits between consecutive segments  

Let \(v^{\text{out}}_{t,s}=\sum_{p\in P}v_{p}\,z_{t,s,p}\) be the speed chosen on segment *s*.  
For consecutive segments *(s,s′)* on train *t*:  

\[
v^{\text{out}}_{t,s'}-v^{\text{out}}_{t,s}\le a_{\max}\bigl(\tau_{t,s'}^{0}-\tau_{t,s}^{1}\bigr)\tag{9}
\]
\[
v^{\text{out}}_{t,s}-v^{\text{out}}_{t,s'}\le |a_{\min}|\bigl(\tau_{t,s'}^{0}-\tau_{t,s}^{1}\bigr)\tag{10}
\]

If the idle time between the two segments is zero, the inequalities force the speed to stay unchanged.

#### 4.9 Linear energy‑consumption calculation  

\[
E_{t}= \sum_{s\in S}\;\sum_{p\in P}E_{p}\,L_{s}\;z_{t,s,p}\qquad\forall t\in T\tag{11}
\]

#### 4.10 Binary linking for the blocked segment  

\[
c_{t}\le x_{t,\hat{s}}\qquad\forall t\tag{12}
\]

If a train never traverses the blocked segment, the conflict variable is forced to 0.

---

### 5️⃣ Complete MILP Summary  

**Variables**  
\(x_{t,s},y_{t,s,d},\tau_{t,s}^{0},\tau_{t,s}^{1},z_{t,s,p},\Delta_{t},E_{t},c_{t},\theta_{t,t',s}\)

**Objective**  
\[
\min \; w_{d}\sum_{t}\Delta_{t}+w_{e}\sum_{t}E_{t}
\]

**Subject to**  
Constraints (1)–(12) listed above, all variables respecting their domains (binary or non‑negative continuous).  

The model is **purely linear** (except for binary decisions) and therefore a **mixed‑integer linear program (MILP)** solvable by any commercial or open‑source MILP solver.

---

### 6️⃣ How to use the model  

1. **Data preparation** – define the set of trains, their original timetables (δₜ, τ̂ₜ), the network topology (which segments each train traverses), segment lengths Lₛ, the blockage interval \([T_{b}^{start},T_{b}^{end}]\) on the affected segment *ŝ*, and the speed‑level set *P* together with (vₚ , Eₚ).  
2. **Parameter choice** – set big‑M larger than the planning horizon, choose realistic acceleration limits a_max / a_min, and pick the weights w_d and w_e according to the operator’s preference between punctuality and energy efficiency.  
3. **Implementation** – write the formulation in a MILP modelling language (AMPL, GAMS, Pyomo, JuMP, OPL …) and hand it to a solver such as CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP, CBC, or HiGHS.  
4. **Solution interpretation** –  
   * \(x_{t,s}=1\) tells the realised route (including possible rerouting around the blocked segment).  
   * \(\tau_{t,s}^{0},\tau_{t,s}^{1}\) give the conflict‑free timetable.  
   * \(z_{t,s,p}=1\) yields the speed‑level on each segment, which can be converted to a concrete speed profile for the train‑control system.  
   * \(\Delta_{t}\) reports the realised delay, \(E_{t}\) the estimated energy use.  

The model can be extended (platform capacity, crew constraints, multi‑objective Pareto front, stochastic disruption occurrence) by adding the corresponding linear constraints and variables while preserving the MILP structure.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) Model for Conflict‑Detection‑and‑Resolution (CDR) under Distance‑to‑Go (DTG) Signalling**  
*(enhanced version of the RECIFE‑MILP model)*  

---

## 1. Sets, Indices and Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|----------|
| **T** | Set of trains, indexed by *t* |
| **S** | Set of track sections (blocks or TTD‑sections), indexed by *s* |
| **N(s)** | Set of predecessor sections of *s* (the section that a train must leave before entering *s*) |
| **F(s)** | Set of successor sections of *s* (the section that a train enters after leaving *s*) |
| **C(s)** | Capacity of section *s* (normally 1 train, but can be >1 for multiple‑track sections) |
| **L<sub>s</sub>** | Physical length of section *s* (km) |
| **v<sub>max,t</sub>** | Maximum admissible speed of train *t* (km/h) |
| **a<sub>t</sub>**, **b<sub>t</sub>** | Positive (acceleration) and negative (braking) longitudinal rates of train *t* (km/h²) – *assumed constant* |
| **τ<sub>dw,t</sub>** | Minimum dwell time of train *t* at a station (min) – *assumed known* |
| **Δ<sub>t</sub>** | Initial delay of train *t* at its first event (min) – taken from real‑time information |
| **β** | Safety factor for the braking distance (≥1) – *assumption* |
| **M** | A big‑M constant (larger than the planning horizon, e.g. 10 000 min) |
| **H** | Planning horizon (min) – *assumption* |

### 1.1 Speed‑dependent separation distance  

For DTG signalling the minimum distance that must be kept between two consecutive trains *i* (leader) and *j* (follower) when the follower is travelling at speed *v* is the **braking distance** plus a safety margin:

\[
\text{sep}_{ij}(v) \;=\; \beta\;\frac{v^{2}}{2\,|b_{j}|}\qquad(\text{km})
\]

Because the MILP must be linear, we discretise the speed range of each train *j* into a small set **V<sub>j</sub>** (e.g. 0, 30, 60, 90 km/h). For each speed level *k∈V<sub>j</sub>* we pre‑compute  

\[
\text{SEP}_{jk}= \beta\;\frac{k^{2}}{2\,|b_{j}|}
\]

and introduce binary variables to select the speed level that is actually used on a section (see Section 2).

---

## 2. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| **x<sub>t,s</sub>** | binary | 1 if train *t* occupies section *s* (i.e. its front passes the entry of *s*) |
| **y<sub>t,s</sub>** | binary | 1 if train *t* leaves section *s* (i.e. its rear passes the exit of *s*) |
| **p<sub>t,s</sub>** | continuous ≥0 | Planned **arrival time** of the front of train *t* at the entry of section *s* (min) |
| **q<sub>t,s</sub>** | continuous ≥0 | Planned **departure time** of the rear of train *t* from the exit of section *s* (min) |
| **v<sub>t,s</sub>** | binary (|V<sub>t</sub>|) | Speed‑level selection: 1 if train *t* travels through *s* with speed level *k∈V<sub>t</sub>* |
| **d<sub>t</sub>** | continuous ≥0 | **Total delay** of train *t* at its final destination (min) |
| **z<sub>i,j,s</sub>** | binary | 1 if train *i* is the **preceding** train of *j* on section *s* (i.e. *i* clears the section before *j* enters) |
| **r<sub>t,s</sub>** | binary | 1 if a **re‑routing** (alternative path) is applied to train *t* on section *s* – optional extension (set to 0 in the base model) |

---

## 3. Objective Function  

The primary operational goal is to **minimise total accumulated delay** of all trains (other objectives such as minimising the number of re‑routings can be added as weighted terms).

\[
\boxed{\min \; \sum_{t\in T} d_{t}}
\]

---

## 4. Model Constraints  

### 4.1. Initial conditions  

\[
p_{t,s_{0}} = \Delta_{t} \qquad \forall t\in T
\]

where *s₀* is the first section (origin) of train *t*.

### 4.2. Flow conservation on the route  

For every train *t* and every interior section *s* (i.e. *s* ∈ route<sub>t</sub> \ {first, last}):

\[
p_{t,s}= q_{t,N(s)} \qquad
\text{(arrival at *s* equals departure from its predecessor)}
\]

If the route contains switches, the predecessor set *N(s)* may contain more than one element; the constraint is applied for the unique predecessor that belongs to train *t*’s path.

### 4.3. Travel time on a section (speed‑dependent)  

Let **Δt<sub>t,k,s</sub>** be the deterministic travel time of train *t* through section *s* when travelling at speed level *k*:

\[
\Delta t_{t,k,s}= \frac{L_{s}}{k}\times 60 \qquad (\text{minutes})
\]

(If *k = 0* the train is stopped; dwell time is added separately.)

For each *t, s* we enforce exactly one speed level:

\[
\sum_{k\in V_{t}} v_{t,s}^{k}=x_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,s
\]

and link the departure time to the selected speed:

\[
q_{t,s} \ge p_{t,s}+ \sum_{k\in V_{t}} \Delta t_{t,k,s}\; v_{t,s}^{k} + \tau_{dw,t}\;x_{t,s}^{\text{stop}}
\]

where **x<sub>t,s</sub><sup>stop</sup>** is a binary variable equal to 1 if *k = 0* (train stops in *s*). For simplicity we embed the dwell time into the travel‑time term for the speed level 0.

### 4.4. Section capacity (one train at a time)  

For every section *s* and every time instant we must guarantee that at most **C(s)** trains are present. Using the “big‑M” formulation with binary ordering variables *z*:

\[
p_{j,s} \ge q_{i,s} - M\,(1-z_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; s\in S
\]

\[
z_{i,j,s}+z_{j,i,s}=1 \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; s\in S
\]

If **C(s) > 1** (multiple tracks) the above can be relaxed to allow up to **C(s)** concurrent trains, e.g. by using a cumulative‑capacity variable, but the base model assumes **C(s)=1**.

### 4.5. DTG‑specific speed‑dependent separation  

When two trains travel on the same section *s* consecutively (i.e. *i* precedes *j*), the **front of the follower** may not enter the section earlier than the **rear of the leader** plus the required separation distance computed at the follower’s speed.

Let *k* be the speed level selected for the follower *j* on *s* (binary variable *v<sub>j,s</sub><sup>k</sup>*). The separation distance expressed as a time offset is:

\[
\theta_{jk}= \frac{\text{SEP}_{jk}}{v_{j}^{k}}\times 60 \qquad (\text{minutes})
\]

(If *v<sub>j</sub><sup>k</sup>=0* we set a large penalty; in practice a follower cannot enter a section while stopped behind a leader.)

The constraint is:

\[
p_{j,s} \ge q_{i,s} + \theta_{jk} - M\,(1-z_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; s\in S,\; k\in V_{j}
\]

Because *θ* depends on the selected speed level, we linearise by linking it with the binary speed‑selection variable:

\[
p_{j,s} \ge q_{i,s} + \sum_{k\in V_{j}} \theta_{jk}\; v_{j,s}^{k} - M\,(1-z_{i,j,s})
\]

Thus the required time headway automatically grows when the follower travels faster.

### 4.6. End‑of‑Authority (EoA) constraint  

The **movement authority** of a train ends at the exit of the last free TTD‑section (or block). Therefore a train may not be granted a new authority before it has cleared the current one:

\[
p_{t,s'} \ge q_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,\; s\in S,\; s' \in \text{Successors}(s) \text{ that belong to the same MA}
\]

In practice this is already enforced by the flow constraints; the formulation above makes the rule explicit for sections that belong to different MA‑chunks (e.g. stations vs. open line).

### 4.7. Total delay definition  

Let *t<sub>dest</sub>* be the last section of train *t* (its scheduled arrival time is *T<sub>t,plan</sub>*). The actual arrival time is *p<sub>t,t<sub>dest</sub></sub>*. Delay is:

\[
d_{t}= p_{t,t_{\text{dest}}} - T_{t,\text{plan}} \qquad \forall t\in T
\]

Optionally, we can enforce non‑negativity:

\[
d_{t}\ge 0 \qquad \forall t\in T
\]

### 4.8. Binary ordering consistency  

For each ordered pair *(i,j)* on a section *s* we need exactly one ordering:

\[
z_{i,j,s}+z_{j,i,s}=1 \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; s\in S
\]

If a train does **not** occupy a section, the corresponding *z* variables are forced to 0:

\[
z_{i,j,s}\le x_{i,s},\qquad 
z_{i,j,s}\le x_{j,s} \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; s\in S
\]

### 4.9. Optional re‑routing (binary switch)  

If a train may be rerouted around a switch, we introduce a binary variable *r<sub>t,s</sub>* that activates an alternative successor set *F′(s)*. The flow constraints are then written with a big‑M term that activates the appropriate successor set. For the base model we set *r<sub>t,s</sub>=0* for all *t,s*.

---

## 5. Assumptions (explicitly stated)

| # | Assumption |
|---|------------|
| A1 | Acceleration and braking rates (*a<sub>t</sub>*, *b<sub>t</sub>*) are constant for each train and known a‑priori. |
| A2 | Speed profile on a section is piece‑wise constant; the train travels at one of a small set of discrete speed levels **V<sub>t</sub>** (e.g., 0, 30, 60, 90 km/h). |
| A3 | The safety factor **β** (≥1) accounts for measurement errors, reaction time, and signalling latency. |
| A4 | Section capacity **C(s)=1** (single‑track block) unless otherwise stated; the model can be extended to *C(s)>1* by a cumulative capacity variable. |
| A5 | Dwell time at stations is a known lower bound **τ<sub>dw,t</sub>**; additional dwell can be introduced by delaying *p* variables. |
| A6 | The planning horizon **H** is large enough to contain all possible rescheduled times; the big‑M constant **M** is set > H. |
| A7 | All trains follow the same route topology (pre‑computed list of sections). Switching decisions are fixed; re‑routing is optional and represented by binary variables *r*. |
| A8 | No overtaking is allowed on a single track (enforced by the ordering variables *z*). |
| A9 | The end‑of‑authority (EoA) is always located at the exit of the last occupied TTD‑section; the model does not consider moving‑block extensions. |
| A10 | All times are measured in **minutes**, lengths in **kilometres**, speeds in **km/h**. |

---

## 6. Complete MILP Formulation  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{t\in T} d_{t} \\
\text{s.t. } 
& p_{t,s_{0}} = \Delta_{t} && \forall t\in T \tag{1}\\
& p_{t,s}= q_{t,N(s)} && \forall t\in T,\; s\in \text{interior sections of }t \tag{2}\\
& \sum_{k\in V_{t}} v_{t,s}^{k}=x_{t,s} && \forall t\in T,\; s\in S \tag{3}\\
& q_{t,s} \ge p_{t,s}+ \sum_{k\in V_{t}} \Delta t_{t,k,s}\; v_{t,s}^{k} && \forall t,s \tag{4}\\
& p_{j,s} \ge q_{i,s}+ \sum_{k\in V_{j}} \theta_{jk}\; v_{j,s}^{k} - M(1-z_{i,j,s}) && \forall i\neq j,\; s\in S \tag{5}\\
& p_{j,s} \ge q_{i,s} - M(1-z_{i,j,s}) && \forall i\neq j,\; s\in S \tag{6}\\
& z_{i,j,s}+z_{j,i,s}=1 && \forall i\neq j,\; s\in S \tag{7}\\
& z_{i,j,s}\le x_{i,s},\; z_{i,j,s}\le x_{j,s} && \forall i\neq j,\; s\in S \tag{8}\\
& d_{t}= p_{t,t_{\text{dest}}} - T_{t,\text{plan}} && \forall t\in T \tag{9}\\
& d_{t}\ge 0 && \forall t\in T \tag{10}\\
& x_{t,s},y_{t,s},z_{i,j,s},r_{t,s}\in\{0,1\} && \forall t,i,j,s \tag{11}\\
& p_{t,s},q_{t,s},d_{t}\ge 0 && \forall t,s \tag{12}
\end{aligned}
\]

Constraints (5)‑(6) together enforce **DTG‑specific speed‑dependent headways** while guaranteeing that at most one train occupies a section at a time. Constraint (7) selects the ordering of any two trains on the same section; (8) deactivates ordering variables when a train does not use the section.  

The model can be solved with any commercial MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress) to obtain a **conflict‑free, delay‑minimised timetable** that respects the distance‑to‑go signalling rules.  

---  

**Remark** – The formulation above is deliberately compact yet complete. Additional practical features (e.g., variable dwell times, train‑specific minimum turnaround times, crew‑linking constraints, or moving‑block extensions) can be incorporated by adding the corresponding variables and linear constraints while preserving the overall MILP structure.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the integrated Train‑Rescheduling & Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial track blockages**

---

### 1️⃣ Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|----------|
| **T** = { i | train *i* } | Set of trains, |T| = N |
| **S** = { s | track segment *s* } | Elementary track segments (including the link between two consecutive stations) |
| **Kᵢ** ⊆ K | Admissible **routes** *k* for train *i* (a route = ordered list of segments) |
| **Rᵢᵏ** ⊆ S | Segments belonging to route *k* of train *i* |
| **L** = { t | speed‑level *t* } | Discrete speed levels (e.g. slow, normal, fast) |
| **Sta(i)** | Ordered list of stations visited by train *i* |
| **Bₛ** = \([B_{s}^{\text{start}},B_{s}^{\text{end}}]\) | Blocking interval on segment *s* (if never blocked set to \([-\infty,+\infty]\)) |
| **S₍ᵢⱼ₎** ⊆ S | Set of **shared** segments that both trains *i* and *j* could occupy (i.e. appear in at least one feasible route of each) |

---

### 2️⃣ Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|--------|----------|------|
| \(a_i^{0}\) | Scheduled arrival of train *i* at its final destination | min |
| \(\tau_{s,t}\) | Travel time of any train on segment *s* when speed level *t* is chosen | min |
| \(\varepsilon_{s,t}\) | Energy consumption on segment *s* with speed level *t* | kWh |
| \(g\) | Required safety‑gap between two successive trains on the same segment | min |
| \(d^{\text{min}}_{\sigma}\) | Minimum dwell time at station \(\sigma\) | min |
| \(M\) | Large constant (big‑M) larger than any feasible time | min |
| \(w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}\) | Non‑negative weights for the two objectives | – |
| \(N_{i}^{\text{final}}\) | Index of the last segment of the chosen route of train *i* | – |

All data are assumed known before optimisation (timetable, speed‑time‑energy tables, blockage windows, etc.).

---

### 3️⃣ Decision variables  

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|--------|------|--------------|
| \(r_{i}^{k}\) | binary | =1 if train *i* uses route *k* |
| \(o_{ij}\) | binary | =1 if train *i* precedes train *j* on every shared segment (right‑of‑way) |
| \(a_{i,s}\) | ≥0 continuous | Arrival time of train *i* at the upstream node of segment *s* |
| \(d_{i,s}\) | ≥0 continuous | Departure time of train *i* at the downstream node of segment *s* |
| \(v_{i,s,t}\) | binary | =1 if train *i* traverses segment *s* with speed level *t* |
| \(\beta_{i,s}\) | binary | =1 if train *i* passes segment *s* **before** the blockage, 0 if **after** |
| \(e_i\) | ≥0 continuous | Total energy used by train *i* |
| \(\alpha_{i,\sigma}\) | ≥0 continuous | Arrival time of train *i* at station \(\sigma\) (derived from \(a_{i,s}\)) |
| \(\delta_{i,\sigma}\) | ≥0 continuous | Departure time of train *i* from station \(\sigma\) (derived from \(d_{i,s}\)) |

---

### 4️⃣ Model  

#### Objective (weighted sum of total delay and total energy)

\[
\min\;
w_{\text{delay}}\;\sum_{i\in T}\bigl(a_{i,N_i^{\text{final}}}-a_i^{0}\bigr)
\;+\;
w_{\text{energy}}\;\sum_{i\in T} e_i
\tag{OBJ}
\]

---

#### 4.1 Route‑choice  

1. **Exactly one route per train**  

\[
\sum_{k\in K_i} r_{i}^{k}=1 \qquad\forall i\in T
\tag{R1}
\]

2. **Activate only segments belonging to the chosen route**  

\[
\sum_{t\in L} v_{i,s,t}\;\le\;\sum_{k:\;s\in R_i^k} r_i^{k}\qquad\forall i\in T,\; s\in S
\tag{R2}
\]

---

#### 4.2 Speed‑level selection  

3. **Exactly one speed level on every *active* segment**  

\[
\sum_{t\in L} v_{i,s,t}= \sum_{k:\;s\in R_i^k} r_i^{k}\qquad\forall i\in T,\; s\in S
\tag{S1}
\]

4. **Binary nature**  

\[
v_{i,s,t}\in\{0,1\}\qquad\forall i,s,t
\tag{S2}
\]

---

#### 4.3 Travel time on a segment  

5. **Deterministic travel time from selected speed**  

\[
d_{i,s}=a_{i,s}+\sum_{t\in L} v_{i,s,t}\,\tau_{s,t}\qquad\forall i,s
\tag{TT}
\]

Since the sum contains at most one non‑zero term, the expression equals the travel time of the chosen speed level.

---

#### 4.4 Energy consumption  

6. **Energy of train *i***  

\[
e_i=\sum_{s\in S}\;\sum_{t\in L} v_{i,s,t}\,\varepsilon_{s,t}\qquad\forall i\in T
\tag{EN}
\]

---

#### 4.5 Station dwell  

For every station \(\sigma\in{\rm Sta}(i)\) let \(s_{\text{in}}(\sigma)\) be the segment just before the station and \(s_{\text{out}}(\sigma)\) the segment just after it.

\[
\alpha_{i,\sigma}=a_{i,s_{\text{in}}(\sigma)},\qquad
\delta_{i,\sigma}=d_{i,s_{\text{out}}(\sigma)}
\tag{STA}
\]

7. **Minimum dwell time**  

\[
\delta_{i,\sigma}\ge \alpha_{i,\sigma}+d^{\text{min}}_{\sigma}
\qquad\forall i,\;\sigma\in{\rm Sta}(i)
\tag{DW}
\]

8. **Continuity across the station node**  

\[
a_{i,s_{\text{out}}(\sigma)}=\delta_{i,\sigma}
\qquad\forall i,\;\sigma\in{\rm Sta}(i)
\tag{CONT}
\]

---

#### 4.6 Safety / headway on shared segments  

For each unordered pair \((i,j)\) with \(i<j\) and each shared segment \(s\in S_{ij}\):

9. **Ordering constraints (big‑M linearisation)**  

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{j,s}&\ge d_{i,s}+g - M\,(1-o_{ij}) &&\forall s\in S_{ij}\\
a_{i,s}&\ge d_{j,s}+g - M\,o_{ij} &&\forall s\in S_{ij}
\end{aligned}
\tag{ORD}
\]

When \(o_{ij}=1\) the first inequality forces train *j* to begin after train *i* has cleared the segment plus the safety gap; when \(o_{ij}=0\) the second inequality does the opposite. The same binary \(o_{ij}\) is used for **all** shared segments of the pair, guaranteeing a coherent precedence.

---

#### 4.7 Blocked segment constraints  

For every segment *s* that is blocked during \([B_{s}^{\text{start}},B_{s}^{\text{end}}]\):

10. **Pass before or after the blockage**  

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{i,s}&\ge B_{s}^{\text{end}} - M\,(1-\beta_{i,s})\\
d_{i,s}&\le B_{s}^{\text{start}} + M\,\beta_{i,s}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall i,s
\tag{BLK}
\]

If \(\beta_{i,s}=1\) the train must finish the segment **before** the blockage ends; if \(\beta_{i,s}=0\) it must start **after** the blockage starts. For a segment that is never blocked, set \(B_{s}^{\text{start}}=-M,\;B_{s}^{\text{end}}=M\) so the constraints are always satisfied.

---

#### 4.8 Domain constraints  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&r_{i}^{k}\in\{0,1\} &&\forall i,k\\
&o_{ij}\in\{0,1\} &&\forall i<j\\
&\beta_{i,s}\in\{0,1\} &&\forall i,s\\
&a_{i,s},\,d_{i,s},\,\alpha_{i,\sigma},\,\delta_{i,\sigma},\,e_i \ge 0 &&\forall\text{continuous variables}
\end{aligned}
\tag{DOM}
\]

---

### 5️⃣ Summary and Remarks  

| Block | Purpose |
|-------|----------|
| **(R1)–(R2)** | Guarantees each train selects exactly one feasible physical route; inactive segments are forced to zero speed‑level variables. |
| **(S1)–(S2)** | Enforces a single speed level on every traversed segment (binary). |
| **(TT)** | Links arrival and departure times through the deterministic travel time of the chosen speed level. |
| **(EN)** | Calculates train‑wise energy consumption as the sum of segment‑level energy of the selected speed levels. |
| **(DW)–(CONT)** | Enforces minimum dwell times at stations and continuity of the timetable across station nodes. |
| **(ORD)** | Implements safety headway on every segment shared by two trains; a single binary per pair guarantees a consistent precedence on all such segments. |
| **(BLK)** | Avoids occupying a blocked segment during its blockage window; the binary \(\beta_{i,s}\) decides whether the train passes before or after the blockage. |
| **(OBJ)** | Minimises a weighted sum of total passenger delay (difference between realised final arrival and scheduled arrival) and total energy use. |
| **(DOM)** | Variable type definitions. |

All constraints are linear (or linearised with the big‑M technique); the model is therefore a **mixed‑integer linear program**. It can be fed directly to commercial MILP solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, …). Additional practical aspects (crew‑assignment, platform capacity, stochastic delay, variable train lengths, etc.) can be incorporated by introducing further linear constraints or binary variables while preserving the MILP structure.
