Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) – Full Linear Formulation**  

The model below captures, in a single mixed‑integer linear program, the three‑fold decision problem that arises when a partial‑segment blockage disrupts a high‑speed railway line:

1. **When** each train departs / arrives at every station (time‑shift decisions).  
2. **Which** track (original or opposite) each train uses on the blocked segment (rerouting decision).  
3. **What** piece‑wise constant speed (or acceleration) is applied on every free‑running sub‑segment so that the chosen travel times are physically feasible and the energy consumption is minimised.

The formulation is deliberately generic; all data that are not supplied in the description are introduced as **assumed parameters** (marked *Assumption*).  

---

## 1. Sets, Indices and Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning | Remarks |
|--------|---------|---------|
| **T** = {1,…,|T|} | Set of trains to be scheduled | – |
| **S** = {0,…,|S|} | Ordered set of stations (including fictitious origin 0 and destination |S|) | – |
| **E** ⊆ S×S | Set of directed track‑segments (i → j) that a train may traverse | Each (i,j) is a physical line section |
| **B** ⊆ E | Sub‑set of *blocked* segments (the disruption area) | Only one direction is blocked; the opposite direction is still usable |
| **U** = E \ B | Set of *unblocked* segments | – |
| **K** = {1,…,Kmax} | Set of discrete speed‑profile “plans” that can be assigned to a train on a segment | Each plan k corresponds to a constant speed \(v_{k}^{ij}\) and a known energy consumption \(e_{k}^{ij}\) (see Assumption 1) |
| **Δt** | Length of the planning horizon discretisation (e.g., 1 min) | Used for time‑window constraints |
| **M** | A sufficiently large constant (big‑M) | – |

### Train‑specific parameters  

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| \(a_i\) | Original scheduled **arrival** time at station i (given) |
| \(d_i\) | Original scheduled **departure** time from station i (given) |
| \(L_{ij}\) | Length of segment (i,j) (km) |
| \(v^{\max}_{ij}\) | Maximum admissible speed on segment (i,j) (km/h) |
| \(v^{\min}_{ij}\) | Minimum admissible speed on segment (i,j) (km/h) |
| \(\alpha_{ij}\) | Acceleration limit on segment (i,j) (km/h²) |
| \(\beta_{ij}\) | Deceleration limit on segment (i,j) (km/h²) |
| \(c^{\text{delay}}_t\) | Penalty cost per minute of delay for train t (monetary) |
| \(c^{\text{energy}}_{ij,k}\) | Energy consumption (kWh) of plan k on segment (i,j) (Assumption 1) |
| \(c^{\text{reroute}}_t\) | Fixed penalty for using the opposite track on the blocked segment (if allowed) |
| \(T^{\text{max}}_t\) | Latest admissible arrival time at final destination for train t (service‑level agreement) |
| \(T^{\text{min}}_t\) | Earliest admissible departure time from origin for train t (operational window) |

### Disruption‑related parameters  

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| \([t^{\text{start}}_b,\,t^{\text{end}}_b]\) | Time window during which the blocked segment **B** is unavailable for its normal direction (minutes from horizon start) |
| \(\gamma\) | Binary indicator of whether the opposite track can be used (1 = allowed, 0 = not allowed) – assumed 1 for this model |

---

## 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| \(A_{t,i}\) | Continuous ≥0 | **Actual arrival** time of train t at station i |
| \(D_{t,i}\) | Continuous ≥0 | **Actual departure** time of train t from station i |
| \(x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij}\) | Binary | 1 if train t traverses segment (i,j) in its **original** direction (i→j) |
| \(x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij}\) | Binary | 1 if train t traverses segment (i,j) in the **opposite** direction (j→i) – only possible for blocked segments when \(\gamma=1\) |
| \(y_{t,ij,k}\) | Binary | 1 if train t uses speed‑plan k on segment (i,j) (or on the opposite direction when rev‑variable =1) |
| \(z_{t}\) | Continuous ≥0 | Total **delay** of train t (minutes) w.r.t. original schedule at final destination |
| \(w_{t}\) | Binary | 1 if train t is **canceled** (optional, see Assumption 2) |
| \(s_{t,ij}\) | Continuous ≥0 | **Travel time** of train t on segment (i,j) (derived from chosen speed plan) |

---

## 3. Assumptions (explicitly stated)  

1. **Piece‑wise constant speed plans** – For each segment (i,j) a small catalogue of admissible constant speeds \(\{v^{ij}_k\}_{k=1}^{K}\) is pre‑computed. The corresponding travel time is \(s_{t,ij}=L_{ij}/v^{ij}_k\) and the energy consumption \(c^{\text{energy}}_{ij,k}\) is known. This linearises the otherwise nonlinear speed‑energy relationship.  
2. **Optional train cancellation** – If a train cannot be feasibly recovered, it may be cancelled at a high penalty \(c^{\text{cancel}}_t\). The binary \(w_t\) forces all other variables of that train to zero (see constraints).  
3. **Single‑track opposite usage** – The opposite track can be used only on the blocked segment(s) and only one train at a time (capacity = 1).  
4. **Deterministic disruption window** – The start and end times of the blockage are known a‑priori.  
5. **Dwell time limits** – Minimum dwell time at every station \( \tau^{\min}_i\) (e.g., 2 min) is assumed; maximum dwell time is not binding.  

---

## 4. Objective Function  

The model simultaneously minimises **total delay**, **energy consumption**, and **rerouting/cancellation penalties**:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} c^{\text{delay}}_t \, z_t}_{\text{Delay cost}} 
      + \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in E}\sum_{k=1}^{K} c^{\text{energy}}_{ij,k}\, y_{t,ij,k}}_{\text{Energy cost}} \\
      & + \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} c^{\text{reroute}}_t \sum_{(i,j)\in B}\bigl(x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij}\bigr)}_{\text{Rerouting penalty}} 
      + \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} c^{\text{cancel}}_t \, w_t}_{\text{Cancellation penalty}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

*All coefficients are assumed non‑negative.*

---

## 5. Constraints  

### 5.1. Basic timetable feasibility  

1. **Departure after arrival (minimum dwell time)**  

\[
D_{t,i} \; \ge \; A_{t,i} + \tau^{\min}_i \;-\; M\, w_t \qquad \forall t\in T,\; i\in S .
\tag{C1}
\]

2. **Travel time linking arrival/departure**  

\[
A_{t,j} \; \ge \; D_{t,i} + s_{t,ij} \;-\; M\,(1-x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij}) \qquad \forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in E .
\tag{C2}
\]

If the train uses the opposite direction on a blocked segment, the same relation holds with the rev‑variable:

\[
A_{t,i} \; \ge \; D_{t,j} + s_{t,ij} \;-\; M\,(1-x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij}) \qquad \forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in B .
\tag{C3}
\]

3. **Selection of exactly one speed plan per traversed segment**  

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{K} y_{t,ij,k} = x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij} + x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij} \qquad \forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in E .
\tag{C4}
\]

4. **Travel time definition from speed plan**  

\[
s_{t,ij} = \sum_{k=1}^{K} \frac{L_{ij}}{v^{ij}_k}\; y_{t,ij,k} \qquad \forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in E .
\tag{C5}
\]

Because \(v^{ij}_k\) are constants, (C5) is linear.

### 5.2. Routing and blockage constraints  

5. **Original direction must be respected outside the blocked area**  

\[
x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij}=0 \qquad \forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in E\setminus B .
\tag{C6}
\]

6. **Capacity of the opposite track on the blocked segment** – at any instant only one train may occupy it. Using a time‑indexed big‑M formulation (discretised by Δt):

\[
\sum_{t\in T} \sum_{k=1}^{K} y_{t,ij,k}\; \mathbf{1}\bigl\{ \tau \in [A_{t,i},A_{t,i}+s_{t,ij}] \bigr\}
\le 1 \qquad \forall (i,j)\in B,\;\forall \tau\in\{0,\Delta t,\dots, H\}.
\tag{C7}
\]

(Here \(H\) is the planning horizon; the indicator can be linearised by standard time‑window big‑M constraints.)

7. **Blocked‑segment availability window** – a train may not use the normal direction during the disruption:

\[
A_{t,i} \ge t^{\text{end}}_b \; \text{or}\; D_{t,i} \le t^{\text{start}}_b 
\quad \text{if } x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij}=1,\;(i,j)\in B .
\tag{C8}
\]

A linear big‑M version:

\[
A_{t,i} \ge t^{\text{end}}_b - M(1-x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij}) ,\qquad
D_{t,i} \le t^{\text{start}}_b + M(1-x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij}) .
\tag{C8'}
\]

### 5.3. Train‑order (conflict‑free) constraints  

For any pair of trains that share a **common track segment** (including opposite‑track usage) we must enforce a **headway** \(h_{ij}\) (minutes) to avoid collisions.

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{t',j} \; \ge \; D_{t,i} + h_{ij} \quad \text{or} \quad
A_{t,j} \; \ge \; D_{t',i} + h_{ij} .
\end{aligned}
\]

Using binary ordering variable \(\theta_{tt',ij}\in\{0,1\}\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{t',j} &\ge D_{t,i} + h_{ij} - M\,(1-\theta_{tt',ij}) ,\\
A_{t,j}  &\ge D_{t',i} + h_{ij} - M\,\theta_{tt',ij} ,\\
\theta_{tt',ij} &\in \{0,1\},
\end{aligned}
\qquad \forall t<t',\;(i,j)\in E .
\tag{C9}
\]

Only pairs that actually traverse the same direction (or opposite direction on the blocked segment) need the constraint; otherwise the corresponding \(\theta\) can be fixed to 0.

### 5.4. Delay definition  

\[
z_t \; \ge \; A_{t,|S|} - a_{|S|} \qquad \forall t\in T .
\tag{C10}
\]

If a train is cancelled, its delay is set to zero:

\[
z_t \le M (1-w_t) \qquad \forall t\in T .
\tag{C11}
\]

### 5.5. Time‑window (service‑level) constraints  

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{t,|S|} &\le T^{\text{max}}_t + M w_t ,\\
D_{t,0}   &\ge T^{\text{min}}_t - M w_t .
\end{aligned}
\tag{C12}
\]

### 5.6. Logical coupling of routing and speed‑plan variables  

If a train does **not** traverse a segment, no speed plan may be selected:

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{K} y_{t,ij,k} \le x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij}+x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij} \qquad \forall t, (i,j).
\tag{C13}
\]

Conversely, if a train is cancelled, all routing variables are forced to zero:

\[
x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij} \le 1-w_t,\qquad
x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij} \le 1-w_t \qquad \forall t,(i,j).
\tag{C14}
\]

### 5.7. Flow conservation (ensuring each train follows a feasible path)  

Let \(o_t\) be the origin station of train t and \(d_t\) its destination (normally 0 and |S|). For every intermediate station i:

\[
\sum_{j:(i,j)\in E} \bigl(x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij}+x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ji}\bigr)
=
\sum_{j:(j,i)\in E} \bigl(x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ji}+x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij}\bigr)
\qquad \forall t,\; i\in S\setminus\{o_t,d_t\}.
\tag{C15}
\]

At the origin and destination:

\[
\sum_{j:(o_t,j)\in E} x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,o_t j}=1-w_t,\qquad
\sum_{j:(j,d_t)\in E} x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,j d_t}=1-w_t .
\tag{C16}
\]

If the opposite track is used on the blocked segment, the flow equations still hold because the rev‑variables are counted as inbound/outbound appropriately.

---

## 6. Complete MILP Statement  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \sum_{t} c^{\text{delay}}_t z_t
      + \sum_{t}\sum_{(i,j)}\sum_{k} c^{\text{energy}}_{ij,k} y_{t,ij,k}
      + \sum_{t} c^{\text{reroute}}_t \sum_{(i,j)\in B} x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij}
      + \sum_{t} c^{\text{cancel}}_t w_t \\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(C1)–(C16)} \\
& A_{t,i}, D_{t,i}, s_{t,ij}, z_t \ge 0 \\
& x^{\text{fwd}}_{t,ij}, x^{\text{rev}}_{t,ij}, y_{t,ij,k}, w_t, \theta_{tt',ij}\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only non‑linearities that could appear (e.g., product of binary and continuous) have been eliminated by standard big‑M linearisation.  

---

## 7. Remarks on Model Use  

* **Scalability** – The number of binary variables grows with \(|T|\times|E|\times K\) and with the pairwise ordering variables \(\theta_{tt',ij}\). In practice, a **decomposition** (as described in the source paper) can be applied: first solve a master IP that decides the routing/reordering (variables \(x^{\text{fwd}},x^{\text{rev}},\theta\)), then generate for each train a set of feasible speed‑plans (variables \(y\)) and solve a selection sub‑problem.  
* **Energy‑aware speed catalogue** – The catalogue \(\{v^{ij}_k\}\) can be built by solving a small convex optimal‑control problem for each segment (minimising energy under acceleration limits) and then discretising the resulting optimal speed into a few representative levels.  
* **Extension to stochastic disruptions** – The deterministic horizon \([t^{\text{start}}_b,t^{\text{end}}_b]\) can be replaced by a set of scenarios with associated probabilities; the objective would then include expected delay/energy.  
* **Robustness** – Minimum dwell times \(\tau^{\min}_i\) and headways \(h_{ij}\) guarantee that the timetable remains feasible under small perturbations (e.g., slight additional delays).  

The formulation above provides a **complete, linear, mixed‑integer representation** of the integrated train‑rescheduling and speed‑management problem under a partial‑segment blockage, ready to be implemented in any standard MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, …).

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the real‑time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)**  

The model is built in three logical stages – **(i) route selection, (ii) train ordering (re‑ordering), and (iii) rescheduling (departure/arrival time adjustment)** – exactly as described in the paper summary.  
All notation, decision variables, parameters and constraints are listed below.  
Where information is missing in the source text, reasonable assumptions are explicitly stated (marked **[Assumption]**).

---

## 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\) |
| \(N\) | Set of network nodes (stations, junctions), indexed by \(i\) |
| \(E\) | Set of directed track‑segments (edges) \((i,j)\) |
| \(R_t\) | Set of admissible routes for train \(t\) (pre‑computed by a routing‑pre‑processor) |
| \(k\in R_t\) | Route‑alternative index for train \(t\) |
| \(P\subseteq T\times T\) | Set of train pairs that **may** conflict (i.e. share at least one common edge) |
| \(S\subseteq T\times T\) | Sub‑set of \(P\) for which a **FIFO** (first‑in‑first‑out) ordering is allowed (e.g. same direction) |
| \(C\subseteq T\times T\) | Sub‑set of \(P\) for which a **re‑ordering** decision is allowed (e.g. opposite directions on a single‑track line) |

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning | Typical value / unit |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| \(\underline{d}_t\) | Planned (pre‑disruption) departure time of train \(t\) at its origin node | minutes from 0 |
| \(\overline{d}_t\) | Latest admissible departure time (e.g. due to service contracts) | minutes |
| \(\tau_{ij}\) | Travel time on edge \((i,j)\) (free‑flow, no delay) | minutes |
| \(c_{ij}\) | Energy consumption (or CO₂) on edge \((i,j)\) per train‑kilometer – used only in an optional secondary objective | kWh/km |
| \(\beta\) | Weight of the secondary objective (energy) in the combined objective function | dimensionless |
| \(M\) | A large constant (big‑M) larger than any feasible delay (e.g. 10 000 min) | – |
| \(\Delta^{\text{safe}}_{ij}\) | Minimum head‑way (safety margin) required between two successive trains on edge \((i,j)\) | minutes |
| \(L^{\text{overlap}}_{i}\) | Minimum overlap (clear‑behind) time that must be respected at node \(i\) when a train stops there | minutes |
| \(\gamma_t\) | Penalty weight for delay of train \(t\) (e.g. passenger importance) | – |
| \(\theta_{t}\) | Binary flag =1 if train \(t\) is a **freight** train (lower penalty) – used only in a weighted objective | – |

**[Assumption]**: All travel times \(\tau_{ij}\) are deterministic and already incorporate speed limits, gradients, and typical dwell times at stations (except for additional delays caused by conflicts).

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,k}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) uses route alternative \(k\in R_t\); 0 otherwise |
| \(y_{t,i}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Actual departure time of train \(t\) from node \(i\) (the “event” time) |
| \(z_{t,i}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Arrival time of train \(t\) at node \(i\) (computed as \(y_{t,i'}+\tau_{i'i}\) on the chosen route) |
| \(w_{t,t'}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) **waits for** train \(t'\) (i.e. \(t\) is placed behind \(t'\) on a conflicting edge); 0 otherwise |
| \(\delta_{t}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Total (primary) delay of train \(t\) measured at its final destination (or a reference node) |
| \(\epsilon_{t}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | **Secondary** delay (energy‑related) – optional, used only if a multi‑objective is desired |
| \(u_{t,t'}\) | binary | 1 if the ordering of the pair \((t,t')\) is **reversed** compared with FIFO (i.e. a re‑ordering decision) – only for \((t,t')\in C\) |

---

## 4. Model Formulation  

### 4.1 Objective Function  

The primary goal is to **minimise the weighted sum of primary delays**.  
A secondary energy‑consumption term can be added with weight \(\beta\).

\[
\boxed{
\min \; \sum_{t\in T} \gamma_t \, \delta_{t}
\;+\; \beta \sum_{(i,j)\in E}\; c_{ij}\;
      \Bigl(\sum_{t\in T} x_{t,k(t,i,j)}\Bigr)
}
\tag{OBJ}
\]

*Explanation*  

* The first term penalises each train’s delay; \(\gamma_t\) can be larger for passenger trains (\(\gamma_t=1\)) and smaller for freight (\(\gamma_t=\theta_t\)).  
* The second term aggregates the energy consumption of all trains on the selected routes (the index \(k(t,i,j)\) denotes the route‑alternative that contains edge \((i,j)\); if a train does not use the edge the contribution is zero).  

If only the delay‑only problem is required, set \(\beta=0\).

---

### 4.2 Route‑selection constraints  

1. **Exactly one route per train**

\[
\sum_{k\in R_t} x_{t,k}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{R1}
\]

2. **Linking event times to the chosen route**  

For each train \(t\) and each edge \((i,j)\) that belongs to route‑alternative \(k\),

\[
z_{t,j} \;\ge\; y_{t,i} + \tau_{ij} - M\,(1-x_{t,k}) \qquad 
\forall t\in T,\; \forall k\in R_t,\; \forall (i,j)\in k
\tag{R2}
\]

\[
y_{t,j} \;\ge\; z_{t,j} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; \forall j\in N
\tag{R3}
\]

(Equation R2 forces the travel‑time relation only when the route is selected; otherwise the big‑M term deactivates it.)

3. **Origin departure window**

\[
\underline{d}_t \;\le\; y_{t,\,\text{origin}(t)} \;\le\; \overline{d}_t
\qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{R4}
\]

---

### 4.3 Conflict‑avoidance (ordering & re‑ordering)  

For every pair \((t,t')\in P\) that share at least one common edge, we must decide which train passes first.  

4.1 **Binary ordering variable**  

\[
w_{t,t'} + w_{t',t} = 1 \qquad \forall (t,t')\in P
\tag{C1}
\]

(Exactly one of the two trains waits for the other.)

4.2 **Head‑way (safety) constraints on each shared edge**  

Let \(\mathcal{E}_{tt'}\) be the set of edges common to the selected routes of \(t\) and \(t'\).  
For every \((i,j)\in\mathcal{E}_{tt'}\):

\[
y_{t',j} \;\ge\; y_{t,i} + \tau_{ij} + \Delta^{\text{safe}}_{ij} - M\,(1-w_{t,t'})
\qquad \forall (t,t')\in P,\;(i,j)\in\mathcal{E}_{tt'}
\tag{C2}
\]

If \(w_{t,t'}=1\) (train \(t\) goes first) the inequality enforces a minimum head‑way; otherwise the big‑M term relaxes it.

4.3 **Re‑ordering (optional) for opposite‑direction conflicts**  

Only pairs \((t,t')\in C\) may be reordered (i.e. FIFO may be violated). Introduce binary \(u_{t,t'}\) that flips the natural order:

\[
w_{t,t'} = \begin{cases}
1 & \text{if } \text{FIFO holds (train }t\text{ first)}\\
0 & \text{if } u_{t,t'}=1 \text{ (re‑ordering)} 
\end{cases}
\tag{C3}
\]

In practice this is linearised as:

\[
w_{t,t'} \ge 1 - u_{t,t'} \qquad
w_{t',t} \ge u_{t,t'} \qquad
u_{t,t'} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \forall (t,t')\in C
\tag{C3‑lin}
\]

If a pair is **not** allowed to be reordered (\((t,t')\notin C\)), we fix \(u_{t,t'}=0\).

---

### 4.4 Delay‑propagation (optional – for the *global‑optimal* model)  

To capture the effect of a train waiting for another on its **total delay** \(\delta_t\), we propagate waiting times along the route.

Define auxiliary variables:

* \(d^{\text{wait}}_{t,i}\) – cumulative waiting time accumulated up to node \(i\).

Constraints:

\[
d^{\text{wait}}_{t,i} \ge d^{\text{wait}}_{t,i'} + \bigl(y_{t,i} - (y_{t,i'}+\tau_{i'i})\bigr) \qquad
\forall (i',i)\in \text{selected route of }t
\tag{D1}
\]

The final delay of train \(t\) (measured at its destination node \(dest(t)\)) is:

\[
\delta_t = d^{\text{wait}}_{t,\,dest(t)} \qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{D2}
\]

If the model is run **without** delay propagation (sub‑optimal version), constraints (D1)–(D2) are omitted and \(\delta_t\) is simply defined as the difference between the actual arrival time at the destination and the planned arrival time \(\underline{a}_t\):

\[
\delta_t = y_{t,\,dest(t)} - \underline{a}_t \qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{D2‑simple}
\]

---

### 4.5 Overlap (clear‑behind) constraints at stations  

When a train stops at a node \(i\) (e.g. a terminal or a station with a signal), a safety overlap must be kept clear before another train can occupy the same block.

For every pair \((t,t')\in P\) that both stop at node \(i\):

\[
y_{t',i} \;\ge\; y_{t,i} + L^{\text{overlap}}_{i} - M\,(1-w_{t,t'})
\qquad \forall (t,t')\in P,\; i\in N
\tag{O1}
\]

---

## 5. Complete MILP  

Putting everything together, the **full MILP** reads:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \sum_{t\in T}\gamma_t \,\delta_t \;+\; \beta\!\sum_{(i,j)\in E}c_{ij}\!\Bigl(\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in R_t} \mathbf{1}_{(i,j)\in k}\,x_{t,k}\Bigr) \\
\text{s.t. } 
&\text{(R1)–(R4)} &&\text{route selection and timing}\\
&\text{(C1)–(C3‑lin)} &&\text{conflict ordering / re‑ordering}\\
&\text{(C2)} &&\text{head‑way safety on shared edges}\\
&\text{(O1)} &&\text{overlap at stations}\\
&\text{(D1)–(D2) or (D2‑simple)} &&\text{delay propagation (optional)}\\
& x_{t,k}\in\{0,1\},\; w_{t,t'}\in\{0,1\},\; u_{t,t'}\in\{0,1\}\\
& y_{t,i},z_{t,i},\delta_t,d^{\text{wait}}_{t,i}\ge 0 \qquad \forall t,i
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 6. Remarks & Assumptions  

| # | Description |
|---|-------------|
| **A1** | **Pre‑computed route set** \(R_t\) is obtained by a fast routing heuristic (e.g., ACO, Dijkstra with capacity penalties). The MILP only chooses among these alternatives – this reduces the combinatorial explosion. |
| **A2** | Travel times \(\tau_{ij}\) are deterministic; stochastic disturbances are not modelled (they could be incorporated by scenario‑based extensions). |
| **A3** | Safety head‑way \(\Delta^{\text{safe}}_{ij}\) is assumed constant for a given edge; in practice it may depend on train length or speed – the model can be extended by indexing it with the pair \((t,t')\). |
| **A4** | Overlap times \(L^{\text{overlap}}_{i}\) are required only at nodes equipped with stop signals; otherwise they are set to zero. |
| **A5** | The big‑M constant \(M\) must be larger than the maximum possible schedule shift (e.g., 10 000 min). A tighter bound improves numerical stability. |
| **A6** | The secondary energy term is linear because the energy consumption of a train on an edge does not depend on the exact departure time (reasonable for electric traction where energy is mainly a function of distance and speed profile). |
| **A7** | The model can be solved in two stages (as in the paper): first a **sub‑optimal** version without constraints (D1)–(D2) to obtain fast route + ordering decisions, then a **full** version fixing \(x_{t,k}\) and \(w_{t,t'}\) and adding delay‑propagation constraints to obtain the global optimum. |
| **A8** | If the railway network is very large, a **decomposition** (e.g., Benders or Lagrangian) can be applied on the set of conflicts \(P\); this is outside the core MILP but compatible with the formulation. |

---

### 7. How to Use the Model  

1. **Data preparation** – Build the graph \((N,E)\), compute \(\tau_{ij}\), safety head‑ways, overlap times, and generate a small set of feasible routes \(R_t\) for each train.  
2. **Parameter tuning** – Choose penalty weights \(\gamma_t\) (higher for passenger services), optionally \(\beta\) for a multi‑objective trade‑off.  
3. **Solve the sub‑optimal MILP** (omit (D1)–(D2)) – yields a fast solution for routing and ordering.  
4. **Fix \(x_{t,k}\) and \(w_{t,t'}\)** from step 3 and solve the full MILP (including delay propagation) – guarantees the global optimum for the original rtRTMP.  
5. **Post‑processing** – Extract the schedule \(\{y_{t,i}\}\), compute total delays \(\delta_t\), and, if required, the estimated energy consumption.

---

**The formulation above constitutes a complete, linear (mixed‑integer) model that captures the three‑stage decomposition (rerouting, reordering, rescheduling) described in the introductory text, includes the necessary safety constraints, and optionally accounts for energy/CO₂ considerations.**

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for rolling‑stock rescheduling with infrastructure‑availability constraints**  

The model is built on the two‑level framework described in the paper excerpt:

* **Level 1 – Rolling‑stock composition model** (the “master” problem).  
  It decides which rolling‑stock unit (RSU) is assigned to each passenger‑train trip and which shunting movements are performed at the selected stations (Utrecht Centraal, Rotterdam Centraal).  

* **Level 2 – Infrastructure feasibility model** (the “sub‑problem”).  
  It checks, for the set of shunting movements proposed by Level 1, whether a feasible time‑space path exists on the available tracks. If not, a Benders‑type cut is generated that forbids the conflicting combination of shunting movements.

Below the complete linear formulation is given.  Wherever the original description does not provide a numeric value, a reasonable assumption is made and explicitly marked **(Assumption)**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|----------|
| **T**   | Set of passenger‑train trips (indexed by *t*). |
| **R**   | Set of rolling‑stock units (RSUs) (indexed by *r*). |
| **S**   | Set of stations where shunting is allowed (here: `{Utrecht, Rotterdam}`). |
| **M**   | Set of possible shunting movements (indexed by *m*). Each movement *m* is defined by a tuple *(r, s, τ_start, τ_end)* – i.e. RSU *r* shunted at station *s* between start time *τ_start* and end time *τ_end*. |
| **K**   | Set of infrastructure tracks (indexed by *k*) that can be used for shunting at a given station. |
| **P**   | Set of passenger‑train events that occupy a track (used in the infrastructure sub‑model). |
| **B**   | Set of binary “Benders cut” indices (generated dynamically). |

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical Value / Assumption |
|--------|-------------|----------------------------|
| `cap_r` | Capacity (seats) of RSU *r*. | (Assumption) given in vehicle data. |
| `demand_t` | Passenger demand of trip *t*. | (Assumption) forecasted demand. |
| `orig_r(t)` | RSU originally assigned to trip *t* in the pre‑disruption schedule. | 0/1 indicator. |
| `Δmax` | Maximum admissible delay (minutes) that can be imposed on any passenger trip to create a window for shunting. | 5 min (Assumption). |
| `pen_delay` | Penalty cost per minute of passenger‑trip delay. | €10 / min (Assumption). |
| `pen_canc` | Penalty cost for cancelling a passenger trip. | €5 000 (Assumption). |
| `pen_sh_move` | Penalty cost for performing a shunting movement (captures crew effort, extra energy, etc.). | €200 per movement (Assumption). |
| `pen_change` | Penalty cost for deviating from the original RSU‑trip assignment (i.e. “stick‑to‑the‑plan”). | €50 per changed assignment (Assumption). |
| `track_avail_{s,k,τ}` | Binary indicator whether track *k* at station *s* is free at minute *τ* (after accounting for the disruption). | 0/1 from infrastructure timetable. |
| `travel_{t,k,τ}` | Binary indicator whether passenger trip *t* occupies track *k* at minute *τ* in the original timetable. | 0/1 from timetable. |
| `bigM` | A sufficiently large constant (≥ planning horizon in minutes). | 10 000 (Assumption). |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| `x_{t,r}` | Binary | 1 if RSU *r* is assigned to passenger trip *t* after rescheduling. |
| `y_{t}`   | Binary | 1 if passenger trip *t* is cancelled. |
| `δ_t`     | Continuous ≥0 | Delay (minutes) applied to trip *t* (only if not cancelled). |
| `z_{m}`   | Binary | 1 if shunting movement *m* (RSU *r* at station *s* during `[τ_start, τ_end]`) is performed. |
| `u_{m,k,τ}` | Binary | 1 if movement *m* uses track *k* at minute *τ* (only defined for τ in `[τ_start, τ_end]`). |
| `θ_b`    | Binary | 1 if Benders cut *b* is active (i.e. the corresponding combination of shunting movements is forbidden). |
| `π_{m}`  | Continuous ≥0 | “Dual” value of the infrastructure sub‑problem for movement *m* (used to generate cuts – optional, shown for completeness). |

---

## 4. Objective Function  

The objective aggregates several practical goals:

\[
\min \;\; 
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\bigl( pen\_delay\; \delta_t + pen\_canc\; y_t \bigr)}_{\text{Passenger service quality}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{m\in M} pen\_sh\_move\; z_m}_{\text{Shunting effort}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{r\in R} pen\_change\; |x_{t,r} - orig\_r(t)|}_{\text{Stick‑to‑plan}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{b\in B} bigM\; \theta_b}_{\text{Penalty for violating Benders cuts (big‑M formulation)}}
\]

*The absolute value can be linearised by introducing auxiliary binaries*:

\[
w_{t,r} \ge x_{t,r} - orig\_r(t),\qquad
w_{t,r} \ge orig\_r(t) - x_{t,r},\qquad
|x_{t,r} - orig\_r(t)| = w_{t,r}.
\]

---

## 5. Core Constraints  

### 5.1 Rolling‑stock assignment  

1. **Each trip receives at most one RSU (or is cancelled):**  

\[
\sum_{r\in R} x_{t,r} + y_t = 1 \qquad \forall t\in T.
\]

2. **Capacity feasibility (passenger demand must be covered):**  

\[
\sum_{r\in R} cap_r \, x_{t,r} \;\ge\; demand_t \;(1-y_t) \qquad \forall t\in T.
\]

3. **RSU availability – a unit cannot be assigned to two trips simultaneously.**  
   Let `occ_{t,τ}` be 1 if trip *t* occupies RSU *r* at minute *τ* (derived from the timetable). Then:

\[
\sum_{t\in T} occ_{t,τ} \, x_{t,r} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall r\in R,\; \forall τ\in \{0,\dots, H\},
\]

where *H* is the planning horizon (e.g., 1440 min).  

*(If the exact per‑minute occupancy data are unavailable, a coarse time‑window can be used – Assumption).*  

### 5.2 Shunting‑movement selection  

4. **A shunting movement can be performed only if the corresponding RSU is used on some trip (or is idle):**  

\[
z_m \le \sum_{t\in T} x_{t,r(m)} \;+\; (1 - \sum_{t\in T} x_{t,r(m)}) \qquad \forall m\in M,
\]

i.e. the movement is allowed if the RSU *r(m)* exists in the fleet (always true) – the constraint mainly links *z* to the master schedule.  

5. **Track‑assignment for each shunting movement:**  

\[
\sum_{k\in K_{s(m)}} u_{m,k,τ} = z_m \qquad \forall m\in M,\; \forall τ\in [τ^{start}_m, τ^{end}_m].
\]

Only one track can be used at any minute of the movement.

### 5.3 Infrastructure feasibility (sub‑problem)  

For every minute τ and track *k* at station *s* we must not exceed the track capacity (normally 1 train per track). The presence of passenger trains and shunting movements is summed:

\[
\underbrace{\sum_{p\in P} travel_{p,k,τ}}_{\text{passenger occupancy}} \;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{m\in M: s(m)=s} u_{m,k,τ}}_{\text{shunting occupancy}} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall k\in K_s,\; \forall τ.
\]

If the inequality is violated, the set of movements involved defines a **conflict set**. A Benders cut is generated:

\[
\sum_{m\in C} z_m \le |C|-1 \qquad\text{(cut }b\in B\text{)}.
\]

In the master problem this cut is added as:

\[
\sum_{m\in C} z_m \le |C|-1 + bigM\;\theta_b,\qquad \theta_b\in\{0,1\},
\]

where setting `θ_b = 0` enforces the cut, and `θ_b = 1` relaxes it at a huge penalty (ensuring the solver will avoid violating the cut unless forced by infeasibility).  

### 5.4 Delay limits  

6. **Maximum admissible delay:**  

\[
0 \le \delta_t \le \Delta_{max}\;(1-y_t) \qquad \forall t\in T.
\]

7. **If a trip is delayed, its RSU must still be available (no overlap with other trips).** This can be enforced by shifting the occupancy windows of the trip by `δ_t` and re‑using constraint (3) with the shifted times. For linearity we use a big‑M formulation:

\[
\text{If } x_{t,r}=1 \text{ and } \delta_t>0,\; \text{then } \forall τ\in [dep_t, arr_t] :\; occ_{t,τ+δ_t}\,x_{t,r}=1.
\]

In practice this is linearised by pre‑computing all feasible delay‑shifted windows (Assumption) and adding binary variables linking `δ_t` to the chosen window.

### 5.5 Logical linking of shunting and delays  

8. **A shunting movement may require a small delay of a conflicting passenger train.** If a movement *m* conflicts with a passenger train *p* on track *k* at minute τ, we may allow a delay `δ_p ≤ Δmax`. This is captured implicitly by the Benders cut: the infrastructure sub‑model, when solving for feasibility, can optionally increase `δ_p` (subject to (6)) to make room. In the master MILP we therefore add:

\[
\delta_p \ge \sum_{m\in M: \text{conflict}(m,p)} \epsilon_{m,p}\;z_m,
\]

where `ε_{m,p}` is the minimal extra minutes needed for movement *m* to be feasible given train *p*. (Assumption: `ε` is pre‑computed from a simple conflict‑graph.)

---

## 6. Linearisation Details  

* **Absolute value in the objective** – already linearised with auxiliary binaries `w_{t,r}`.  
* **Product of binary and continuous (e.g., `δ_t * y_t`)** – avoided by using big‑M constraints.  
* **Benders cuts** – added iteratively; each cut is a pure linear inequality.  

---

## 7. Complete MILP (compact notation)

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\; & \sum_{t\in T}\bigl( pen\_delay\,\delta_t + pen\_canc\,y_t \bigr)
      + \sum_{m\in M} pen\_sh\_move\,z_m
      + \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{r\in R} pen\_change\,w_{t,r}
      + \sum_{b\in B} bigM\,\theta_b \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\sum_{r\in R} x_{t,r} + y_t = 1 && \forall t\in T \\[2pt]
& \sum_{r\in R} cap_r\,x_{t,r} \ge demand_t\,(1-y_t) && \forall t\in T \\[2pt]
& \sum_{t\in T} occ_{t,τ}\,x_{t,r} \le 1 && \forall r\in R,\; \forall τ \\[2pt]
& w_{t,r} \ge x_{t,r} - orig\_r(t),\;
  w_{t,r} \ge orig\_r(t) - x_{t,r} && \forall t,r \\[2pt]
& 0 \le \delta_t \le \Delta_{max}\,(1-y_t) && \forall t\\[2pt]
& \sum_{k\in K_{s(m)}} u_{m,k,τ}=z_m && \forall m,\; \forall τ\in[m] \\[2pt]
& \sum_{p\in P} travel_{p,k,τ} + \sum_{m:s(m)=s,\,k\in K_s} u_{m,k,τ} \le 1 && \forall k,s,τ \\[2pt]
& \sum_{m\in C_b} z_m \le |C_b|-1 + bigM\,\theta_b && \forall b\in B \\[2pt]
& \theta_b\in\{0,1\},\; x_{t,r},y_t,z_m,u_{m,k,τ},w_{t,r}\in\{0,1\},\;
   \delta_t\ge 0. 
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 8. Remarks & Assumptions  

| # | Description |
|---|-------------|
| 1 | **Time discretisation** – the planning horizon is divided into 1‑minute intervals (typical for railway timetabling). |
| 2 | **`occ_{t,τ}` and `travel_{p,k,τ}`** are derived from the original timetable; if only departure/arrival times are known, a simple block‑occupation model (departure → arrival) is used. |
| 3 | **Maximum delay `Δmax`** is set to a small value (5 min) to respect existing buffer times; larger values can be allowed at the cost of higher passenger‑delay penalties. |
| 4 | **Shunting‑movement set `M`** is generated beforehand: for each RSU that could be needed at a disrupted station, a feasible time window is created (e.g., “move RSU r from depot to Utrecht between 08:10 and 08:20”). |
| 5 | **Track‑capacity** is assumed to be 1 train per track per minute; if a track can host multiple trains (e.g., siding), the RHS of the infrastructure constraint can be changed accordingly. |
| 6 | **Benders cuts** are added iteratively (exact algorithm) or one‑by‑one (iterative heuristic) as described in the paper. The MILP above already contains the generic cut form. |
| 7 | **Cost coefficients** (`pen_delay`, `pen_canc`, `pen_sh_move`, `pen_change`) are tunable to reflect the operator’s strategic priorities (passenger service vs. operational cost). |
| 8 | **Crew availability for shunting** is not modelled explicitly; it can be added by a simple capacity constraint on the number of simultaneous shunting movements at a station. |
| 9 | **Binary `θ_b`** variables are a linearisation trick to keep the model pure MILP; in a pure Benders implementation they are omitted because cuts are added as constraints only. |

---

### How to use the model  

1. **Pre‑processing** – generate sets `M`, `K_s`, and the conflict sets `C_b` by solving the infrastructure sub‑problem for the initial master solution.  
2. **Solve the master MILP** – obtain a candidate rolling‑stock assignment (`x`) and a set of shunting movements (`z`).  
3. **Run the infrastructure feasibility check** – if any conflict set `C_b` is found, add the corresponding cut (or set `θ_b=0`) and re‑solve.  
4. **Iterate** until no new cuts appear (exact approach) or until a time limit is reached (heuristic).  

The final solution guarantees:

* Every passenger trip is either served (with a feasible RSU) or cancelled.  
* All shunting movements are scheduled on tracks that are actually free, possibly after applying small passenger‑trip delays not exceeding `Δmax`.  
* The plan stays as close as possible to the original schedule (through `pen_change`).  

This MILP captures the essential trade‑offs discussed in the paper and can be extended with additional realistic constraints (crew shifts, maintenance windows, depot capacities, etc.) without changing the overall structure.

**Variables**

| Symbol | Meaning | Type | Bounds |
|--------|---------|------|--------|
| \(d_t\) | departure time of train \(t\) from its origin station | continuous | \(\ge 0\) |
| \(a_t\) | arrival time of train \(t\) at its final station | continuous | \(\ge 0\) |
| \(d_{t,s}\) | departure time of train \(t\) from station \(s\) (so arrival at station \(s+1\) is \(d_{t,s}+ \hat\tau_{t,s}\)) | continuous | \(\ge 0\) |
| \(\hat\tau_{t,s}\) | realised travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) (depends on the chosen speed plan) | continuous | \(\ge 0\) |
| \(\hat e_t\) | realised energy consumption of train \(t\) | continuous | \(\ge 0\) |
| \(y_{t,k}\) | 1 if train \(t\) follows speed plan \(k\), 0 otherwise | binary | 0‑1 |
| \(r_t\) | 1 if train \(t\) uses the opposite‑direction (rerouted) track on the blocked segment, 0 if it stays on the original direction | binary | 0‑1 |
| \(o_{t,t'}\) | 1 if train \(t\) passes a shared segment before train \(t'\); 0 otherwise (for every unordered pair \((t,t')\)) | binary | 0‑1 |
| \(z_t\) | auxiliary binary used in the blockage constraint (train passes before the blockage if \(z_t=1\), after if \(z_t=0\)) | binary | 0‑1 |

**Parameters**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T\) | set of trains, indexed by \(t\) |
| \(S\) | ordered set of stations on a train’s route, indexed by \(s\) (station \(s\) is followed by segment \(s\)) |
| \(L\) | set of track segments, indexed by \(s\) (segment \(s\) connects station \(s\) to \(s+1\)) |
| \(K\) | set of admissible speed plans, indexed by \(k\) |
| \(d_t^{0}\) | planned (original) departure time of train \(t\) from its origin |
| \(a_t^{0}\) | planned arrival time of train \(t\) at its final station |
| \(\tau_{t,k,s}\) | travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) if speed plan \(k\) is chosen |
| \(e_{t,k}\) | energy consumption of train \(t\) under speed plan \(k\) |
| \(\underline{\tau}_{t,s},\ \overline{\tau}_{t,s}\) | minimum / maximum feasible travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) (physical limits) |
| \(l^{*}\) | index of the partially blocked segment |
| \([b^{\text{start}},b^{\text{end}}]\) | time window during which segment \(l^{*}\) is blocked |
| \(w^{\text{delay}},\ w^{\text{energy}}\) | weighting coefficients in the objective |
| \(M\) | a sufficiently large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints |

**Objective function**

\[
\min\; w^{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(a_t-a_t^{0}\bigr)
      \;+\; w^{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in T}\hat e_t
\]

The first term minimises total delay; the second term minimises total energy consumption.

**Constraints**

1. **Exactly one speed plan per train**  
   \[
   \sum_{k\in K} y_{t,k}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T
   \]

2. **Link speed‑plan selection to travel times and energy**  
   \[
   \hat\tau_{t,s}= \sum_{k\in K}\tau_{t,k,s}\,y_{t,k}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in L
   \]
   \[
   \hat e_t= \sum_{k\in K} e_{t,k}\,y_{t,k}\qquad\forall t\in T
   \]

3. **Travel‑time bounds**  
   \[
   \underline{\tau}_{t,s}\le \hat\tau_{t,s}\le \overline{\tau}_{t,s}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in L
   \]

4. **Time propagation along the route**  
   \[
   d_{t,0}=d_t \qquad\forall t\in T
   \]
   \[
   d_{t,s}+ \hat\tau_{t,s}= d_{t,s+1}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in L
   \]
   \[
   a_t = d_{t,|S|-1}\qquad\forall t\in T
   \]

5. **Blockage avoidance on the disrupted segment**  
   For a train that stays on the original direction (\(r_t=0\)) it must either finish the segment before the blockage starts or start it after the blockage ends:
   \[
   d_{t,l^{*}-1}+ \hat\tau_{t,l^{*}} \le b^{\text{start}} + M\bigl(r_t + (1-z_t)\bigr)
   \]
   \[
   d_{t,l^{*}-1} \ge b^{\text{end}} - M\bigl(r_t + z_t\bigr)
   \qquad\forall t\in T
   \]
   The binary \(z_t\) forces exactly one of the two alternatives when \(r_t=0\); if the train is rerouted (\(r_t=1\)) the big‑M term relaxes the constraints.

6. **Conflict‑avoidance on shared segments**  
   For every unordered pair of trains \((t,t')\) that may occupy the same segment, an ordering binary is introduced:
   \[
   o_{t,t'} + o_{t',t}=1 \qquad\forall t<t',\;t,t'\in T
   \]
   If train \(t\) precedes train \(t'\) on segment \(s\):
   \[
   d_{t,s}+ \hat\tau_{t,s} \le d_{t',s}+ M\bigl(1-o_{t,t'}\bigr)
   \qquad\forall s\in L,\;t<t',\;t,t'\in T
   \]
   The symmetric inequality with \(o_{t',t}\) guarantees the opposite ordering when \(o_{t,t'}=0\).

7. **Variable domains**  
   \[
   d_t,\ a_t,\ d_{t,s},\ \hat\tau_{t,s},\ \hat e_t \ge 0
   \]
   \[
   y_{t,k},\ r_t,\ o_{t,t'},\ z_t \in \{0,1\}
   \]

**Assumptions (explicitly stated)**  

* All trains follow the same ordered list of stations; if a train uses the opposite direction on the blocked segment it does not occupy that segment during the blockage.  
* The set of speed plans \(K\) is pre‑computed; each plan provides deterministic travel times \(\tau_{t,k,s}\) and energy \(e_{t,k}\).  
* The big‑M constant \(M\) is chosen larger than the maximal possible schedule horizon (e.g., several thousand minutes).  
* Conflict constraints are applied to every segment; if in a particular instance only a subset of trains share a segment, the corresponding constraints can be omitted.  

The model above is a complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the integrated **Train Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP)** under a partial segment blockage, capturing route choice, speed‑plan selection, blockage avoidance, bidirectional conflict resolution, and the weighted objective of delay plus energy consumption.

Text:
**Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage**  

---

### 1. Sets & Indices
| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|----------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\). |
| \(N\) | Set of network nodes (stations, junctions), indexed by \(i\). |
| \(S\subseteq N\times N\) | Set of directed track‑segments \((i,j)\). |
| \(K\) | Set of admissible speed‑levels per segment, indexed by \(k\). |
| \(U_{ij}\in\{L,R\}\) | Set of usable track‑sides for segment \((i,j)\) (left/right). |
| \(B\subseteq S\) | Subset of segments that are partially blocked (one side unavailable). |
| \(P_t\subseteq S\) | Original (nominal) route of train \(t\). |
| \(R_t\subseteq S\) | Detour segments that become feasible only after rerouting. |
| \(orig(t),\;dest(t)\) | Origin and destination node of train \(t\). |
| \(S_t\) | Planned arrival time of train \(t\) at its destination (baseline schedule). |
| \(D_t\) | Release (planned departure) time of train \(t\) from its origin. |
| \(M\) | Large constant (big‑M). |
| \(\epsilon>0\) | Small constant to avoid strict inequalities (e.g. 0.1 min). |

---

### 2. Parameters
| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|--------|----------|------|
| \(L_{ij}\) | Length of segment \((i,j)\) | km |
| \(v_{ij}^k\) | Speed associated with level \(k\) on \((i,j)\) | km/h |
| \(\tau_{ij}^k = \dfrac{L_{ij}}{v_{ij}^k}\times 60\) | Travel time on \((i,j)\) with level \(k\) | min |
| \(e_{ij}^k\) | Energy consumption on \((i,j)\) with level \(k\) | kWh |
| \(\tau_i^{\min}\) | Minimum dwell time at node \(i\) | min |
| \(\Delta_{ij}^{\text{block}} \in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if side **R** of \((i,j)\) is blocked, else 0 |
| \(a^{\max}\) | Maximum permissible acceleration (km/h²) |
| \(d^{\max}\) | Maximum permissible deceleration (km/h²) |
| \(w^{\text{delay}}, w^{\text{energy}} >0\) | Weights for the two objectives |

---

### 3. Decision Variables
| Variable | Type | Interpretation |
|----------|------|----------------|
| \(x_{t,i}\) | Continuous \(\ge 0\) | Arrival time of train \(t\) at node \(i\). |
| \(d_{t,i}\) | Continuous \(\ge 0\) | Departure time of train \(t\) from node \(i\). |
| \(z_{t,ij}^k \in\{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 iff train \(t\) traverses \((i,j)\) with speed level \(k\). |
| \(y_{t,ij}^{u}\in\{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 iff train \(t\) uses side \(u\in U_{ij}\) on \((i,j)\). |
| \(p_{t,ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 iff train \(t\) follows its **original** segment \((i,j)\in P_t\). |
| \(r_{t,ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 iff train \(t\) uses a **detour** segment \((i,j)\in R_t\). |
| \(D_t^{\text{tot}}\ge0\) | Continuous | Total delay of train \(t\) (actual – planned arrival). |
| \(E_t\ge0\) | Continuous | Total energy consumption of train \(t\). |

---

### 4. Objective Function
\[
\boxed{
\min\; 
w^{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in T} D_t^{\text{tot}}
\;+\;
w^{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in T} E_t
}
\]
The objective simultaneously minimises weighted total delay and total energy usage.

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Routing & side selection
1. **Exactly one side for every traversed segment**  
\[
\sum_{u\in U_{ij}} y_{t,ij}^{u}= \sum_{k\in K} z_{t,ij}^{k}\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in S
\tag{R1}
\]

2. **Original vs. detour usage**  
\[
p_{t,ij}+r_{t,ij}= \sum_{k\in K} z_{t,ij}^{k}\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in S
\tag{R2}
\]

3. **Blocked side cannot be used**  
\[
y_{t,ij}^{R}\le 1-\Delta_{ij}^{\text{block}}\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in B
\tag{R3}
\]

#### 5.2 Travel‑time linking (speed‑level determines travel time)
\[
x_{t,j} \;\ge\; d_{t,i} + \tau_{ij}^{k} - M\bigl(1- z_{t,ij}^{k}\bigr)
\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in S,\;k\in K
\tag{T1}
\]
\[
x_{t,j} \;\le\; d_{t,i} + \tau_{ij}^{k} + M\bigl(1- z_{t,ij}^{k}\bigr)
\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j),k
\tag{T2}
\]

If \(z_{t,ij}^{k}=1\) the two inequalities collapse to the exact equality
\(x_{t,j}=d_{t,i}+\tau_{ij}^{k}\).

#### 5.3 Minimum dwell time at stations
\[
d_{t,i} \;\ge\; x_{t,i}+ \tau_i^{\min}\qquad\forall t,\;i\in N
\tag{D1}
\]

#### 5.4 Track‑capacity (conflict‑free usage of each side)  
For any two distinct trains \(t\neq t'\) that could occupy the same side \(u\) of segment \((i,j)\):
\[
x_{t',j} \;\ge\; d_{t,i}+ \tau_{ij}^{k} - M\bigl(2- y_{t,ij}^{u}-y_{t',ij}^{u}\bigr)
\qquad\forall t\neq t',\;(i,j),\;u\in U_{ij},\;k\in K
\tag{C1}
\]
\[
x_{t,j} \;\ge\; d_{t',i}+ \tau_{ij}^{k'} - M\bigl(2- y_{t,ij}^{u}-y_{t',ij}^{u}\bigr)
\qquad\forall t\neq t',\;(i,j),\;u,\;k'
\tag{C2}
\]
Only one of the two disjunctive inequalities is active; the big‑M term de‑activates the other when the side is not simultaneously chosen.

#### 5.5 Acceleration / deceleration limits (linearized speed‑difference)
Define the effective speed of train \(t\) on segment \((i,j)\):
\[
\hat v_{t,ij}= \sum_{k\in K} v_{ij}^{k}\,z_{t,ij}^{k}
\]

For every internal node \(i\) of train \(t\) (i.e., a node that has a predecessor and a successor on its route):
\[
\hat v_{t,i\,\text{next}} - \hat v_{t,\text{prev}\,i} \;\le\; a^{\max}\;\frac{\tau_{\text{prev}\,i}}{60}
\tag{A1}
\]
\[
\hat v_{t,\text{prev}\,i} - \hat v_{t,i\,\text{next}} \;\le\; d^{\max}\;\frac{\tau_{\text{prev}\,i}}{60}
\tag{A2}
\]

These linear inequalities enforce that speed changes between consecutive segments respect the given acceleration/deceleration limits.

#### 5.6 Delay calculation
\[
D_t^{\text{tot}} \;\ge\; x_{t,dest(t)} - S_t \qquad\forall t\in T
\tag{DEL}
\]

If early arrival is not allowed, add \(x_{t,dest(t)}\ge S_t\).

#### 5.7 Energy accounting
\[
E_t = \sum_{(i,j)\in S}\sum_{k\in K} e_{ij}^{k}\,z_{t,ij}^{k}\qquad\forall t\in T
\tag{EN}
\]

#### 5.8 Origin departure anchoring
\[
d_{t,orig(t)} \;\ge\; D_t \qquad\forall t\in T
\tag{ORIG}
\]

---

### 6. Complete MILP Formulation  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&
w^{\text{delay}}\!\sum_{t\in T} D_t^{\text{tot}}
+ w^{\text{energy}}\!\sum_{t\in T} E_t\\[4pt]
\text{s.t. }&
\text{Routing constraints } (R1)-(R3)\\
&\text{Travel‑time constraints } (T1)-(T2)\\
&\text{Dwell time } (D1)\\
&\text{Capacity / conflict avoidance } (C1)-(C2)\\
&\text{Acceleration / deceleration } (A1)-(A2)\\
&\text{Delay definition } (DEL)\\
&\text{Energy definition } (EN)\\
&\text{Origin departure } (ORIG)\\
&x_{t,i},d_{t,i},D_t^{\text{tot}},E_t \ge 0\quad\forall t,i\\
&z_{t,ij}^{k},y_{t,ij}^{u},p_{t,ij},r_{t,ij}\in\{0,1\}\quad\forall t,(i,j),k,u
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 7. Modeling Assumptions (explicitly stated)

| # | Assumption |
|---|------------|
| A1 | Each physical segment has two parallel tracks (left/right). A partial blockage removes one side for the whole disruption window. |
| A2 | Speed is selected from a small discrete set \(K\); travel time and energy are linear in the binary speed‑level variables. |
| A3 | Acceleration/deceleration limits are approximated by linear bounds on the speed difference between consecutive segments. |
| A4 | Only one train may occupy a given side of a segment at a time (capacity = 1). |
| A5 | Minimum dwell time at stations is a known constant; non‑stations have \(\tau_i^{\min}=0\). |
| A6 | The disruption window and which side is blocked are known beforehand, enforced by (R3). |
| A7 | Big‑M is chosen larger than the longest possible schedule horizon (e.g., 10 000 min) to safely deactivate constraints. |
| A8 | Early arrivals are allowed (delay defined as non‑negative excess over planned arrival). Add a constraint if early arrival must be penalised. |
| A9 | Energy consumption per segment is additive and independent of exact timing (no regenerative braking). |
| A10| All times are expressed in minutes; conversion factor 60 is used when relating speeds (km/h) to travel times (min). |

---

**The model above is a fully linear mixed‑integer program that simultaneously determines:**
* a conflict‑free timetable (arrival/departure times),
* the side of the track each train uses (including possible rerouting around a blocked side),
* the discrete speed level for every traversed segment (hence a feasible speed profile),
* and it minimises a weighted sum of total passenger delay and total energy consumption.

It can be directly implemented in any MILP solver (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, SCIP). Adjust the weight parameters, the speed‑level set, or add tighter time‑indexed capacity constraints if a stronger LP relaxation is required for larger instances.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) for Partial Segment Blockages**  

---

### 1. Sets, parameters and data  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **I** | Set of trains, indexed by *i* (|I| = N). |
| **Kᵢ** | Ordered list of stations visited by train *i* (including origin 0 and destination *last*). |
| **S** | Set of railway segments (track between two consecutive stations). |
| **Sᵢ ⊂ S** | Segments traversed by train *i* (|Sᵢ| = |Kᵢ|‑1). |
| **B ⊂ S** | Segments that are **partially blocked** (only one side unavailable). |
| **Side(s) = {L,R}** | Two parallel sides (left/right) of a segment *s*. |
| **ℓₛ** | Length of segment *s* (km). |
| **c₁ , c₂** | Positive energy‑cost coefficients. |
| **vᵐᵢⁿ , vᵐᵃˣ** | Global speed limits (km h⁻¹). |
| **aᵐᵢⁿ , aᵐᵃˣ** | Max. deceleration / acceleration (km h⁻¹ min⁻¹). |
| **τᵈʷ₍i,k₎⁽ᵐⁱⁿ⁾ , τᵈʷ₍i,k₎⁽ᵐᵃˣ⁾** | Minimum / maximum dwell time of train *i* at station *k*. |
| **schedᵢ** | Scheduled arrival time of train *i* at its final station (reference). |
| **T_start(s), T_end(s)** | Start / end of the disruption on segment *s* (the blocked side cannot be used in this interval). |
| **M** | Big‑M constant (≥ maximal feasible time, e.g. 10 000 min). |
| **Δt** | Small positive constant to enforce strict ordering (Δt = 0.1 min). |
| **α , β ≥ 0** | Decision‑maker weights for delay and energy, respectively. |

---

### 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **rᵢₛᴸ , rᵢₛᴿ** | binary | 1 if train *i* uses side **L** (resp. **R**) of blocked segment *s* ∈ B; 0 otherwise. |
| **oᵢⱼₛ** | binary | 1 if train *i* precedes train *j* on the **same side** of segment *s* (i.e. *i* exits before *j* enters). |
| **aᵢₖ** | ≥0 | Arrival time of train *i* at station *k* ∈ Kᵢ. |
| **dᵢₖ** | ≥0 | Departure time of train *i* from station *k* ∈ Kᵢ. |
| **tᵢₛ** | ≥0 | Travel time of train *i* on segment *s* ∈ Sᵢ. |
| **vᵢₛ** | ≥0 | Average speed of train *i* on segment *s* (km h⁻¹). |
| **δᵢₛ** | ≥0 | Linearisation variable for the product *vᵢₛ·tᵢₛ* (so that ℓₛ = δᵢₛ). |
| **zᵢₛ** | binary | 1 if train *i* actually traverses segment *s* (zᵢₛ = 1 for all *s* ∈ Sᵢ). |
| **yᵢₛ , wᵢₛ** | ≥0 | Auxiliary variables for the quadratic and reciprocal terms in the energy expression (see §4). |

---

### 3. Linearised relationships  

#### 3.1 Distance consistency (δ‑linearisation)  
For every *i* and *s* ∈ Sᵢ  

\[
\ell_s = \delta_{i,s},\qquad
\delta_{i,s} \le v_{i,s}^{\max} t_{i,s}+M(1-z_{i,s}),\;
\delta_{i,s} \ge v_{i,s}^{\min} t_{i,s}-M(1-z_{i,s}).
\]

Because *zᵢₛ = 1* for all traversed segments, the constraints enforce  
\(\delta_{i,s}=v_{i,s}t_{i,s}\) and \(\ell_s = v_{i,s}t_{i,s}\).

#### 3.2 Speed limits  

\[
v^{\min} z_{i,s} \le v_{i,s} \le v^{\max} z_{i,s}\qquad\forall i,s.
\]

#### 3.3 Acceleration / deceleration between consecutive segments  

If *s* and *s′* are consecutive on train *i*  

\[
v_{i,s'}-v_{i,s} \le a^{\max} t_{i,s}+M(1-z_{i,s})+M(1-z_{i,s'}),\\
v_{i,s}-v_{i,s'} \le a^{\min} t_{i,s}+M(1-z_{i,s})+M(1-z_{i,s'}).
\]

#### 3.4 Dwell‑time bounds  

For every intermediate station *k* (k = 1,…,|Kᵢ|‑1)  

\[
\tau^{\text{dw}}_{\min,i,k}\le d_{i,k}-a_{i,k}\le \tau^{\text{dw}}_{\max,i,k}.
\]

#### 3.5 Time feasibility (link stations and segments)  

For each segment *s* that connects station *k* to *k+1* on train *i*  

\[
a_{i,k+1}= d_{i,k}+t_{i,s}\qquad\forall i,\; s\in S_i.
\]

#### 3.6 Route choice on blocked segments  

For every blocked segment *s* ∈ B traversed by train *i*  

\[
r_{i,s}^{L}+r_{i,s}^{R}=1.
\]

If *s* is not blocked, the two binaries are fixed to 1 (or omitted).

#### 3.7 Disruption‑window feasibility  

Let side **b(s)** be the **blocked** side of *s* during \([T_{\text{start}}(s),T_{\text{end}}(s)]\).  
The unblocked side is \(\overline{b(s)}\).  

\[
a_{i,\text{up}(s)} \ge T_{\text{end}}(s)+\Delta t
      -M\bigl(1-r_{i,s}^{\overline{b(s)}}\bigr),\\
a_{i,\text{up}(s)}+t_{i,s} \le T_{\text{start}}(s)-\Delta t
      +M\bigl(1-r_{i,s}^{\overline{b(s)}}\bigr),
\]

where \(\text{up}(s)\) is the upstream station of *s*.  
If the train chooses the **unblocked** side (\(r_{i,s}^{\overline{b(s)}}=1\)) the traversal interval must lie completely **outside** the disruption window; otherwise the big‑M term relaxes the constraints.

#### 3.8 Pairwise precedence on a shared side  

Consider any two distinct trains *i* and *j* that both use the **same side** σ of segment *s* (i.e. \(r_{i,s}^{\sigma}=r_{j,s}^{\sigma}=1\)).  

\[
a_{j,\text{up}(s)} \ge d_{i,\text{down}(s)}+\Delta t-M\bigl(1-o_{i j s}\bigr),\\
a_{i,\text{up}(s)} \ge d_{j,\text{down}(s)}+\Delta t-M\bigl(o_{i j s}\bigr),\\
o_{i j s}+o_{j i s}=1.
\]

Thus exactly one ordering holds.

#### 3.9 Transitivity of order variables (consistency)  

For any three trains *i, j, k* sharing the same side of *s*  

\[
o_{i j s}+o_{j k s}-o_{i k s}\le 1,\qquad
o_{i j s}+o_{j k s}-o_{i k s}\ge 0.
\]

These linear constraints guarantee a consistent total order on each side.

#### 3.10 Energy‑term linearisation  

Energy on segment *s* for train *i* is modelled as  

\[
E_{i,s}= \bigl(c_1 v_{i,s}^{2}+c_2/v_{i,s}\bigr)\,t_{i,s}.
\]

Introduce auxiliary variables  

\[
y_{i,s}=v_{i,s}^{2},\qquad w_{i,s}=1/v_{i,s},
\]

and linearise the bilinear products \(y_{i,s}t_{i,s}\) and \(w_{i,s}t_{i,s}\) with standard McCormick envelopes (bounds derived from \(v^{\min},v^{\max}\)).  
Then  

\[
\widehat{E}_{i,s}=c_1\,\tilde{y}_{i,s}+c_2\,\tilde{w}_{i,s},
\]

where \(\tilde{y}_{i,s}\) and \(\tilde{w}_{i,s}\) are the linearised representations of \(y_{i,s}t_{i,s}\) and \(w_{i,s}t_{i,s}\).

---

### 4. Objective function  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
\alpha\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(a_{i,\text{last}}-\text{sched}_i\bigr)}_{\text{total passenger delay}}
\;+\;
\beta\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S_i}\widehat{E}_{i,s}}_{\text{total energy consumption}}
}
\]

*α* and *β* are user‑defined weights reflecting the relative importance of punctuality versus energy efficiency.

---

### 5. Complete MILP formulation  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \alpha\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(a_{i,\text{last}}-\text{sched}_i\bigr)
      +\beta\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S_i}\widehat{E}_{i,s}\\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } 
&\text{(1) Route choice on blocked segments: } 
      r_{i,s}^{L}+r_{i,s}^{R}=1 &&\forall i,\; s\in B\cap S_i\\[2pt]
&\text{(2) Distance consistency (δ‑linearisation)}\\
&\ell_s = \delta_{i,s} &&\forall i,\; s\in S_i\\
&\delta_{i,s}=v_{i,s}t_{i,s}\;\;(\text{McCormick})\\[2pt]
&\text{(3) Speed limits} && v^{\min}z_{i,s}\le v_{i,s}\le v^{\max}z_{i,s}\\[2pt]
&\text{(4) Acceleration / deceleration constraints}\\
&v_{i,s'}-v_{i,s}\le a^{\max}t_{i,s}+M(1-z_{i,s})+M(1-z_{i,s'}),\\
&v_{i,s}-v_{i,s'}\le a^{\min}t_{i,s}+M(1-z_{i,s})+M(1-z_{i,s'});\\[2pt]
&\text{(5) Dwell‑time bounds}\\
&\tau^{\text{dw}}_{\min,i,k}\le d_{i,k}-a_{i,k}\le \tau^{\text{dw}}_{\max,i,k}
   &&\forall i,\;k=1,\dots,|K_i|-1\\[2pt]
&\text{(6) Time feasibility (stations ↔ segments)}\\
&a_{i,k+1}=d_{i,k}+t_{i,s} &&\forall i,\; s\in S_i,\; k\text{ upstream of }s\\[2pt]
&\text{(7) Disruption‑window feasibility}\\
&a_{i,\text{up}(s)}\ge T_{\text{end}}(s)+\Delta t-M\bigl(1-r_{i,s}^{\overline{b(s)}}\bigr),\\
&a_{i,\text{up}(s)}+t_{i,s}\le T_{\text{start}}(s)-\Delta t+M\bigl(1-r_{i,s}^{\overline{b(s)}}\bigr)
   &&\forall i,\; s\in B\cap S_i\\[2pt]
&\text{(8) Pairwise precedence on a shared side}\\
&a_{j,\text{up}(s)}\ge d_{i,\text{down}(s)}+\Delta t-M(1-o_{i j s}),\\
&a_{i,\text{up}(s)}\ge d_{j,\text{down}(s)}+\Delta t-M(o_{i j s}),\\
&o_{i j s}+o_{j i s}=1 &&\forall i<j,\; s\text{ shared}\\[2pt]
&\text{(9) Transitivity of order variables}\\
&o_{i j s}+o_{j k s}-o_{i k s}\le 1,\\
&o_{i j s}+o_{j k s}-o_{i k s}\ge 0
   &&\forall i,j,k\text{ sharing side }s\\[2pt]
&\text{(10) Energy linearisation (McCormick)}\\
&y_{i,s}=v_{i,s}^{2},\; w_{i,s}=1/v_{i,s},\;
\tilde{y}_{i,s}=y_{i,s}t_{i,s},\;
\tilde{w}_{i,s}=w_{i,s}t_{i,s}\\
&\widehat{E}_{i,s}=c_1\tilde{y}_{i,s}+c_2\tilde{w}_{i,s}\\[2pt]
&\text{(11) Variable domains}\\
&r_{i,s}^{L},r_{i,s}^{R},o_{i j s},z_{i,s}\in\{0,1\},\\
&a_{i,k},d_{i,k},t_{i,s},v_{i,s},\delta_{i,s},y_{i,s},w_{i,s}\ge 0.
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only non‑linear products have been replaced by the auxiliary variables and McCormick envelopes, yielding a **Mixed‑Integer Linear Program (MILP)**.

---

### 6. Remarks & modelling assumptions  

1. **Fixed route topology** – the sequence of stations for each train is known; only the side on a blocked segment is a decision.  
2. **Single‑track per side** – each side can host at most one train at any instant; enforced by the pairwise precedence variables.  
3. **Big‑M** – choose *M* larger than the longest possible schedule horizon (e.g., 10 000 min).  
4. **Energy linearisation** – McCormick envelopes give a tight convex approximation of the quadratic and reciprocal terms; additional break‑points can be added for higher accuracy.  
5. **Disruption handling** – a train that selects the **unblocked** side must finish its traversal outside the blocked time window; trains forced onto the blocked side are simply prohibited (binary set to 0).  
6. **Scalability** – the number of binary order variables grows with the number of train pairs sharing a side; in practice, pairs whose earliest possible arrivals do not overlap can be omitted to reduce model size.  

---

### 7. How to use the formulation  

1. **Data preparation** – for each train compute its station list, segment lengths, scheduled arrival times, and identify blocked segments and the side that is unavailable.  
2. **Parameter selection** – set α, β, energy coefficients (c₁,c₂), speed/acceleration limits, dwell‑time windows, and a suitable big‑M.  
3. **Implementation** – encode the MILP in any MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, SCIP, etc.).  
4. **Solution interpretation** – the optimal solution provides:  
   * side choice \(r_{i,s}^{\sigma}\) for each blocked segment,  
   * conflict‑free timetable \((a_{i,k},d_{i,k})\),  
   * feasible speed profile \((v_{i,s})\) and travel times \((t_{i,s})\),  
   * precedence order on each side \((o_{i j s})\).  

The objective value directly quantifies the trade‑off between **total passenger delay** and **energy consumption** under the given partial blockage scenario.

Text:
**Sets**

\[
\begin{aligned}
I & : \text{set of trains } i\\
S & : \text{set of track segments } s\\
T & : \text{set of discrete time periods } t\\
R_i & : \text{set of feasible routes } r \text{ for train } i\\
L & : \text{set of speed levels (used only for bounds)} 
\end{aligned}
\]

**Parameters**

\[
\begin{aligned}
\hat a_i & : \text{scheduled arrival period of train } i\\
\underline v ,\; \overline v & : \text{minimum / maximum admissible speed (km/h)}\\
\Delta v^{\max} ,\; \Delta v^{\min} & : \text{maximum acceleration / deceleration per period}\\
\text{Cap}_s & : \text{capacity of segment } s \;(=1\text{ for bidirectional conflict)}\\
\text{Block}_{s,t} & =\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if segment } s \text{ is blocked at period } t\\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}\\
\text{Dwell} & : \text{required dwell time at a station (periods)}\\
w^{\text{delay}} ,\; \alpha ,\; \beta & : \text{weights in the objective}\\
M & : \text{big‑M constant (chosen } M\ge \overline v\text{)} 
\end{aligned}
\]

**Decision variables**

\[
\begin{aligned}
x_{i,r} &\in\{0,1\} &&\text{1 if train } i \text{ uses route } r\\[2pt]
y_{i,s,t} &\in\{0,1\} &&\text{1 if train } i \text{ occupies segment } s \text{ at period } t\\[2pt]
v_{i,s,t} &\ge 0 &&\text{speed of train } i \text{ on segment } s \text{ at period } t\\[2pt]
a_{i,s,t} &\in\{0,1\} &&\text{1 if a speed change occurs for train } i \text{ on } s \text{ at } t\\[2pt]
\text{Arr}_i &\ge 0 &&\text{arrival period of train } i \text{ at its final station}
\end{aligned}
\]

**Objective function**

\[
\min \; 
w^{\text{delay}}\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(\text{Arr}_i-\hat a_i\bigr)
\;+\;
\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{t\in T}
\Bigl(\alpha\,v_{i,s,t}^{2}+\beta\,a_{i,s,t}\Bigr)
\]

The first term minimises total delay, the second term represents energy consumption (quadratic speed term) plus a penalty for acceleration/deceleration.

**Constraints**

1. **Route selection**  
   \[
   \sum_{r\in R_i} x_{i,r}=1 \qquad \forall i\in I
   \]

2. **Occupancy – route linking (big‑M)**  
   \[
   y_{i,s,t}\le \sum_{\substack{r\in R_i\\ s\in r}} x_{i,r}
   \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T
   \]

3. **At most one segment per train per period**  
   \[
   \sum_{s\in S} y_{i,s,t}\le 1 \qquad \forall i\in I,\; t\in T
   \]

4. **Flow continuity along a chosen route**  
   For every train \(i\), route \(r\in R_i\) with ordered segment list \((s_1,\dots ,s_{|r|})\):
   \[
   y_{i,s_k,t}+y_{i,s_{k+1},t+1}\ge x_{i,r}
   \qquad \forall k=1,\dots ,|r|-1,\; t\in T\setminus\{T_{\max}\}
   \]
   (the train must either stay on the same segment or move to the next one).

5. **Arrival‑time definition**  
   Let \(s_i^{\text{last}}(r)\) be the last segment of route \(r\).  
   \[
   \text{Arr}_i = \sum_{r\in R_i}\sum_{t\in T} t\; y_{i,s_i^{\text{last}}(r),t}\; x_{i,r}
   \qquad \forall i\in I
   \]

6. **No early arrival (optional)**  
   \[
   \text{Arr}_i \ge \hat a_i \qquad \forall i\in I
   \]

7. **Blockage constraint**  
   \[
   y_{i,s,t}=0 \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T \text{ with } \text{Block}_{s,t}=1
   \]

8. **Segment capacity (bidirectional conflict)**  
   \[
   \sum_{i\in I} y_{i,s,t}\le \text{Cap}_s \qquad \forall s\in S,\; t\in T
   \]

9. **Speed limits linked to occupancy**  
   \[
   \underline v \, y_{i,s,t}\le v_{i,s,t}\le \overline v \, y_{i,s,t}
   \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T
   \]

10. **Acceleration / deceleration linking** (linearised with binary \(a_{i,s,t}\))  

    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    v_{i,s,t+1}-v_{i,s,t} &\le \Delta v^{\max}+M(1-a_{i,s,t})\\
    v_{i,s,t}-v_{i,s,t+1} &\le -\Delta v^{\min}+M(1-a_{i,s,t})\\
    v_{i,s,t+1}-v_{i,s,t} &\le M a_{i,s,t}\\
    v_{i,s,t}-v_{i,s,t+1} &\le M a_{i,s,t}
    \end{aligned}
    \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S,\; t\in T\setminus\{T_{\max}\}
    \]

    The first two inequalities enforce that a speed change larger than the allowed limits can occur only if \(a_{i,s,t}=1\); the last two force the speed to stay unchanged when \(a_{i,s,t}=0\).

11. **Dwell‑time at stations** (first and last segment of each route are stations)  

    For every train \(i\), route \(r\) and its first segment \(s^{\text{first}}_i(r)\) and last segment \(s^{\text{last}}_i(r)\):
    \[
    \sum_{d=0}^{\text{Dwell}-1} y_{i,s^{\text{first}}_i(r),t+d}\ge \text{Dwell}\; y_{i,s^{\text{first}}_i(r),t}
    \qquad \forall t\in T,\; i\in I,\; r\in R_i
    \]
    \[
    \sum_{d=0}^{\text{Dwell}-1} y_{i,s^{\text{last}}_i(r),t+d}\ge \text{Dwell}\; y_{i,s^{\text{last}}_i(r),t}
    \qquad \forall t\in T,\; i\in I,\; r\in R_i
    \]

12. **Binary and non‑negativity domains** (already stated with the variables).

---

**Assumptions (explicitly stated)**  

* Time is discretised into equal periods; within a period a train can occupy at most one segment.  
* Each segment can host at most one train at any period (capacity = 1), which captures bidirectional conflict on the shared track.  
* Speed is constant on a segment during a period; acceleration/deceleration is modelled between consecutive periods.  
* The disruption is a *partial segment blockage*: the binary parameter `Block_{s,t}` forces zero occupancy on the blocked segment during its time window.  
* Dwell time is required only at the first and last stations of a route (extensions to intermediate stations are straightforward).  
* Energy consumption is approximated by a quadratic speed term plus a linear penalty for any speed change; coefficients α and β are user‑defined.  

The model above fully describes the integrated **train rescheduling and speed management problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages, ready for implementation in any MILP solver.
