Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for rolling‑stock rescheduling with infrastructure‑availability constraints**  

The model integrates two sub‑problems that were described in the paper:

1. **Composition model** – decides which rolling‑stock unit (RSU) is assigned to each passenger‑train trip and which shunting movements are performed.  
2. **Infrastructure model** – checks that every shunting movement can be executed on the available tracks of the stations (Utrecht C and Rotterdam C) without violating capacity or causing excessive delays to other trains.

The MILP below is a *single‑level* formulation that can be used either directly (exact approach) or as the master problem of a Benders‑type decomposition.  
All sets, parameters, decision variables, the objective function and the constraints are listed explicitly.  
Where data are not given in the description, reasonable assumptions are stated and marked as **(Assumption)**.

---

## 1. Indices, sets and parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning | Remarks |
|--------|---------|---------|
| \(T\) | Set of passenger‑train trips (indexed by \(t\)) | includes original timetable trips and any trips created by disruption handling |
| \(R\) | Set of rolling‑stock units (RSUs) (indexed by \(r\)) | each RSU is a trainset that can be coupled/decoupled |
| \(S\) | Set of stations where shunting is allowed (here \(S=\{Utrecht, Rotterdam\}\) ) |
| \(K_s\) | Set of shunting‑tracks at station \(s\) (indexed by \(k\)) | each track has a capacity of one shunting movement at a time |
| \(P_t\) | Planned departure time of trip \(t\) (minutes from midnight) |
| \(\overline{P}_t\) | Planned arrival time of trip \(t\) |
| \(\Delta^{\max}\) | Maximum admissible delay for any passenger train (Assumption: 5 min) |
| \(\theta^{\max}\) | Maximum admissible delay for a shunting movement (Assumption: 3 min) |
| \(c^{\text{delay}}_t\) | Penalty cost per minute of delaying trip \(t\) (e.g. passenger dissatisfaction) |
| \(c^{\text{shunt}}_{s,k}\) | Cost of using shunting track \(k\) at station \(s\) (e.g. driver labour) |
| \(c^{\text{change}}_{t,r}\) | Cost of assigning RSU \(r\) to trip \(t\) different from the original plan (stick‑to‑the‑plan) |
| \(M\) | Large constant (≥ 24 h expressed in minutes) |
| \(\alpha\) | Weight for the similarity‑to‑original‑plan objective (Assumption: 0.3) |
| \(\beta\) | Weight for the passenger‑delay objective (Assumption: 0.5) |
| \(\gamma\) | Weight for the shunting‑cost objective (Assumption: 0.2) |
| \(a_{t,s}\) | Binary parameter = 1 if trip \(t\) starts/ends at station \(s\) (i.e. a shunting opportunity) |
| \(d^{\text{min}}_{s,k}\) | Minimum headway (in minutes) required between two consecutive shunting movements on track \(k\) at station \(s\) (Assumption: 2 min) |

---

## 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if RSU \(r\) is assigned to trip \(t\) |
| \(y_{t} \ge 0\) | continuous | delay (in minutes) applied to departure/arrival of trip \(t\) (same value added to both) |
| \(z_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if a shunting movement for trip \(t\) is performed on track \(k\) at station \(s\) |
| \(\tau_{t,s,k} \ge 0\) | continuous | start time (in minutes) of the shunting movement of trip \(t\) on \((s,k)\) |
| \(\delta_{t,s,k} \ge 0\) | continuous | duration (in minutes) of the shunting movement (including any induced delay) |
| \(\omega_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if shunting movement \((t,s,k)\) is **canceled** (i.e. not performed) |
| \(u_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if RSU \(r\) **remains** on its original trip (used for similarity objective) |

---

## 3. Objective function  

The overall objective is a weighted sum of three criteria that were highlighted in the paper:

1. **Similarity to the original rolling‑stock plan** – keep the original RSU‑trip assignments.  
2. **Passenger‑service quality** – minimise total delay of passenger trips.  
3. **Operational shunting cost** – minimise number / duration of shunting movements and penalise cancellations.

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & 
\alpha \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{r\in R} c^{\text{change}}_{t,r}\;(x_{t,r} - u_{t,r})}_{\text{(A) deviation from original RSU assignment}} \\
& + \beta \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} c^{\text{delay}}_{t}\; y_{t}}_{\text{(B) passenger‑delay cost}} \\
& + \gamma \underbrace{\Big( \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K_s} c^{\text{shunt}}_{s,k}\; z_{t,s,k}
        + \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K_s} M\; \omega_{t,s,k}\Big)}_{\text{(C) shunting cost + cancellation penalty}} 
\end{aligned}
\]

*The large constant \(M\) forces the model to avoid cancellations unless infeasible.*

---

## 4. Constraints  

### 4.1 Rolling‑stock assignment constraints  

1. **Each trip receives exactly one RSU**  

\[
\sum_{r\in R} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{1}
\]

2. **RSU continuity (circulation) – a RSU can start a new trip only after it has finished the previous one**  

Let \( \operatorname{pred}(t) \) be the predecessor trip of \(t\) in the original timetable (if any).  
If the predecessor is not defined, the constraint is omitted.

\[
P_{t}+y_{t} \;\ge\; \overline{P}_{\operatorname{pred}(t)}+y_{\operatorname{pred}(t)} 
\;-\; M\,(1-x_{t,r}+x_{\operatorname{pred}(t),r}) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; r\in R
\tag{2}
\]

(If the same RSU is used for both trips, the inequality forces a feasible temporal order.)

3. **Similarity variable definition** – \(u_{t,r}=1\) only if the original assignment is kept.  
Assume that the original plan is known via a parameter \(x^{\text{orig}}_{t,r}\in\{0,1\}\).

\[
u_{t,r}\le x^{\text{orig}}_{t,r} \qquad \forall t,r
\tag{3a}
\]
\[
u_{t,r}\le x_{t,r} \qquad \forall t,r
\tag{3b}
\]
\[
u_{t,r}\ge x^{\text{orig}}_{t,r}+x_{t,r}-1 \qquad \forall t,r
\tag{3c}
\]

Thus \(u_{t,r}=1\) iff the original and new assignments coincide.

### 4.2 Delay limits  

\[
0 \le y_{t} \le \Delta^{\max} \qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{4}
\]

### 4.3 Shunting‑movement activation  

A shunting movement can only be scheduled if the trip actually visits the station:

\[
z_{t,s,k} \le a_{t,s} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S,\; k\in K_s
\tag{5}
\]

If a movement is cancelled, its start‑time and duration are forced to zero:

\[
\tau_{t,s,k} \le M\,(1-\omega_{t,s,k}) \qquad \forall t,s,k
\tag{6a}
\]
\[
\delta_{t,s,k} \le M\,(1-\omega_{t,s,k}) \qquad \forall t,s,k
\tag{6b}
\]

Conversely, if the movement is performed, cancellation must be zero:

\[
\omega_{t,s,k} \le 1- z_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall t,s,k
\tag{6c}
\]

### 4.4 Timing of shunting movements  

The shunting start time must respect the (possibly delayed) arrival of the train at the station:

\[
\tau_{t,s,k} \;\ge\; \overline{P}_{t} + y_{t} - M\,(1-z_{t,s,k}) \qquad \forall t,s,k
\tag{7}
\]

The duration of a shunting movement is bounded by the maximum allowed shunting delay:

\[
0 \le \delta_{t,s,k} \le \theta^{\max} \; z_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall t,s,k
\tag{8}
\]

The finish time of the shunting movement is therefore \(\tau_{t,s,k}+\delta_{t,s,k}\).

### 4.5 Track‑capacity (resource) constraints  

For every pair of shunting movements that use the same track, a minimum headway must be respected. Using the classic “big‑M” disjunctive formulation:

\[
\tau_{t,s,k} + \delta_{t,s,k} \;\le\; \tau_{t',s,k} \;+\; M\; w_{t,t',s,k}
\qquad \forall t<t',\; s\in S,\; k\in K_s
\tag{9a}
\]

\[
\tau_{t',s,k} + \delta_{t',s,k} \;\le\; \tau_{t,s,k} \;+\; M\;(1-w_{t,t',s,k})
\qquad \forall t<t',\; s\in S,\; k\in K_s
\tag{9b}
\]

where \(w_{t,t',s,k}\in\{0,1\}\) decides the ordering of the two movements.  
If either movement is cancelled (\(\omega=1\)) the corresponding constraints become inactive automatically because \(\delta\) and \(\tau\) are forced to zero.

An alternative, more compact formulation (when the number of movements is moderate) uses a **cumulative** constraint, but the disjunctive form above is linear and fits MILP solvers.

### 4.6 Interaction with passenger‑train timetable  

If a shunting movement on a track forces a delay of *other* passenger trains that use the same track segment, we model this by allowing a *buffer* delay on those trains (already captured by \(y_t\)). To keep the model linear we impose a simple **conflict‑avoidance** rule:

For every passenger train \(t\) that uses a track segment \(e\) at station \(s\) during the interval \([P_t+y_t,\;\overline{P}_t+y_t]\) and for every shunting movement \((t',s,k)\) that occupies the same physical track (parameter \(b_{e,k}=1\) if shunting track \(k\) blocks segment \(e\)) we require:

\[
\bigl(P_t + y_t \bigr) \;\ge\; \tau_{t',s,k} + \delta_{t',s,k} - M\,(1-b_{e,k}) \quad\text{or}\quad
\bigl(\overline{P}_t + y_t \bigr) \;\le\; \tau_{t',s,k} + M\,(1-b_{e,k})
\tag{10}
\]

In practice this is linearised using additional binary ordering variables analogous to (9).

### 4.7 Feasibility of shunting at the two stations  

The paper assumes that shunting **is** allowed at Utrecht and Rotterdam only during the disruption window \([T^{\text{start}}, T^{\text{end}}]\). We enforce:

\[
\tau_{t,s,k} \ge T^{\text{start}} \;-\; M\,(1-z_{t,s,k}) \qquad \forall s\in\{Utrecht, Rotterdam\},\; t,k
\tag{11a}
\]
\[
\tau_{t,s,k} + \delta_{t,s,k} \le T^{\text{end}} \;+\; M\,(1-z_{t,s,k}) \qquad \forall s\in\{Utrecht, Rotterdam\},\; t,k
\tag{11b}
\]

All other stations have the default \(z_{t,s,k}=0\).

### 4.8 Logical linking of shunting to RSU assignment (optional)  

If a shunting movement is performed, the RSU that is currently coupled to the train must be the one that will continue after the movement. This can be expressed by:

\[
z_{t,s,k} \le \sum_{r\in R} x_{t,r}\;x_{t',r} \qquad \forall (t,t')\text{ consecutive trips linked by shunting at }s
\tag{12}
\]

(Linearisation uses additional binaries; omitted here for brevity.)

---

## 5. Summary of the MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\; & \alpha\sum_{t,r}c^{\text{change}}_{t,r}(x_{t,r}-u_{t,r})
      + \beta\sum_{t}c^{\text{delay}}_{t}y_{t}
      + \gamma\Big(\sum_{t,s,k}c^{\text{shunt}}_{s,k}z_{t,s,k}
                 + M\sum_{t,s,k}\omega_{t,s,k}\Big)\\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } & \text{(1)–(12) as listed above}\\
              & x_{t,r}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\},\;
                \omega_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\},\;
                w_{t,t',s,k}\in\{0,1\},\\
              & y_{t},\;\tau_{t,s,k},\;\delta_{t,s,k}\ge 0.
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 6. Remarks & Assumptions  

| # | Assumption made (not explicit in the text) |
|---|-------------------------------------------|
| A1 | Maximum passenger‑train delay \(\Delta^{\max}=5\) min (typical buffer). |
| A2 | Maximum shunting‑movement delay \(\theta^{\max}=3\) min (short driver‑delay). |
| A3 | Headway between two shunting movements on the same track \(d^{\text{min}}_{s,k}=2\) min (safety margin). |
| A4 | Cost parameters \(c^{\text{delay}}_t, c^{\text{shunt}}_{s,k}, c^{\text{change}}_{t,r}\) are linear and known from the operator’s cost database. |
| A5 | The disruption window \([T^{\text{start}},T^{\text{end}}]\) is given (e.g., 60 min). |
| A6 | The original RSU‑trip assignment \(x^{\text{orig}}_{t,r}\) is known and used for the similarity objective. |
| A7 | All shunting tracks are modelled as single‑capacity resources (one movement at a time). |
| A8 | The binary ordering variables \(w_{t,t',s,k}\) are introduced for each pair of shunting movements on the same track; the number of such pairs is assumed tractable for the instances considered (the paper reports solving 7 instances in a few minutes). |
| A9 | The “cancellation penalty” uses a big‑\(M\) term to discourage cancelling shunting movements unless infeasible. |
| A10| The model can be used as the master problem in a **Combinatorial Benders** decomposition: the infrastructure model returns feasibility cuts that are linear in the \(z\)-variables, which can be added iteratively. |

---

### How the model reflects the paper’s contributions  

* **Exact approach** – the MILP captures both composition and infrastructure constraints simultaneously; when solved to optimality it yields the same solution as the combinatorial Benders scheme described.  
* **Iterative heuristic** – the same formulation can be used in a *column‑generation*‑like loop where shunting variables \(z_{t,s,k}\) are introduced one‑by‑one, mimicking the interaction between rolling‑stock and infrastructure dispatchers.  
* **Objective balance** – the weighted sum (α,β,γ) directly mirrors the three‑fold goal of (i) staying close to the original plan, (ii) minimising passenger delay, and (iii) limiting shunting effort, as discussed in the introduction.  
* **Infrastructure feasibility** – constraints (5)–(11) guarantee that each shunting movement fits into the available track capacity and respects the disruption‑time window, which is the novel aspect of the research.  

The presented MILP is a **complete, linear model** that can be handed to any standard MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP) and is ready for computational experiments on the instances described in the paper.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP)**  
The model below captures, in a single mixed‑integer linear program, the three‑fold decision problem that arises when a partial‑segment blockage forces a high‑speed railway operator to (i) **retime** trains, (ii) **reorder / reroute** them on the opposite track, and (iii) **choose feasible speed profiles** for every train‑run.  

All notation, sets, parameters and decision variables are defined first, followed by the objective function and the complete list of linear constraints.  Wherever data are not supplied in the description, a **reasonable assumption** is explicitly stated.

---

## 1. Sets, Indices and Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning (assumption) |
|--------|----------------------|
| **T** = {1,…,|T|} | Set of trains that are scheduled to run during the planning horizon (including those that may be cancelled). |
| **S** = {1,…,|S|} | Set of stations (including the origin and terminal of each train). |
| **L** = {1,…,|L|} | Set of line‑segments (track sections) between two consecutive stations. Each segment *ℓ* has a **direction** d(ℓ) ∈ {+1 (forward), –1 (backward)}. |
| **K** = {1,…,|K|} | Set of **time‑intervals** used to discretise the planning horizon (e.g. 1‑minute slots). |
| **B** ⊆ L | Subset of line‑segments that are **blocked** (partial blockage) during a known time window \([t^{\text{blk}}_{start},t^{\text{blk}}_{end}]\). |
| **P** = {1,…,|P|} | Set of **pre‑computed speed‑profile plans** for each train *i* on each feasible route (see Section 4). A plan *p* contains a complete schedule of departure/arrival times on every visited segment and the associated energy consumption. |
| **R\_i** ⊆ P | Feasible plan set for train *i* (generated by a speed‑profile generation sub‑problem). |
| **Δk** | Length of time‑interval *k* (e.g. 1 min). |
| **c\_p** | Energy consumption (or cost) of plan *p* (kWh). |
| **τ\_{i,ℓ}^{\min}, τ\_{i,ℓ}^{\max}** | Minimum / maximum feasible travel time for train *i* on segment ℓ (derived from physical limits, speed limits, and safety headways). |
| **d\_{i,s}^{\text{sched}}** | Scheduled departure time of train *i* from station *s* (original timetable). |
| **a\_{i,s}^{\text{sched}}** | Scheduled arrival time of train *i* at station *s*. |
| **M** | A large constant (big‑M) used for logical constraints. |
| **α** ∈ [0,1] | Weight of the energy‑efficiency term in the objective (assumption: operator wants a trade‑off between delay and energy). |
| **β** > 0 | Penalty weight for train cancellation (assumption: high penalty to avoid unnecessary cancellations). |
| **γ** > 0 | Penalty weight for violating dwell‑time windows (see later). |

---

## 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|----------|
| **x\_{i,p}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if plan *p* ∈ R\_i is selected for train *i*; 0 otherwise. |
| **y\_{i}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if train *i* is **cancelled**; 0 otherwise. (If y\_i = 1 then all x\_{i,p}=0.) |
| **t\_{i,ℓ,k}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if train *i* occupies segment ℓ during time‑interval *k* (i.e. its front passes ℓ at that slot). |
| **d\_{i,s}** ≥ 0 | Continuous | Actual **departure time** of train *i* from station *s* (in minutes from horizon start). |
| **a\_{i,s}** ≥ 0 | Continuous | Actual **arrival time** of train *i* at station *s*. |
| **z\_{i,ℓ,k}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if train *i* **starts** traversing segment ℓ at the beginning of interval *k* (used to enforce travel‑time limits). |
| **w\_{i,ℓ,k}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if train *i* **finishes** traversing segment ℓ at the end of interval *k*. |
| **u\_{i,ℓ,k}** ∈ {0,1} | Binary | 1 if train *i* **uses** the opposite‑track direction on segment ℓ (i.e. rerouted). |
| **δ\_{i,s}** ≥ 0 | Continuous | Dwell‑time of train *i* at station *s* (departure – arrival). |

---

## 3. Linking Variables to Selected Plans  

Each plan *p* for train *i* specifies a deterministic schedule of segment‑occupancy times \(\hat t^{p}_{i,ℓ,k}\) (0/1) and a deterministic dwell‑time \(\hat δ^{p}_{i,s}\). The following constraints force the operational variables to follow the chosen plan.

### 3.1 Plan selection
\[
\sum_{p\in R_i} x_{i,p} + y_i = 1 \qquad \forall i\in T
\tag{1}
\]

### 3.2 Occupancy consistency
\[
t_{i,\ell,k} = \sum_{p\in R_i} \hat t^{p}_{i,\ell,k}\, x_{i,p} \qquad \forall i,\ell,k
\tag{2}
\]

### 3.3 Arrival / departure times
\[
a_{i,s} = \sum_{p\in R_i} \hat a^{p}_{i,s}\, x_{i,p} \qquad
d_{i,s} = \sum_{p\in R_i} \hat d^{p}_{i,s}\, x_{i,p} \qquad \forall i,s
\tag{3}
\]

### 3.4 Dwell‑time definition
\[
\delta_{i,s}= d_{i,s}-a_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,s
\tag{4}
\]

### 3.5 Rerouting indicator
If a plan uses the opposite track on a blocked segment, the plan data set the corresponding \(u^{p}_{i,\ell}=1\). Then:
\[
u_{i,\ell}= \sum_{p\in R_i} u^{p}_{i,\ell}\, x_{i,p} \qquad \forall i,\ell\in B
\tag{5}
\]

---

## 4. Physical and Operational Constraints  

### 4.1 Travel‑time limits on each segment  
For each train *i* and segment ℓ that it traverses, the total number of occupied intervals must lie between the minimum and maximum travel times:

\[
\tau^{\min}_{i,\ell}\; \le \; \sum_{k\in K} \Delta k \, t_{i,\ell,k} \; \le \; \tau^{\max}_{i,\ell}
\qquad \forall i,\ell\in L_i
\tag{6}
\]

where \(L_i\) is the set of segments belonging to the route of train *i* (as defined by the selected plan).

### 4.2 Blockage feasibility  
A train may occupy a blocked segment ℓ only **outside** the blockage window *or* only if it uses the opposite track (i.e. rerouted). Let \(K^{\text{blk}} = \{k\mid \text{interval }k \subseteq [t^{\text{blk}}_{start},t^{\text{blk}}_{end}]\}\).

\[
t_{i,\ell,k} \le 1- u_{i,\ell} \qquad
\forall i,\ell\in B,\; k\in K^{\text{blk}}
\tag{7}
\]

If \(u_{i,\ell}=1\) (train uses opposite track), the inequality becomes non‑binding, allowing the train to occupy the segment during the blockage.

### 4.3 Headway (conflict‑free) constraints  
For any two trains *i* and *j* that travel **in the same direction** on the same physical track (including opposite‑track usage), a minimum safety headway \(h\) (in minutes) must be respected. Using the occupancy binaries:

\[
\sum_{k'=k}^{k+\lceil h/\Delta k\rceil} t_{i,\ell,k'} + \sum_{k'=k}^{k+\lceil h/\Delta k\rceil} t_{j,\ell,k'} \le 1
\qquad \forall \ell\in L,\; \forall i<j,\; \forall k\in K
\tag{8}
\]

If the trains travel in opposite directions on the same physical track, a **bidirectional conflict** is also prohibited; the same constraint (8) applies because the occupancy variables refer to the *track* (not the direction).

### 4.4 Dwell‑time windows (platform capacity)  
Each station *s* has a maximal allowed dwell‑time \( \delta^{\max}_s\) (e.g., due to platform turnover).  

\[
\delta_{i,s} \le \delta^{\max}_s \qquad \forall i,s
\tag{9}
\]

A penalty for exceeding a soft bound \( \delta^{\text{soft}}_s\) can be added later (see objective).

### 4.5 Logical linking of start/finish variables (optional, improves linearity)  

\[
z_{i,\ell,k} \le t_{i,\ell,k} \qquad
w_{i,\ell,k} \le t_{i,\ell,k} \qquad \forall i,\ell,k
\tag{10}
\]

\[
\sum_{k\in K} z_{i,\ell,k}=1,\;\;
\sum_{k\in K} w_{i,\ell,k}=1 \qquad \forall i,\ell\in L_i
\tag{11}
\]

These ensure each train has exactly one start and one finish time on each segment, which together with (6) enforce the travel‑time bounds.

### 4.6 Cancellation logic  

If a train is cancelled, all its occupancy, arrival/departure and dwell variables are forced to zero:

\[
t_{i,\ell,k} \le 1-y_i \qquad \forall i,\ell,k
\tag{12}
\]

\[
a_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i),\; d_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \qquad \forall i,s
\tag{13}
\]

---

## 5. Objective Function  

The operator wishes to **minimise a weighted sum of total energy consumption, total passenger delay, and cancellation penalties**.  

*Passenger delay* is measured as the absolute deviation from the original schedule (both arrival and departure). Because the model is linear, we use a **positive‑only deviation** (late arrivals) and a penalty for early arrivals (which may cause idle platform time).  

Define:

\[
\text{Delay}_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} = \max\{0, a_{i,s} - a^{\text{sched}}_{i,s}\}
\]
\[
\text{Delay}_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} = \max\{0, d_{i,s} - d^{\text{sched}}_{i,s}\}
\]

These are linearised with auxiliary non‑negative variables \( \theta^{a}_{i,s},\theta^{d}_{i,s}\):

\[
\theta^{a}_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a^{\text{sched}}_{i,s},\;
\theta^{a}_{i,s} \ge 0
\tag{14}
\]
\[
\theta^{d}_{i,s} \ge d_{i,s} - d^{\text{sched}}_{i,s},\;
\theta^{d}_{i,s} \ge 0
\tag{15}
\]

The total objective is:

\[
\min \;
\underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{p\in R_i} c_{p}\, x_{i,p}}_{\text{Energy consumption}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{(1-\alpha)\Bigl[ \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\bigl(\theta^{a}_{i,s}+ \theta^{d}_{i,s}\bigr) \Bigr]}_{\text{Passenger delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\beta \sum_{i\in T} y_i}_{\text{Cancellation penalty}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\gamma \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\max\{0,\delta_{i,s}-\delta^{\text{soft}}_s\}}_{\text{Soft dwell‑time penalty}}
\tag{16}
\]

The last term can be linearised by introducing slack variables \( \psi_{i,s}\ge 0\) with:

\[
\psi_{i,s} \ge \delta_{i,s} - \delta^{\text{soft}}_s,\qquad \psi_{i,s}\ge 0
\tag{17}
\]

and then using \(\sum_{i,s}\psi_{i,s}\) in (16).

---

## 6. Summary of the MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \text{(16)}\\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{Plan selection } (1)\\
& \text{Occupancy linking } (2)-(5)\\
& \text{Physical feasibility } (6)-(9)\\
& \text{Headway / conflict‑free } (8)\\
& \text{Logical start/finish } (10)-(11)\\
& \text{Cancellation logic } (12)-(13)\\
& \text{Delay linearisation } (14)-(15)\\
& \text{Dwell‑time soft‑penalty linearisation } (17)\\

The MILP only selects among these pre‑computed plans, which guarantees linearity.

Text:
**Variables**

- \(y_{t,\tau}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(t\in\mathcal T\) departs at discrete time \(\tau\in\mathcal{K}\).  
- \(z_{t,\tau}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(t\) arrives at time \(\tau\).  
- \(x_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(t\) traverses track segment \(s\in\mathcal S\) (original or rerouted).  
- \(v_{t,s}\) – speed of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) (km/h), bounded by \(v^{\min}\le v_{t,s}\le v^{\max}\).  
- \(u_{t,\tau}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(t\) performs an acceleration/deceleration decision at time \(\tau\).  
- \(w_{t,s,\tau}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(t\) occupies segment \(s\) during period \(\tau\).  
- \(\lambda_{t,s}^{k}\ge 0\) – convex‑combination weights for a piece‑wise linear approximation of travel time on segment \(s\) (index \(k\) runs over the break‑points).  
- \(\operatorname{travel}_{t,s}\ge 0\) – approximated travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\).  

**Auxiliary linear expressions**

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{departure time of }t &: \; d_t=\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal K}\tau\,y_{t,\tau},\\[2mm]
\text{arrival   time of }t &: \; a_t=\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal K}\tau\,z_{t,\tau}.
\end{aligned}
\]

**Objective function**

\[
\min \; 
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal K}
\tau\bigl(d_t-\bar d_t\bigr)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
\alpha\underbrace{\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}
e_s\,v_{t,s}\,\bar\tau_{t,s}}_{\text{energy consumption}},
\]

where \(\bar d_t\) is the original scheduled departure of train \(t\),  
\(\bar\tau_{t,s}\) is the nominal (schedule) travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\),  
\(e_s\) is the energy‑cost coefficient of segment \(s\) and \(\alpha>0\) balances the two terms.

**Constraints**

1. **Unique departure / arrival**  

\[
\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal K} y_{t,\tau}=1 \qquad\forall t\in\mathcal T,
\qquad
\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal K} z_{t,\tau}=1 \qquad\forall t\in\mathcal T.
\]

2. **Piece‑wise linear travel‑time approximation**  

Let \(\bigl(v^{k},\beta^{k}\bigr)\) be the speed break‑points and the corresponding
travel‑time factor (so that \(\operatorname{travel}_{t,s}= \sum_k \lambda_{t,s}^{k}\,\beta^{k}\,\bar\tau_{t,s}\)).  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{k}\lambda_{t,s}^{k}=x_{t,s} &&\forall t,s,\\
&\sum_{k}\lambda_{t,s}^{k}\,v^{k}=v_{t,s} &&\forall t,s,\\
&\operatorname{travel}_{t,s}= \sum_{k}\lambda_{t,s}^{k}\,\beta^{k}\,\bar\tau_{t,s} &&\forall t,s,\\
&\lambda_{t,s}^{k}\ge 0 &&\forall t,s,k.
\end{aligned}
\]

3. **Time‑consistency (departure + total travel ≤ arrival)**  

\[
\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\operatorname{travel}_{t,s}
\le a_t-d_t+M\!\left(1-\sum_{s}x_{t,s}\right) \qquad\forall t,
\]

where \(M\) is a sufficiently large constant.

4. **Capacity of each segment (bidirectional)**  

\[
\sum_{t\in\mathcal T} w_{t,s,\tau}\le \kappa_s \qquad\forall s\in\mathcal S,\;\forall \tau\in\mathcal K,
\]

with \(\kappa_s\) the (bidirectional) capacity of segment \(s\).

5. **Linking occupancy to usage and timing** (big‑M linearisation)

\[
\begin{aligned}
&w_{t,s,\tau}\le x_{t,s} &&\forall t,s,\tau,\\
&w_{t,s,\tau}\ge x_{t,s}+ \frac{d_t-\tau}{M}-1 &&\forall t,s,\tau,\\
&w_{t,s,\tau}\ge x_{t,s}+ \frac{\tau-a_t}{M}-1 &&\forall t,s,\tau.
\end{aligned}
\]

6. **Disruption handling** – if segment \(s\) is blocked during
\([\Delta^{\text{start}}_s,\Delta^{\text{end}}_s]\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
&b_{t,s}\in\{0,1\} &&\text{(train \(t\) overlaps the blocked window)},\\
&d_t\le \Delta^{\text{end}}_s+M(1-b_{t,s}) &&\forall t,s,\\
&a_t\ge \Delta^{\text{start}}_s-M(1-b_{t,s}) &&\forall t,s,\\
&x_{t,s}\le 1-b_{t,s} &&\forall t,s.
\end{aligned}
\]

7. **Speed limits** – already enforced by variable bounds  

\[
v^{\min}\le v_{t,s}\le v^{\max}\qquad\forall t,s.
\]

8. **Acceleration / deceleration limits**  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&v_{t,s'}-v_{t,s}\le \Delta v_{\max}+M(1-u_{t,\tau})\\
&v_{t,s}-v_{t,s'}\le \Delta v_{\max}+M(1-u_{t,\tau})
\qquad\forall t,\tau,\; s,s'\text{ occupied at }\tau,\tau+1,
\end{aligned}
\]

where \(\Delta v_{\max}\) is the maximum admissible speed change per period.

9. **Minimum dwell time at stations**  

Assuming each train visits stations in order, for two consecutive segments
\(s\) and \(s'\) that meet at a station,

\[
\operatorname{travel}_{t,s'}\ge d^{\min}\qquad\forall t,\; (s,s')\text{ consecutive},
\]

with \(d^{\min}\) the minimum dwell time (in periods).

10. **Rerouting mutual‑exclusion** – for a blocked segment \(s\) and its opposite
track \(s^{\text{opp}}\),

\[
x_{t,s}+x_{t,s^{\text{opp}}}\le 1\qquad\forall t.
\]

**Assumptions (clearly stated)**  

- Time is discretised into equal periods \(\tau\in\mathcal K\).  
- Each train uses at most one departure and one arrival time (binary variables).  
- Travel time on a segment is approximated by a piece‑wise linear function of speed; the break‑points are pre‑specified.  
- Capacity \(\kappa_s\) is the total number of trains (in both directions) that may occupy segment \(s\) during any period.  
- The disruption window \([\Delta^{\text{start}}_s,\Delta^{\text{end}}_s]\) is known a‑priori for every affected segment.  
- Energy consumption on a segment is linear in the chosen speed (coefficient \(e_s\)).  
- Minimum dwell time \(d^{\min}\) is the same for all stations (can be made station‑specific if required).  
- Big‑M constants are chosen large enough not to cut off any feasible solution but small enough to keep the model numerically stable.

The presented formulation is a **complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) model** that simultaneously decides train departure/arrival times, segment selection (including possible rerouting), speed profiles, and acceleration actions while respecting disruption constraints, capacity, dwell times, and energy efficiency.

**Variables**

- \(x_{tp}\) – binary, 1 if train \(t\in\mathcal T\) uses route \(p\in\mathcal P\) (original or a rerouted alternative).  
- \(y_{tl}\) – binary, 1 if train \(t\) traverses segment \(l\in\mathcal L\).  
- \(r_{tl}\) – binary, 1 if train \(t\) uses a rerouted version of segment \(l\) (required when \(l\) is blocked).  
- \(A_{ts}\) – actual arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\in\mathcal S\).  
- \(D_{ts}\) – actual departure time of train \(t\) from station \(s\).  
- \(\tau_{tl}\) – actual travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(l\).  
- \(z_{t t' l}\) – binary, 1 if train \(t\) passes segment \(l\) before train \(t'\) (conflict‑free ordering).  

**Parameters (assumed given)**  

- \(a^{0}_{ts}\) – scheduled arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\).  
- \(d^{0}_{ts}\) – scheduled departure time of train \(t\) from station \(s\).  
- \(\underline{\tau}_{tl},\ \overline{\tau}_{tl}\) – lower/upper bounds on travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(l\).  
- \(e_{tl}\) – energy cost per unit travel time on segment \(l\) for train \(t\).  
- \(\underline{dwell}_{ts}\) – minimum dwell time of train \(t\) at station \(s\).  
- \(B_l\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if segment \(l\) is blocked during the disruption window, 0 otherwise.  
- \(\delta_{pl}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if route \(p\) uses segment \(l\).  
- \(\text{entry}(l),\ \text{exit}(l)\) – entry and exit stations of segment \(l\).  
- \(M\) – a sufficiently large constant (big‑M).  
- \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) – weight of the delay term in the objective (e.g., \(\alpha=0.7\)).  

**Objective**

\[
\min\; \underbrace{\alpha\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\bigl(A_{ts}-a^{0}_{ts}\bigr)}_{\text{total passenger delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{(1-\alpha)\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{l\in\mathcal L} e_{tl}\,\tau_{tl}}_{\text{total energy consumption}} .
\]

**Constraints**

1. **Route selection** (exactly one route per train)  
   \[
   \sum_{p\in\mathcal P} x_{tp}=1 \qquad\forall t\in\mathcal T .
   \]

2. **Link route choice to segment usage**  
   \[
   y_{tl}= \sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\delta_{pl}\,x_{tp} \qquad\forall t\in\mathcal T,\;l\in\mathcal L .
   \]

3. **Travel‑time bounds** (only if the segment is used)  
   \[
   \underline{\tau}_{tl}\; y_{tl}\le \tau_{tl}\le \overline{\tau}_{tl}\; y_{tl}
   \qquad\forall t,l .
   \]

4. **Blockage handling** – a blocked segment cannot be traversed unless the train reroutes  
   \[
   y_{tl}\le 1- r_{tl}\qquad\forall t,l\text{ with }B_l=1 .
   \]

5. **Arrival‑departure relationship** (for every station except the first)  
   \[
   A_{ts}= D_{t,\text{prev}(s)} + \sum_{l\in\mathcal L}\tau_{tl}\,
          \mathbf{1}\bigl\{\text{entry}(l)=\text{prev}(s),\ \text{exit}(l)=s\bigr\}
   \qquad\forall t,\; s\neq s_{\text{first}} .
   \]

6. **Minimum dwell time**  
   \[
   D_{ts}\ge A_{ts}+ \underline{dwell}_{ts}\qquad\forall t,s .
   \]

7. **Conflict‑free ordering on shared segments**  
   For any two distinct trains using the same segment,
   \[
   z_{t t' l}+z_{t' t l}=1 \qquad\forall t\neq t',\;l\text{ with }y_{tl}=y_{t'l}=1 ,
   \]
   \[
   D_{t,\text{exit}(l)}\le A_{t',\text{entry}(l)}+M\bigl(1- z_{t t' l}\bigr)
   \qquad\forall t\neq t',\;l\text{ with }y_{tl}=y_{t'l}=1 ,
   \]
   \[
   D_{t',\text{exit}(l)}\le A_{t,\text{entry}(l)}+M\bigl(1- z_{t' t l}\bigr)
   \qquad\forall t\neq t',\;l\text{ with }y_{tl}=y_{t'l}=1 .
   \]

8. **Variable domains**  
   \[
   x_{tp},y_{tl},r_{tl},z_{t t' l}\in\{0,1\},\qquad
   A_{ts},D_{ts},\tau_{tl}\ge 0 .
   \]

---

**Assumptions (added for completeness)**  

- The railway line is linear; each segment connects two consecutive stations.  
- The disruption window is represented by the binary block indicator \(B_l\); detailed time‑window constraints are omitted for brevity.  
- Energy consumption is approximated as linear in travel time on each segment (a piece‑wise linear approximation can replace this if needed).  
- Headway constraints are captured implicitly by the ordering variables \(z_{t t' l}\).  

The model above fully describes the integrated train‑rescheduling and speed‑management problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockages as a mixed‑integer linear program (MILP).

Text:
Below is a **complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) formulation** for the **Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP)** under a partial‑segment blockage.  
All sets, parameters, decision variables, the objective function and the linear constraints are listed together with the modelling assumptions that are needed to obtain a linear model.  Whenever data are not given in the description, a reasonable assumption is stated explicitly.

---

## 1.  Index Sets  

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\). |
| \(S\) | Set of stations (including depot and terminal), indexed by \(s\). |
| \(L\) | Set of line‑segments (track sections) between two successive stations, indexed by \(\ell\). |
| \(B\subseteq L\) | Sub‑set of **blocked** segments (the disruption area). |
| \(\mathcal{P}_t\) | Set of **pre‑defined speed‑plans** (time‑indexed speed profiles) that train \(t\) can follow on each segment \(\ell\).  (These plans are generated in a preprocessing step; each plan is a feasible piece‑wise linear speed trajectory.) |
| \(K\) | Set of **time‑points** used for discretisation of the horizon, indexed by \(k\).  (Typically 1‑min or 5‑min slots.) |
| \(\mathcal{R}_t\subseteq\{0,1\}\) | Set of admissible **routing decisions** for train \(t\) (0 = original direction, 1 = use opposite track inside the blockage). |

---

## 2.  Parameters (assumed known)

| Symbol | Meaning | Typical values / source |
|--------|---------|--------------------------|
| \(a_{\ell}^{\min}, a_{\ell}^{\max}\) | Minimum / maximum **acceleration** on segment \(\ell\) (m s\(^{-2}\)). | From train technical data. |
| \(d_{\ell}^{\min}, d_{\ell}^{\max}\) | Minimum / maximum **deceleration** on segment \(\ell\) (positive numbers). | From train technical data. |
| \(v_{\ell}^{\max}\) | Maximum admissible speed on segment \(\ell\) (m s\(^{-1}\)). | Infrastructure limit. |
| \(L_{\ell}\) | Physical length of segment \(\ell\) (km). | Track geometry. |
| \(E_{t,\ell}^p\) | **Energy consumption** (kWh) of train \(t\) when it follows speed‑plan \(p\in\mathcal{P}_t\) on segment \(\ell\). | Obtained from a linearised energy model (see Assumption A‑4). |
| \(\tau_{t,s}^{\text{orig}}\) | Original scheduled **arrival** time of train \(t\) at station \(s\) (minutes from horizon start). | Timetable. |
| \(\tau_{t,s}^{\text{orig,dep}}\) | Original scheduled **departure** time of train \(t\) from station \(s\). | Timetable. |
| \(\Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{\min}\) | Minimum dwell time at any station (minutes). | Regulation (e.g., 2 min). |
| \(\Delta^{\text{head}}_{\min}\) | Minimum **headway** (time separation) between two successive trains moving in the **same direction** on the same segment (minutes). | Safety rule. |
| \(\Delta^{\text{conf}}_{\min}\) | Minimum **conflict‑free interval** for two opposite‑direction trains sharing a single track (minutes). | Safety rule for bidirectional usage. |
| \(\beta_{t}^{\text{cancel}}\) | Penalty cost for **cancelling** train \(t\). | Large constant (e.g., 10 000). |
| \(M\) | Big‑M constant (larger than longest possible travel time). |   |
| \(\theta^{\text{block}}_{\ell,k}\in\{0,1\}\) | Equals 1 if segment \(\ell\in B\) is **blocked** during time slot \(k\); 0 otherwise. | Known from disruption forecast. |
| \(\omega_{t}^{\text{delay}}\) | Weight (cost) per minute of delay for train \(t\). | Service‑level agreement. |
| \(\omega_{t}^{\text{early}}\) | Weight per minute of **early arrival** (negative if early is discouraged). | Policy. |
| \(\omega^{\text{energy}}\) | Global weight for total energy consumption (kWh). | Decision‑maker preference. |

---

## 3.  Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | **Actual arrival time** of train \(t\) at station \(s\) (minutes). |
| \(x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | **Actual departure time** of train \(t\) from station \(s\). |
| \(y_{t,\ell}^{p}\) | Binary | Equals 1 if train \(t\) uses speed‑plan \(p\in\mathcal{P}_t\) on segment \(\ell\). |
| \(z_{t,\ell}^{k}\) | Binary | Equals 1 if train \(t\) **occupies** segment \(\ell\) during time slot \(k\). |
| \(r_{t}\) | Binary | 0 = train follows its original route; 1 = train **reroutes** (uses opposite track inside the blockage). |
| \(c_{t}\) | Binary | 1 = train \(t\) is **cancelled**; 0 = it runs. |
| \(\delta_{t,s}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | **Delay** (positive) of train \(t\) at station \(s\) relative to original schedule: \(\delta_{t,s}=x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}}-\tau_{t,s}^{\text{orig}}\) if positive, 0 otherwise (modelled with linearisation). |
| \(\epsilon_{t,s}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | **Earliness** (positive) of train \(t\) at station \(s\): \(\epsilon_{t,s}= \tau_{t,s}^{\text{orig}}-x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}}\) if positive, 0 otherwise. |
| \(\eta_{t}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | **Total energy consumption** of train \(t\) (kWh). |

Auxiliary binary variables are introduced for the classic “max(…,0)” linearisation of delay/earliness and for the head‑way/conflict constraints (see constraints below).

---

## 4.  Modelling Assumptions  

1. **A‑1 (Discrete time horizon).** The planning horizon is divided into equal slots \(k\in K\) (e.g., 1 min). All train‑segment occupancies are modelled per slot.  
2. **A‑2 (Pre‑computed linear speed‑plans).** For each train‑segment pair a finite set \(\mathcal{P}_t\) of feasible piece‑wise‑linear speed trajectories is generated beforehand respecting acceleration, deceleration and speed limits. Selecting a plan is therefore a binary choice.  
3. **A‑3 (Linear energy model).** Energy consumption of a plan is approximated by a linear function of the travelled distance and the average speed (or obtained directly from simulation). Hence a constant \(E_{t,\ell}^{p}\) can be used in the objective.  
4. **A‑4 (Rerouting only inside the blocked zone).** If \(r_t=1\), the train uses the opposite track **only** while traversing any \(\ell\in B\); outside the blockage it follows the original direction. This yields a simple binary “direction” variable per train.  
5. **A‑5 (Cancellation).** When a train is cancelled (\(c_t=1\)) all its variables are forced to zero; a large penalty \(\beta_t^{\text{cancel}}\) guarantees that cancellation occurs only when necessary.  
6. **A‑6 (Conflict‑free occupancy).** Two trains travelling in the **same direction** on the same segment need a minimum headway \(\Delta^{\text{head}}_{\min}\). Two trains travelling in **opposite directions** on a single‑track segment need a larger separation \(\Delta^{\text{conf}}_{\min}\). These are enforced through the binary occupancy variables \(z_{t,\ell}^{k}\).  
7. **A‑7 (Blockage time windows).** The binary parameters \(\theta^{\text{block}}_{\ell,k}\) indicate exactly when a segment is unavailable for the original direction. If a train tries to occupy a blocked segment in the blocked direction, the model forces either rerouting (\(r_t=1\)) or cancellation.  

All assumptions are standard in the railway‑rescheduling literature and keep the model linear.

---

## 5.  Objective Function  

The decision maker wants to **(i)** minimise passenger service degradation (delay/earliness), **(ii)** avoid cancellations, and **(iii)** minimise total energy consumption. A weighted sum is used:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & 
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} \Big( \omega^{\text{delay}}_{t}\,\delta_{t,s} \;+\; \omega^{\text{early}}_{t}\,\epsilon_{t,s} \Big)}_{\text{Delay / early penalties}} \\
& + \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} \beta_{t}^{\text{cancel}} \, c_{t}}_{\text{Cancellation penalty}}\\
& + \underbrace{\omega^{\text{energy}} \, \sum_{t\in T}\eta_{t}}_{\text{Energy cost}} .
\end{aligned}
\tag{Obj}
\]

---

## 6.  Constraints  

### 6.1  Time‑flow constraints (timetable consistency)

For every train \(t\) and every pair of consecutive stations \((s,s')\) linked by segment \(\ell\):

\[
\boxed{
x_{t,s'}^{\text{arr}} \;\ge\; x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} \;+\; \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t} \tau_{t,\ell}^{p}\, y_{t,\ell}^{p} \;-\; M\,(c_t)
}
\qquad \forall t,\;\forall (s,s')\;\text{with}\;\ell\in L(s,s')
\tag{C1}
\]

where \(\tau_{t,\ell}^{p}\) is the **travel time** of plan \(p\) on segment \(\ell\) (pre‑computed).  

Departure after arrival with minimum dwell time:

\[
\boxed{
x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} \;\ge\; x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} \;+\; \Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{\min} \;-\; M\,(c_t)
}
\qquad \forall t,\; \forall s\in S\setminus\{ \text{terminal}\}
\tag{C2}
\]

### 6.2  Delay / earliness linearisation  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\delta_{t,s} \ge x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} - \tau_{t,s}^{\text{orig}} && \forall t,s \\
&\delta_{t,s} \ge 0 && \forall t,s\\
&\epsilon_{t,s} \ge \tau_{t,s}^{\text{orig}} - x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} && \forall t,s \\
&\epsilon_{t,s} \ge 0 && \forall t,s
\end{aligned}
\tag{C3}
\]

Only one of \(\delta_{t,s}\) and \(\epsilon_{t,s}\) can be positive; the objective will drive the unnecessary one to zero.

### 6.3  Selection of a unique speed‑plan per segment  

\[
\boxed{
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t} y_{t,\ell}^{p} = 1 \qquad \forall t\in T,\;\forall \ell\in L
}
\tag{C4}
\]

If a train is cancelled the plan variables are forced to zero:

\[
y_{t,\ell}^{p} \le 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t,\ell,p .
\tag{C5}
\]

### 6.4  Energy accumulation  

\[
\boxed{
\eta_{t}= \sum_{\ell\in L}\;\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t} E_{t,\ell}^{p}\; y_{t,\ell}^{p} \qquad \forall t\in T
}
\tag{C6}
\]

### 6.5  Occupancy of track segments (binary linking)

Let \(\tau_{t,\ell}^{p,\text{start}}\) be the **start time** of the plan on segment \(\ell\) when train \(t\) follows plan \(p\). Because the timetable provides arrival/departure times, we can compute the start‐time as the departure from the upstream station plus cumulative travel times of the preceding segments. For linearisation we introduce an auxiliary binary “occupancy” variable.

A **big‑M** linking for each train‑segment‑time slot:

\[
\boxed{
z_{t,\ell}^{k} \;\le\; \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t} y_{t,\ell}^{p}\;\; 
\text{and}\;\;
z_{t,\ell}^{k} \ge 
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if } k\in\big[ \text{start}_{t,\ell}^{p},\; \text{end}_{t,\ell}^{p}\big]  \\[2pt]
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
}
\tag{C7}
\]

In a pure MILP these interval‑membership conditions are expressed with **additional binary variables** that indicate whether the departure/arrival times fall within slot \(k\); the formulation below uses a standard “time‑window” linearisation:

Define auxiliary binaries \(u_{t,\ell}^{k}\) and \(v_{t,\ell}^{k}\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} \;-\; k\; \le\; M\; u_{t,\ell}^{k} \\
&k \;-\; x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} \; \le\; M\;(1-u_{t,\ell}^{k}) \\
&x_{t,s'}^{\text{arr}} \;-\; k\; \le\; M\; v_{t,\ell}^{k} \\
&k \;-\; x_{t,s'}^{\text{arr}} \; \le\; M\;(1-v_{t,\ell}^{k}) 
\end{aligned}
\qquad \forall t,\; \ell=(s,s')
\]

Then the occupancy variable is forced to 1 only if the train is on the segment during slot \(k\):

\[
z_{t,\ell}^{k} \ge u_{t,\ell}^{k}+v_{t,\ell}^{k}-1 \qquad \forall t,\ell,k .
\tag{C8}
\]

If the train is cancelled, all occupancies are forced to 0:

\[
z_{t,\ell}^{k} \le 1- c_t \qquad \forall t,\ell,k .
\tag{C9}
\]

### 6.6  Conflict‑free headway (same‑direction trains)

For any two distinct trains \(t\neq t'\) that travel **in the same direction** on the same segment \(\ell\) (direction implied by \(r_t\) and \(r_{t'}\)), the occupancy variables must be separated by at least \(\Delta^{\text{head}}_{\min}\) slots. Using a classic *big‑M* linearisation with binary ordering variables \(\phi_{t,t',\ell}\in\{0,1\}\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{k\in K} k \, z_{t,\ell}^{k} \;+\; \Delta^{\text{head}}_{\min} \;\le\; \sum_{k\in K} k \, z_{t',\ell}^{k} \;+\; M \, \phi_{t,t',\ell} \\
&\sum_{k\in K} k \, z_{t',\ell}^{k} \;+\; \Delta^{\text{head}}_{\min} \;\le\; \sum_{k\in K} k \, z_{t,\ell}^{k} \;+\; M \, (1-\phi_{t,t',\ell})
\end{aligned}
\qquad \forall \ell,\; \forall t<t' \text{ with same direction}
\tag{C10}
\]

If either train is cancelled the constraint is relaxed by the big‑M term (already ensured by C9).

### 6.7  Conflict‑free opposite‑direction usage (single‑track blockage)

When a segment \(\ell\in B\) is **single‑track** (only one train can occupy it at a time), opposite‑direction trains must be separated by \(\Delta^{\text{conf}}_{\min}\). Using the same ordering binaries \(\psi_{t,t',\ell}\) :

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{k\in K} k \, z_{t,\ell}^{k} \;+\; \Delta^{\text{conf}}_{\min} \;\le\; \sum_{k\in K} k \, z_{t',\ell}^{k} \;+\; M \, \psi_{t,t',\ell}\\
&\sum_{k\in K} k \, z_{t',\ell}^{k} \;+\; \Delta^{\text{conf}}_{\min} \;\le\; \sum_{k\in K} k \, z_{t,\ell}^{k} \;+\; M \, (1-\psi_{t,t',\ell})
\end{aligned}
\qquad \forall \ell\in B,\; \forall t<t' \text{ with opposite direction}
\tag{C11}
\]

Direction of each train on \(\ell\) is known from \(r_t\) (original vs rerouted).  

### 6.8  Blockage feasibility  

A train may **not** occupy a blocked segment in its original direction unless it reroutes:

\[
z_{t,\ell}^{k} \;\le\; \theta^{\text{block}}_{\ell,k} \;+\; r_t \;+\; c_t \qquad \forall t,\;\forall \ell\in B,\;\forall k\in K .
\tag{C12}
\]

Explanation:  
- If \(\theta^{\text{block}}_{\ell,k}=1\) (segment blocked), the RHS is at most \(1+r_t+c_t\).  
- When \(r_t=0\) (no rerouting) and \(c_t=0\) (train runs), RHS = 1, forcing \(z_{t,\ell}^{k}=0\).  
- If the train reroutes (\(r_t=1\)) or is cancelled (\(c_t=1\)), the constraint is satisfied.

### 6.9  Rerouting indicator  

Rerouting may be used **only** on blocked segments; outside the blockage the train must keep its original direction. This is automatically satisfied by the occupancy definition, but we add a linking constraint for completeness:

\[
r_t \le \sum_{\ell\in B}\sum_{k\in K} z_{t,\ell}^{k} \qquad \forall t .
\tag{C13}
\]

Thus \(r_t=1\) can only be set if the train actually occupies at least one blocked segment.

### 6.10  Cancellation logic  

If a train is cancelled, all its timing variables are fixed to a dummy value (here we use the horizon end \(H\)) and all binary variables are forced to zero:

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} = H \; (1-c_t) + H\;c_t &&\forall t,s\\
&x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} = H \; (1-c_t) + H\;c_t &&\forall t,s\\
&y_{t,\ell}^{p} \le 1-c_t &&\forall t,\ell,p\\
&z_{t,\ell}^{k} \le 1-c_t &&\forall t,\ell,k .
\end{aligned}
\tag{C14}
\]

---

## 7.  Full MILP Statement  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\bigl(\omega^{\text{delay}}_{t}\,\delta_{t,s} + \omega^{\text{early}}_{t}\,\epsilon_{t,s}\bigr)
      + \sum_{t\in T}\beta^{\text{cancel}}_{t}c_{t}
      + \omega^{\text{energy}} \sum_{t\in T}\eta_{t}  \\[2pt]
\text{s.t. } & \text{(C1)–(C14)}\\
& x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}},x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}},\delta_{t,s},\epsilon_{t,s},\eta_{t}\ge 0 \\
& y_{t,\ell}^{p}, z_{t,\ell}^{k}, u_{t,\ell}^{k}, v_{t,\ell}^{k},
   \phi_{t,t',\ell},\psi_{t,t',\ell}\in\{0,1\} \\
& r_t,c_t\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

---

## 8.  Remarks for Practitioners  

* **Scalability.** The number of binary variables grows with \(|T|\times|L|\times|K|\). In practice one applies the **decomposition** described in the original paper (IP master + train‑plan sub‑problems) or a **column‑generation** approach where each train‑plan \(p\) is generated on‑the‑fly.  
* **Plan generation (A‑2).** A short‑time optimal control model (linearised train dynamics) can be solved for each segment to obtain a set of Pareto‑efficient speed‑plans (travel time vs. energy).  
* **Robustness.** If the disruption time window \(\theta^{\text{block}}_{\ell,k}\) is uncertain, a **robust** or **stochastic** extension can be built by adding scenario indices.  
* **Parameter tuning.** The weights \(\omega^{\text{delay}}_t,\ \omega^{\text{early}}_t,\ \omega^{\text{energy}}\) allow the railway operator to express the relative importance of punctuality vs. energy savings.  

The formulation above captures **all essential elements** mentioned in the introductory text:

* **Rescheduling decisions** (arrival/departure times, dwell, headways).  
* **Rerouting** of trains inside a blocked segment (binary variable \(r_t\)).  
* **Speed‑profile selection** (binary plan variables \(y_{t,\ell}^{p}\)).  
* **Energy consumption** (objective term \(\eta_t\)).  
* **Conflict‑free operation** (headway and opposite‑direction constraints).  
* **Cancellation** as a last‑resort measure.  

It is therefore a self‑contained, linear (MILP) model ready for implementation in any standard optimisation solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, …).

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for rolling‑stock rescheduling with infrastructure‑availability constraints**  

The model integrates two sub‑problems that are solved iteratively (or in a Benders‑type exact scheme):

1. **Composition sub‑problem** – decides which rolling‑stock units (RSUs) are assigned to which passenger trips and which shunting movements are performed.  
2. **Infrastructure sub‑problem** – checks the feasibility of the selected shunting movements on the railway tracks and, if necessary, introduces short delays for passenger trains.

Below a complete linear formulation is given.  Missing data are filled with reasonable, clearly marked **assumptions** (A‑1 … A‑5).  

---

## 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|----------|
| **T**   | Set of passenger train trips (including the original timetable). Index *t*. |
| **S**   | Set of shunting movements that may be performed (each movement is defined by a departure/arrival station, track, and time window). Index *s*. |
| **R**   | Set of available rolling‑stock units (train sets). Index *r*. |
| **N**   | Set of stations where shunting may take place (e.g., Utrecht C, Rotterdam C). |
| **K**   | Set of tracks at a station *n∈N* (track *k* at station *n*). |
| **P**   | Set of time periods (discrete minutes) covering the planning horizon. Index *p*. |
| **B**   | Set of binary “cut” identifiers generated by the infrastructure model (Benders cuts). |

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical value / source |
|--------|-------------|------------------------|
| `c_rt` | Capacity (number of seats) of RSU *r* on trip *t*. | From rolling‑stock technical data. |
| `d_t` | Passenger demand (seats) of trip *t*. | Timetable / demand forecast. |
| `α_t` | Original planned start time of trip *t* (in minutes from horizon start). | Original timetable. |
| `β_t` | Latest admissible start time of trip *t* (allowing a short delay). | `α_t + Δ_max` (see A‑2). |
| `γ_s` | Duration (in minutes) of shunting movement *s*. | Engineering data. |
| `τ_s` | Earliest possible start time of shunting *s* (depends on disruption). | Computed from disruption scenario. |
| `π_s` | Latest possible start time of shunting *s*. | `τ_s + L_s` (see A‑3). |
| `δ_k` | Binary indicator: track *k* is usable for shunting (1) or blocked (0). | From infrastructure model (track occupancy). |
| `M`   | Large constant (≥ horizon length). | e.g. 10 000. |
| `w_1 , w_2 , w_3` | Weights for the three components of the objective (see §4). | Decision‑maker preference. |
| `Δ_max` | Maximum allowed delay for a passenger trip (in minutes). | **A‑2**: 5 min (typical buffer). |
| `L_s` | Maximum shift of shunting *s* from its earliest start (in minutes). | **A‑3**: 10 min. |
| `C_cut` | Right‑hand side of a Benders cut generated by the infrastructure model. | Computed by the sub‑problem. |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|--------|
| `x_{r t}` | binary | 1 if RSU *r* is assigned to passenger trip *t*, 0 otherwise. |
| `y_{s}`   | binary | 1 if shunting movement *s* is performed, 0 otherwise. |
| `z_{t}`   | integer (≥0) | Number of seats of demand *d_t* that remain **unserved** (penalised). |
| `u_{t}`   | integer (≥0) | Delay (in minutes) applied to the start of trip *t*. |
| `v_{s p}` | binary | 1 if shunting *s* starts at time period *p*, 0 otherwise. |
| `w_{k p}` | binary | 1 if track *k* is occupied at time *p* by any shunting movement, 0 otherwise. |
| `θ_b`    | binary | 1 if Benders cut *b* is **active** (i.e. the corresponding combination of shunting movements is forbidden). |

---

## 4. Objective Function  

The planner wants to (i) serve as many passengers as possible, (ii) keep the schedule close to the original plan (few delays), and (iii) minimise the number of shunting movements (to reduce night‑time relocations).  

\[
\min\; \underbrace{w_{1}\sum_{t\in T} z_{t}}_{\text{unserved demand}} 
      + \underbrace{w_{2}\sum_{t\in T} u_{t}}_{\text{total delay}} 
      + \underbrace{w_{3}\sum_{s\in S} y_{s}}_{\text{number of shunting moves}} .
\]

*If the decision maker prefers to maximise served demand, the first term can be written as \(-w_{1}\sum_{t} (d_t-z_t)\) – the formulation above is equivalent because \(d_t\) is constant.*

---

## 5. Constraints  

### 5.1 Rolling‑stock assignment  

1. **Each trip receives exactly one RSU (or none, in which case demand is unmet).**  

   \[
   \sum_{r\in R} x_{r t} + \frac{z_{t}}{d_{t}} = 1 \qquad \forall t\in T. \tag{C1}
   \]

   *Explanation*: If no RSU is assigned (`∑ x = 0`) then `z_t = d_t` (all demand unserved).  

2. **Capacity feasibility** – an assigned RSU must have enough seats for the served part of the demand.  

   \[
   c_{r t}\,x_{r t} \ge d_{t} - z_{t} \qquad \forall r\in R,\; t\in T. \tag{C2}
   \]

### 5.2 Shunting‑movement selection  

3. **A shunting movement can be performed only once.**  

   \[
   \sum_{p\in P} v_{s p} = y_{s} \qquad \forall s\in S. \tag{C3}
   \]

4. **Time‑window feasibility** – if the movement is selected, it must start inside its admissible window.  

   \[
   \tau_{s}\,y_{s} \le \sum_{p\in P} p\,v_{s p} \le \pi_{s}\,y_{s} \qquad \forall s\in S. \tag{C4}
   \]

5. **Track‑occupancy coupling** – a shunting uses a specific track *k(s,n)* at station *n(s)* for its whole duration.  

   For every period *p* that belongs to the interval \([p_s, p_s+γ_s-1]\) where \(p_s\) is the start time chosen for *s*:

   \[
   w_{k(s)n(s),p} \ge v_{s p_s} \qquad \forall s\in S,\; p\in\{p_s,\dots,p_s+γ_s-1\}. \tag{C5}
   \]

   (Implemented via big‑M linearisation: see A‑4.)

6. **Track‑availability** – a track cannot be used if it is blocked.  

   \[
   w_{k p} \le \delta_{k} \qquad \forall k\in K,\; p\in P. \tag{C6}
   \]

7. **No overlapping shunting on the same track** – at most one shunting may occupy a track at a given period.  

   \[
   \sum_{s\in S:\,k(s)=k} \sum_{p' = p-γ_s+1}^{p} v_{s p'} \le 1 \qquad \forall k\in K,\; p\in P. \tag{C7}
   \]

### 5.3 Passenger‑train delay limits  

8. **Delay bounds**  

   \[
   0 \le u_{t} \le \beta_{t} - \alpha_{t} \qquad \forall t\in T. \tag{C8}
   \]

9. **If a shunting movement uses a track that a passenger train would occupy, the train may be delayed to create a free window.**  
   (Linearised using binary variables `d_{t s}` – see A‑5.)  

   \[
   u_{t} \ge \bigl( \text{required free interval for } s \bigr) - M\,(1-d_{t s}) \qquad \forall t,s. \tag{C9}
   \]

   where `d_{t s}=1` only if train *t* and shunting *s* share the same track at overlapping times.

### 5.4 Benders (infrastructure) cuts  

10. **Cuts generated by the infrastructure model forbid infeasible combinations of shunting movements.**  

    For each cut *b∈B* (derived from a conflict set *S_b ⊆ S*):

    \[
    \sum_{s\in S_b} y_{s} \le |S_b| - 1 + M\,\theta_b \qquad \forall b\in B. \tag{C10}
    \]

    When the cut is **active** (`θ_b = 0`) the sum of selected shunting movements from the conflict set cannot reach the full size, i.e. at least one of them must be omitted.  

    The master problem may set `θ_b = 1` to relax a cut temporarily; in a pure Benders scheme `θ_b` is fixed to 0 after the cut is generated.

---

## 6. Assumptions (explicitly stated)

| # | Statement |
|---|------------|
| **A‑1** | The planning horizon is discretised into 1‑minute periods (`P`). This granularity is sufficient for the short‑delay context (≤ 5 min). |
| **A‑2** | A passenger trip may be delayed by at most `Δ_max = 5` minutes without violating service‑level agreements. |
| **A‑3** | Each shunting movement may be shifted up to `L_s = 10` minutes from its earliest feasible start (`τ_s`). This captures the flexibility allowed by the buffer times in the timetable. |
| **A‑4** | Big‑M value `M` is set to the horizon length (e.g., 1440 min for a 24‑h day) so that constraints (C5)–(C10) are correctly linearised. |
| **A‑5** | Binary linking variable `d_{t s}` (train *t* interferes with shunting *s*) is introduced only when the two use the same track at the same station; otherwise it is forced to 0. The infrastructure sub‑problem supplies the set of potentially conflicting pairs. |

---

## 7. Model Summary  

Putting everything together, the MILP is:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& w_{1}\sum_{t\in T} z_{t}
      + w_{2}\sum_{t\in T} u_{t}
      + w_{3}\sum_{s\in S} y_{s}  \\
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(C1)–(C10)} \\
& x_{r t}\in\{0,1\}\;\forall r,t,\qquad
  y_{s},\,z_{t},\,v_{s p},\,w_{k p},\,\theta_b\in\{0,1\},\\
& u_{t}\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\;\forall t .
\end{aligned}
\]

The model can be solved either:

* **Exactly** – using a *Combinatorial Benders* loop: the master problem contains (C1)–(C9) and the current set of cuts (C10); after each master solution, the infrastructure sub‑problem checks feasibility of the selected shunting set and, if a conflict is found, generates a new cut (C10).  
* **Iteratively (heuristic)** – the master proposes a single shunting movement at a time (forcing `y_s = 1` for one *s*), the infrastructure sub‑problem validates it (possibly adding a small delay `u_t`), and the process repeats until no more feasible shunting moves exist.

Both solution strategies respect the legal separation of tasks (rolling‑stock dispatcher vs. infrastructure dispatcher) while guaranteeing that any accepted shunting movement can be executed on the available tracks.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling & Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP)**  

The model simultaneously decides (i) which route each train will use, (ii) the new arrival/departure times, (iii) the order of trains on every shared single‑track segment, and (iv) a feasible speed profile for each train while minimising total passenger delay and energy consumption. All constraints are linear; the quadratic energy term is linearised with a piece‑wise‑linear approximation.

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **I** | Trains, indexed by *i* (|I| = *N*). |
| **K** | Feasible routes for a train, indexed by *k*. A route is a sequence of track‑segments (including possible detours). |
| **S** | Stations (including origin 0 and terminal L), indexed by *s*. |
| **T** | Discrete time‑intervals covering the planning horizon, indexed by *t*. |
| **E** | Track‑segments (edges) of the network, indexed by *e*. |
| **E​b** ⊂ **E** | Segments that are **blocked** during a known time window. |
| **E​pair(i,j)** = *E​i(k) ∩ E​j(k’)* | Segments that could be used by both trains *i* and *j* (conflict segments). |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning | Typical unit |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| *L*<sub>i,k,e</sub> | Length of segment *e* for train *i* on route *k*. | km |
| *v*<sup>min</sup>, *v*<sup>max</sup> | Global lower / upper speed limits. | km/h |
| *a*<sup>max</sup>, *a*<sup>min</sup> | Max acceleration / deceleration. | km/h² |
| τ<sup>dwell</sup> | Minimum dwell time at any station. | min |
| τ<sup>head</sup> | Minimum headway on a single‑track segment. | min |
| *sched*<sub>i</sub> | Scheduled arrival time of train *i* at its final station (reference timetable). | min |
| *c* | Energy‑cost coefficient (≈ kWh per (km/h)²). | kWh/(km/h)² |
| *M* | Large constant for “big‑M’’ linearisation ( > any feasible time or speed product). |
| δ<sub>i,k,e</sub> | =1 if segment *e* belongs to route *k* of train *i*; 0 otherwise. |
| β<sub>e</sub> | =1 if segment *e* is single‑track (capacity = 1); 0 otherwise. |
| γ<sub>e</sub> | =1 if segment *e* belongs to the blocked set **E​b**; 0 otherwise. |

---

### 3. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| *y*<sub>i,k</sub> | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* uses route *k*. |
| *x*<sub>i,j</sub> | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* precedes train *j* on every shared segment. |
| *a*<sub>i,s</sub> | ≥0 | Arrival time of train *i* at station *s*. |
| *d*<sub>i,s</sub> | ≥0 | Departure time of train *i* from station *s*. |
| *c*<sub>i,e</sub> | ≥0 | **Start** time of train *i* on segment *e*. |
| *p*<sub>i,e</sub> | ≥0 | **End** time of train *i* on segment *e*. |
| *u*<sub>i,t</sub> ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* is moving during interval *t*. |
| *v*<sub>i,t</sub> ≥0 | continuous | Average speed of train *i* during interval *t*. |
| *s*<sub>i,t</sub>⁽ℓ⁾ ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ speed level ℓ (ℓ = 1…L) is chosen in interval *t* (piece‑wise linear energy). |

---

### 4. Objective  

Minimise a weighted sum of **total delay** and **total energy**:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \alpha \underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(a_{i,\text{last}}-sched_i\bigr)}_{\text{total passenger delay}} \\
        & +\; \beta \underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L} e_{\ell}\, s_{i,t}^{(\ell)}}_{\text{energy (linearised)}}
\end{aligned}
\]

*α, β > 0 are decision‑maker weights.  
\(e_{\ell}=c\;(\hat v_{\ell})^{2}\) are pre‑computed energy coefficients for the selected speed levels \(\hat v_{\ell}\).

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Route selection  

1. **Exactly one route per train**  

   \[
   \sum_{k\in K} y_{i,k}=1 \qquad\forall i\in I.
   \]

2. **Link segment‑occupation to route choice** (big‑M)  

   \[
   c_{i,e}\ge 0,\;p_{i,e}\ge 0,
   \qquad
   c_{i,e}\le M\,y_{i,k},
   \qquad
   p_{i,e}\le M\,y_{i,k}
   \quad\forall i,k,e\text{ with }\delta_{i,k,e}=1.
   \]

#### 5.2 Timing at stations  

3. **Dwell time**  

   \[
   d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}\;\ge\;\tau^{\text{dwell}}\;y_{i,k}
   \qquad\forall i,s,k\text{ with }s\in\text{stations}(k).
   \]

4. **Travel time on a segment**  

   \[
   p_{i,e}-c_{i,e}= \Delta t\sum_{t\in T}\theta_{i,e,t}
   \qquad\forall i,e,
   \]
   where \(\theta_{i,e,t}\in\{0,1\}\) indicates that train *i* occupies segment *e* during interval *t*.
   The occupancy linking is  

   \[
   \sum_{e\in E} \theta_{i,e,t}=u_{i,t}\qquad\forall i,t .
   \]

5. **Speed‑distance consistency**  

   \[
   \Delta t\;v_{i,t}\;\ge\;\sum_{e\in E}\;L_{i,k,e}\;\theta_{i,e,t}
   \qquad\forall i,t,k.
   \]

#### 5.3 Speed limits & dynamics  

6. **Bounds**  

   \[
   v^{\text{min}}\,u_{i,t}\le v_{i,t}\le v^{\text{max}}\,u_{i,t}\qquad\forall i,t.
   \]

7. **Acceleration / deceleration**  

   \[
   v_{i,t+1}-v_{i,t}\le a^{\text{max}}\Delta t,\qquad
   v_{i,t}-v_{i,t+1}\le a^{\text{min}}\Delta t
   \qquad\forall i,\;t=1,\dots,|T|-1.
   \]

#### 5.4 Blockage avoidance  

8. **Forbidden use of blocked segments** (for every blockage window \((t_{1},t_{2})\) of segment *e*):  

   \[
   c_{i,e}\ge t_{2}\;-\;M\bigl(1-y_{i,k}\bigr)
   \quad\text{or}\quad
   p_{i,e}\le t_{1}\;+\;M\bigl(1-y_{i,k}\bigr)
   \qquad\forall i,k,e\text{ with }\gamma_{e}=1,\;\delta_{i,k,e}=1.
   \]

#### 5.5 Single‑track capacity & headway  

9. **Ordering variables** (only needed when two trains could share a segment)  

   \[
   x_{i,j}+x_{j,i}=1 \qquad\forall i<j,\;e\in E\_{pair(i,j)} .
   \]

10. **Headway enforcement** (minimum safe gap τ<sup>head</sup>)  

    \[
    c_{j,e}\ge p_{i,e}+ \tau^{\text{head}} - M\bigl(1-x_{i,j}\bigr)
    \qquad\forall i\neq j,\;e\in E\_{pair(i,j)} .
    \]

11. **Capacity of a single‑track segment** (alternative view)  

    \[
    \sum_{i\in I}\theta_{i,e,t}\le 1\qquad\forall e\text{ with }\beta_{e}=1,\;\forall t\in T .
    \]

#### 5.6 Energy‑linearisation (speed‑level)  

12. **Exactly one speed level if the train moves**  

    \[
    \sum_{\ell=1}^{L}s_{i,t}^{(\ell)} = u_{i,t}\qquad\forall i,t .
    \]

13. **Reconstruct speed from the chosen level**  

    \[
    v_{i,t}= \sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\hat v_{\ell}\;s_{i,t}^{(\ell)}\qquad\forall i,t .
    \]

14. **Energy contribution (already used in the objective)**  

    \[
    \text{Energy}_{i}= \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L} e_{\ell}\,s_{i,t}^{(\ell)} .
    \]

#### 5.7 Logical consistency  

15. **Binary domains**  

    \[
    y_{i,k},\,x_{i,j},\,u_{i,t},\,\theta_{i,e,t},\,s_{i,t}^{(\ell)}\in\{0,1\}.
    \]

16. **Non‑negativity**  

    \[
    a_{i,s},\,d_{i,s},\,c_{i,e},\,p_{i,e},\,v_{i,t}\ge 0 .
    \]

---

### 6. Complete MILP (compact form)

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \alpha\sum_{i}(a_{i,\text{last}}-sched_i)
      +\beta\sum_{i}\sum_{t}\sum_{\ell}e_{\ell}s_{i,t}^{(\ell)}\\[4pt]
\text{s.t. }&
\sum_{k}y_{i,k}=1 &&\forall i\\
&c_{i,e},p_{i,e}\ge0 &&\forall i,e\\
&c_{i,e}\le My_{i,k},\;p_{i,e}\le My_{i,k}
   &&\forall i,k,e\text{ with }\delta_{i,k,e}=1\\
&d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}\ge\tau^{\text{dwell}}y_{i,k}
   &&\forall i,s,k\text{ with }s\in\text{stations}(k)\\
&p_{i,e}-c_{i,e}= \Delta t\sum_{t}\theta_{i,e,t}
   &&\forall i,e\\
&\sum_{e}\theta_{i,e,t}=u_{i,t}
   &&\forall i,t\\
&\Delta t\,v_{i,t}\ge\sum_{e}L_{i,k,e}\theta_{i,e,t}
   &&\forall i,t,k\\
&v^{\text{min}}u_{i,t}\le v_{i,t}\le v^{\text{max}}u_{i,t}
   &&\forall i,t\\
&v_{i,t+1}-v_{i,t}\le a^{\text{max}}\Delta t,\;
 v_{i,t}-v_{i,t+1}\le a^{\text{min}}\Delta t
   &&\forall i,t\\
&c_{i,e}\ge t_{2}-M(1-y_{i,k})\;\text{or}\;
 p_{i,e}\le t_{1}+M(1-y_{i,k})
   &&\forall i,k,e\text{ with }\gamma_{e}=1\\
&x_{i,j}+x_{j,i}=1 &&\forall i<j,\;e\in E\_{pair(i,j)}\\
&c_{j,e}\ge p_{i,e}+ \tau^{\text{head}}-M(1-x_{i,j})
   &&\forall i\neq j,\;e\in E\_{pair(i,j)}\\
&\sum_{i}\theta_{i,e,t}\le1
   &&\forall e\text{ with }\beta_{e}=1,\;\forall t\\
&\sum_{\ell}s_{i,t}^{(\ell)}=u_{i,t}
   &&\forall i,t\\
&v_{i,t}= \sum_{\ell}\hat v_{\ell}s_{i,t}^{(\ell)}
   &&\forall i,t\\
&y_{i,k},x_{i,j},u_{i,t},\theta_{i,e,t},s_{i,t}^{(\ell)}\in\{0,1\}\\
& a_{i,s},d_{i,s},c_{i,e},p_{i,e},v_{i,t}\ge0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 7. What the solution provides  

* **Route choice** (`y_{i,k}`) – detour around the blocked segment if necessary.  
* **Rescheduled timetable** – arrival/departure times (`a_{i,s}`, `d_{i,s}`) that respect dwell times, headways, and blockage windows.  
* **Order of trains** on every shared single‑track segment (`x_{i,j}`) guaranteeing conflict‑free use.  
* **Executable speed profile** (`v_{i,t}` or the speed‑level binaries) that respects acceleration limits and yields a linear estimate of energy consumption.  

The model can be solved with any commercial MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, …). The resulting schedule is conflict‑free, physically feasible, and optimally balances delay reduction against energy efficiency for high‑speed railways under partial‑segment blockages.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) – Partial Segment Blockage**  

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | Set of trains, *t* ∈ T |
| **N** | Set of stations (including origins and destinations) |
| **L** | Set of directed track links ℓ = (i ,j) , i ,j ∈ N |
| **Lᵣ** ⊂ L | Links that belong to the **blocked side** of the partially blocked segment |
| **K** | Finite set of admissible **speed levels** k = 1,…,K (each with speed *vₖ* and energy coefficient *eₖ*) |
| **Aₜ** ⊂ L | Original (planned) route links of train *t* |
| **Rₜ** ⊂ L | Feasible **alternative** links for train *t* (used when rerouted) |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| **dₜ** | Planned departure time of train *t* from its origin | min |
| **τᵢⱼ** | Length of link (i ,j) | km |
| **T⁽ᵐⁱⁿ⁾** | Minimum dwell time at any station | min |
| **H** | Minimum head‑way between two successive trains on the same link | min |
| **Δᵥ⁽ᵘᵖ⁾**, **Δᵥ⁽ᵈⁿ⁾** | Max. admissible relative speed increase / decrease between consecutive links | – |
| **Bℓ = (bℓ^{start}, bℓ^{end})** | Blocking time window for every ℓ ∈ Lᵣ (no train may occupy the blocked side) | min |
| **wᵈ**, **wᵉ** | Weight for total delay and total energy in the objective | – |
| **eₖ** | Energy consumption per kilometre at speed level *k* | kWh/km |
| **vₖ** | Speed associated with level *k* | km/h |
| **M** | Large constant ( > any feasible time, e.g. 10⁶ ) | min |
| **αₜᵢⱼ** | 1 if (i ,j) ∈ Aₜ, 0 otherwise | – |
| **βₜᵢⱼ** | 1 if (i ,j) ∈ Rₜ, 0 otherwise | – |

---

### 3. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **xₜᵢⱼ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* traverses link (i ,j) |
| **sₜᵢⱼₖ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* uses speed level *k* on link (i ,j) |
| **aₜⱼ** ≥ 0 | cont. | Arrival time of train *t* at station *j* |
| **dₜⱼ** ≥ 0 | cont. | Departure time of train *t* from station *j* |
| **Δₜᵢⱼ** ≥ 0 | cont. | Travel time of train *t* on link (i ,j) |
| **zₜ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* is rerouted (uses at least one link from Rₜ) |
| **γₜₜ′ᵢⱼ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | Ordering variable for head‑way on link (i ,j) (t < t′) |
| **uₜℓ^{before}, uₜℓ^{after}** ∈ {0,1} | binary | “outside‑window’’ indicators for blocked link ℓ |

---

### 4. Objective  

\[
\min\; 
w^{d}\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(d_{t}^{\text{actual}}-d_{t}\bigr)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
w^{e}\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in L}\sum_{k\in K} e_{k}\,\tau_{ij}\, s_{tij k}}_{\text{total energy}}
\]

where \(d_{t}^{\text{actual}} = d_{t,\text{last}}\) (departure from the final station of train *t*).

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Flow (routing)  

*Origin* (first station *oₜ* of train *t*):
\[
\sum_{j:(o_t,j)\in L} x_{t\,o_t j}=1,\qquad 
\sum_{i:(i,o_t)\in L} x_{t i o_t}=0 .
\]

*Destination* (last station *dₜ*):
\[
\sum_{i:(i,d_t)\in L} x_{t i d_t}=1,\qquad 
\sum_{j:(d_t,j)\in L} x_{t d_t j}=0 .
\]

*Intermediate stations* (conservation):
\[
\sum_{j:(i,j)\in L} x_{tij}= \sum_{j:(j,i)\in L} x_{tji}\qquad
\forall i\in N\setminus\{o_t,d_t\},\; \forall t\in T .
\]

#### 5.2 Rerouting indicator  

\[
\sum_{(i,j)\in R_t} x_{tij}\le |R_t|\,z_t ,\qquad
\sum_{(i,j)\in A_t} x_{tij}\ge 1-z_t .
\]

If \(z_t=0\) the train must stay on its original route.

#### 5.3 Speed‑level selection  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} s_{tij k}=x_{tij}\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in L .
\]

#### 5.4 Travel‑time from speed level  

\[
\Delta_{tij}= \sum_{k\in K}\frac{\tau_{ij}}{v_k}\; s_{tij k}\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in L .
\]

(The coefficient \(\tau_{ij}/v_k\) is a known constant.)

#### 5.5 Temporal consistency  

\[
a_{tj}= d_{ti}+ \Delta_{tij}\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in L .
\]

#### 5.6 Minimum dwell  

\[
d_{tj}\ge a_{tj}+ T^{\text{min}}\qquad\forall t,\;j\in N .
\]

#### 5.7 Origin departure cannot be earlier than planned  

\[
d_{t\,o_t}\ge d_t\qquad\forall t\in T .
\]

#### 5.8 Head‑way (conflict‑avoidance)  

For any two trains \(t<t'\) that may use the same link (i ,j):

\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{ti}+ \Delta_{tij}+ H &\le d_{t' i}+ M\,\gamma_{tt'ij},\\
d_{t'i}+ \Delta_{t'ij}+ H &\le d_{ti}+ M\,(1-\gamma_{tt'ij}),\\
\gamma_{tt'ij}&\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Only pairs sharing a link need to be generated.

#### 5.9 Blockage‑avoidance (links in Lᵣ)  

For every ℓ=(i ,j) ∈ Lᵣ and every train *t*:

\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{ti}+ \Delta_{tij} &\le b^{start}_\ell + M\,u^{after}_{t\ell},\\
d_{ti} &\ge b^{end}_\ell - M\,u^{before}_{t\ell},\\
u^{after}_{t\ell}+u^{before}_{t\ell} &\ge x_{tij},\\
u^{after}_{t\ell},u^{before}_{t\ell}&\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

If the train uses the blocked link (xₜᵢⱼ =1) it must travel either **before** the start or **after** the end of the blockage.

#### 5.10 Acceleration / Deceleration limits  

Let (i′,j′) be the predecessor link of (i ,j) on train *t* (i.e., xₜᵢ′ⱼ′ = xₜᵢⱼ =1).  
Define binary \(y_{t,i'j',ij}\) that is 1 when both links are used (it can be linearised by \(y\le x\)). Then:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{k} v_k\, s_{tij k} &\le (1+Δ^{up}_v)\,\sum_{k} v_k\, s_{ti'j' k}+ M\,(1-y_{t,i'j',ij}),\\
\sum_{k} v_k\, s_{tij k} &\ge (1-Δ^{dn}_v)\,\sum_{k} v_k\, s_{ti'j' k}- M\,(1-y_{t,i'j',ij}).
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus the speed on two consecutive links cannot change by more than the prescribed fractions.

#### 5.11 Domain  

\[
\begin{aligned}
x_{tij},\,s_{tij k},\,z_t,\,\gamma_{tt'ij},\,u^{before}_{t\ell},\,u^{after}_{t\ell}&\in\{0,1\},\\
a_{tj},\,d_{tj},\,\Delta_{tij}&\ge 0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 6. Complete MILP  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ll}
\displaystyle \min\; w^{d}\sum_{t}(d_{t}^{\text{actual}}-d_{t})\;+\; w^{e}\sum_{t}\sum_{(i,j)}\sum_{k} e_{k}\,\tau_{ij}\, s_{tij k}\\[4pt]
\text{s.t.} \\
\text{(Flow constraints)}\\
\text{(Rerouting indicator)}\\
\text{(Speed‑level selection)}\\
\text{(Travel‑time = distance / speed)}\\
\text{(Temporal consistency)}\\
\text{(Minimum dwell)}\\
\text{(Origin departure ≥ planned)}\\
\text{(Head‑way ordering)}\\
\text{(Blockage‑avoidance)}\\
\text{(Acceleration / deceleration limits)}\\
\text{(Variable domains)} .
\end{array}
}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only non‑continuous variables are binaries that encode routing, speed‑level choice, head‑way ordering, and blockage‑avoidance.  

The model can be solved with any standard MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, SCIP, …).  

**Outputs**:  
* Binary routing decisions \(x_{tij}\) (original vs. rerouted).  
* Arrival / departure times \(a_{tj}, d_{tj}\).  
* Speed‑level decisions \(s_{tij k}\) → travel times \(\Delta_{tij}\) and energy consumption.  

Thus the MILP simultaneously solves the **train‑rescheduling** (routing & timing) and **speed‑management** (energy‑aware speed selection) problems while respecting partial‑segment blockages and all safety/operational constraints.
