Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP‑MILP)**  
The formulation below captures (i) the selection of a feasible timetable (arrival / departure, train ordering and possible rerouting) and (ii) the generation of a linear‑piece speed profile for every train‑segment‑time‑interval. All variables, parameters and constraints are listed explicitly; missing data are indicated and reasonable default assumptions are proposed.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\) |
| \(S\) | Set of stations, indexed by \(s\) (including start‑ and terminal stations) |
| \(L\) | Set of line‑segments (track sections) between two consecutive stations, indexed by \(\ell\) |
| \(D\) | Set of disruption‑areas (sub‑segments that are blocked for a time window) |
| \(K\) | Set of *speed‑profile* time‑bins used to discretise a run on a segment, indexed by \(k\) |
| \(R\) | Set of feasible *routes* (original route or rerouted via opposite track) for a train, indexed by \(r\) |
| \(B\) | Set of binary *conflict‑resolution* orderings between any two trains on a shared track, indexed by ordered pair \((t,t')\) |

Auxiliary derived sets:  

* \(L_{t}\subseteq L\) – segments traversed by train \(t\) on the chosen route.  
* \(K_{\ell}\) – set of time‑bins used on segment \(\ell\) (identical for all trains).  
* \(B_{\ell}\subseteq B\) – ordered pairs of trains that both intend to occupy segment \(\ell\).

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical value / assumption |
|--------|-------------|---------------------------|
| \(\underline{a}_{t,s}\) | Scheduled (original) arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\). | From the pre‑disruption timetable. |
| \(\overline{a}_{t,s}\) | Latest permissible arrival (deadline) at \(s\). | \(\underline{a}_{t,s}+ \Delta^{\max}_{\text{delay}}\). |
| \(\underline{d}_{t,s}\) | Minimum dwell time at station \(s\). | 2–5 min (regulation). |
| \(\overline{d}_{t,s}\) | Maximum dwell time (may be extended for conflict resolution). | 10 min (assumption). |
| \(\underline{v}_{\ell}\), \(\overline{v}_{\ell}\) | Minimum / maximum admissible speed on segment \(\ell\). | 200–350 km/h (HSR). |
| \(L_{\ell}^{\text{len}}\) | Physical length of segment \(\ell\) (km). | From infrastructure data. |
| \(\alpha_{t,\ell}\) | Acceleration (km/h²) capability of train \(t\). | 0.5 km/h² (typical high‑speed EMU). |
| \(\beta_{t,\ell}\) | Deceleration (km/h²) capability (positive number). | 0.6 km/h². |
| \(E^{\text{acc}}_{t,\ell}\) | Energy (kWh) consumed per unit of acceleration on \(\ell\). | 0.05 kWh/(km/h²·km) – assumed linear. |
| \(E^{\text{cruise}}_{\ell}\) | Energy (kWh) per km when cruising at constant speed \(\overline{v}_{\ell}\). | 5 kWh/km (typical). |
| \(\psi^{\text{pen}}_{\text{delay}}\) | Penalty cost (€/min) for passenger delay. | 0.2 €/min. |
| \(\psi^{\text{pen}}_{\text{canc}}\) | Penalty for train cancellation (fixed). | 10 000 €. |
| \(\psi^{\text{pen}}_{\text{reroute}}\) | Additional penalty for using a rerouted path (cost of extra conflicts). | 500 €. |
| \(T^{\text{block}}_{d}\), \(T^{\text{release}}_{d}\) | Start / end time of disruption window on area \(d\). | Provided by event data. |
| \(M\) | Large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints. | 10⁶. |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

### 3.1 Timetable / Rescheduling  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|----------|
| \(a_{t,s}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Actual arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\). |
| \(d_{t,s}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Actual departure time from station \(s\). |
| \(y_{t,r}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) uses route \(r\) (original or rerouted). |
| \(\theta_{t,t',\ell}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) is scheduled **before** train \(t'\) on segment \(\ell\); 0 otherwise. |
| \(c_t\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) is cancelled. |
| \(\delta_{t,\ell,k}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(t\) occupies time‑bin \(k\) on segment \(\ell\). |

### 3.2 Speed‑profile (linear pieces)  

For each train‑segment‑bin \((t,\ell,k)\) we introduce a *speed level* \(v_{t,\ell,k}\) (continuous). To keep the model linear we pre‑define a small set of admissible speed levels  

\[
\mathcal{V}_{\ell}=\{v^{(1)}_{\ell},v^{(2)}_{\ell},\dots ,v^{(p)}_{\ell}\},\qquad 
\underline{v}_{\ell}=v^{(1)}_{\ell}<\dots <v^{(p)}_{\ell}=\overline{v}_{\ell}.
\]

A *selection* binary variable chooses one level:

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|----------|
| \(\sigma_{t,\ell,k}^{q}\) | Binary | 1 if speed level \(v^{(q)}_{\ell}\) is used by train \(t\) in bin \(k\) on segment \(\ell\). |

These satisfy \(\sum_{q}\sigma_{t,\ell,k}^{q}= \delta_{t,\ell,k}\) (i.e., a speed is defined only if the bin is occupied).

---

## 4. Objective Function  

We minimise a weighted sum of passenger delay, energy consumption, and penalty costs:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; Z \; = \;& 
\underbrace{\psi^{\text{pen}}_{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\bigl(a_{t,s}-\underline{a}_{t,s}\bigr)^{+}}_{\text{Delay penalty}} \\
&+ \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L_{t}}\sum_{k\in K_{\ell}}\sum_{q\in\mathcal{V}_{\ell}}
\Bigl(E^{\text{acc}}_{t,\ell}\,a_{t,\ell,k}^{q}+E^{\text{cruise}}_{\ell}\,v^{(q)}_{\ell}\Bigr)\,\sigma_{t,\ell,k}^{q}}_{\text{Energy cost}}\\
&+ \underbrace{\psi^{\text{pen}}_{\text{canc}}\sum_{t\in T}c_{t}}_{\text{Cancellation penalty}}\\
&+ \underbrace{\psi^{\text{pen}}_{\text{reroute}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{r\in R\setminus\{r^{\text{orig}}_t\}} y_{t,r}}_{\text{Reroute penalty}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

The operator \((\cdot)^{+}=\max\{0,\cdot\}\) can be linearised with an auxiliary variable \(u_{t,s}\) and constraints  

\[
u_{t,s}\ge a_{t,s}-\underline{a}_{t,s},\quad u_{t,s}\ge 0,
\]

and replace the term by \(\psi^{\text{pen}}_{\text{delay}}\sum_{t,s}u_{t,s}\).

---

## 5. Constraints  

### 5.1 Timetable feasibility  

1. **Arrival – departure relationship** (minimal dwell)  

\[
d_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} + \underline{d}_{t,s}\;(1-c_t)\quad \forall t,s.
\]

2. **Maximum dwell (allows extensions for conflict resolution)**  

\[
d_{t,s} \le a_{t,s} + \overline{d}_{t,s}\;(1-c_t)\quad \forall t,s.
\]

3. **Travel time on a segment** – linearised using selected speed level:  

Let the travel time contributed by bin \(k\) be  

\[
\tau_{t,\ell,k}= \frac{L_{\ell}}{v_{t,\ell,k}}\,\delta_{t,\ell,k}.
\]

Because \(v_{t,\ell,k}\) is a selected discrete level, we write  

\[
\tau_{t,\ell,k}= \sum_{q}\frac{L_{\ell}}{v^{(q)}_{\ell}}\;\sigma_{t,\ell,k}^{q}.
\]

4. **Linking arrivals / departures across consecutive stations**  

For each train \(t\) and each pair of consecutive stations \((s,s')\) linked by segment \(\ell\in L_t\):

\[
a_{t,s'} = d_{t,s} + \sum_{k\in K_{\ell}}\tau_{t,\ell,k}\; + \;M\;c_{t}.
\]

If the train is cancelled, the constraint is relaxed by the big‑M term.

5. **Route selection**  

\[
\sum_{r\in R} y_{t,r}=1-c_{t}\qquad \forall t .
\]

If a rerouted route is chosen, the corresponding set \(L_t\) is the list of segments belonging to that route.  

6. **Blocking (disruption) constraints** – a train may not occupy a blocked area during the disruption window:

For every disruption area \(d\in D\) that covers segment \(\ell\),

\[
\sum_{k\in K_{\ell}} \delta_{t,\ell,k}\; \mathbf{1}_{\text{bin }k\in [T^{\text{block}}_{d},\,T^{\text{release}}_{d}]} =0
\qquad \forall t\ \text{if }\ell\in L_{d}.
\]

(The indicator can be implemented through pre‑computed binary parameters \(b_{k}^{d}\).)

### 5.2 Binary occupancy consistency  

7. **A bin is either occupied or not**  

\[
\sum_{q}\sigma_{t,\ell,k}^{q}= \delta_{t,\ell,k}\qquad \forall t,\ell,k.
\]

8. **If a train is cancelled, it occupies no bins**  

\[
\delta_{t,\ell,k} \le 1-c_{t}\qquad \forall t,\ell,k.
\]

### 5.3 Conflict‑avoidance on shared tracks (bidirectional conflict)  

For each ordered pair \((t,t')\in B_{\ell}\) sharing segment \(\ell\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{k\in K_{\ell}} \bigl( k\cdot \Delta_{k}\bigr)\,\delta_{t,\ell,k} 
\;\le\; 
\sum_{k\in K_{\ell}} \bigl( k\cdot \Delta_{k}\bigr)\,\delta_{t',\ell,k}
\;+\; M\,(1-\theta_{t,t',\ell}) ,\\
&\sum_{k\in K_{\ell}} \bigl( k\cdot \Delta_{k}\bigr)\,\delta_{t',\ell,k}
\;\le\;
\sum_{k\in K_{\ell}} \bigl( k\cdot \Delta_{k}\bigr)\,\delta_{t,\ell,k}
\;+\; M\,\theta_{t,t',\ell},
\end{aligned}
\]

where \(\Delta_{k}\) is the duration of time‑bin \(k\). The two constraints force a total ordering on the occupancy intervals; exactly one of the binaries \(\theta_{t,t',\ell}\) (or its complement) will be 1, guaranteeing non‑overlap.

### 5.4 Acceleration / deceleration feasibility (linearised)  

Because we use piecewise constant speeds per bin, the speed change between consecutive bins must respect train dynamics:

\[
\bigl| v_{t,\ell,k+1} - v_{t,\ell,k} \bigr|
\le 
\alpha_{t,\ell}\,\Delta_{k} \quad \forall t,\ell,k,
\]
\[
\bigl| v_{t,\ell,k+1} - v_{t,\ell,k} \bigr|
\le 
\beta_{t,\ell}\,\Delta_{k} \quad \forall t,\ell,k,
\]

which can be linearised with auxiliary continuous variables \(z^{+}_{t,\ell,k},z^{-}_{t,\ell,k}\):

\[
v_{t,\ell,k+1} - v_{t,\ell,k}= z^{+}_{t,\ell,k}-z^{-}_{t,\ell,k},
\qquad
z^{+}_{t,\ell,k},z^{-}_{t,\ell,k}\ge 0,
\]
\[
z^{+}_{t,\ell,k}\le \alpha_{t,\ell}\Delta_{k},
\qquad
z^{-}_{t,\ell,k}\le \beta_{t,\ell}\Delta_{k}.
\]

If a bin is not occupied (\(\delta_{t,\ell,k}=0\)), the corresponding speed variables are forced to zero via  

\[
v_{t,\ell,k}\le \overline{v}_{\ell}\,\delta_{t,\ell,k}.
\]

### 5.5 Domain restrictions  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}\ge 0,\quad  \forall t,s,\\
& v_{t,\ell,k}\ge 0,\quad  \forall t,\ell,k,\\
& \theta_{t,t',\ell}\in\{0,1\},\; y_{t,r}\in\{0,1\},\; c_{t}\in\{0,1\},\;
\delta_{t,\ell,k}\in\{0,1\},\;
\sigma_{t,\ell,k}^{q}\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 6. Remarks on Linearisation & Model Size  

* **Delay‑penalty linearisation** – replace \((a_{t,s}-\underline{a}_{t,s})^{+}\) by auxiliary non‑negative variable \(u_{t,s}\) with the two constraints shown in Section 4.  
* **Speed selection** – The discrete speed‑set \(\mathcal{V}_{\ell}\) makes the energy term linear. If a finer speed resolution is required, increase the cardinality of \(\mathcal{V}_{\ell}\) (trade‑off with model size).  
* **Time‑bin discretisation** – Typical bin length \(\Delta_{k}=1\) min gives a tractable number of bins while maintaining enough flexibility for acceleration/deceleration.  
* **Big‑M values** – Choose \(M\) just large enough to deactivate constraints when a train is cancelled; e.g., \(M= 10^4\) min (far larger than any feasible schedule horizon).  

---

## 7. Complete MILP Statement  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ll}
\displaystyle \min\; Z & \text{(Section 4)}\\[4pt]
\text{s.t.} \\
\text{Arrival/Departure, dwell limits} & \text{(5.1)}\\
\text{Travel‑time linkages} & \text{(5.1)}\\
\text{Route choice} & \text{(5.1)}\\
\text{Blockage avoidance} & \text{(5.1)}\\
\text{Bin‑occupancy ↔ speed selection} & \text{(5.2)}\\
\text{Conflict ordering on shared segments} & \text{(5.3)}\\
\text{Dynamic feasibility (acc/dec)} & \text{(5.4)}\\
\text{Variable domains} & \text{(5.5)}\\
\end{array}
}
\]

---

### Interpretation  

* **Decision variables** determine *when* each train arrives/departs, *whether* it is cancelled or rerouted, *how* the trains are ordered on the contested segment, and *what* speed level they adopt in each time‑bin.  
* **Objective** simultaneously reduces passenger delay, total traction energy, and the economic impact of cancellations/rerouting.  
* **Constraints** guarantee feasibility with respect to (i) the physical railway infrastructure (speed limits, segment lengths), (ii) the disruption (blocked area & time window), (iii) train dynamics (acceleration/deceleration), and (iv) safety (no two trains occupy the same track section at the same instant).  

---

## 8. Possible Extensions (Not Modelled)  

* **Energy‑regeneration** – introduce negative energy terms for braking phases.  
* **Crew & rolling‑stock constraints** – add linking constraints to enforce feasible crew shifts and train‑set availability after cancellations.  
* **Passenger‑connection penalties** – extra terms for missed transfers.  

These could be added without altering the core linear structure, simply by defining additional binary/continuous variables and linear penalty terms.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP)**  

The model below is a *complete* mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) formulation that captures the problem described in the prompt: a high‑speed railway suffers a **partial segment blockage**; trains may have to **reroute**, **re‑time**, and **choose speed levels**; bidirectional trains share the same track and must avoid conflicts; the objective is a weighted sum of **total passenger delay** and **energy consumption**.  

All symbols are defined, the objective is linear, and every constraint is written in a linear form (big‑M or auxiliary binaries are used where logical conditions appear). The formulation can be copied directly into any MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP, …).

---

## 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T**  | Set of trains, indexed by *t* (|T| = N). |
| **S**  | Set of track **segments** (between two consecutive stations), indexed by *s*. |
| **P**  | Set of admissible **speed levels** (including a “stop’’ level 0), indexed by *p*. |
| **D**  | Directions on a bi‑directional line: **F** (forward) or **B** (backward). |
| **B**  | Set of **partial blockages**; each element is a pair *(s,b)* meaning that a part *b* of segment *s* is blocked. |
| **Adj**| Set of ordered adjacent‑segment pairs \((s,s')\) that can follow each other on any feasible route. |

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| \(L_s\) | Length of segment *s* | km |
| \(v_p\) | Nominal speed for speed level *p* | km h⁻¹ (for *p = 0* a very small value \(\varepsilon\) is used) |
| \(E_p\) | Energy consumption per kilometre at speed level *p* | kWh km⁻¹ |
| \(\Delta^{\text{acc}}_{p,p'}\) | Minimum time needed to change from speed level *p* to *p'* on a segment (accounts for acceleration/deceleration) | min |
| \(C_{s,b}\) | **Clearance time** – earliest instant at which the blocked part *b* of segment *s* can be traversed | min |
| \(A^{\text{plan}}_t\) | Planned (original) arrival time of train *t* at its final destination | min |
| \(T^{0}_t\) | Planned (original) departure time of train *t* from its origin | min |
| \(\gamma\) | Weight of delay in the objective (e.g. € min⁻¹) | – |
| \(\beta\)  | Weight of energy in the objective (e.g. € kWh⁻¹) | – |
| \(M\) | “Big‑M’’ constant larger than any feasible time (e.g. horizon length) | min |
| \(\varepsilon\) | Small positive number (≈ 0.001 min) to avoid division by zero | min |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,s,p}\) | Binary | Train *t* uses **speed level p** while traversing segment *s*. |
| \(y_{t,s}\)   | Binary | Train *t* **occupies** segment *s* (i.e. is present on it). |
| \(z_{t,s,d}\) | Binary | Train *t* traverses segment *s* in **direction d** (F or B). |
| \(\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\) | Continuous ≥0 | **Departure time** of train *t* from the upstream end of segment *s*. |
| \(\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\) | Continuous ≥0 | **Arrival time** of train *t* at the downstream end of segment *s*. |
| \(\delta_t\) | Continuous ≥0 | **Total delay** of train *t* (actual final arrival – planned arrival). |
| \(e_t\) | Continuous ≥0 | **Total energy** consumed by train *t* on its whole route. |
| \(u_{t,s,\theta}\) | Binary | Train *t* occupies segment *s* during discrete time‑slice \(\theta\) (used for bidirectional conflict). |

---

## 4. Objective  

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\gamma \,\delta_t}_{\text{delay cost}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\beta \,e_t}_{\text{energy cost}}
}
\]

---

## 5. Constraints  

### 5.1 Speed‑level selection  

1. **Exactly one speed level on a traversed segment**  

\[
\forall t\in T,\;\forall s\in S:\qquad 
\sum_{p\in P} x_{t,s,p}= y_{t,s}
\tag{1}
\]

If a train does **not** occupy the segment (\(y_{t,s}=0\)) all speed‑level binaries are forced to 0.

### 5.2 Travel‑time (linearised)

2. **Travel time on a segment**  

\[
\forall t\in T,\;\forall s\in S:\qquad
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\;\ge\;
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}
\;+\;
\sum_{p\in P}\frac{L_s}{v_p}\,x_{t,s,p}
\;+\;
\sum_{p\in P}\Delta^{\text{acc}}_{p,0}\,x_{t,s,p}
\tag{2}
\]

The first summation is the pure travel time \(L_s/v_p\); the second adds a (linear) penalty for acceleration/deceleration.

### 5.3 Temporal flow along a train’s route  

3. **Successor‑segment timing**  

\[
\forall t\in T,\;\forall (s,s')\in\text{Adj}:\qquad
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s'} \;\ge\;
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\;+\;\varepsilon
\tag{3}
\]

4. **Origin departure cannot be earlier than the original plan**  

\[
\forall t\in T:\qquad 
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,\text{first}(t)} \;\ge\; T^{0}_t
\tag{4}
\]

### 5.4 Delay definition  

5. **Total delay of a train**  

Let \(s^{\text{last}}(t)\) be the last segment of train *t*.  

\[
\forall t\in T:\qquad
\delta_t \;\ge\;
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s^{\text{last}}(t)} - A^{\text{plan}}_t
\tag{5}
\]

Because \(\delta_t\ge 0\), early arrivals do not create negative delay.

### 5.5 Energy accounting  

6. **Energy consumption**  

\[
\forall t\in T:\qquad
e_t \;=\;
\sum_{s\in S}\;\sum_{p\in P} E_p\,L_s\,x_{t,s,p}
\tag{6}
\]

### 5.6 Partial‑blockage handling  

7. **Cannot enter a segment before the blockage is cleared**  

\[
\forall t\in T,\;\forall (s,b)\in B:\qquad
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\;\ge\; C_{s,b}\;-\;M\,(1-y_{t,s})
\tag{7}
\]

If the train does not occupy the segment (\(y_{t,s}=0\)) the big‑M term deactivates the constraint.

8. **If the free length after the blocked part is insufficient, the train may only stop (speed level 0) on that segment**  

Define a binary parameter  

\[
a_s=
\begin{cases}
1 &\text{if }L_s-\tau_{s,b}>0\ (\text{enough free length})\\
0 &\text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\]

Then  

\[
\forall t\in T,\;\forall s\in S:\qquad
\sum_{p\in P\setminus\{0\}} x_{t,s,p}\;\le\; a_s
\tag{8}
\]

When \(a_s=0\) the train can only choose the stop level \(p=0\).

### 5.7 Bidirectional conflict (single‑track protection)  

9. **At any discrete time‑slice a segment can be occupied by at most one train, regardless of direction**  

Introduce a time‑grid \(\Theta=\{0,\Delta,\!2\Delta,\dots,H\}\) where \(H\) is the planning horizon and \(\Delta\) a small slice (e.g. 1 min).  

Link the slice variable to the continuous times:

\[
u_{t,s,\theta}\;\ge\;
y_{t,s}
-\frac{\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}-\theta}{\Delta}
-\frac{\theta-\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}}{\Delta}
\qquad\forall t,s,\theta\in\Theta
\tag{9a}
\]

(standard big‑M linearisation omitted for brevity).  

**Capacity constraint**

\[
\forall s\in S,\;\forall\theta\in\Theta:\qquad
\sum_{t\in T} u_{t,s,\theta}\;\le\;1
\tag{9b}
\]

Thus no two trains (even in opposite directions) can be on the same physical track at the same instant.

### 5.8 Direction coupling  

10. **Direction binary equals occupancy**  

\[
\forall t\in T,\;\forall s\in S:\qquad
z_{t,s,F}+z_{t,s,B}= y_{t,s}
\tag{10}
\]

### 5.9 Logical linking (already implied)  

11. **Speed‑level binary implies occupancy**  

\[
x_{t,s,p}\le y_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,s,p
\tag{11}
\]

---

## 6. Complete MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(\gamma\,\delta_t+\beta\,e_t\bigr)\\[4pt]
\text{s.t.}&\quad (1)-(11)\\
&\;x_{t,s,p},\,y_{t,s},\,z_{t,s,d},\,u_{t,s,\theta}\in\{0,1\}\\
&\;\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s},\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s},\delta_t,e_t\ge 0
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only integer variables are the binaries that encode logical decisions (speed choice, segment occupancy, direction, time‑slice occupancy). Consequently the model is a **mixed‑integer linear program**.

---

## 7. Remarks & Practical Use  

* **Data preparation** – supply the sets, segment lengths, speed‑level catalogue \((v_p,E_p,\Delta^{\text{acc}}_{p,p'})\), original timetable \((T^{0}_t, A^{\text{plan}}_t)\), and blockage data \((C_{s,b},a_s)\).  
* **Big‑M selection** – set \(M\) to the length of the planning horizon (e.g. 1440 min for a 24 h horizon).  
* **Time‑slice granularity** – \(\Delta\) can be 1 min for high‑resolution conflict handling; coarser slices reduce the number of \(u\) variables.  
* **Scalability** – for large networks the model can be decomposed (e.g. Benders or column generation) exactly as described in the paper; the formulation above is the *master* that guarantees conflict‑free, feasible speed profiles.  
* **Extensions** – crew‑working‑time limits, platform‑occupancy windows, renewable‑energy incentives, or train‑cancellation decisions can be added by inserting further linear constraints or binary variables without breaking the MILP structure.

---

**Result:** The formulation above is a self‑contained, linear MILP that simultaneously decides **which route each train uses, when it enters and leaves every segment, and at which speed level it travels**, while respecting **partial blockages**, **bidirectional track‑sharing conflicts**, **acceleration limits**, and **energy‑delay trade‑offs**. It directly implements the integrated TRSMP problem described in the introductory text.

Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.

Text:
**Variables**

*Binary variables*  
\(x_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) – train \(t\) uses segment \(s\) in its original direction.  
\(y_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) – train \(t\) uses segment \(s\) in the opposite direction (rerouting).  

\(z_{t,k}\in\{0,1\}\) – train \(t\) is active (occupies a segment) in time interval \(k\).

*Continuous variables*  
\(a_{t,n}\ge 0\) – actual arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(n\).  
\(d_{t,n}\ge 0\) – departure time of train \(t\) from station \(n\).  
\(v_{t,k}\ge 0\) – average speed of train \(t\) in interval \(k\) (km/min).  
\(w^{x}_{t,s,k}\ge 0\) – linearisation of \(x_{t,s}\,z_{t,k}\).  
\(w^{y}_{t,s,k}\ge 0\) – linearisation of \(y_{t,s}\,z_{t,k}\).  
\(\Delta_t\ge 0\) – total delay of train \(t\) (arrival at its last station minus the original arrival).

**Parameters (assumed known)**  

\(T\) – set of trains, \(S\) – set of track segments, \(N_t\) – ordered list of stations for train \(t\), \(K\) – set of discrete time intervals.  

\(a^0_{t,n}, d^0_{t,n}\) – original timetable (arrival/departure).  

\(\ell_s\) – length of segment \(s\).  

\(\underline{\tau}_s,\ \overline{\tau}_s\) – minimum/maximum admissible travel time on segment \(s\).  

\(B\subseteq S\) – set of partially blocked segments.  

\(u_s, v_s\) – start and end of the disruption window on blocked segment \(s\).  

\(c_k\) – energy cost coefficient for interval \(k\).  

\(w^{\text{delay}}, w^{\text{energy}}\) – weighting factors in the objective.  

\(M\) – a sufficiently large constant for linearisation.

**Objective function**

\[
\min\; w^{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_t \;+\; w^{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in K}c_k\,v_{t,k}
\]

**Constraints**

1. **Path choice (direction selection)**  
   \[
   x_{t,s}+y_{t,s}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in S_t
   \tag{1}
   \]
   where \(S_t\) is the set of segments that train \(t\) must traverse.

2. **Rerouting only on blocked segments**  
   \[
   y_{t,s}=0 \qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in S\setminus B
   \tag{2}
   \]

3. **Dwell time at stations**  
   \[
   d_{t,n}\ge a_{t,n}+ \text{dwell} \qquad\forall t\in T,\; n\in N_t
   \tag{3}
   \]

4. **Travel‑time – speed linking (linearised)**  

   For each train‑segment‑interval triple introduce auxiliary variables \(w^{x}_{t,s,k},w^{y}_{t,s,k}\) that satisfy  

   \[
   \begin{aligned}
   w^{x}_{t,s,k}&\le x_{t,s},\\
   w^{x}_{t,s,k}&\le z_{t,k},\\
   w^{x}_{t,s,k}&\ge x_{t,s}+z_{t,k}-1,
   \end{aligned}
   \qquad
   \begin{aligned}
   w^{y}_{t,s,k}&\le y_{t,s},\\
   w^{y}_{t,s,k}&\le z_{t,k},\\
   w^{y}_{t,s,k}&\ge y_{t,s}+z_{t,k}-1,
   \end{aligned}
   \qquad\forall t,s,k
   \tag{4}
   \]

   The travel time contributed by segment \(s\) is expressed as  

   \[
   \tau_{t,s}= \sum_{k\in K}\frac{\ell_s}{v_{t,k}}\bigl(w^{x}_{t,s,k}+w^{y}_{t,s,k}\bigr)
   \tag{5}
   \]

   and must respect the admissible bounds  

   \[
   \underline{\tau}_s \le \tau_{t,s}\le \overline{\tau}_s \qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in S_t
   \tag{6}
   \]

5. **Capacity (conflict‑free usage of a segment)**  

   \[
   \sum_{t\in T}\bigl(w^{x}_{t,s,k}+w^{y}_{t,s,k}\bigr)\le 1 
   \qquad\forall s\in S,\; k\in K
   \tag{7}
   \]

6. **Temporal feasibility between consecutive stations**  

   Let \(s_{t,i}\) be the segment linking station \(n_{t,i}\) to \(n_{t,i+1}\). Then  

   \[
   a_{t,n_{t,i+1}}\ge d_{t,n_{t,i}}+\tau_{t,s_{t,i}}
   \qquad\forall t\in T,\; i=1,\dots,|N_t|-1
   \tag{8}
   \]

7. **Delay definition**  

   \[
   \Delta_t = a_{t,\,\text{last}(t)}-a^{0}_{t,\,\text{last}(t)} 
   \qquad\forall t\in T
   \tag{9}
   \]

8. **Binary variable domains** – already imposed by variable definitions.

**Assumptions (explicitly stated)**  

* The timetable is discretised into a finite set of intervals \(K\); within an interval the speed of a train is constant.  
* Each train occupies at most one segment per interval (captured by binary \(z_{t,k}\)).  
* Energy consumption is approximated by a linear function of the average speed in each interval (coefficient \(c_k\)).  
* The disruption window on a blocked segment only restricts the possibility of using the original direction; rerouting to the opposite track is allowed throughout the window.  
* Dwell time at every station is a fixed constant (can be made train‑specific if needed).  

The model above constitutes a complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockage, capturing bidirectional conflict resolution, rescheduling decisions, speed‑profile selection, and a combined objective of delay minimisation and energy efficiency.

Text:
**Variables**

* \(y_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) – train \(t\) uses segment \(s\) (including opposite‑track rerouting).  
* \(z_{t,\tau}\in\{0,1\}\) – train \(t\) departs in time period \(\tau\) (retiming).  
* \(x_{t,s,\tau}\in\{0,1\}\) – train \(t\) occupies segment \(s\) during period \(\tau\).  
* \(v_{t,s,\tau}\ge v_{\min }\) – speed of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) in period \(\tau\) (km/h).  
* \(a_{t,n}\) – arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(n\) (minutes).  
* \(d_{t,n}\) – departure time of train \(t\) from station \(n\) (minutes).  
* \(e_t\) – total energy consumption of train \(t\) (kWh).  
* \(w_{t,s,\tau}\) – auxiliary variable for linearising \(v_{t,s,\tau}^2\).  
* \(\delta_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}\) – ordering binary for two trains sharing segment \(s\).

**Parameters (assumed known)**  

* \(a^0_{t,n}\) – planned arrival time.  
* \(\mathrm{dwell}_{t,n}\) – minimum dwell time at station \(n\).  
* \(\ell_s\) – length of segment \(s\) (km).  
* \(v_{\min},v_{\max}\) – speed limits (km/h).  
* \(\alpha_s\) – energy coefficient for segment \(s\).  
* \(w_{\text{delay}},w_{\text{energy}}\) – objective weights.  
* \(\mathcal{B}\) – set of periods belonging to the disruption window.  
* \(\text{blocked}_s\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if segment \(s\) is blocked on its normal side.  
* \(\text{cap}_s\) – capacity of segment \(s\) (1 during blockage, 2 otherwise).  
* \(M\) – big‑M (maximum number of periods a train can occupy a segment).  
* \(L\) – allowed early‑arrival advance.  
* \(\overline{D}\) – maximum permissible delay.  
* \(\Delta\tau\) – length of a time period (minutes).  
* \(\text{path}_{t,n}\) – segment linking station \(n\) to \(n+1\) for train \(t\).

**Objective**

\[
\min\;
w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{n\in\mathcal N}\bigl(a_{t,n}-a^0_{t,n}\bigr)
\;+\;
w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in\mathcal T} e_t .
\]

**Constraints**

1. **Dwell time (flow)**
   \[
   d_{t,n}=a_{t,n}+ \mathrm{dwell}_{t,n}\qquad\forall t,\;n .
   \]

2. **Travel time between consecutive stations**  
   For the unique segment \(s=\text{path}_{t,n}\) linking \(n\rightarrow n+1\):
   \[
   a_{t,n+1}=d_{t,n}+ \sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\frac{\ell_s}{v_{t,s,\tau}}\,x_{t,s,\tau}
   \qquad\forall t,\;n=0,\dots,|\mathcal N|-2 .
   \]

3. **Speed limits (linked to segment usage)**
   \[
   v_{\min}\, y_{t,s}\le v_{t,s,\tau}\le v_{\max}\, y_{t,s}
   \qquad\forall t,s,\tau .
   \]

4. **Segment capacity**
   \[
   \sum_{t\in\mathcal T} y_{t,s}\le
   \begin{cases}
   1 & \text{if } \tau\in\mathcal B\text{ and }\text{blocked}_s=1,\\[2pt]
   2 & \text{otherwise},
   \end{cases}
   \qquad\forall s,\;\tau .
   \]

5. **Blockage exclusion**
   \[
   y_{t,s}=0,\;x_{t,s,\tau}=0
   \qquad\forall t,\;s\text{ with }\text{blocked}_s=1,\;\tau\in\mathcal B .
   \]

6. **Ordering of trains on a shared segment**  
   For every unordered pair \((t,t')\), \(t\neq t'\):
   \[
   \sum_{\tau}x_{t,s,\tau}\le M\,(1-\delta_{t,t',s}),\qquad
   \sum_{\tau}x_{t',s,\tau}\le M\,\delta_{t,t',s},
   \]
   \[
   \delta_{t,t',s}\le y_{t,s},\qquad
   \delta_{t,t',s}\le y_{t',s},
   \qquad\forall s .
   \]

7. **Energy consumption (linearised)**
   \[
   w_{t,s,\tau}\le v_{\max}^{2}\,x_{t,s,\tau},\qquad
   w_{t,s,\tau}\ge v_{\min}^{2}\,x_{t,s,\tau},
   \]
   \[
   w_{t,s,\tau}\ge v_{t,s,\tau}^{2}-(v_{\max}^{2})(1-x_{t,s,\tau}),
   \qquad\forall t,s,\tau .
   \]
   \[
   e_t=\sum_{s,\tau}\alpha_s\,w_{t,s,\tau}\qquad\forall t .
   \]

8. **Binary linking of occupation and usage**
   \[
   x_{t,s,\tau}\le y_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,s,\tau .
   \]

9. **Early‑arrival allowance**
   \[
   a_{t,n}\ge a^0_{t,n}-L\qquad\forall t,n .
   \]

10. **Maximum delay**
    \[
    a_{t,n}\le a^0_{t,n}+\overline{D}\qquad\forall t,n .
    \]

11. **Departure‑time definition (optional)**
    \[
    d_{t,0}= \sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\tau\,\Delta\tau\,z_{t,\tau},
    \qquad
    \sum_{\tau}z_{t,\tau}=1\qquad\forall t .
    \]

All variables and constraints are now fully specified; the model is a mixed‑integer linear program (the quadratic term in the energy definition is linearised via the auxiliary variable \(w_{t,s,\tau}\)). This formulation captures train retiming, rerouting (through \(y_{t,s}\)), bidirectional conflict resolution (ordering binaries \(\delta\)), and the coupling with speed‑profile decisions, while simultaneously minimising total delay and energy consumption.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockages**

---

### 1. Sets, indices and parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|----------|
| **T** | set of trains, indexed by *t* |
| **S** | set of stations (including origins and terminals) |
| **E** | set of directed track segments *e = (i → j)*,  *i , j ∈ S* |
| **Rₜ** ⊆ **R** | feasible routes for train *t*, indexed by *r* |
| **K** | set of speed‑profile pieces (piece‑wise linear blocks), indexed by *k* |
| **B** ⊆ **E** | blocked segments (or sub‑segments) |
| **Δ** = \([Δ^{\text{start}},Δ^{\text{end}}]\) | disruption time window (known) |
| \(τ^{\text{orig}}_{t}\) | original scheduled arrival time of train *t* at its final destination |
| \(w_{t}\) | weight of train *t* in the objective (e.g. passenger importance) |
| \(c_{t,k}\) | energy‑consumption coefficient of speed piece *k* for train *t* |
| \(L_{e}\) | length of segment *e* (km) |
| \(v^{\max}_{e}\) | maximum admissible speed on segment *e* |
| \(a^{\max}, d^{\max}\) | maximal acceleration / deceleration (km/h²) |
| \(h_{e}\) | minimum headway (time) between opposite‑direction trains on segment *e* |
| \(d^{\min}_{t,s}, d^{\max}_{t,s}\) | minimum / maximum dwell time of train *t* at station *s* |
| \(M\) | a sufficiently large constant (big‑M) |

Derived parameters  

\[
\text{travel}_{e,k}= \frac{L_{e}}{v_{e,k}} \qquad
(\text{travel time on }e\text{ if speed piece }k\text{ is used})
\]

Only speed pieces with \(v_{e,k}\le v^{\max}_{e}\) are kept.

---

### 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|----------|
| \(x_{t,r}\) ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* uses route *r* |
| \(z_{t,e}\) ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* traverses segment *e* |
| \(y_{t,e,k}\) ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* uses speed piece *k* on segment *e* |
| \(a_{t,s}\) ≥ 0 | continuous | arrival time of train *t* at station *s* |
| \(d_{t,s}\) ≥ 0 | continuous | departure time of train *t* from station *s* |
| \(\delta_{t,e}\) ≥ 0 | continuous | travel time of train *t* on segment *e* |
| \(\beta_{t}\) ≥ 0 | continuous | delay of train *t* at its final destination |
| \(b_{t,e}\) ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* passes blocked segment *e* **after** the disruption window |
| \(\gamma_{t,t',e}\) ∈ {0,1} | binary | head‑way ordering on segment *e* for opposite‑direction pair \((t,t')\) |

---

### 3. Objective function  

\[
\min\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} w_{t}\,\beta_{t}}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\lambda \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{k\in K} c_{t,k}\,y_{t,e,k}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
\]

\(\lambda>0\) balances the two criteria.

---

### 4. Constraints  

#### 4.1 Routing (exactly one route per train)  

\[
\sum_{r\in R_{t}} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T \tag{R1}
\]

#### 4.2 Link route choice to segment usage  

\[
z_{t,e}= \sum_{r\in R_{t}} \mathbf{1}_{e\in r}\,x_{t,r}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\in E \tag{R2}
\]

(\(\mathbf{1}_{e\in r}=1\) if segment *e* belongs to route *r*, else 0.)

#### 4.3 Speed‑piece selection per used segment  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} y_{t,e,k}=z_{t,e}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\in E \tag{S1}
\]

#### 4.4 Travel‑time definition  

\[
\delta_{t,e}= \sum_{k\in K} \text{travel}_{e,k}\, y_{t,e,k}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\in E \tag{S2}
\]

#### 4.5 Time feasibility along a chosen route  

For every consecutive pair of stations \((s,s')\) linked by segment \(e=(s\rightarrow s')\):

\[
a_{t,s'} \ge d_{t,s}+ \delta_{t,e} - M\,(1-z_{t,e})
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\in E \tag{T1}
\]

If \(z_{t,e}=0\) the constraint is inactive.

#### 4.6 Blockage avoidance (train must be completely before or after the disruption)  

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{t,i} &\ge Δ^{\text{end}} - M\,b_{t,e}\\
d_{t,i} &\le Δ^{\text{start}} + M\,(1-b_{t,e})\\
b_{t,e}&\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e=(i\rightarrow j)\in B \tag{B1}
\]

If \(b_{t,e}=1\) the train passes **after** the window, otherwise **before**.

#### 4.7 Bidirectional head‑way (conflict‑free sharing of a segment)  

For every unordered pair \((t,t')\) that use the same segment *e* in opposite directions:

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{t,i} &\ge d_{t',j}+h_{e} - M\,\gamma_{t,t',e}\\
a_{t',i}&\ge d_{t,j}+h_{e} - M\,(1-\gamma_{t,t',e})\\
\gamma_{t,t',e}&\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall e\in E,\; t<t',\; z_{t,e}=z_{t',e}=1 \tag{H1}
\]

#### 4.8 Dwell‑time limits at stations  

\[
d^{\min}_{t,s}\le d_{t,s}-a_{t,s}\le d^{\max}_{t,s}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S \tag{D1}
\]

If a train does not stop at a station, set both bounds to 0.

#### 4.9 Acceleration / deceleration limits (linearised)  

Only speed pieces that respect the physical limits are kept, i.e.

\[
y_{t,e,k}=0\quad\text{if}\;v_{e,k}>v^{\max}_{e}
\]

If a finer representation of acceleration is required, admissible **pairs** \((k_{acc},k_{cruise})\) are pre‑computed such that  

\[
\frac{v_{e,k_{cruise}}-v_{e,k_{acc}}}{\ell_{e,k_{acc}}}\le a^{\max},
\qquad
\frac{v_{e,k_{acc}}-v_{e,k_{cruise}}}{\ell_{e,k_{acc}}}\le d^{\max}
\]

and a binary variable selects exactly one admissible pair per segment (omitted here for brevity).

#### 4.10 Definition of delay at the final destination  

Let \(s^{\text{dest}}_{t}\) be the terminal station of train *t*.

\[
\beta_{t}\ge a_{t,s^{\text{dest}}_{t}}-τ^{\text{orig}}_{t},
\qquad
\beta_{t}\ge 0
\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{Delay}
\]

---

### 5. Complete MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{t\in T} w_{t}\,\beta_{t}
      +\lambda\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{k\in K} c_{t,k}\,y_{t,e,k}\\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(R1)–(R2), (S1)–(S2), (T1), (B1), (H1), (D1), \\
&\text{acceleration‑limit pre‑processing, (Delay)}\\
&x_{t,r},y_{t,e,k},z_{t,e},b_{t,e},\gamma_{t,t',e}\in\{0,1\}\\

\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 6. Modelling assumptions (explicit)

1. **Deterministic disruption window** – start and end times are known.  
2. **Finite set of feasible routes** for each train has been pre‑computed.  
3. **Piece‑wise constant speed** – each speed piece keeps a constant speed on its whole segment; the overall speed profile is the concatenation of selected pieces.  
4. **No overtaking** – trains keep their order on each line; overtaking would need extra binaries.  
5. **Linear energy approximation** – \(c_{t,k}\) is a linear coefficient (e.g., proportional to \(v_{e,k}^2\)).  
6. **Big‑M values** are chosen as the planning horizon (or a tight upper bound on any possible time).  

The model is a pure MILP and can be handed to any commercial/open‑source MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP, …).  With route‑pre‑selection and a modest number of speed pieces per segment, the formulation is tractable for realistic high‑speed‑rail instances (tens of trains, a few hundred segments).

**Sets**

\[
\begin{aligned}
T & : \text{set of trains},\\
S & : \text{set of track segments},\\
N & : \text{ordered set of stations},\\
I & : \text{discrete time intervals},\; i=0,\dots ,|I|-1 .
\end{aligned}
\]

**Parameters**

\[
\begin{aligned}
\ell_s      &:\text{length of segment }s\;(m)\\
\text{cap}_s&:\text{capacity of segment }s\;(\#\text{trains per interval})\\[2mm]
B^{\text{start}}_s,\;B^{\text{end}}_s &:\text{first/last interval of blockage on }s 
          \;(B^{\text{start}}_s=-1\;\Rightarrow\; \text{no blockage})\\[2mm]
\text{start}_s,\;\text{end}_s &:\text{up‑ and downstream stations of segment }s\\[2mm]
\Delta t    &:\text{length of one interval (seconds)}\\
H          &:\text{minimum headway (seconds)}\\
M          &:\text{large constant (big‑M)}\\[2mm]
e_v        &:\text{energy cost per speed unit ( $/(\text{m/s})$ )}\\
v^{\max},v^{\min}&:\text{speed limits (m/s)}\\
a^{\max},d^{\max}&:\text{acceleration / deceleration limits (m/s}^{2}\text{)}\\[2mm]
\text{dwell}_{t,n}&:\text{minimum dwell time of train }t\text{ at station }n\;(s)\\
\text{sched}_{t,n}&:\text{scheduled arrival time of }t\text{ at }n\;(s)\\[2mm]
\pi_{\text{canc}} &:\text{cancellation penalty (large $)$}\\[2mm]
w_{\text{delay}},w_{\text{energy}}&:\text{weights for the two objectives (optional).}
\end{aligned}
\]

**Decision variables**

\[
\begin{aligned}
x_{t,s,i}&\in\{0,1\} &&\text{train }t\text{ uses segment }s\text{ on its normal track in interval }i\\
z_{t,s,i}&\in\{0,1\} &&\text{train }t\text{ uses segment }s\text{ on the opposite track (reroute)}\\
y_{t,n}&\ge 0      &&\text{arrival time of train }t\text{ at station }n\\
v_{t,i}&\ge v^{\min},\; v_{t,i}\le v^{\max} &&\text{speed of train }t\text{ during interval }i\\
a_{t,i}&\ge -d^{\max},\; a_{t,i}\le a^{\max}
               &&\text{acceleration of train }t\text{ during interval }i\\
u_{t}&\in\{0,1\} &&\text{cancellation indicator (1 = cancelled).}
\end{aligned}
\]

**Objective (weighted sum of delay, energy, and cancellation penalty)**  

\[
\min\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{n\in N}\bigl(y_{t,n}-\text{sched}_{t,n}\bigr)(1-u_t)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in I} e_v\,v_{t,i}\,\Delta t\;(1-u_t)}_{\text{total energy}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\pi_{\text{canc}}\sum_{t\in T} u_t}_{\text{cancellation penalty}} .
\]

(If desired: multiply the first two terms by weights \(w_{\text{delay}},w_{\text{energy}}\).)

**Constraints**

1. **Travel‑time (flow) consistency** – for any train that traverses segment \(s\) in interval \(i\) (normal or opposite track):

\[
y_{t,\text{end}_s}\;\ge\;
y_{t,\text{start}_s}
\;+\;
\frac{\ell_s}{v_{t,i}}\bigl(x_{t,s,i}+z_{t,s,i}\bigr)
\;-\;
M\bigl(1-x_{t,s,i}-z_{t,s,i}\bigr),\qquad
\forall t,s,i.
\]

2. **Segment capacity on normal track** (only outside blockage window):

\[
\sum_{t\in T} x_{t,s,i}\;\le\;\text{cap}_s,
\qquad
\forall s,i\;:\;i\notin[B^{\text{start}}_s,\,B^{\text{end}}_s].
\]

3. **Segment capacity on opposite track** (same capacity, allowed also during blockage):

\[
\sum_{t\in T} z_{t,s,i}\;\le\;\text{cap}_s,
\qquad\forall s,i .
\]

4. **Blockage restriction** – normal‑track usage forbidden during blockage:

\[
x_{t,s,i}=0,
\qquad\forall t,s,i\;:\;i\in[B^{\text{start}}_s,\,B^{\text{end}}_s].
\]

5. **Speed limits** – already enforced by bounds on \(v_{t,i}\).

6. **Acceleration definition** (for \(i>0\)):

\[
a_{t,i}= \frac{v_{t,i}-v_{t,i-1}}{\Delta t},
\qquad\forall t,i>0 .
\]

7. **Dwell‑time requirement** at each station (except the last):

\[
y_{t,n+1}-y_{t,n}\;\ge\;\text{dwell}_{t,n}\;(1-u_t),
\qquad\forall t,\;n\neq\max N .
\]

8. **Headway (conflict‑avoidance) for trains sharing a segment** – if two trains occupy the same segment in the same interval, a headway \(H\) must separate their arrivals at the downstream station:

\[
y_{t_2,\text{end}_s}\;\ge\;y_{t_1,\text{end}_s}+H
   -M\bigl(2-x_{t_1,s,i}-x_{t_2,s,i}\bigr),
\qquad\forall t_1\neq t_2,\;s,i .
\]

9. **Linking normal and opposite‑track usage** (mutual exclusion):

\[
z_{t,s,i}\le 1- x_{t,s,i},
\qquad\forall t,s,i .
\]

10. **Cancellation logic** – when a train is cancelled, all operational variables are forced to zero:

\[
\begin{aligned}
x_{t,s,i}&\le 1-u_t,\\
z_{t,s,i}&\le 1-u_t,\\
v_{t,i}&\le v^{\max}(1-u_t),\\
\text{(the delay term in the objective already vanishes).}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t,s,i .
\]

---

### Assumptions (explicit)

* Time is discretised into equal intervals of length \(\Delta t\).  
* Each train uses a single constant speed within an interval.  
* Opposite‑track capacity equals normal‑track capacity.  
* All trains travel in the same direction; headway constraints are applied on any common segment‑interval pair.  
* Energy consumption is approximated linearly by \(e_v\,v_{t,i}\,\Delta t\).  
* Cancellation incurs a large fixed penalty \(\pi_{\text{canc}}\) to discourage unnecessary cancellation.  

The model above constitutes a complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the **integrated train rescheduling and speed management problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages, addressing bidirectional conflicts, speed‑profile feasibility, and energy efficiency.

**Variables**

| Symbol | Meaning | Type |
|--------|---------|------|
| \(x_{t,s}\) | 1 if train \(t\) uses blocked segment \(s\) in its original direction, 0 otherwise | binary |
| \(y_{t,s}\) | 1 if train \(t\) uses blocked segment \(s\) in the opposite (rerouted) direction, 0 otherwise | binary |
| \(a_{t,n}\) | Actual arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(n\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) |
| \(d_{t,n}\) | Actual departure time of train \(t\) from station \(n\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) |
| \(v_{t,k}\) | Average speed of train \(t\) in time interval \(k\) | continuous, \(v_{\min}\le v_{t,k}\le v_{\max}\) |
| \(z_{t,k}\) | 1 if train \(t\) is travelling during interval \(k\), 0 otherwise | binary |
| \(\delta_{t,k}\) | \(|v_{t,k}-v^{0}_{t,k}|\) (linearised) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) |
| \(o_{t,t',s}\) | 1 if train \(t\) precedes train \(t'\) on segment \(s\) (conflict‑avoidance) | binary |

**Parameters**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(\mathcal T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\) |
| \(\mathcal S\) | Set of track segments (original direction), indexed by \(s\) |
| \(\mathcal N=\{0,\dots,N\}\) | Set of stations, \(0\) = origin, \(N\) = last |
| \(\mathcal K\) | Set of discrete time intervals, indexed by \(k\) |
| \(\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal S\) | Set of blocked segments |
| \(a^{0}_{t,N}\) | Planned arrival time of train \(t\) at the last station (baseline) |
| \(\tau^{\text{dwell}}_{n}\) | Minimum dwell time at station \(n\) |
| \(\underline{t}_{t,s},\ \overline{t}_{t,s}\) | Minimum / maximum feasible travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) (derived from distance and speed limits) |
| \([u_{s},v_{s}]\) | Disruption time window on blocked segment \(s\) (no passage in original direction) |
| \(v^{0}_{t,k}\) | Nominal speed of train \(t\) in interval \(k\) (from the original timetable) |
| \(c_{k}\) | Energy‑cost coefficient for speed deviation in interval \(k\) |
| \(M\) | Large constant for big‑M linearisation (greater than the planning horizon) |
| \(W^{\text{delay}},\;W^{\text{energy}}\) | Weights in the objective function |

**Objective function**

\[
\min\; 
W^{\text{delay}}\;\underbrace{\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\bigl(a_{t,N}-a^{0}_{t,N}\bigr)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
W^{\text{energy}}\;\underbrace{\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_{k}\,\delta_{t,k}}_{\text{total energy cost}}
\]

with linearisation of the absolute value:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\delta_{t,k} &\ge v_{t,k}-v^{0}_{t,k} &&\forall t,k\\
\delta_{t,k} &\ge v^{0}_{t,k}-v_{t,k} &&\forall t,k
\end{aligned}
\]

**Constraints**

1. **Direction choice on blocked segments** (each train must either keep the original direction or be rerouted):
   \[
   x_{t,s}+y_{t,s}=1 \qquad \forall t\in\mathcal T,\; s\in\mathcal B
   \]

2. **Capacity of a segment per interval** (at most one train may occupy a segment in a given direction during an interval):
   \[
   \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\bigl(x_{t,s}\,z_{t,k}+y_{t,s}\,z_{t,k}\bigr)\le 1 
   \qquad\forall s\in\mathcal S,\;k\in\mathcal K
   \]

   \[
   x_{t,s}=0 \qquad\forall t\in\mathcal T,\; s\in\mathcal B\text{ with }[u_{s},v_{s}]\cap\text{interval }k\neq\emptyset
   \]

4. **Dwell time at stations**:
   \[
   d_{t,n}=a_{t,n}+\tau^{\text{dwell}}_{n}\qquad\forall t\in\mathcal T,\; n\in\mathcal N\setminus\{N\}
   \]

5. **Time‑propagation (travel between consecutive stations)**  
   Let \(s(n)\) be the segment linking station \(n\) to \(n+1\) and let \(k(t,n)\) be the interval in which train \(t\) traverses that segment (pre‑computed or modelled with additional binaries). Then:
   \[
   a_{t,n+1}=d_{t,n}+ \frac{\underline{t}_{t,s(n)}+\overline{t}_{t,s(n)}}{2\,v_{t,k(t,n)}} 
   \qquad\forall t\in\mathcal T,\; n\in\{0,\dots,N-1\}
   \]

6. **Speed limits** (already imposed by variable bounds):
   \[
   v_{\min}\le v_{t,k}\le v_{\max}\qquad\forall t,k
   \]

7. **Linking binary \(z_{t,k}\) with actual travelling** (big‑M):
   \[
   a_{t,N}\le k\;M+(1-z_{t,k})M,\qquad
   d_{t,0}\ge (k-1)M-(1-z_{t,k})M\qquad\forall t,k
   \]

8. **Non‑negative delay at the last station**:
   \[
   a_{t,N}\ge a^{0}_{t,N}\qquad\forall t\in\mathcal T
   \]

9. **Conflict‑avoidance ordering on shared segments** (optional, to guarantee conflict‑free bidirectional use):
   \[
   a_{t,n}+ \frac{\underline{t}_{t,s}+\overline{t}_{t,s}}{2\,v_{t,k(t,n)}}\le 
   a_{t',n}+M\bigl(1-o_{t,t',s}\bigr)
   \qquad\forall t\neq t',\; s\in\mathcal S,\; n\text{ upstream of }s
   \]
   \[
   o_{t,t',s}+o_{t',t,s}=1\qquad\forall t\neq t',\; s\in\mathcal S
   \]

**Assumptions (explicitly stated)**  

* The planning horizon is discretised into a finite set of intervals \(\mathcal K\); each train traverses a segment completely within a single interval (or a pre‑computed mapping \(k(t,n)\) is used).  
* Travel time on a segment is approximated by the average of its lower and upper bounds divided by the average speed chosen for the interval.  
* Energy consumption is modelled as a linear function of the absolute deviation of the chosen speed from the nominal speed; more detailed power models can replace the coefficient \(c_k\).  
* Capacity of a segment is one train per direction per interval; bidirectional sharing is allowed only when a train is rerouted to the opposite track.  
* Binary ordering variables \(o_{t,t',s}\) are introduced only if the instance contains bidirectional conflicts; they can be omitted for a simpler formulation.  

The formulation above constitutes a complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) model for the **Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages, capturing timetable feasibility, rerouting decisions, speed‑profile optimisation, and energy efficiency.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages**  

All symbols are defined in the tables below; the model is linear (mixed‑integer) and can be solved with any standard MILP solver.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|----------|
| **T** | Trains, *t* ∈ T |
| **S** | Directed track‑segments, *s* ∈ S |
| **V** | Stations (network nodes), *v* ∈ V |
| **A** ⊂ S | Segments that are partially blocked (δₛ>0) |
| **K** | Discrete admissible speed levels, *k* ∈ K |
| **τ** = {0,…,τₘₐₓ} | Discrete time‑steps (Δt minutes) |
| **P(t)** | Pre‑generated feasible paths for train *t* (ordered list of segments) |
| **U** | Set of ordered pairs *(t₁,t₂,s)* that could conflict on segment *s* |

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|------|
| Lₛ | Length of segment *s* | km |
| vₖ | Speed value of level *k* | km h⁻¹ |
| Δt | Length of one time‑step | min |
| αₖ | Energy per km for cruising at speed *vₖ* | kWh km⁻¹ |
| βₖ | Energy per (km h⁻¹)² for acceleration/deceleration at level *k* | kWh (km h⁻¹)⁻² |
| γₛ | Minimum head‑way on segment *s* | min |
| δₛ ∈[0,1] | Fraction of width of segment *s* that is blocked (δₛ=0 ⇔ free) |
| Tᵈʷₙᵗʳᵉₗᵥ | Minimum dwell time at a stop | min |
| Tᵘₚₚₑᵣ | Maximum dwell time allowed | min |
| τ^{plan}_t | Planned arrival time of train *t* at its final destination | min |
| w₁ , w₂ >0 | Weight of total delay and total energy in the objective |
| M | Large constant (≥ longest possible schedule) |
| Δ⁺, Δ⁻ | Max admissible speed change between consecutive segments | km h⁻¹ |
| τ^{blk,start}_s , τ^{blk,end}_s | Start / end of the blockage time window on *s* | time‑step index |
| v^{max}_s = (1‑δₛ)·v^{max} , v^{min}_s = v^{min} | Effective speed limits on a partially blocked segment |
| T^{min}_s = Lₛ / v^{max}_s ,   T^{max}_s = Lₛ / v^{min}_s | Minimum / maximum feasible travel time on *s* |

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| x_{t p} ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* uses path *p* ∈ P(t) |
| y_{t s τ} ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* occupies segment *s* during time‑step τ |
| a_{t v} ≥ 0 | continuous | Arrival time of train *t* at station *v* |
| d_{t v} ≥ 0 | continuous | Departure time of train *t* from station *v* |
| T_{t s} ≥ 0 | continuous | Travel time of train *t* on segment *s* |
| u_{t s} ≥ 0 | continuous | Inverse speed on *s*: u_{t s}=∑ₖ (1/vₖ) z_{t s k} |
| z_{t s k} ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* traverses segment *s* with speed level *k* |
| e_{t s k} ≥ 0 | continuous | Energy contributed on *s* at speed level *k* |
| e_t ≥ 0 | continuous | Total energy of train *t* |
| π_{t₁ t₂ s} ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ *t₁* passes *s* before *t₂* (ordering) |
| b_{t s} ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* traverses a blocked segment *s* ∈ A |
| σ_{t s} ≥ 0 | continuous | Start time of train *t* on segment *s* (auxiliary, defined below) |

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Objective  

\[
\boxed{
\min\; 
w_{1}\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(a_{t,\text{dest}(t)}-\tau^{\text{plan}}_{t}\bigr)
\;+\;
w_{2}\sum_{t\in T} e_{t}
}
\]

*First term = total passenger delay; second term = total electrical energy.*

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Constraints  

#### (1) Path selection  
\[
\sum_{p\in P(t)} x_{t p}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T
\]

#### (2) Single‑track occupancy (conflict)  
\[
\sum_{t\in T} y_{t s \tau}\le 1 \qquad\forall s\in S,\;\forall \tau\in\tau
\]

Link occupancy to the chosen path and travel time (big‑M formulation): for every *t,s* that belong to the chosen path,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sigma_{t s} &\le \tau\Delta t + M\bigl(1-y_{t s \tau}\bigr) \\
\sigma_{t s}+T_{t s} &\ge (\tau+1)\Delta t - M\bigl(1-y_{t s \tau}\bigr)
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t,s,\tau
\]

#### (3) Train dynamics – speed ↔ travel time  

Inverse‑speed definition (linear):  
\[
u_{t s}= \sum_{k\in K}\frac{1}{v_{k}}\,z_{t s k}\qquad\forall t,s
\]

Travel time:  
\[
T_{t s}=L_{s}\,u_{t s}\qquad\forall t,s
\]

Acceleration / deceleration limits (for any two consecutive segments *s^{in}, s^{out}* of the same train):

\[
\sum_{k}v_{k}z_{t s^{out}k}-\sum_{k}v_{k}z_{t s^{in}k}\le \Delta^{+}
\]
\[
\sum_{k}v_{k}z_{t s^{in}k}-\sum_{k}v_{k}z_{t s^{out}k}\le \Delta^{-}
\qquad\forall t,\;(s^{in},s^{out})
\]

#### (4) Dwell‑time windows  

\[
T^{\min}_{\text{dwell}}\le d_{t v}-a_{t v}\le T^{\max}_{\text{dwell}}
\qquad\forall t,\;v\in V\text{ visited by }t
\]

#### (5) Blockage availability  

For any blocked segment *s∈A* and any τ inside its blockage window:

\[
y_{t s \tau}=0 \qquad\forall t,\;\forall \tau\in\bigl[ \tau^{\text{blk,start}}_{s},\;\tau^{\text{blk,end}}_{s}\bigr]
\]

#### (6) Ordering (re‑ordering) variables  

For each conflict pair *(t₁,t₂,s)∈U* :

\[
\sigma_{t_{1}s}+ \gamma_{s}\le \sigma_{t_{2}s}+M\bigl(1-\pi_{t_{1}t_{2}s}\bigr)
\]
\[
\sigma_{t_{2}s}+ \gamma_{s}\le \sigma_{t_{1}s}+M\pi_{t_{1}t_{2}s}
\]
\[
\pi_{t_{1}t_{2}s}+ \pi_{t_{2}t_{1}s}=1
\qquad\forall (t_{1},t_{2},s)\in U
\]

#### (7) Rerouting on blocked segment  

\[
b_{t s}\ge \sum_{p\in P(t)}x_{t p}\,\mathbf{1}_{\{s\in p\}}\qquad\forall t,\;s\in A
\]

(Optionally add a penalty term \(+w_{blk}\sum_{t,s\in A}b_{t s}\) to the objective.)

#### (8) Linearised speed‑energy relation  

\[
e_{t s k}= \bigl(\alpha_{k}+\beta_{k}\bigr)L_{s}\,z_{t s k}
\qquad\forall t,s,k
\]
\[
e_{t}= \sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} e_{t s k}\qquad\forall t
\]

#### (9) Feasible travel‑time bounds  

\[
T^{\min}_{s}\;\sum_{p}x_{t p}\mathbf{1}_{\{s\in p\}}\le T_{t s}\le 
T^{\max}_{s}\;\sum_{p}x_{t p}\mathbf{1}_{\{s\in p\}}
\qquad\forall t,s
\]

#### (10) Consistency between speed choice and path  

\[
\sum_{k\in K}z_{t s k}= \sum_{p\in P(t)}x_{t p}\,\mathbf{1}_{\{s\in p\}}
\qquad\forall t,s
\]

#### (11) Timing continuity on a path  

If *s^{in}* precedes *s^{out}* on the chosen path of *t* :

\[
\sigma_{t s^{out}} = \sigma_{t s^{in}} + T_{t s^{in}}
\qquad\forall t,\;(s^{in},s^{out})\text{ consecutive on the selected path}
\]

The arrival/departure times at stations are linked to the segment start times in the usual way (first segment start = departure from origin, last segment end = arrival at destination).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 6. Variable Domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t p}, y_{t s \tau}, z_{t s k}, b_{t s}, \pi_{t_{1}t_{2}s} \in\{0,1\}\\
&a_{t v}, d_{t v}, T_{t s}, u_{t s}, \sigma_{t s}, e_{t s k}, e_{t}\ge 0
\end{aligned}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 7. Modelling Assumptions (explicit)

1. **Pre‑generated feasible paths** *P(t)* are given (e.g., k‑shortest‑paths); the MILP only selects among them.  
2. **Speed discretisation**: a small finite set *K* of cruise speeds approximates the continuous speed envelope.  
3. **Energy linearisation**: total energy per segment is approximated by a constant cruise term plus a linearised acceleration term (αₖ,βₖ).  
4. **Partial blockage** reduces the usable speed limit on the segment to *v^{max}_s = (1‑δₛ)v^{max}* and forbids occupancy during the specified time window.  
5. **Head‑way safety** is guaranteed by the minimum separation γₛ and the ordering binaries π.  
6. **Dwell‑time limits** are imposed at every scheduled stop; optional stops can be modelled by an additional binary if required.  
7. **Time‑step Δt** is fine enough that a train occupies at most one step per segment; otherwise the big‑M linking constraints correctly capture the occupancy interval.  
8. **Big‑M** value M is set larger than any feasible schedule (e.g., 10⁶ min).  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 8. How to use  

1. **Data preparation** – build the network, compute lengths *Lₛ*, blockage fractions *δₛ* and windows, generate *P(t)* and the conflict set *U*.  
2. **Parameter calibration** – choose realistic αₖ, βₖ (from the train’s power‑energy curve) and weights *w₁, w₂*.  
3. **Solve** – feed the MILP to a solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP, CBC, …).  
4. **Interpretation** – *x_{t p}* gives the selected route; *z_{t s k}* gives the cruise speed level on each traversed segment, from which a continuous speed profile (including linear ramps respecting Δ⁺, Δ⁻) can be reconstructed.  

The formulation above satisfies **all required elements**: routing, re‑ordering, time‑indexed conflict avoidance, linearised train dynamics, dwell‑time windows, disruption‑time restrictions, binary activation of blocked‑segment usage, and a linear speed‑energy trade‑off, delivering a complete MILP description of the integrated train‑rescheduling and speed‑management problem.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (Partial Segment Blockage)**  

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | Set of trains, indexed by *t* |
| **S** | Set of track segments, indexed by *s* (segment *s* connects stations *i(s)*–*j(s)*) |
| **R** | Set of possible routes for a train (normally *R={0,1}*: original track =0, opposite track =1) |
| **K** | Set of speed‑level blocks (piece‑wise linear), indexed by *k* |
| **I** | Set of stations, indexed by *i* |
| **B** | Set of blocked side‑track segments (usually a single segment *s\** ) |
| **Ŝ** | Subset of **S** that are single‑track (bidirectional) – i.e. shared by opposite directions |
| **τ** | (optional) set of discrete time indices for “or‑” linearisation |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Definition | Unit |
|--------|------------|------|
| \(L_s\) | Length of segment *s* | km |
| \(\underline v_k ,\overline v_k\) | Min / max speed of speed level *k* | km h⁻¹ |
| \(v_k\) | Representative speed of level *k* (e.g. midpoint) | km h⁻¹ |
| \(\alpha_k\) | Energy coefficient of level *k* (kWh · km⁻¹) | kWh · km⁻¹ |
| \(d^{\text{dwell}}_{i,t}\) | Minimum dwell time of train *t* at station *i* | min |
| \(a^{\max},a^{\min}\) | Max acceleration / deceleration | km h⁻² |
| \(H\) | Minimum safety head‑way on a shared segment | min |
| \(T^{\text{start}}_{s\*},T^{\text{end}}_{s\*}\) | Disruption window on blocked side *s\*** | min (absolute clock) |
| \(\hat A_{i,t}\) | Planned (pre‑disruption) arrival time of *t* at station *i* | min |
| \(w_{\text{delay}},w_{\text{energy}}\) | Positive weights in the objective | – |
| \(c^{\text{route}}_r\) | Fixed cost (or penalty) for using route *r* | – |
| \(M\) | Large constant for big‑M linearisation | min (larger than planning horizon) |
| \(\rho_{s,r}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if route *r* contains segment *s* (pre‑computed) | – |
| \(\Delta^{\text{acc}}_{k,k'}\) | Minimum extra travel time required when speed level changes from *k* to *k'* (derived from \(a^{\max},a^{\min}\)) | min |

All parameters are assumed known from the timetable, infrastructure data and the disruption description.

---

### 3. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,r}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train *t* uses route *r* |
| \(y_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train *t* traverses segment *s* (implied by route) |
| \(z_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train *t* uses speed level *k* on segment *s* |
| \(A_{i,t}\ge0\) | continuous | Arrival time of *t* at station *i* (absolute) |
| \(D_{i,t}\ge0\) | continuous | Departure time of *t* from station *i* |
| \(\theta_{t,s}\ge0\) | continuous | Travel time of *t* on segment *s* |
| \(\delta_{i,t}\ge0\) | continuous | Delay of *t* at station *i*: \(\delta_{i,t}=A_{i,t}-\hat A_{i,t}\) |
| \(\eta_{t,s}\ge0\) | continuous | Energy consumption of *t* on segment *s* |
| \(\pi_{t_1,t_2,s}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | Ordering on shared segment *s*: 1 if *t₁* passes before *t₂* |
| \(\beta_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train *t* uses the **blocked side** of segment *s* (only relevant for *s∈B*) |
| \(\tilde\theta_{t,s,k}\ge0\) | continuous | Linearisation of \(\theta_{t,s}z_{t,s,k}\) (used in energy term) |

---

### 4. Objective  

\[
\min\;
w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in I}\delta_{i,t}
\;+\;
w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\eta_{t,s}
\;+\;
\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{r\in R}c^{\text{route}}_r\,x_{t,r}
\]

*Minimise a weighted sum of total passenger delay, total energy consumption and (optional) route‑change cost.*

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Route choice and segment usage  

1. **Exactly one route per train**  
   \[
   \sum_{r\in R} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T   \tag{R1}
   \]

2. **Link route to traversed segments**  
   \[
   y_{t,s}= \sum_{r\in R}\rho_{s,r}\,x_{t,r} \qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S   \tag{R2}
   \]

#### 5.2 Speed‑level selection  

3. **One speed level on a used segment**  
   \[
   \sum_{k\in K} z_{t,s,k}= y_{t,s} \qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S   \tag{S1}
   \]

#### 5.3 Travel‑time – speed relationship (piece‑wise linear)  

4. **Travel time equals length / chosen speed**  
   \[
   \theta_{t,s}= \sum_{k\in K}\frac{L_s}{v_k}\,z_{t,s,k} \qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S   \tag{T1}
   \]

#### 5.4 Acceleration / deceleration limits  

5. **If speed level changes, enforce extra time** (linearised with auxiliary binaries)  

   For every consecutive pair \((s,s')\) on the path of train *t*  
   \[
   \theta_{t,s'} \;\ge\; \theta_{t,s}
   +\sum_{k,k'\in K}\Delta^{\text{acc}}_{k,k'}\,w_{t,s,k,k'}   \tag{A1}
   \]  

   where \(w_{t,s,k,k'}\) is a binary product \(z_{t,s,k}\,z_{t,s',k'}\) linearised by standard big‑M constraints.

#### 5.5 Time propagation  

6. **Dwell time**  
   \[
   D_{i,t}\ge A_{i,t}+d^{\text{dwell}}_{i,t}\qquad\forall t,i   \tag{D1}
   \]

7. **Travel from station *i* to *j***  
   \[
   A_{j,t}= D_{i,t}+ \theta_{t,s(i,j)}\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\text{ adjacent}   \tag{P1}
   \]

8. **Delay definition**  
   \[
   \delta_{i,t}=A_{i,t}-\hat A_{i,t}\qquad\forall t,i   \tag{Del1}
   \]

#### 5.6 Disruption (blocked side‑track)  

9. **No occupation of blocked side during the disruption window**  

   For every train *t* that would use the blocked side of segment *s\** (\(\beta_{t,s\*}=1\)) we enforce  
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
   &A_{i(s\*),t}\;\ge\; T^{\text{end}}_{s\*}\;-\;M\,(1-\beta_{t,s\*})\\
   \text{or}\;&\; D_{i(s\*),t}\;\le\; T^{\text{start}}_{s\*}\;+\;M\,(1-\beta_{t,s\*})
   \end{aligned}
   \tag{B1}
   \]  

   The “or’’ is linearised with an auxiliary binary \(\gamma_{t}\) (standard big‑M technique).

10. **Link blocked‑side indicator to segment usage**  
    \[
    \beta_{t,s\*}\le y_{t,s\*}\qquad\forall t   \tag{B2}
    \]

#### 5.7 Bidirectional conflict on a shared (single‑track) segment  

11. **Exactly one ordering for each pair using the same shared segment**  

    \[
    \pi_{t_1,t_2,s}+ \pi_{t_2,t_1,s}= y_{t_1,s}\,y_{t_2,s}\qquad
    \forall s\in\widehat S,\;t_1\neq t_2   \tag{O1}
    \]  

    The product \(y_{t_1,s}y_{t_2,s}\) is linearised with an auxiliary binary.

12. **Safety head‑way**  

    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    &A_{i(s),t_2}\;\ge\; D_{i(s),t_1}+H\;-\;M\bigl(1-\pi_{t_1,t_2,s}\bigr)\\
    &A_{i(s),t_1}\;\ge\; D_{i(s),t_2}+H\;-\;M\bigl(1-\pi_{t_2,t_1,s}\bigr)
    \end{aligned}
    \qquad\forall s\in\widehat S,\;t_1\neq t_2   \tag{O2}
    \]

#### 5.8 Energy consumption (piece‑wise linear)  

13. **Linearisation of \(\theta_{t,s}z_{t,s,k}\)**  

    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    &\tilde\theta_{t,s,k}\le M\,z_{t,s,k}\\
    &\tilde\theta_{t,s,k}\le \theta_{t,s}\\
    &\tilde\theta_{t,s,k}\ge \theta_{t,s}-M\,(1-z_{t,s,k})\\
    &\tilde\theta_{t,s,k}\ge 0
    \end{aligned}
    \qquad\forall t,s,k
    \]

14. **Energy on a segment**  

    \[
    \eta_{t,s}= \sum_{k\in K}\alpha_k\,\tilde\theta_{t,s,k}\qquad\forall t,s   \tag{E1}
    \]

#### 5.9 Optional service‑level constraints  

*Maximum allowed delay*: \(\delta_{i,t}\le \Delta^{\max}_t\) (if required).  
*No‑reverse movement*: enforce route‑direction consistency (model‑specific).

---

### 6. Complete MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{t,i}\delta_{i,t}
      + w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{t,s}\eta_{t,s}
      + \sum_{t,r}c^{\text{route}}_r x_{t,r}\\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(R1)–(R2)} && \text{route choice}\\
&\text{(S1)} && \text{speed‑level selection}\\
&\text{(T1)} && \text{travel time = length / speed}\\
&\text{(A1)} && \text{acceleration limits (linearised)}\\
&\text{(D1)} && \text{minimum dwell}\\
&\text{(P1)} && \text{time propagation}\\
&\text{(Del1)} && \text{delay definition}\\
&\text{(B1)–(B2)} && \text{blocked side‑track constraints}\\
&\text{(O1)–(O2)} && \text{single‑track ordering and headway}\\
&\text{(E1)} && \text{energy calculation}\\
&\text{(auxiliary linearisation constraints)}\\
&x_{t,r},y_{t,s},z_{t,s,k},\pi_{t_1,t_2,s},\beta_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\\
& A_{i,t},D_{i,t},\theta_{t,s},\delta_{i,t},\eta_{t,s},\tilde\theta_{t,s,k}\ge0
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; binary‑product terms are replaced by standard big‑M auxiliary binaries, preserving the **mixed‑integer linear programming** nature.

---

### 7. How the Model Works  

1. **Route decision** (\(x_{t,r}\)) determines which physical segments each train uses.  
2. **Speed‑level decision** (\(z_{t,s,k}\)) fixes a constant speed on each traversed segment, giving a deterministic travel time via (T1).  
3. **Acceleration limits** (A1) ensure feasible speed changes between consecutive segments.  
4. **Timetable propagation** (D1, P1) builds a conflict‑free schedule of arrivals/departures.  
5. **Disruption handling** (B1‑B2) forces any train that would use the blocked side of the disrupted segment to stay completely before or after the blockage.  
6. **Bidirectional conflict** (O1‑O2) resolves the single‑track sharing problem by ordering trains and imposing a safety headway.  
7. **Delay and energy** are computed and fed to the objective, which trades off passenger punctuality against energy consumption (and optionally route‑change costs).  

The solution provides **for every train**: the chosen route, the speed level on each segment, and the exact arrival/departure times that respect all safety, operational and disruption constraints while minimising the weighted sum of delay and energy.

---

### 8. Implementation Remarks  

* Choose \(M\) larger than the planning horizon (e.g., several hours).  
* Linearise each binary product with the standard three‑constraint formulation.  
* The set of ordering binaries \(\pi_{t_1,t_2,s}\) can be pruned by a preprocessing step: only pairs whose nominal schedules overlap need a variable.  
* The piece‑wise linear speed‑energy approximation (set **K**) can be refined (5–10 levels) to capture the quadratic nature of aerodynamic drag while keeping the model linear.  
* The model can be solved directly with any MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, SCIP, …). For very large instances a decomposition (Benders, column generation) or a two‑stage heuristic (first fix routes, then solve speed‑management) may be employed.  

---

**This MILP formulation is complete, linear, and directly reflects the description of an integrated train‑rescheduling and speed‑management problem under a partial segment blockage.**
