Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP)**  
The model simultaneously decides (i) a feasible post‑disruption timetable (arrival/departure times, train order and possible rerouting) and (ii) a set of piece‑wise‑linear speed profiles that respect train dynamics, track‑capacity and energy‑consumption considerations.  

---

## 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T=\{1,\dots ,|T|\}\) | Set of trains (both directions). |
| \(S=\{1,\dots ,|S|\}\) | Set of stations (including the origin 0 and the terminal \(|S|+1\)). |
| \(L=\{(i,j)\mid i\in S,\;j\in S,\;i<j\}\) | Set of line‑segments (track sections) between two consecutive stations. |
| \(D\subseteq L\) | Sub‑set of *disruption segments* (blocked on one track side). |
| \(\mathcal{K}=\{1,\dots ,K\}\) | Set of *speed‑profile intervals* (time discretisation). |
| \(\mathcal{P}_t\) | Set of *feasible plans* for train \(t\) (each plan contains a route, a sequence of segment‑travel times and a speed‑profile). |
| \(\mathcal{B}\subseteq T\times T\) | Set of *potential bidirectional conflicts* (pairs of trains that may occupy the same physical track at the same time). |

---

## 2. Parameters (assumptions are indicated)  

| Symbol | Description | Typical value / source |
|--------|-------------|------------------------|
| \(a^{\max}_t\) | Maximum admissible acceleration (m s\(^{-2}\)) – **assumption** constant for each train type. |
| \(d^{\max}_t\) | Maximum admissible deceleration (positive value, m s\(^{-2}\)). |
| \(v^{\max}_{t,ij}\) | Speed limit of train \(t\) on segment \((i,j)\) (m s\(^{-1}\)). |
| \(L_{ij}\) | Length of segment \((i,j)\) (m). |
| \(\Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{t,i}\) | Minimum dwell time of train \(t\) at station \(i\) (s). |
| \(\Delta^{\text{head}}_{ij}\) | Minimum headway (time separation) required between two trains travelling in the **same** direction on segment \((i,j)\) (s). |
| \(\Delta^{\text{conf}}_{ij}\) | Minimum time separation required between two trains travelling in **opposite** directions on a single‑track segment \((i,j)\) (s). |
| \(E^{\text{base}}_{t,ij}\) | Energy consumption (kWh) of train \(t\) when travelling segment \((i,j)\) at the *nominal* speed (used for linearisation). |
| \(\beta\) | Weight of the energy‑minimisation term in the objective (user‑defined). |
| \(T^{\text{disr}}_{ij}=[\tau^{\text{start}}_{ij},\tau^{\text{end}}_{ij}]\) | Time window during which disruption blocks one track side of segment \((i,j)\in D\). |
| \(M\) | Large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints. |
| \(\gamma_{t,ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | Indicator: 1 if train \(t\) uses the *alternative* (opposite‑track) direction on disrupted segment \((i,j)\in D\); 0 otherwise – **assumption** that rerouting is limited to the opposite track only. |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

### 3.1 Timetable variables  

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| \(a_{t,i}\) | Actual **arrival** time of train \(t\) at station \(i\) (continuous). |
| \(d_{t,i}\) | Actual **departure** time of train \(t\) from station \(i\) (continuous). |
| \(x_{t,ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(t\) traverses segment \((i,j)\) on its *original* track, 0 otherwise (used to model rerouting). |
| \(y_{t,ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(t\) traverses segment \((i,j)\) on the *alternative* track (only possible for \((i,j)\in D\)). |
| \(z_{t,ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(t\) **cancels** service on segment \((i,j)\) (i.e., does not pass). |

### 3.2 Speed‑profile variables (piece‑wise linear)  

For each train \(t\) and each segment \((i,j)\) that it actually traverses (\(x_{t,ij}+y_{t,ij}=1\)) we introduce a set of interval‑based speed variables:

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| \(\theta^{k}_{t,ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if interval \(k\) is selected for the speed profile on segment \((i,j)\) (binary). |
| \(\tau^{k}_{t,ij}\) | Travel time of train \(t\) on segment \((i,j)\) **if** interval \(k\) is chosen (continuous). |
| \(v^{k}_{t,ij}\) | Average speed associated with interval \(k\) (parameter, pre‑computed from a speed‑profile library). |
| \(e^{k}_{t,ij}\) | Energy consumption associated with interval \(k\) (parameter, derived from the same library). |

The library is built beforehand by solving the continuous speed‑control problem for each segment and storing a small set of *representative* speed‑time‑energy triples \((v^{k},\tau^{k},e^{k})\). This linearises the otherwise nonlinear speed‑energy relationship.

### 3.3 Conflict‑resolution binaries  

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| \(\delta^{\text{same}}_{t,t',ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(t\) precedes train \(t'\) on segment \((i,j)\) travelling in the **same** direction. |
| \(\delta^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(t\) precedes train \(t'\) on segment \((i,j)\) travelling in **opposite** directions (bidirectional conflict). |

---

## 4. Objective Function  

The model minimises a weighted sum of total delay (relative to the original schedule) and total energy consumption of the selected speed profiles.

\[
\min\; \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in S}\bigl( a_{t,i}-a^{\text{orig}}_{t,i}\bigr)}_{\text{Total passenger delay}} \;+\;
\beta\; \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in L}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} e^{k}_{t,ij}\,\theta^{k}_{t,ij}}_{\text{Total energy consumption}} .
\]

* \(a^{\text{orig}}_{t,i}\) are the pre‑disruption planned arrival times (data).  
* The first term penalises any lateness; early arrivals are allowed but do not reduce the objective (they are neutral).  

---

## 5. Constraints  

### 5.1 Logical linking of routing decisions  

1. **Exactly one route per segment (original / alternative / cancel)**  

\[
x_{t,ij}+y_{t,ij}+z_{t,ij}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in L .
\]

2. **Alternative track can be used only on disrupted segments**  

\[
y_{t,ij}\le \mathbf{1}_{\{(i,j)\in D\}} \qquad \forall t,\;(i,j)\in L .
\]

3. **If a segment is cancelled, no speed‑profile is selected**  

\[
\theta^{k}_{t,ij}\le 1-z_{t,ij}\qquad \forall t,(i,j),k .
\]

### 5.2 Time‑flow (timetable) constraints  

4. **Departure after minimum dwell**  

\[
d_{t,i}\ge a_{t,i}+ \Delta^{\text{dwell}}_{t,i}\qquad \forall t,\; i\in S .
\]

5. **Travel‑time consistency with selected speed interval**  

\[
a_{t,j}= d_{t,i}+ \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \tau^{k}_{t,ij}\,\theta^{k}_{t,ij}\qquad 
\forall t,\;(i,j)\in L .
\]

6. **Headway for same‑direction trains**  

\[
d_{t,i}+ \Delta^{\text{head}}_{ij}\le a_{t',i}+M\bigl(1-\delta^{\text{same}}_{t,t',ij}\bigr) \qquad
\forall (t,t')\in\mathcal{B},\;(i,j)\in L,\; \text{same direction}.
\]

\[
d_{t',i}+ \Delta^{\text{head}}_{ij}\le a_{t,i}+M\bigl(\delta^{\text{same}}_{t,t',ij}\bigr) .
\]

7. **Bidirectional conflict (single‑track) constraints**  

\[
d_{t,i}+ \Delta^{\text{conf}}_{ij}\le a_{t',i}+M\bigl(1-\delta^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',ij}\bigr) \qquad
\forall (t,t')\in\mathcal{B},\;(i,j)\in L,\; \text{opposite directions}.
\]

\[
d_{t',i}+ \Delta^{\text{conf}}_{ij}\le a_{t,i}+M\bigl(\delta^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',ij}\bigr) .
\]

8. **Disruption‑window feasibility** – a train using the *original* track may not occupy the blocked side during the disruption window; the alternative track is allowed.

\[
a_{t,i}\ge \tau^{\text{end}}_{ij}\;-\;M\,y_{t,ij}\qquad 
\forall t,\;(i,j)\in D,\; \text{if } x_{t,ij}=1 .
\]

\[
a_{t,i}\le \tau^{\text{start}}_{ij}\;+\;M\,(1-y_{t,ij})\qquad 
\forall t,\;(i,j)\in D,\; \text{if } x_{t,ij}=1 .
\]

(Using big‑M to deactivate the constraint when the alternative track is chosen.)

### 5.3 Speed‑profile feasibility  

9. **Acceleration / deceleration limits** – linearised by bounding the travel time on each segment.

\[
\frac{L_{ij}}{v^{\max}_{t,ij}} \le \sum_{k}\tau^{k}_{t,ij}\,\theta^{k}_{t,ij} \le 
\frac{L_{ij}}{v^{\min}_{t,ij}} \qquad \forall t,(i,j) .
\]

where a minimum feasible speed \(v^{\min}_{t,ij}\) is derived from the deceleration limit:

\[
v^{\min}_{t,ij}= \sqrt{2\,d^{\max}_t\,L_{ij}} \quad\text{(worst‑case constant deceleration)} .
\]

10. **Exactly one speed interval per traversed segment**  

\[
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \theta^{k}_{t,ij}= x_{t,ij}+y_{t,ij}\qquad \forall t,(i,j) .
\]

### 5.4 Train‑order (reordering) variables (optional)  

If the planner allows reordering of trains on a given line, introduce binary order variables \(o_{t,t'}\in\{0,1\}\) (1 if \(t\) precedes \(t'\) on the whole line). The headway constraints above already enforce a local order; a global order can be added for consistency:

\[
o_{t,t'}+o_{t',t}=1 \qquad \forall t\neq t' .
\]

and link with the segment‑level precedence binaries:

\[
\delta^{\text{same}}_{t,t',ij}\le o_{t,t'}\qquad 
\delta^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',ij}\le o_{t,t'} \qquad \forall (t,t'),(i,j).
\]

### 5.5 Cancellation (service reduction)  

If a train is cancelled on a segment, downstream times are set to a large penalty (or the train is removed from the objective). The model already forces \(z_{t,ij}=1\) → no travel time, but to keep the timetable consistent we may set:

\[
a_{t,j}=a_{t,i}\qquad \forall t,(i,j)\text{ with }z_{t,ij}=1 .
\]

---

## 6. Summary of the MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in S}\bigl(a_{t,i}-a^{\text{orig}}_{t,i}\bigr)
      \;+\;\beta\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in L}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} e^{k}_{t,ij}\,\theta^{k}_{t,ij}\\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(4)–(10)   timetable flow, dwell, travel‑time}\\
&\text{(5)–(7)   headway / conflict resolution (same / opposite direction)}\\
&\text{(8)–(9)   disruption‑window feasibility}\\
&\text{(10)–(12) routing binary logic (original / alternative / cancel)}\\
&\text{(13)–(15) speed‑profile selection and dynamics limits}\\
&\text{(optional) global reordering constraints}\\
&\text{Variables: } a_{t,i},d_{t,i}\in\mathbb{R}_{+},\;
x_{t,ij},y_{t,ij},z_{t,ij},\theta^{k}_{t,ij},\delta^{\cdot}_{t,t',ij}\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only non‑continuous elements are the binary routing, conflict‑resolution and speed‑interval selection variables, making the formulation a **mixed‑integer linear program (MILP)**.

---

## 7. Modeling Assumptions (explicit)

| # | Assumption |
|---|------------|
| A1 | Trains are homogeneous with respect to acceleration/deceleration limits; parameters \(a^{\max}_t,d^{\max}_t\) are known. |
| A2 | The disruption blocks **only one** of the two parallel tracks on a segment; the opposite track remains usable (hence the binary \(\gamma_{t,ij}\)). |
| A3 | Rerouting is limited to using the opposite track on the disrupted segment; no long‑detour alternative routes are considered. |
| A4 | Speed‑profile library \(\{(v^{k},\tau^{k},e^{k})\}\) is pre‑computed for each segment and train type, providing a piece‑wise‑linear approximation of the true nonlinear speed‑energy relationship. |
| A5 | Headway and conflict separation times are deterministic and constant for each segment (derived from signalling rules). |
| A6 | Early arrivals are allowed without penalty; only lateness contributes to the delay term. |
| A7 | Cancellation of a segment is modelled by a binary \(z_{t,ij}\); if a whole train is cancelled, all its \(z\)’s are set to 1 and the delay term for that train is omitted (or a large penalty can be added). |
| A8 | The big‑M constant is chosen sufficiently large to deactivate logical constraints but not so large as to cause numerical instability (e.g., \(M = 10^5\) s). |
| A9 | All time variables are measured in seconds; energy in kWh; distances in meters – consistent units throughout. |

---

### How to use the model  

1. **Data preparation** – collect the original timetable \((a^{\text{orig}}_{t,i})\), segment lengths, speed limits, disruption windows, and build the speed‑profile library for each segment.  
2. **Model implementation** – encode the MILP in a solver such as Gurobi, CPLEX or SCIP.  
3. **Solution** – the optimal solution yields (i) a conflict‑free timetable (arrival/departure times, possible reordering and rerouting decisions) and (ii) a concrete speed‑profile (choice of interval \(k\) for each traversed segment) that respects acceleration limits and minimises the weighted sum of delay and energy.  
4. **Post‑processing** – translate the selected speed intervals back into detailed acceleration/deceleration curves for the train‑control system.

The presented MILP captures **all three core challenges** highlighted in the introduction: (1) bidirectional conflict resolution on a shared track, (2) coupling between rescheduling decisions (times, order, rerouting) and speed‑control decisions, and (3) a co‑optimisation of service quality (delay) and energy efficiency.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) for Partial Segment Blockage**

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T\) | set of trains, indexed by *t* |
| \(S\) | set of directed track segments, indexed by *s* |
| \(L\subseteq S\times S\) | set of ordered links \((s,s')\) (consecutive segments) |
| \(K\) | set of speed‑bins (piece‑wise constant speed intervals) |
| \(R^{t}\) | feasible routes for train *t* (original direction and, if allowed, opposite direction) |
| \(\mathcal C\subseteq T\times T\times S\) | set of **conflict triples** – unordered train pairs that may occupy the same segment *s* in opposite directions |
| \(B\subseteq S\) | set of **blocked** segments (the side of the double‑track that is unavailable) |
| \(\mathcal S_{t}\subseteq S\) | segments that contain a scheduled station for train *t* (for dwell‑time constraints) |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
|\(T^{\text{arr}}_{t}\) | scheduled arrival time of train *t* at its destination | s |
|\(d^{\min}_{t}\) | minimum dwell time at any station for train *t* | s |
|\(l_{s}\) | length of segment *s* | km |
|\(v^{\max }_{s},\,v^{\min }_{s}\) | speed limits on segment *s* | km h\(^{-1}\) |
|\(a^{\max },\,d^{\max }\) | maximal acceleration / deceleration (positive) | km h\(^{-2}\) |
|\(w_{1},w_{2}\) | weights of delay and energy in the objective ( \(w_{1}+w_{2}=1\) ) | – |
|\(E_{k}\) | energy consumption coefficient for speed‑bin *k* (kWh per km) | kWh km\(^{-1}\) |
|\(v_{k}^{\text{low}},v_{k}^{\text{up}}\) | lower/upper speed of bin *k* | km h\(^{-1}\) |
|\( \bar v_{k}\) | representative speed of bin *k* (e.g., midpoint) | km h\(^{-1}\) |
|\( \tau_{s,k}=l_{s}/v_{k}\) | travel time on segment *s* with bin *k* | s |
|\( \tau^{\max }_{s}= \max_{k}\tau_{s,k}\) | safe upper bound on travel time of segment *s* | s |
|\(T^{B}_{\text{st}},T^{B}_{\text{en}}\) | start / end of the blockage window | s |
|\(U_{t}\) | planning horizon (upper bound on any time variable for train *t*) | s |
|\(M\) | big‑M constant (≥ \(U_{t}\) for all *t*) | s |
|\(p_{t}\) | big‑M for ordering constraints (≥ \(U_{t}\)) | s |
|\( \mathbf 1_{s\in r}\) | 1 if segment *s* belongs to route *r*, else 0 | – |

---

### 3. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
|\(x_{t,r}\) | binary | 1 if train *t* uses route *r∈R^{t}\) |
|\(y_{t,s}\) | binary | 1 if train *t* traverses segment *s* |
|\(z_{t,(s,s')}\) | binary | 1 if train *t* uses directed link \((s,s')\) |
|\(o_{t,t',s}\) | binary | ordering on shared segment *s*: 1 ⇒ *t* passes before *t'* |
|\(a_{t,s}\) | continuous ≥0 | arrival time of train *t* at upstream end of *s* |
|\(d_{t,s}\) | continuous ≥0 | departure time of train *t* from downstream end of *s* |
|\(u_{t,s,k}\) | binary | 1 if train *t* travels on *s* with speed in bin *k* |
|\(v_{t,s}\) | continuous | average speed of train *t* on segment *s* |
|\(\Delta_{t}\) | continuous ≥0 | delay of train *t* (relative to \(T^{\text{arr}}_{t}\)) |
|\(E_{t}\) | continuous ≥0 | energy consumption of train *t* |
|\(w_{t,s}\) | binary | auxiliary variable for “outside‑blockage‑window” condition |

---

### 4. Objective  

\[
\min \; 
w_{1}\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_{t}
\;+\;
w_{2}\sum_{t\in T}E_{t}
\]

where  

\[
\Delta_{t}= \max\{0,\;a_{t,s^{\text{dest}}}-T^{\text{arr}}_{t}\},
\qquad
E_{t}= \sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} E_{k}\,l_{s}\,u_{t,s,k}.
\]

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Route selection  

1. **Exactly one route per train**  
\[
\sum_{r\in R^{t}} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T
\]

2. **Link route choice to segment usage**  
\[
y_{t,s}= \sum_{r\in R^{t}} \mathbf 1_{s\in r}\;x_{t,r}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S
\tag{R‑1}
\]

3. **Flow conservation on each train’s path** (including virtual source/sink nodes)  

\[
\sum_{s' : (s,s')\in L} z_{t,(s,s')}
-\sum_{s' : (s',s)\in L} z_{t,(s',s)}
=
\begin{cases}
 1 & s = s^{\text{source}}_{t}\\[2pt]
-1 & s = s^{\text{sink}}_{t}\\[2pt]
 0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S
\tag{R‑2}
\]

4. **Link‑segment coupling**  

\[
z_{t,(s,s')} \le y_{t,s},\qquad
z_{t,(s,s')} \le y_{t,s'} \qquad\forall t\in T,\;(s,s')\in L
\tag{R‑3}
\]

#### 5.2 Conflict ordering on shared segments  

For each \((t,t',s)\in\mathcal C\):

\[
a_{t,s}+ \tau^{\max }_{s}\,y_{t,s}\;\le\; a_{t',s}+ p_{t}\,(1-o_{t,t',s})
\tag{C‑1}
\]

\[
a_{t',s}+ \tau^{\max }_{s}\,y_{t',s}\;\le\; a_{t,s}+ p_{t}\,o_{t,t',s}
\tag{C‑2}
\]

\(o_{t,t',s}=1\) forces *t* to go before *t'*; the big‑M \(p_{t}\) disables the opposite inequality.

#### 5.3 Time‑speed coupling  

1. **Exactly one speed‑bin per traversed segment**  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} u_{t,s,k}= y_{t,s}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S
\tag{S‑1}
\]

2. **Travel time on a segment**  

\[
d_{t,s}= a_{t,s}+ \sum_{k\in K}\tau_{s,k}\,u_{t,s,k}\qquad\forall t,s
\tag{S‑2}
\]

3. **Link continuity** (if link \((s,s')\) is used)  

\[
a_{t,s'}\;\ge\; d_{t,s}-M\,(1-z_{t,(s,s')})\qquad\forall t,\;(s,s')\in L
\tag{S‑3}
\]

4. **Minimum dwell time at stations**  

\[
d_{t,s}\;\ge\; a_{t,s}+ d^{\min }_{t}\qquad\forall t,\;s\in\mathcal S_{t}
\tag{S‑4}
\]

#### 5.4 Blockage‑window feasibility  

For every blocked segment \(s\in B\) and train *t*:

\[
a_{t,s}\;\ge\; T^{B}_{\text{en}}-M\,(1-w_{t,s})
\tag{B‑1}
\]

\[
d_{t,s}\;\le\; T^{B}_{\text{st}}+M\,w_{t,s}
\tag{B‑2}
\]

\(w_{t,s}=0\) forces the whole traversal to lie **after** the blockage; \(w_{t,s}=1\) forces it to lie **before**.

#### 5.5 Speed limits (implicit via bin feasibility)  

If a bin *k* violates the segment limits, set \(u_{t,s,k}=0\) (remove the pair from the model).  

#### 5.6 Acceleration / deceleration limits (linearised)  

Average speed on a segment:

\[
v_{t,s}= \sum_{k\in K}\bar v_{k}\,u_{t,s,k}\qquad\forall t,s
\tag{A‑1}
\]

Acceleration between consecutive traversed segments:

\[
v_{t,s'}-v_{t,s}\;\le\; a^{\max }\;\frac{l_{s}}{v_{t,s}} \qquad\forall t,(s,s')\in L
\tag{A‑2}
\]

Deceleration:

\[
v_{t,s}-v_{t,s'}\;\le\; d^{\max }\;\frac{l_{s}}{v_{t,s'}} \qquad\forall t,(s,s')\in L
\tag{A‑3}
\]

(If a linear formulation is required, replace the right‑hand sides by piece‑wise linear approximations or additional binaries.)

#### 5.7 Delay definition  

\[
\Delta_{t}\;\ge\; a_{t,s^{\text{dest}}}-T^{\text{arr}}_{t}\qquad\forall t\in T
\tag{D‑1}
\]

\(\Delta_{t}\ge 0\).

#### 5.8 Energy calculation (used in the objective)  

\[
E_{t}= \sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} E_{k}\,l_{s}\,u_{t,s,k}\qquad\forall t\in T
\tag{E‑1}
\]

#### 5.9 Variable bounds  

\[
0\le a_{t,s},d_{t,s}\le U_{t}\qquad\forall t,s
\]

All binary variables belong to \(\{0,1\}\); continuous variables are non‑negative.

---

### 6. Complete MILP (compact form)

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& w_{1}\sum_{t}\Delta_{t}+w_{2}\sum_{t}E_{t}\\[2pt]
\text{s.t. }&
\sum_{r}x_{t,r}=1 &&\forall t\\
&y_{t,s}= \sum_{r}\mathbf 1_{s\in r}x_{t,r} &&\forall t,s\\
&\text{flow conservation (R‑2)} &&\forall t,s\\
&z_{t,(s,s')}\le y_{t,s},\;z_{t,(s,s')}\le y_{t,s'} &&\forall t,(s,s')\\
&\sum_{k}u_{t,s,k}=y_{t,s} &&\forall t,s\\
&d_{t,s}=a_{t,s}+ \sum_{k}\tau_{s,k}u_{t,s,k} &&\forall t,s\\
&a_{t,s'}\ge d_{t,s}-M(1-z_{t,(s,s')}) &&\forall t,(s,s')\\
&d_{t,s}\ge a_{t,s}+d^{\min }_{t} &&\forall t,s\in\mathcal S_{t}\\
&\text{conflict (C‑1),(C‑2)} &&\forall (t,t',s)\in\mathcal C\\
&a_{t,s}\ge T^{B}_{\text{en}}-M(1-w_{t,s}),\;
d_{t,s}\le T^{B}_{\text{st}}+M w_{t,s} &&\forall t,s\in B\\
&v_{t,s}= \sum_{k}\bar v_{k}u_{t,s,k} &&\forall t,s\\
&v_{t,s'}-v_{t,s}\le a^{\max }\frac{l_{s}}{v_{t,s}} &&\forall t,(s,s')\\
&v_{t,s}-v_{t,s'}\le d^{\max }\frac{l_{s}}{v_{t,s'}} &&\forall t,(s,s')\\
&\Delta_{t}\ge a_{t,s^{\text{dest}}}-T^{\text{arr}}_{t} &&\forall t\\
&E_{t}= \sum_{s}\sum_{k}E_{k}l_{s}u_{t,s,k} &&\forall t\\
&0\le a_{t,s},d_{t,s}\le U_{t} &&\forall t,s\\
&x,y,z,u,w,o\in\{0,1\},\;\Delta,E\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 7. Modelling Assumptions (to be documented)

1. **Two possible directions per train** – original or opposite (if allowed).  
2. **Speed is constant on a segment** – captured by binary speed‑bin variables.  
3. **Travel time per bin is pre‑computed**; acceleration inside a segment is approximated by the inter‑segment acceleration constraints.  
4. **Only one side of a double‑track segment is blocked**; the opposite side remains usable.  
5. **Conflict pairs are enumerated a‑priori**; for large networks a separation routine can be added.  
6. **Energy consumption is linear in speed‑bin usage** (coefficients \(E_{k}\)).  
7. **Big‑M constants \(M,p_{t}\) are set to the planning horizon** to avoid numerical issues.  

The formulation above is a **complete mixed‑integer linear program** that simultaneously decides (i) which route each train will follow, (ii) the order of trains on shared segments, (iii) the exact arrival/departure times, (iv) the speed bin used on each segment, and (v) the resulting delay and energy consumption. Solving the MILP yields a conflict‑free timetable together with executable speed profiles that respect the partial‑segment blockage and minimise a weighted combination of total delay and energy use.

Text:
**Passenger‑oriented Real‑time Train‑Scheduling MILP (MPC‑style)**  

The model below follows the description in the prompt.  
It is a **mixed‑integer linear program (MILP)** that is solved at every MPC step (prediction horizon \(H\)).  
All symbols are defined in the *Sets, Parameters, Decision Variables* section; the *Assumptions* section lists the modelling simplifications that were necessary because the source text does not give exact numerical data.

---

## 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(\mathcal{L}\) | Set of train lines (for a single‑line case \(\mathcal{L}=\{l\}\)). |
| \(\mathcal{S}=\{1,\dots,S\}\) | Ordered set of stations on line \(l\). |
| \(\mathcal{T}=\{1,\dots,T\}\) | Set of scheduled train trips (each trip = one physical train). |
| \(\mathcal{K}=\{1,\dots,K\}\) | Set of admissible **train composition types** (e.g. 4‑car, 6‑car, 8‑car). |
| \(\mathcal{H}=\{1,\dots,H\}\) | Set of discrete time intervals in the MPC prediction horizon (piece‑wise constant demand). |
| \(\mathcal{P}\) | Set of rolling‑stock pools (e.g. depot \(p=0\) and intermediate yards). |
| \(\mathcal{D}\subseteq \mathcal{T}\times \mathcal{T}\) | Set of feasible **precedence pairs** \((t,t')\) meaning train \(t'\) may follow train \(t\) on the same unit of rolling stock. |

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning | Typical unit |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| \(d_{s,h}\) | Passenger demand (boardings) at station \(s\) during interval \(h\). | persons |
| \(\Delta_h\) | Length of interval \(h\) (seconds). | s |
| \(C_k\) | Seating capacity of composition type \(k\). | persons |
| \(c^{\text{run}}_{s,s'}\) | Nominal running time between consecutive stations \(s\) and \(s'\). | s |
| \(c^{\text{dwell}}_{s}\) | Minimum dwell time for door opening/closing at station \(s\). | s |
| \(M\) | Large constant (big‑M) for linearisation. | – |
| \(B^{\max}\) | Maximum allowed headway (seconds) between any two consecutive trains on the line. | s |
| \(B^{\min}\) | Minimum allowed headway (seconds) (safety). | s |
| \(\alpha^{\text{op}}\) | Unit operating cost of a train (fuel/energy, staff) per second. | \$/s |
| \(\beta^{\text{wait}}\) | Penalty cost per passenger‑minute of waiting. | \$/person·min |
| \(\gamma^{\text{travel}}\) | Penalty cost per passenger‑minute of in‑vehicle travel (including extra dwell). | \$/person·min |
| \(R^{\text{avail}}_p\) | Number of rolling‑stock units available in pool \(p\). | units |
| \(\tau^{\text{turn}}_p\) | Minimum turnaround time for a train returning to pool \(p\). | s |
| \(\pi_{t}\) | Planned (nominal) departure time of train \(t\) from the first station (used for deviation penalty). | s |
| \(\lambda^{\text{dev}}\) | Weight for timetable deviation in the objective. | – |

*All parameters are assumed known at the beginning of each MPC step (e.g. demand forecasts are piece‑wise constant over \(\Delta_h\)).*

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,k}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) uses composition type \(k\). |
| \(y_{t,p}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) starts (or ends) its circulation at pool \(p\). |
| \(a_{t,s}\ge 0\) | continuous | Actual arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\). |
| \(d_{t,s}\ge 0\) | continuous | Actual departure time of train \(t\) from station \(s\). |
| \(w_{s,h}\ge 0\) | continuous | Number of passengers waiting at station \(s\) at the *end* of interval \(h\). |
| \(u_{s,h}\ge 0\) | continuous | Number of passengers that board train(s) at station \(s\) during interval \(h\). |
| \(z_{t,t'}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t'\) is the immediate successor of train \(t\) on the same rolling‑stock unit (used for circulation constraints). |
| \(\delta_{t}\ge 0\) | continuous | Absolute deviation of the first‑departure time of train \(t\) from its nominal \(\pi_t\). |

*Only the integer variables \(\{x_{t,k},y_{t,p},z_{t,t'}\}\) are supplied by the learning module (e.g. an LSTM). The remaining variables are obtained by solving the MILP with those integers fixed.*

---

## 4. Model Assumptions (explicit)

1. **Piece‑wise constant demand** – Passenger arrivals at each station are approximated by a constant rate within each interval \(h\).  
2. **Deterministic travel times** – Nominal running times \(c^{\text{run}}_{s,s'}\) are used; any deviation is captured by the decision variables \(a_{t,s},d_{t,s}\).  
3. **Single line, unidirectional** – The formulation can be duplicated for each direction; the presented version assumes one direction only.  
4. **No overtaking** – Trains keep their order on the line; the precedence set \(\mathcal{D}\) enforces this.  
5. **Capacity is only seat capacity** – Standing passengers are ignored (or assumed to be covered by the same capacity).  
6. **Rolling‑stock pools are homogeneous** – Any composition type can be assembled at any pool, subject to availability.  
7. **Headway limits are hard constraints** – Safety‑related minimum/maximum headways must be respected for every pair of consecutive trains.  
8. **All passengers that cannot board a train wait for the next one** – No passenger loss is allowed.  

---

## 5. Objective Function  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & 
\underbrace{\alpha^{\text{op}}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} (d_{t,s}-a_{t,s})}_{\text{operational time cost}} \\
& + \underbrace{\beta^{\text{wait}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{h\in\mathcal{H}} w_{s,h}\,\frac{\Delta_h}{60}}_{\text{passenger waiting cost (min)}}\\
& + \underbrace{\gamma^{\text{travel}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{h\in\mathcal{H}} u_{s,h}\,\frac{\Delta_h}{60}}_{\text{in‑vehicle travel (extra dwell) cost}}\\
& + \underbrace{\lambda^{\text{dev}}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} \delta_{t}}_{\text{timetable deviation penalty}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

All terms are linear because \(\delta_t\) will be linearised (see constraints).

---

## 6. Constraints  

### 6.1. Train‑composition selection  

\[
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} x_{t,k}=1 \qquad \forall t\in\mathcal{T} \tag{C1}
\]

### 6.2. Rolling‑stock pool assignment  

\[
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} y_{t,p}=1 \qquad \forall t\in\mathcal{T} \tag{C2}
\]

### 6.3. Capacity feasibility (boarding ≤ capacity)  

For each station‑interval pair, the total number of boarding passengers cannot exceed the sum of capacities of the trains that actually stop there during that interval.

First define a binary **stop** indicator (derived from the timetable):

\[
\theta_{t,s}= 
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if } a_{t,s}\le d_{t,s} \text{ (train stops)}\\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\]

Because the model is linear, we replace \(\theta_{t,s}\) by a big‑M formulation:

\[
d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \ge c^{\text{dwell}}_{s}\,\theta_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C3a}
\]
\[
d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \le M\,\theta_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C3b}
\]

Now capacity:

\[
\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} \theta_{t,s}\, C_{k}\,x_{t,k} \;\ge\; u_{s,h} \qquad \forall s\in\mathcal{S},\;h\in\mathcal{H} \tag{C4}
\]

### 6.4. Passenger‑flow balance  

At each station and interval, the waiting passengers evolve as:

\[
w_{s,h}= w_{s,h-1}+ d_{s,h} - u_{s,h} \qquad \forall s,\;h\ge 2 \tag{C5a}
\]
\[
w_{s,1}= d_{s,1} - u_{s,1} \qquad \forall s \tag{C5b}
\]

where \(d_{s,h}\) is the external demand arriving during interval \(h\) (given by \(d_{s,h}\) parameter).  
Thus:

\[
w_{s,h}= w_{s,h-1}+ d_{s,h} - u_{s,h} \qquad \forall s,\;h\ge 2 \tag{C5}
\]

All waiting variables must be non‑negative:

\[
w_{s,h}\ge 0 \qquad \forall s,h \tag{C6}
\]

### 6.5. Train dynamics (running‑time constraints)  

For any two consecutive stations \(s\) and \(s'\) (with \(s' = s+1\)):

\[
a_{t,s'} \ge d_{t,s} + c^{\text{run}}_{s,s'} \qquad \forall t,\; s=1,\dots,S-1 \tag{C7}
\]

### 6.6. Headway limits  

Let \(t\) and \(t'\) be two trains that travel the same direction and are ordered (i.e. \(t\) precedes \(t'\) on the line). The headway at the first station is:

\[
B_{t,t'} = a_{t',1} - a_{t,1} \qquad \forall (t,t')\in \mathcal{D} \tag{C8a}
\]

Enforce bounds:

\[
B^{\min} \le B_{t,t'} \le B^{\max} \qquad \forall (t,t')\in \mathcal{D} \tag{C8b}
\]

### 6.7. Rolling‑stock circulation (successor linking)  

If train \(t'\) is the immediate successor of train \(t\) on the same unit, then the departure from the last station of \(t\) plus turnaround must precede the departure of \(t'\) from the first station:

\[
a_{t',1} \ge d_{t,S} + \tau^{\text{turn}}_{p}\;-\; M\,(1-z_{t,t'}) \qquad \forall (t,t')\in \mathcal{D},\; p\in\mathcal{P} \tag{C9a}
\]

And each train can have at most one predecessor and one successor:

\[
\sum_{t' : (t,t')\in\mathcal{D}} z_{t,t'} \le 1 \qquad \forall t \tag{C9b}
\]
\[
\sum_{t : (t,t')\in\mathcal{D}} z_{t,t'} \le 1 \qquad \forall t' \tag{C9c}
\]

Link to pool assignment (if a train starts at pool \(p\) then its predecessor must end at the same pool):

\[
y_{t',p} \ge y_{t,p} - (1- z_{t,t'}) \qquad \forall (t,t')\in\mathcal{D},\;p\in\mathcal{P} \tag{C9d}
\]

Pool capacity (total number of trains simultaneously using a pool cannot exceed availability):

\[
\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} y_{t,p} \le R^{\text{avail}}_p \qquad \forall p\in\mathcal{P} \tag{C10}
\]

### 6.8. Timetable deviation linearisation  

\[
\delta_t \ge a_{t,1} - \pi_t \qquad \forall t \tag{C11a}
\]
\[
\delta_t \ge \pi_t - a_{t,1} \qquad \forall t \tag{C11b}
\]

### 6.9. Variable domains  

\[
x_{t,k}\in\{0,1\},\; y_{t,p}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{t,t'}\in\{0,1\} \qquad \forall t,k,p,t' \tag{C12}
\]
\[
a_{t,s},d_{t,s},w_{s,h},u_{s,h},\delta_t \ge 0 \qquad \forall t,s,h \tag{C13}
\]

---

## 7. Complete MILP Statement  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min_{x,y,z,a,d,w,u,\delta}&\; \text{Objective (Section 5)}\\
\text{s.t. } & \text{Constraints (C1)–(C13)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 8. Remarks on the **Learning‑driven MPC**  

* At each MPC step the demand forecast \(\{d_{s,h}\}\) for the next \(H\) intervals is supplied.  
* An LSTM (or any other predictor) is trained offline to output a **reduced set of integer variables**:  
  * composition decisions \(\{x_{t,k}\}\) for the trains that are still in the planning horizon,  
  * pool‑assignment decisions \(\{y_{t,p}\}\), and  
  * successor links \(\{z_{t,t'}\}\).  
* Those integer values are **fixed** in the MILP; the remaining continuous variables \((a,d,w,u,\delta)\) are then obtained by solving the linear program defined above.  
* Because the integer block is much smaller (thanks to the four presolve techniques described in the source text), the MILP can be solved within the typical MPC sampling time (seconds to a few minutes).  

---

### 9. Potential Extensions (not in the core model)

* **Energy consumption** – add a term \(\alpha^{\text{energy}}\sum_t \sum_{s} (d_{t,s}-a_{t,s})\) with train‑specific energy coefficients.  
* **Multi‑direction lines** – duplicate the index set with a direction flag and add crossing‑conflict constraints.  
* **Stochastic demand** – replace deterministic \(d_{s,h}\) by scenarios and add chance‑constraint or robust‑optimization cuts.  

The formulation above is a **complete linear MILP** that captures the essential elements highlighted in the literature review: time‑varying passenger demand, flexible train composition, rolling‑stock circulation, and MPC‑type receding‑horizon optimisation. All missing numerical details have been introduced as reasonable assumptions and are clearly marked.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for rolling‑stock rescheduling with infrastructure‑availability constraints**  

The formulation below combines two sub‑models that appear in the paper description  

* **Composition sub‑model** – decides which rolling‑stock unit (RSU) is assigned to each passenger trip and which shunting movements are created.  
* **Infrastructure sub‑model** – checks whether the chosen shunting movements can be performed on the available tracks of the stations (Utrecht C and Rotterdam C) and, if necessary, introduces short delays for other passenger trains.  

The two sub‑models are linked through Benders‑type feasibility cuts (exact algorithm) or by feeding the shunting decisions one‑by‑one to the infrastructure model (iterative heuristic).  
For the purpose of a single, self‑contained MILP we embed the feasibility conditions directly as “big‑M” constraints; the same model can be used in a Benders decomposition framework.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T\) | Set of passenger trips (indexed by \(t\)). |
| \(R\) | Set of rolling‑stock units (indexed by \(r\)). |
| \(S\) | Set of stations where shunting is allowed (here \(S=\{Utrecht, Rotterdam\}\)). |
| \(M_s\) | Set of shunting tracks at station \(s\) (indexed by \(m\)). |
| \(K\) | Set of possible shunting movements (indexed by \(k\)). Each movement \(k\) is defined by a tuple \((r,s,m,\tau^{start}_k,\tau^{end}_k)\) – the RSU that must be moved, the station, the track, and the time window in which the movement must start / finish. |
| \(P\) | Set of passenger‑train events that occupy a track at a station (indexed by \(p\)). Each event \(p\) is defined by \((s,m,\tau^{start}_p,\tau^{end}_p)\). |
| \(L\) | Set of “delay‑levels’’ that can be applied to a passenger event (e.g. 0 min, 1 min, 2 min, 3 min). |

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical value / assumption |
|--------|-------------|-----------------------------|
| \(c^{trip}_{t,r}\) | Cost (or penalty) of assigning RSU \(r\) to trip \(t\). | 0 if feasible, large \(M\) if not (e.g. RSU not compatible). |
| \(c^{sh}_{k}\) | Cost (or penalty) for performing shunting movement \(k\). | Positive (reflects driver time, fuel, wear). |
| \(c^{delay}_\ell\) | Penalty for delaying a passenger event by the amount associated with level \(\ell\). | Small (e.g. 1 €/min). |
| \(c^{dev}_t\) | Penalty for deviating from the original assignment of trip \(t\) (e.g. using a different RSU than originally planned). | Positive. |
| \(\Delta^{max}\) | Maximum admissible extra delay for any passenger event (in minutes). | 3 min (as stated). |
| \(M\) | Large constant for “big‑M’’ constraints (larger than the planning horizon, e.g. 10 000). |
| \(\alpha\) | Weight for similarity‑to‑original‑plan objective (0 ≤ α ≤ 1). |
| \(\beta\) | Weight for total operational cost objective (β = 1 − α). |
| \(T^{orig}_t\) | Original RSU assigned to trip \(t\) (used for similarity term). | – |
| \(start_t, end_t\) | Scheduled start / end time of trip \(t\) (fixed). | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if RSU \(r\) is assigned to trip \(t\). |
| \(y_k \in \{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if shunting movement \(k\) is performed. |
| \(z_{p,\ell} \in \{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if passenger event \(p\) is delayed by level \(\ell\). (Only one level can be chosen.) |
| \(s_{p} \in \mathbb{R}_+\) | continuous | Actual start time of passenger event \(p\) after possible delay. |
| \(e_{p} \in \mathbb{R}_+\) | continuous | Actual end time of passenger event \(p\) after possible delay. |
| \(u_{k} \in \{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if shunting movement \(k\) **conflicts** with at least one passenger event on the same track (used for Benders cut generation). |
| \(w_{k,p} \in \{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 if shunting movement \(k\) and passenger event \(p\) overlap on the same track (auxiliary). |

---

## 4. Model Formulation  

### 4.1 Objective  

We combine three goals:

1. **Operational cost** – assignment + shunting + delay penalties.  
2. **Similarity to the original plan** – minimise the number of trips that receive a different RSU.  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \beta\Bigg[ \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{r\in R} c^{trip}_{t,r}\,x_{t,r}}_{\text{trip‑assignment cost}}
          + \underbrace{\sum_{k\in K} c^{sh}_{k}\,y_{k}}_{\text{shunting cost}}
          + \underbrace{\sum_{p\in P}\sum_{\ell\in L} c^{delay}_\ell \,z_{p,\ell}}_{\text{delay penalty}} \Bigg] \\
        & + \alpha\Bigg[ \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\Bigl(1-\sum_{r\in R} \mathbf{1}_{\{r=T^{orig}_t\}}\,x_{t,r}\Bigr)}_{\text{deviation from original RSU}} \Bigg]
\end{aligned}
\]

where \(\mathbf{1}_{\{condition\}}\) is 1 if the condition holds, 0 otherwise.  
If \(\alpha=0\) we only minimise costs; if \(\alpha=1\) we only maximise similarity.

---

### 4.2 Assignment constraints  

*Each trip receives exactly one RSU*  

\[
\sum_{r\in R} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{A1}
\]

*RSU flow balance (circulation)* – a RSU that finishes a trip must either start the next assigned trip or be used for a shunting movement. Let  

\[
\text{next}(t) = \{t' \in T \mid \text{the scheduled arrival of }t \text{ is before the departure of }t' \text{ and } r\text{ can be reused}\}
\]

For each RSU \(r\):

\[
\sum_{t\in T} x_{t,r} = \sum_{t\in T} x_{t,r} \quad\text{(trivial)} 
\]

In practice we enforce a **circulation** using a time‑expanded network; a compact way is:

\[
\sum_{t\in T: \; end_t \le H} x_{t,r} \;-\; \sum_{t\in T: \; start_t \ge 0} x_{t,r} = 0 \qquad \forall r\in R
\tag{A2}
\]

where \(H\) is the planning horizon (e.g. 24 h). This ensures that the number of departures equals the number of arrivals for each RSU.

---

### 4.3 Shunting‑movement feasibility  

A shunting movement \(k=(r,s,m,\tau^{start}_k,\tau^{end}_k)\) can be performed **only** if the RSU \(r\) is available (i.e., not assigned to a passenger trip at that time) **and** the track \(m\) at station \(s\) is free.

*Link to RSU assignment*  

\[
y_k \le \sum_{t\in T: \; r\text{ is used on }t \text{ and } [\tau^{start}_k,\tau^{end}_k]\cap [start_t,end_t]\neq\emptyset } x_{t,r} \;+\; (1 - \text{bigM}) 
\tag{S1}
\]

A more readable formulation uses an auxiliary binary \(a_{k}\) that equals 1 if RSU \(r\) is **busy** during the shunting window:

\[
a_{k} \ge x_{t,r} \quad \forall t\in T \text{ with } [\tau^{start}_k,\tau^{end}_k]\cap [start_t,end_t]\neq\emptyset
\]
\[
y_k \le 1 - a_{k}
\tag{S1‑alt}
\]

*Track‑occupancy conflicts*  

For each passenger event \(p\) that uses the same track \((s,m)\) we introduce binary overlap variable \(w_{k,p}\):

\[
w_{k,p} \ge y_k + z_{p,\ell} - 1 \qquad \forall \ell\in L,\; p\in P \text{ with } (s,m) \text{ equal}
\tag{S2}
\]

If both shunting \(k\) and passenger event \(p\) are scheduled (possibly delayed) then \(w_{k,p}=1\).

The actual time windows after delay are:

\[
s_p = start_p + \sum_{\ell\in L}\ell\;z_{p,\ell}, \qquad
e_p = end_p + \sum_{\ell\in L}\ell\;z_{p,\ell}
\tag{S3}
\]

The overlap condition (big‑M formulation) :

\[
w_{k,p} \le 
\frac{(\tau^{end}_k - s_p)}{M}
+ \frac{(e_p - \tau^{start}_k)}{M}
\tag{S4}
\]

If the intervals do **not** overlap, the RHS ≤ 0, forcing \(w_{k,p}=0\).

Finally, a shunting movement is **allowed** only if it does not overlap any passenger event on the same track:

\[
y_k \le 1 - \sum_{p\in P:(s,m)} w_{k,p} \qquad \forall k\in K
\tag{S5}
\]

---

### 4.4 Delay limits  

Only one delay level per passenger event:

\[
\sum_{\ell\in L} z_{p,\ell} \le 1 \qquad \forall p\in P
\tag{D1}
\]

Maximum admissible delay:

\[
\sum_{\ell\in L} \ell \, z_{p,\ell} \le \Delta^{max} \qquad \forall p\in P
\tag{D2}
\]

---

### 4.5 Benders‑type feasibility indicator (optional)  

If the model is used inside a Benders decomposition, we keep the auxiliary binary \(u_k\) that becomes 1 when a conflict is detected; the master problem then adds a cut  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} u_k \le |K|-1
\tag{B1}
\]

In the monolithic MILP we simply set \(u_k = y_k\) and enforce (S5); the cut is not needed.

---

### 4.6 Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\} &&\forall t\in T,\; r\in R\\
&y_k \in \{0,1\} &&\forall k\in K\\
&z_{p,\ell} \in \{0,1\} &&\forall p\in P,\; \ell\in L\\
&s_p, e_p \in \mathbb{R}_+ &&\forall p\in P\\
&w_{k,p} \in \{0,1\} &&\forall k\in K,\; p\in P\\
&a_k \in \{0,1\} &&\forall k\in K
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 5. Remarks & Modeling Assumptions  

| # | Assumption (explicitly stated) | Reason / comment |
|---|-------------------------------|------------------|
| 1 | **Discrete delay levels** – we allow only a few integer minute delays (0‑3 min). This matches the “short delay” policy described in the paper. |
| 2 | **Big‑M value** – \(M\) is chosen larger than the planning horizon (e.g., 10 000 min) to safely linearise the overlap conditions. |
| 3 | **Shunting tracks are pre‑identified** – the set \(M_s\) is known for each station (Utrecht C, Rotterdam C). No capacity limit per track other than “one movement at a time”. |
| 4 | **RSU compatibility** – the cost \(c^{trip}_{t,r}\) is set to a very large value (or \(x_{t,r}=0\) forced) when the RSU cannot physically serve the trip (different class, length, power). |
| 5 | **Circulation balance** – the simplified equation (A2) assumes the planning horizon is long enough that each RSU that departs also returns; more detailed time‑expanded network can be used if needed. |
| 6 | **Objective weighting** – the user can tune \(\alpha\) (similarity) vs. \(\beta\) (cost) to reflect the “stick‑to‑the‑plan” vs. “operational cost” trade‑off discussed in the paper. |
| 7 | **Exact vs. heuristic** – the model can be solved directly (heuristic) or embedded in a Benders loop where the infrastructure model returns cuts (exact). The formulation above contains the necessary binaries to generate such cuts. |
| 8 | **No driver‑availability constraints** – the paper mentions shunting drivers; they are omitted here for brevity but can be added analogously (binary driver‑assignment variables with shift‑length limits). |
| 9 | **No explicit passenger‑capacity penalties** – the model focuses on feasibility and cost; passenger‑satisfaction (standing, waiting) could be added as extra terms using load variables, but is left out to keep the MILP concise. |

---

## 6. How the Model Captures the Paper’s Goals  

* **Feasibility of shunting** – constraints (S1)–(S5) guarantee that a shunting movement is only selected if the RSU is free and the track is free, possibly after delaying other trains within the allowed short window.  
* **Minimal disruption** – the similarity term (weighted by \(\alpha\)) penalises any change of RSU compared with the original schedule, encouraging solutions “close to the original plan”.  
* **Cost minimisation** – the operational part (weighted by \(\beta\)) accounts for the cost of using a particular RSU on a trip, the cost of each shunting movement, and the penalty for any induced delays.  
* **Iterative/Exact interaction** – the binary \(u_k\) (or the direct use of (S5)) can be interpreted as the cut that the infrastructure model would return in a Benders decomposition; feeding shunting decisions one‑by‑one to the infrastructure model reproduces the iterative heuristic described.  

---

## 7. Example of a Small Instance (illustrative)  

| Trips \(T\) | RSUs \(R\) | Original RSU | Start–End (min) |
|------------|-----------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | A, B | A | 60–120 |
| 2 | A, B | B | 130–190 |
| 3 | A, B | A | 200–260 |

| Shunting movements \(K\) (only at Utrecht) | RSU | Track | Window (min) |
|--------------------------------------------|-----|-------|--------------|
| k1 | A | m1 | 125–130 |
| k2 | B | m1 | 115–120 |

| Passenger events \(P\) on track m1 (Utrecht) | Original interval (min) |
|--------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| p1 | 118–122 |
| p2 | 128–132 |

With \(\Delta^{max}=3\) min we can delay p1 by 1 min (119–123) and then perform k2 (115–120) without conflict, etc. The MILP will automatically decide which shunting movements to keep, which delays to apply, and whether to re‑assign RSUs.

---

### 8. Solver notes  

* The model is a pure MILP (linear objective, linear constraints, binary/integer variables).  
* State‑of‑the‑art solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress) can handle instances of the size reported in the paper (several hundred trips, a few dozen shunting movements) within minutes.  
* For the exact Benders version, keep only the master‑problem variables \((x,y)\) and generate feasibility cuts using the infrastructure sub‑problem (a pure feasibility check) after each master solution.  

---

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP)**  
The model below simultaneously decides (i) a conflict‑free timetable (arrival / departure times, train order and possible rerouting) and (ii) feasible speed profiles for every train on every track segment.  The formulation is linearised (mixed‑integer) by discretising time and speed, and by using big‑M techniques for logical conditions.  All symbols are defined in the *Sets & Indices* and *Parameters* sections; missing data are marked as **Assumption** and can be calibrated with real‑world values.

---

## 1. Sets, Indices and Assumptions  

| Symbol | Meaning | Assumption / Comment |
|--------|----------|----------------------|
| **T** | Set of trains,  *t = 1,…,|T|* | – |
| **S** | Set of stations (including origin 0 and destination |S|+1) | – |
| **L** | Set of directed track‑segments (links)  *l = (i→j), i,j ∈ S* | – |
| **B ⊆ L** | Sub‑set of *blocked* segments (partial blockage) | – |
| **K** | Set of discrete speed levels (k = 1,…,K) | Speed levels are equally spaced between 0 and the maximum admissible speed *vmax* (Assumption). |
| **Δ** | Length of the time‑discretisation interval (minutes) | Typical value 1 min (Assumption). |
| **τ = {0,Δ,2Δ,…,H}** | Discrete time horizon (0 … planning horizon *H*) | H = 24 h (Assumption). |
| **P** | Set of *plan* indices for a train (see §4.3) | Each plan corresponds to a feasible combination of (route, departure‑time, speed‑profile). |
| **R ⊆ L × L** | Set of *conflict pairs* – two opposite‑direction segments that share the same physical track (bidirectional usage) | – |

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical value / source |
|--------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **τ⁰_t** | Original scheduled departure time of train *t* from its origin station | From the pre‑disruption timetable. |
| **τᵈ_t** | Original scheduled arrival time of train *t* at its destination | – |
| **c_t** | Energy consumption coefficient for train *t* (kWh per km·(speed level)²) | Calibrated from train characteristics (Assumption). |
| **d_l** | Length of segment *l* (km) | – |
| **v_k** | Speed corresponding to level *k* (km/h) | v₁ = 0, v_K = vmax (Assumption). |
| **α_l**, **β_l** | Minimum and maximum admissible travel time on segment *l* (Δ‑units) | α_l = ⌈d_l / v_K⌉, β_l = ⌈d_l / v_1⌉ (Assumption). |
| **M** | Large constant for Big‑M linearisation (≥ H/Δ) | – |
| **γ₁, γ₂** | Weight of timetable deviation and energy consumption in the objective | γ₁ = 1, γ₂ = 0.01 (Assumption – can be tuned). |
| **Δᵇ_l, Δᵉ_l** | Beginning and ending time of the blockage on segment *l* (Δ‑units) | 0 if *l∉B*. |
| **σ_t** | Binary flag =1 if train *t* is cancelled (service interruption) | – |
| **ρ_t** | Binary flag =1 if train *t* uses the *opposite* track (rerouting) on a blocked segment | – |
| **δ_{tt'}** | Minimum headway (Δ‑units) required between any two trains travelling in the same direction on the same physical track | Typically 2 Δ (Assumption). |
| **θ_{tt'}** | Minimum headway (Δ‑units) for opposite‑direction trains sharing a bidirectional track (conflict pair) | Typically 4 Δ (Assumption). |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|----------|
| **x_{t,l,k,τ} ∈ {0,1}** | binary | 1 if train *t* traverses segment *l* at speed level *k* during time interval *τ*. |
| **a_{t,i} ≥ 0** | continuous | Arrival time of train *t* at station *i* (Δ‑units). |
| **d_{t,i} ≥ 0** | continuous | Departure time of train *t* from station *i* (Δ‑units). |
| **z_{t,p} ∈ {0,1}** | binary | 1 if plan *p* (specific route, departure time and speed‑profile) is selected for train *t*. |
| **σ_t ∈ {0,1}** | binary | Cancellation flag (σ_t=1 → train *t* is removed from service). |
| **ρ_t ∈ {0,1}** | binary | Rerouting flag (ρ_t=1 → train *t* uses opposite track on blocked segments). |
| **y_{tt',l,τ} ∈ {0,1}** | binary | 1 if trains *t* and *t'* occupy the same physical track segment *l* at the same time *τ* (conflict indicator). |
| **e_t ≥ 0** | continuous | Total energy consumption of train *t* (kWh). |

---

## 4. Model Formulation  

### 4.1 Objective  

\[
\min \; \underbrace{\gamma_{1}\sum_{t\in T}\Bigl(|a_{t,|S|+1}-\tau^{d}_{t}|+|d_{t,0}-\tau^{0}_{t}|\Bigr)}_{\text{Timetable deviation}} \;+\;
\underbrace{\gamma_{2}\sum_{t\in T} e_{t}}_{\text{Energy consumption}} \;
+\; \underbrace{\Lambda\sum_{t\in T}\sigma_{t}}_{\text{Penalty for cancellations (optional)}}
\]

where **Λ** is a large penalty (e.g., 10⁶) to discourage cancellations unless unavoidable.

---

### 4.2 Feasibility of a Selected Plan  

For each train *t* we pre‑compute a **plan set**  \(\mathcal{P}_t\).  
A plan *p* fixes:

* a route (sequence of segments, possibly using opposite track on blocked segments),
* a departure time from the origin,
* a feasible speed‑level assignment on each traversed segment (hence travel times).

Plan feasibility is ensured by a separate *single‑train* MILP (see §4.3).  
The integrated model only needs to **choose** one plan per train:

\[
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t} z_{t,p}=1-\sigma_t \qquad \forall t\in T \tag{1}
\]

If the train is cancelled (σ_t=1) no plan is selected.

---

### 4.3 Linking Plan Variables to Timetable & Speed Variables  

Let **A_{t,i,p}**, **D_{t,i,p}** be the arrival/departure times at station *i* implied by plan *p* (computed offline).  
Let **X_{t,l,k,τ,p}** be the binary indicator that plan *p* uses segment *l* with speed *k* at time *τ* (also pre‑computed).

Then for every train, station and time:

\[
a_{t,i}= \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t} A_{t,i,p}\;z_{t,p} \qquad\forall t,i \tag{2}
\]
\[
d_{t,i}= \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t} D_{t,i,p}\;z_{t,p} \qquad\forall t,i \tag{3}
\]

and for the binary traversal variables:

\[
x_{t,l,k,\tau}= \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t} X_{t,l,k,\tau,p}\;z_{t,p} \qquad\forall t,l,k,\tau \tag{4}
\]

Thus the global MILP never decides speed directly; it only **selects** a pre‑validated plan.

---

### 4.4 Headway / Conflict Constraints  

#### 4.4.1 Same‑direction conflicts (same physical track)  

For every pair of trains \((t,t')\) that travel **in the same direction** on a common physical segment *l* (i.e. both use the same track orientation) and for every time *τ*:

\[
\sum_{k} x_{t,l,k,\tau} + \sum_{k} x_{t',l,k,\tau} \le 1 + M\; y_{tt',l,\tau} \qquad \forall t<t',\,l,\tau \tag{5}
\]

If both occupy the segment at the same time, the binary conflict variable \(y_{tt',l,\tau}=1\).  
Enforce the required headway:

\[
\sum_{\tau' = \tau}^{\tau+\delta_{tt'}-1} y_{tt',l,\tau'} = 0 \qquad \forall t<t',\,l,\tau \tag{6}
\]

where \(\delta_{tt'} = \lceil \text{minimum headway}/\Delta\rceil\).

#### 4.4.2 Opposite‑direction conflicts on bidirectional track  

For any conflict pair \((l,l')\in R\) (two opposite‑direction directed links sharing the same physical line) and any time *τ*:

\[
\sum_{k} x_{t,l,k,\tau} + \sum_{k} x_{t',l',k,\tau} \le 1 + M\; y_{tt',l,\tau} \qquad \forall t,t',\, (l,l')\in R,\;\tau \tag{7}
\]

and enforce the opposite‑direction headway \(\theta_{tt'}\) analogously to (6) with \(\theta_{tt'}\) instead of \(\delta_{tt'}\).

---

### 4.5 Blockage (Partial Segment) Constraints  

If segment *l* is blocked during the interval \([Δ^{b}_{l}, Δ^{e}_{l}]\) the train may only traverse it **if** it uses the opposite track (rerouting flag ρ_t=1).  

\[
\sum_{k}\sum_{\tau = Δ^{b}_{l}}^{Δ^{e}_{l}} x_{t,l,k,\tau} \le M\; \rho_t \qquad \forall t,\; l\in B \tag{8}
\]

If ρ_t=0 the left‑hand side must be zero, i.e. the train cannot occupy the blocked segment during the blockage window.

---

### 4.6 Dwell‑time and Minimum Stop Constraints  

For every intermediate station *i* (excluding origin 0 and final destination |S|+1) :

\[
d_{t,i} - a_{t,i} \ge \underline{h}_i \;(1-\sigma_t) \qquad \forall t,i\in S\setminus\{0,|S|+1\} \tag{9}
\]

where \(\underline{h}_i\) is the minimum dwell time (e.g., 2 Δ).  

If a train is cancelled (σ_t=1) all arrivals/departures are forced to zero by (2)–(4).

---

### 4.7 Energy Consumption Linearisation  

Energy on a segment is assumed proportional to distance and the square of speed level (common approximation for electric traction).  

\[
e_t = \sum_{l\in L}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{\tau\in τ} c_t \; d_l \; \Bigl(\frac{v_k}{v_{\max}}\Bigr)^{2}\; x_{t,l,k,\tau} \qquad \forall t\in T \tag{10}
\]

Because \(x_{t,l,k,\tau}\) is binary, (10) is already linear.

---

### 4.8 Logical Consistency for Rerouting Flag  

If a train uses the opposite track on **any** blocked segment, ρ_t must be set to 1. This is enforced by a big‑M linking:

\[
\rho_t \ge \frac{1}{M}\sum_{l\in B}\sum_{k}\sum_{\tau} x_{t,l,k,\tau} \qquad \forall t\in T \tag{11}
\]

Conversely, if ρ_t=1 the model may (but is not forced to) use opposite tracks; the decision is embedded in the pre‑computed plans.

---

### 4.9 Domain Restrictions  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,l,k,\tau}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{t,p}\in\{0,1\},\; y_{tt',l,\tau}\in\{0,1\},\\
&\sigma_t\in\{0,1\},\; \rho_t\in\{0,1\},\\
&a_{t,i},d_{t,i},e_t \ge 0 \qquad \forall t,i,l,k,\tau .
\end{aligned}
\]

---

## 5. Summary of Model Structure  

| Component | What it Guarantees |
|-----------|-------------------|
| **Plan‑selection constraints (1)–(4)** | Guarantees that each train follows a *feasible* single‑train speed‑profile (pre‑validated) while allowing the optimizer to choose the best combination of plans. |
| **Headway / conflict constraints (5)–(7)** | Enforces conflict‑free usage of shared track resources for both same‑direction and opposite‑direction trains. |
| **Blockage constraints (8)** | Implements the partial‑segment blockage window; only trains with a rerouting flag may occupy the blocked segment. |
| **Dwell‑time constraints (9)** | Guarantees realistic station stops and respects minimum dwell times. |
| **Energy calculation (10)** | Provides a linear expression for total energy consumption, enabling its inclusion in the objective. |
| **Logical linking (11)** | Couples the rerouting flag to the actual use of opposite tracks. |
| **Objective (section 4.1)** | Minimises a weighted sum of timetable deviation, energy consumption and (optional) cancellation penalties, reflecting the dual goals of service reliability and sustainability. |

---

## 6. Remarks & Possible Extensions  

1. **Plan Generation (Pre‑processing)** – For each train a *set* of feasible plans \(\mathcal{P}_t\) is generated by solving a *single‑train* MILP that respects speed limits, acceleration/deceleration limits, and the blockage window.  The number of plans can be limited by a granularity parameter (e.g., departure time rounded to 5 min).  

2. **Decomposition** – The integrated MILP can be decomposed as described in the source text: (i) an *integer master* that selects plans (variables \(z_{t,p}\)), (ii) a set of *sub‑problems* that verify feasibility of the selected plans (already embedded in the pre‑computed data).  This yields the **IP‑plan selection** model used in the adaptive iterative algorithm.  

3. **Scalability** – The big‑M constants are set to the horizon length (M = H/Δ) which is safe but can be tightened by problem‑specific analysis to improve LP‑relaxation quality.  

4. **Additional Objectives** – The formulation can be extended to include (i) passenger‑delay penalties (weighted by train capacity), (ii) crew‑schedule consistency, or (iii) carbon‑emission costs (linear function of energy).  

5. **Robustness** – Stochastic extensions (scenario‑based) can be added by replicating the model for several disruption scenarios and linking the plan‑selection variables across scenarios (two‑stage stochastic MILP).  

---

**The model above provides a complete, linear (mixed‑integer) representation of the *Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem* under partial‑segment blockages, ready for implementation in any MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress).**

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for Conflict‑Detection‑and‑Resolution (CDR) under Distance‑to‑Go (DTG) signalling**  
*(enhanced version of the RECIFE‑MILP model)*  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Sets, indices and parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T**   | Set of trains, indexed by *t* |
| **S**   | Set of track sections (blocks or TTD‑sections), indexed by *s* |
| **V**   | Set of stations (subset of *S* that contain a dwell stop) |
| **P**   | Set of possible speed‑profile options (e.g. *p* = {“full‑speed”, “reduced”, “coasting”}) |
| **N(s)**| Set of immediate successor sections of *s* (direction of travel) |
| **len\_s**| Physical length of section *s* (km) |
| **v\_max,t**| Maximum permissible speed of train *t* (km/h) |
| **a\_brk,t**| Absolute braking deceleration of train *t* (km/h²) – assumed constant for a given train |
| **τ\_dwell,t,v**| Minimum dwell time of train *t* at station *v* (minutes) |
| **Δ\_init,t**| Initial delay of train *t* at the start of the horizon (minutes) (given) |
| **M**   | Large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints (e.g. 10 000) |
| **ε**   | Small positive number (e.g. 0.001) used to enforce strict inequalities when needed |
| **β\_s**| Binary flag = 1 if section *s* is a switch (or a special TTD‑section) – used to enforce different separation rules (assumption) |
| **γ\_p**| Speed‑profile factor for option *p* (ratio of nominal speed, 0 < γ ≤ 1) – assumption to model slower profiles |
| **c\_t**| Cost weight for delay of train *t* (normally = 1 for all trains) |

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **x\_{t,s}** | binary | = 1 if train *t* occupies section *s* (enters) during the planning horizon |
| **y\_{t,s}** | binary | = 1 if train *t* **leaves** section *s* (i.e. the end‑of‑authority for *t* is after *s*) |
| **z\_{t,p}** | binary | = 1 if train *t* uses speed‑profile option *p* for the whole trip (single‑choice) |
| **δ\_{t}** | continuous ≥ 0 | Total (final) delay of train *t* (minutes) – decision variable to be minimised |
| **θ\_{t,s}** | continuous ≥ 0 | Entry time of train *t* into section *s* (minutes from the start of the horizon) |
| **φ\_{t,s}** | continuous ≥ 0 | Exit time of train *t* from section *s* (minutes) |
| **b\_{t,s}** | continuous ≥ 0 | **Brake‑indication point** (distance from the beginning of *s*) for train *t* when *s* is the last free section before the next occupied one (km). For sections that are not the last free one, b\_{t,s}=0. |
| **σ\_{t,s}** | continuous ≥ 0 | **Speed‑dependent separation distance** required between train *t* and the train ahead when train *t* enters *s* (km). Computed from the braking curve (see constraint (9)). |

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Assumptions (explicitly stated)  

1. **Single speed‑profile per train** – the train keeps the same γ‑factor for the whole trip (reasonable for a short‑term rescheduling horizon).  
2. **Constant braking deceleration** – a linear braking curve is used; the brake‑indication point can be expressed analytically (see (9)).  
3. **Deterministic travel times** – once a speed‑profile is chosen, the travel time of a train through a section is deterministic:  

\[
tt_{t,s}^{p}= \frac{len_s}{\gamma_p \, v_{max,t}} \quad (\text{minutes})
\]

4. **Section‑wise conflict resolution** – conflicts are only checked at the **end of authority** (EoA) of each section, which coincides with the end of the corresponding TTD‑section.  
5. **Switch sections (β\_s = 1)** may require a larger safety margin; this is captured by a factor ρ > 1 (set to 1.2 in the numerical tests).  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Objective function  

\[
\boxed{\min \; \sum_{t\in T} c_t \, \delta_t}
\]

*Minimise the total (weighted) delay of all trains.*

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Core constraints  

#### 5.1. Speed‑profile selection (single‑choice)  

\[
\sum_{p\in P} z_{t,p}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T                                           \tag{1}
\]

#### 5.2. Section occupation logic  

A train must **enter** a section before it can **leave** it, and the sequence of sections follows the network topology.

\[
\theta_{t,s} + \varepsilon \le \phi_{t,s} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S          \tag{2}
\]

\[
\theta_{t,s'} \ge \phi_{t,s} \;-\; M\,(1-x_{t,s}) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S,\; s'\in N(s) \tag{3}
\]

If train *t* occupies section *s* (x\_{t,s}=1) then its exit time from *s* must be before the entry time into any successor *s′*.

\[
x_{t,s} \le y_{t,s} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S                              \tag{4}
\]

*Interpretation*: y\_{t,s}=1 only if the train really passes the EoA of *s* (i.e. it continues beyond *s*).  

#### 5.3. Travel‑time definition (depends on speed profile)  

\[
\phi_{t,s} = \theta_{t,s} + \sum_{p\in P} tt_{t,s}^{p}\,z_{t,p} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S \tag{5}
\]

where  

\[
tt_{t,s}^{p}= \frac{len_s}{\gamma_p \, v_{max,t}} .
\]

#### 5.4. Dwell‑time constraints (stations)  

If *s* ∈ V (station section) the train must stop at least τ\_dwell:

\[
\phi_{t,s} \ge \theta_{t,s} + \tau_{dwell,t,s}\;x_{t,s} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in V \tag{6}
\]

#### 5.5. Initial delay propagation  

The entry time into the first section (indexed by *s\_0(t)*) must respect the given initial delay:

\[
\theta_{t,s_0(t)} = \Delta_{init,t} \qquad \forall t\in T \tag{7}
\]

#### 5.6. Definition of total delay  

The final delay of a train is the difference between its actual arrival at the last section *s\_last(t)* and the **planned** (reference) arrival time *T\_plan\_{t}* (given from the original timetable).  

\[
\delta_t \ge \phi_{t,s_{last}(t)} - T_{plan,t} \qquad \forall t\in T \tag{8}
\]

(If the train finishes earlier than planned, δ\_t can be zero because of the non‑negativity of δ\_t.)

#### 5.7. Speed‑dependent separation distance (DTG principle)  

When a train *t* enters a section *s*, the **minimum distance** to the preceding train *k* (already occupying *s* or a downstream section) must be at least the braking distance that *t* needs to stop before the **end of authority** of *s*. The braking distance for a constant deceleration a\_brk,t and current speed v = γ\_p·v\_max,t is  

\[
d^{brk}_{t,p}= \frac{(\gamma_p v_{max,t})^{2}}{2\,a_{brk,t}} \quad\text{[km]}. \tag{9}
\]

The required separation σ\_{t,s} is therefore  

\[
\sigma_{t,s}= d^{brk}_{t,p} \;+\; \rho^{\beta_s}\,\varepsilon_{s} \tag{10}
\]

where ε\_s is a small safety margin (e.g. 0.01 km) and ρ = 1.2 if β\_s=1 (switch) otherwise ρ = 1.

#### 5.8. Conflict‑avoidance constraints (core DTG CDR)  

Consider any ordered pair of distinct trains *(t,k)* that travel in the **same direction** on a common section *s*. Let *k* be the **preceding** train (i.e. it entered *s* earlier). The following linearised condition guarantees that the distance between them never falls below σ\_{t,s}:

\[
\bigl(\theta_{t,s} - \theta_{k,s}\bigr) \; \ge\; \frac{\sigma_{t,s}}{v_{max,t}^{*}} \;-\; M\,(2 - x_{t,s} - x_{k,s}) \qquad \forall t\neq k,\; s\in S \tag{11}
\]

where  

\[
v_{max,t}^{*}= \sum_{p\in P}\gamma_p v_{max,t}\,z_{t,p}
\]

is the selected cruising speed of train *t*.  

Explanation of (11):  
* If both trains occupy *s* (x\_{t,s}=x\_{k,s}=1) the big‑M term disappears and the constraint forces the entry time of the following train *t* to be delayed enough so that, moving at its selected speed, it would be at least σ\_{t,s} behind the predecessor when it reaches the EoA of *s*.  
* If at least one of the trains does **not** use *s*, the right‑hand side becomes a very negative number (‑M) and the constraint is automatically satisfied.

#### 5.9. End‑of‑Authority (EoA) – block / TTD boundary  

For DTG signalling the **movement authority** of a train ends at the **end of a TTD‑section** (or block). Therefore a train may only proceed to the next section if the **preceding train’s EoA** is already beyond the current section. This is modelled by linking y\_{k,s} (the predecessor has passed the EoA of *s*) with the entry of the follower:

\[
\theta_{t,s} \ge \phi_{k,s} \;-\; M\,(1-y_{k,s}+1-x_{t,s}) \qquad \forall t\neq k,\; s\in S \tag{12}
\]

If the predecessor *k* has already cleared the EoA of *s* (y\_{k,s}=1) and the follower intends to occupy *s* (x\_{t,s}=1), then the follower’s entry time cannot be earlier than the predecessor’s exit time.

#### 5.10. Logical linking of x and y  

A train that **does not** continue beyond a section cannot have y\_{t,s}=1:

\[
y_{t,s} \le x_{t,s} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S \tag{13}
\]

If a train leaves the network after section *s* (i.e. it does not occupy any successor), we set y\_{t,s}=0.

#### 5.11. Binary‑variable linearisation (if needed)  

If the product of a binary and a continuous variable appears (e.g. in (5) we have a sum of binary‑weighted travel times), it is already linear because the binary variables are multiplied by constants. No extra linearisation is required.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 6. Complete MILP formulation  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{t\in T} c_t \,\delta_t \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &\text{(1)–(13)} \\
&\delta_t \ge 0 \qquad\forall t\in T\\
&x_{t,s},y_{t,s},z_{t,p}\in\{0,1\} \qquad\forall t,s,p\\
&\theta_{t,s},\phi_{t,s},b_{t,s},\sigma_{t,s}\ge 0 \qquad\forall t,s
\end{aligned}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 7. Remarks on implementation  

* **Big‑M value** – choose M larger than the maximum possible schedule horizon (e.g. 10 000 min).  
* **Safety factor ρ** – can be tuned per infrastructure (switches, level‑crossings, etc.).  
* **Multiple speed‑profiles** – the model can be extended to allow piece‑wise profiles per section by introducing *z\_{t,s,p}* (binary per section) and adapting (5) and (9).  
* **Bidirectional traffic** – the formulation above assumes a single direction; for opposite directions a similar set of constraints must be added, using the opposite orientation of sections.  
* **Computational tractability** – the number of binary variables is |T|·|S| + |T|·|P|, which is comparable to the original RECIFE‑MILP model and can be solved with modern MILP solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress) for realistic horizons (up to a few hundred trains and a few thousand sections).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 8. How the model captures DTG‑specific features  

1. **Speed‑dependent separation (σ\_{t,s})** is derived from the braking distance (9) rather than a fixed number of blocks.  
2. **Brake‑indication point (b\_{t,s})** can be computed from σ\_{t,s} and the length of the section; it is implicitly enforced by the entry‑time constraints (11) and (12).  
3. **End‑of‑Authority at TTD‑sections** is modelled by y\_{t,s} and the logical coupling (12).  
4. **Switch‑specific safety margins** are introduced via β\_s and the factor ρ in (10).  

Thus the presented MILP is a **complete, linear, mixed‑integer model** for conflict detection and resolution in a railway network equipped with distance‑to‑go signalling, ready to be embedded in a real‑time traffic‑management decision‑support system.

Text:
**MILP for Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage**  

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(t\). |
| \(S\) | Set of line **segments** (track pieces) between two consecutive stations/control points, indexed by \(s\). |
| \(K=\{1,\dots ,K_{\max }\}\) | Discrete **time‑interval indices** (e.g. 1 min each). |
| \(L=\{1,\dots ,L_{\max }\}\) | Set of admissible **speed levels** (constant speed over a segment). |
| \(\mathcal{P}_t\) | Set of feasible **paths** (routes) for train \(t\); each path \(p\) is an ordered list of segments \((s^p_1,\dots ,s^p_{|p|})\). |
| \(\mathcal{B}_s\subseteq K\) | Time intervals in which segment \(s\) is **blocked on the original (right‑hand) track**. |
| \(\mathcal{O}_s\subseteq K\) | Time intervals in which segment \(s\) is **blocked on the opposite (left‑hand) track** (if known). |
| \(S_{\text{station}}\subseteq S\) | Set of segments that correspond to stations (where dwell time is required). |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning | Typical value / comment |
|---|---|---|
| \(L_s\) | Length of segment \(s\) (km). |
| \(v^{\ell}\) | Physical speed (km/h) of speed level \(\ell\). |
| \(\tau^{\ell}_s = \dfrac{L_s}{v^{\ell}}\) | Deterministic travel time (min) to traverse segment \(s\) at speed level \(\ell\). |
| \(e^{\ell}_s\) | Energy consumption (kWh) for segment \(s\) at speed level \(\ell\) (often proportional to \(L_s\)). |
| \(d^{\text{sched}}_{t}\) | Scheduled departure time of train \(t\) from its origin (in minutes). |
| \(a^{\text{sched}}_{t}\) | Scheduled arrival time of train \(t\) at its final destination (in minutes). |
| \(\underline{D}_t\) | Minimum dwell time at any station for train \(t\) (min). |
| \(M\) | Large constant for “big‑M” linearisation (e.g. \(M=K_{\max}\)). |
| \(\lambda_{\text{delay}}, \lambda_{\text{energy}} >0\) | Weights for the bi‑objective (delay vs. energy). |
| \(c^{\text{acc}}_{\ell,\ell'}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if a speed change from \(\ell\) to \(\ell'\) respects acceleration/deceleration limits, 0 otherwise (pre‑computed). |
| \(R_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if, on the chosen path, train \(t\) uses the **original** track for segment \(s\); 0 if it uses the opposite track. |

---

### 3. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| \(x_{t,p}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | Train \(t\) chooses path \(p\) (exactly one). |
| \(y_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | Train \(t\) occupies segment \(s\) during interval \(k\). |
| \(z_{t,s,\ell}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | Train \(t\) traverses segment \(s\) with speed level \(\ell\). |
| \(\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\ge0\) | continuous | Arrival time of train \(t\) at upstream node of segment \(s\) (min). |
| \(\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\ge0\) | continuous | Departure time of train \(t\) from downstream node of segment \(s\) (min). |
| \(\delta_t\ge0\) | continuous | Total delay of train \(t\) (actual final arrival – scheduled). |

All times are expressed in the same unit as the discretisation (minutes).

---

### 4. Model  

#### 4.1 Objective  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
\lambda_{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in T}\delta_t
\;+\;
\lambda_{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{\ell\in L} e^{\ell}_s \, z_{t,s,\ell}
}
\tag{OBJ}
\]

The first term penalises passenger/operational delay, the second term penalises total energy consumption.

---

#### 4.2 Path‑selection  

\[
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t} x_{t,p}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T \tag{R1}
\]

\[
y_{t,s,k}\le \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_t}\mathbf{1}_{\{s\in p\}}\,x_{t,p} 
\qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S,\; k\in K \tag{R2}
\]

(\(\mathbf{1}_{\{s\in p\}}=1\) if segment \(s\) belongs to path \(p\), otherwise 0.)

---

#### 4.3 Speed‑level selection  

\[
\sum_{\ell\in L} z_{t,s,\ell}= \sum_{k\in K} y_{t,s,k}\qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S \tag{S1}
\]

\[
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}= \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}
        +\sum_{\ell\in L}\tau^{\ell}_s\,z_{t,s,\ell}
        \qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in S \tag{S2}
\]

---

#### 4.4 Temporal continuity  

For every pair \((s, s^{+})\) of successive segments on the chosen path of train \(t\) (denote \(s^{+}= \text{succ}_t(s)\)):

\[
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s^{+}}\ge \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in S \text{ with a successor} \tag{T1}
\]

If \(s\) is a station (\(s\in S_{\text{station}}\)):

\[
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}-\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\ge \underline{D}_t\,
      \sum_{k\in K} y_{t,s,k}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in S_{\text{station}} \tag{T2}
\]

Initial departure:

\[
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s^{\text{orig}}_t}= d^{\text{sched}}_{t}
\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{T3}
\]

where \(s^{\text{orig}}_t\) is the first segment of the selected path.

---

#### 4.5 Blockage handling  

Original‑track blockage forces use of opposite track:

\[
y_{t,s,k}\le M\,(1-R_{t,s}) + M\,(1-\mathbf{1}_{\{k\in\mathcal{B}_s\}})
\qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in S,\; k\in K \tag{B1}
\]

If the opposite track is also blocked (\(k\in\mathcal{O}_s\)) an analogous constraint is added with \((1-R_{t,s})\) replaced by \(R_{t,s}\).

---

#### 4.6 Conflict‑avoidance (single‑track occupancy)  

\[
\sum_{t\in T} y_{t,s,k}\le 1 \qquad\forall s\in S,\; k\in K \tag{C1}
\]

(If the line is double‑track with separate directions, the inequality can be relaxed per direction.)

---

#### 4.7 Acceleration limits  

\[
z_{t,s,\ell}+z_{t,s^{+},\ell'}\le 1+ c^{\text{acc}}_{\ell,\ell'}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in S,\; \ell,\ell'\in L \tag{A1}
\]

If a speed transition is infeasible (\(c^{\text{acc}}_{\ell,\ell'}=0\)), the inequality forces at most one of the two binary variables to be 1, thus prohibiting the forbidden change.

---

#### 4.8 Delay definition  

Let \(s^{\text{dest}}_t\) be the last segment of the selected path of train \(t\).

\[
\delta_t \ge \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s^{\text{dest}}_t}- a^{\text{sched}}_{t},
\qquad
\delta_t \ge 0
\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{D1}
\]

---

#### 4.9 Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,p}\in\{0,1\} &&\forall t,p\\
&y_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\} &&\forall t,s,k\\
&z_{t,s,\ell}\in\{0,1\} &&\forall t,s,\ell\\
&\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s},\;\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\ge 0 &&\forall t,s\\
&\delta_t\ge 0 &&\forall t
\end{aligned}
\tag{DOM}
\]

---

### 5. Remarks  

* **Linearisation of speed‑dependent travel time** – by enumerating a finite set of admissible speed levels \(\ell\), the travel time \(\tau^{\ell}_s\) becomes a known constant; the binary variable \(z_{t,s,\ell}\) selects the appropriate constant, keeping the model linear.  
* **Blockage logic** – the binary matrix \(R_{t,s}\) tells whether the train would travel on the original or opposite track for a given path. The big‑M constraint (B1) forces occupancy to be zero on a blocked original track, while allowing the opposite track if it is free.  
* **Conflict‑avoidance** – constraint (C1) guarantees a conflict‑free timetable: at most one train may occupy a physical segment in any time interval.  
* **Acceleration limits** – the pre‑computed matrix \(c^{\text{acc}}_{\ell,\ell'}\) encodes admissible speed‑level transitions; constraint (A1) removes forbidden changes without creating products of variables.  
* **Objective** – the weighted sum of total delay and total energy is linear; additional terms (e.g., passenger‑count penalties, crew‑working‑time limits) can be added similarly.  

The presented formulation is a **complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) model** for the integrated train rescheduling and speed management problem under partial segment blockages. It can be solved directly with commercial MILP solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, SCIP, …).
