Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP‑MILP)**  
The formulation below captures, in a single mixed‑integer linear program, the three‑fold decision problem that arises when a high‑speed railway suffers a *partial‑segment blockage* (one‑track closure) during a known disruption time window \([t^{\text{start}}_d ,\,t^{\text{end}}_d]\).

The model simultaneously decides  

* (i) **when** each train departs/arrives at every station (timetable),  
* (ii) **which side** of the double‑track a train uses on each segment (routing / possible rerouting to the opposite track), and  
* (iii) **how fast** the train travels on each elementary time‑distance interval (speed profile).  

All decisions are linearised so that the model can be solved by a standard MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, …).

---

## 1. Sets, Indices and Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(\mathcal T =\{1,\dots ,T\}\) | Set of trains (indexed by \(k\)). |
| \(\mathcal N =\{0,1,\dots ,N\}\) | Set of stations (node 0 = origin, node \(N\) = final). |
| \(\mathcal S =\{(i,i+1)\mid i=0,\dots ,N-1\}\) | Set of line segments (ordered pairs of consecutive stations). |
| \(\mathcal D =\{d\}\) | Set of disruption events (here a single event). |
| \(\mathcal L =\{1,2\}\) | Set of track‑sides (1 = “normal” side, 2 = “opposite” side). |
| \(\mathcal P =\{p\}\) | Set of *speed‑intervals* (time‑distance discretisation, see §2). |
| \(\mathcal C\) | Set of *conflict pairs* \((k,k',i,\ell)\) – two trains that could occupy the same side \(\ell\) of segment \(i\) at overlapping times. |

### Input data (assumed known)

| Parameter | Description | Typical source |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| \(L_i\) | Length of segment \(i\) (km). | Infrastructure data. |
| \(\underline v_i, \overline v_i\) | Minimum / maximum admissible speed on segment \(i\) (km/h). | Technical limits. |
| \(\underline a_i, \overline a_i\) | Minimum (braking) / maximum (acceleration) rate on segment \(i\) (km/h²). | Train performance. |
| \(t^{\text{sched}}_{k,i}\) | Planned (pre‑disruption) arrival time of train \(k\) at station \(i\). | Existing timetable. |
| \(\Delta^{\text{dwell}}_i\) | Minimum dwell time at station \(i\) (min). | Operational rule. |
| \(\Delta^{\text{head}}_{k,k'}\) | Minimum headway (time separation) required between train \(k\) and its predecessor \(k'\) when using the **same** track side on a segment (min). | Safety regulation. |
| \(E^{\text{unit}}_{i}\) | Energy consumption per km at unit speed on segment \(i\) (kWh/km). Used for linear energy approximation (see §4). | Energy model. |
| \(M\) | Large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints. |
| \(\theta^{\text{max}}_k\) | Maximum allowable schedule deviation for train \(k\) (min). | Service‑level agreement. |
| \(\beta^{\text{pen}}_k\) | Penalty weight for deviation of train \(k\) (cost per minute). | Economic objective. |
| \(c^{\text{reroute}}_{k,i}\) | Fixed cost (or penalty) for rerouting train \(k\) on segment \(i\) to the opposite side. | Operational cost. |
| \(t^{\text{start}}_d, t^{\text{end}}_d\) | Beginning / end of the disruption window (min). | Event data. |
| \(\mathcal B_{i}\subseteq \mathcal L\) | Set of sides that are **blocked** on segment \(i\) during the disruption (normally \(\{1\}\) or \(\{2\}\)). | Disruption description. |
| \(\tau_{p}\) | Length of speed‑interval \(p\) (min). | Discretisation choice. |
| \(x^{\text{dist}}_{p}\) | Distance covered in interval \(p\) (km) – a decision variable (see §2). | – |

---

## 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| \(a_{k,i}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | **Arrival time** of train \(k\) at station \(i\). |
| \(d_{k,i}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | **Departure time** of train \(k\) from station \(i\). |
| \(z_{k,i,\ell}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(k\) traverses segment \((i,i+1)\) on side \(\ell\) (0 otherwise). |
| \(r_{k,i}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(k\) **reroutes** (uses opposite side) on segment \(i\) (i.e. \(z_{k,i,\ell}=1\) for \(\ell\neq\) normal side). |
| \(y_{k,i,p}\) | Binary | 1 if speed‑interval \(p\) is **selected** for train \(k\) on segment \(i\). (Exactly one interval per segment per train.) |
| \(v_{k,i,p}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Speed (km/h) of train \(k\) on segment \(i\) during interval \(p\). |
| \(e_{k,i}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | **Energy consumption** of train \(k\) on segment \(i\). |
| \(\delta^{\text{head}}_{k,k',i}\) | Binary | 1 if train \(k\) is **preceding** train \(k'\) on side \(\ell\) of segment \(i\) (used to enforce headway). |
| \(\Delta^{\text{dev}}_{k,i}\) | Continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Absolute deviation of arrival time from the original schedule: \(|a_{k,i}-t^{\text{sched}}_{k,i}|\). (Linearised with two vars.) |

---

## 3. Linearised Speed‑Interval Representation  

To keep the model linear, the continuous speed on a segment is approximated by a **convex combination** of a finite set of pre‑defined speed‑intervals (piece‑wise constant). For each segment \(i\) we define a small catalogue of admissible speeds \(\{\bar v_{i}^{p}\}_{p\in\mathcal P}\) (e.g. 200, 220, 250 km/h).  

*Exactly one* interval is chosen:

\[
\sum_{p\in\mathcal P} y_{k,i,p}=1 \qquad\forall k\in\mathcal T,\; i\in\mathcal N\setminus\{N\}
\tag{1}
\]

The selected speed and the corresponding travel time are linked by:

\[
v_{k,i,p}= \bar v_{i}^{p}\; y_{k,i,p} \qquad\forall k,i,p
\tag{2}
\]

Travel time on segment \(i\) for train \(k\) (denoted \(\theta_{k,i}\)) becomes:

\[
\theta_{k,i}= \sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\frac{L_i}{\bar v_{i}^{p}}\, y_{k,i,p}
\tag{3}
\]

*Acceleration / deceleration* constraints are enforced by limiting the admissible speed‑intervals to those compatible with the preceding/following speeds. With a **big‑M** formulation:

\[
v_{k,i,p} - v_{k,i-1,q} \le \overline a_i \, \tau_{p} + M\,(1- y_{k,i,p} - y_{k,i-1,q})
\]
\[
v_{k,i-1,q} - v_{k,i,p} \le \underline a_i \, \tau_{p} + M\,(1- y_{k,i,p} - y_{k,i-1,q})
\qquad\forall k,\,i>0,\,p,q\in\mathcal P
\tag{4}
\]

---

## 4. Objective Function  

A **bi‑objective** is linearised as a weighted sum:

\[
\min\; 
\underbrace{\sum_{k\in\mathcal T}\sum_{i\in\mathcal N}\beta^{\text{pen}}_k \,\Delta^{\text{dev}}_{k,i}}_{\text{(A) timetable deviation penalty}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{k\in\mathcal T}\sum_{i\in\mathcal N\setminus\{N\}} e_{k,i}}_{\text{(B) total energy consumption}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{k\in\mathcal T}\sum_{i\in\mathcal N\setminus\{N\}} c^{\text{reroute}}_{k,i}\, r_{k,i}}_{\text{(C) rerouting cost}}
\tag{5}
\]

### Linearisation of absolute deviation  

Introduce two non‑negative variables \(\Delta^{+}_{k,i},\Delta^{-}_{k,i}\) :

\[
a_{k,i} - t^{\text{sched}}_{k,i}= \Delta^{+}_{k,i} - \Delta^{-}_{k,i},
\qquad
\Delta^{\text{dev}}_{k,i}= \Delta^{+}_{k,i}+ \Delta^{-}_{k,i}
\tag{6}
\]

and bound them by the service‑level limit:

\[
\Delta^{+}_{k,i} \le \theta^{\text{max}}_k,\qquad
\Delta^{-}_{k,i} \le \theta^{\text{max}}_k
\tag{7}
\]

### Energy linearisation  

Energy on segment \(i\) is approximated by a **piece‑wise linear** function of speed. Using the pre‑defined speeds \(\bar v_i^{p}\) we pre‑compute the energy per km \(e_i^{p}\) (e.g. from a regression of the actual power‑vs‑speed curve). Then

\[
e_{k,i}= \sum_{p\in\mathcal P} e_i^{p}\, L_i \, y_{k,i,p}
\tag{8}
\]

---

## 5. Core Scheduling Constraints  

### 5.1 Temporal consistency (travel‑time coupling)

\[
a_{k,i+1}= d_{k,i}+ \theta_{k,i} \qquad\forall k\in\mathcal T,\; i=0,\dots ,N-1
\tag{9}
\]

### 5.2 Minimum dwell time at stations  

\[
d_{k,i} \ge a_{k,i}+ \Delta^{\text{dwell}}_i \qquad\forall k,i
\tag{10}
\]

### 5.3 Logical link between routing side and blockage  

A train cannot be assigned to a blocked side during the disruption window:

\[
z_{k,i,\ell}\le 1-\mathbf{1}\bigl\{ \ell\in\mathcal B_i \bigr\}\;\;\;\forall k,i,\ell
\tag{11}
\]

If the segment is blocked on side 1, then only side 2 is feasible (and vice‑versa).  

### 5.4 Rerouting indicator  

Define the *normal* side for each segment as \(\ell^{\text{norm}}_i\) (normally side 1).  

\[
r_{k,i}= 1-\;z_{k,i,\ell^{\text{norm}}_i}\qquad\forall k,i
\tag{12}
\]

Thus \(r_{k,i}=1\) iff the train uses the opposite side (i.e. reroutes).

### 5.5 Single‑side occupancy (conflict‑avoidance)  

For every conflict pair \((k,k',i,\ell)\in\mathcal C\) we enforce a binary ordering variable \(\delta^{\text{head}}_{k,k',i,\ell}\) :

\[
d_{k,i} + \theta_{k,i} \le a_{k',i} + M\,(1-\delta^{\text{head}}_{k,k',i,\ell}) \qquad\forall (k,k',i,\ell)\in\mathcal C
\tag{13}
\]

\[
d_{k',i} + \theta_{k',i} \le a_{k,i} + M\,\delta^{\text{head}}_{k,k',i,\ell} \qquad\forall (k,k',i,\ell)\in\mathcal C
\tag{14}
\]

Only one of the two inequalities can be active, guaranteeing that the two trains do **not** occupy the same side \(\ell\) of segment \(i\) at overlapping times.  

A minimum headway is also required:

\[
a_{k',i} - \bigl(d_{k,i}+ \theta_{k,i}\bigr) \ge \Delta^{\text{head}}_{k,k'} \;-\; M\,(1-\delta^{\text{head}}_{k,k',i,\ell})
\tag{15}
\]

### 5.6 Train order preservation (precedence)  

If a train \(k\) is originally scheduled **behind** train \(k'\) on a segment, we keep the same order (unless a reroute forces a change). This can be modelled by fixing \(\delta^{\text{head}}_{k,k',i,\ell}\) to the original order for non‑blocked sides, and leaving it free only when one of the trains uses the opposite side.

---

## 6. Additional Physical Constraints  

### 6.1 Speed limits  

\[
\underline v_i \le v_{k,i,p} \le \overline v_i \qquad\forall k,i,p
\tag{16}
\]

Because of (2), (16) are automatically satisfied if the catalogue \(\{\bar v_i^{p}\}\) respects the limits.

### 6.2 Acceleration / deceleration limits across stations  

If a train stops at a station, the speed at departure must be feasible given the dwell time and the maximum acceleration. A simple linear bound:

\[
v_{k,i,\,\text{dep}} \le \overline a_i \, (d_{k,i}-a_{k,i}) + \underline v_i
\tag{17}
\]

where \(v_{k,i,\,\text{dep}}\) is the speed used on the next segment (obtained from the selected interval).

---

## 7. Complete MILP Statement  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \;& \sum_{k,i}\beta^{\text{pen}}_k \bigl(\Delta^{+}_{k,i}+ \Delta^{-}_{k,i}\bigr)
      +\sum_{k,i} \sum_{p} e_i^{p}\,L_i\, y_{k,i,p}
      +\sum_{k,i} c^{\text{reroute}}_{k,i}\, r_{k,i} \\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(1)–(17) } \\
& y_{k,i,p}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{k,i,\ell}\in\{0,1\},\; r_{k,i}\in\{0,1\},\;
   \delta^{\text{head}}_{k,k',i,\ell}\in\{0,1\} \\
& a_{k,i},d_{k,i},v_{k,i,p},e_{k,i},\Delta^{\pm}_{k,i}\ge 0
\end{aligned}
}
\]

---

## 8. Modeling Assumptions (explicitly stated)

| # | Assumption | Rationale / Source |
|---|------------|--------------------|
| A1 | **Time‑distance discretisation** – each segment’s speed is approximated by a finite set of constant speed levels \(\bar v_i^{p}\). | Guarantees linearity; typical in MILP speed‑profile models. |
| A2 | **Piece‑wise linear energy model** – energy per km is linear in the selected speed level (pre‑computed). | Sufficient accuracy for high‑speed trains and keeps the model linear. |
| A3 | **Single‑track usage per segment** – a train occupies exactly one side of a double‑track segment at any moment. | Mirrors the physical reality of a blocked side. |
| A4 | **Deterministic disruption window** – start/end times are known a‑priori and do not change. | Standard in disruption‑recovery literature. |
| A5 | **Headway enforcement via binary ordering** – only pairwise conflicts are considered (no three‑train simultaneous conflict). | Captures the essential safety requirement while remaining linear. |
| A6 | **No overtaking** – trains keep the same order on a given side unless a reroute forces a side change. | Reflects typical high‑speed railway operating rules. |
| A7 | **Maximum schedule deviation \(\theta^{\text{max}}_k\)** is the same for early and late arrivals. | Simplifies the absolute‑value linearisation. |
| A8 | **Uniform dwell time** \(\Delta^{\text{dwell}}_i\) for all trains at a station. | Common practice; can be relaxed by train‑specific parameters if data are available. |
| A9 | **Big‑M value** \(M\) is chosen large enough to deactivate constraints when the corresponding binary variable is 0, but not excessively large to avoid numerical issues. | Standard MILP technique. |
| A10 | **Acceleration / deceleration limits are applied only between consecutive segments** (no intra‑segment speed changes). | Consistent with the constant‑speed interval representation. |

---

## 9. Remarks on Solving the Model  

* **Decomposition** – The model can be decomposed exactly as described in the source paper: (i) an integer master problem that decides the binary routing / ordering variables \((z, r, \delta^{\text{head}})\); (ii) a set of *train‑plan* sub‑problems (one per train) that, for a fixed routing, compute the optimal speed‑interval selection and timing (a small linear program).  
* **Iterative refinement** – The speed‑interval catalogue \(\mathcal P\) can be refined adaptively (add intermediate speeds) in neighborhoods where the current solution is infeasible or sub‑optimal, following the “adaptive iterative algorithm” described in the paper.  
* **Scalability** – The number of binary variables grows with \(|\mathcal T|\times|\mathcal S|\times|\mathcal L|\) (routing) plus \(|\mathcal C|\) (conflict ordering). For realistic high‑speed networks (hundreds of trains, dozens of segments) the decomposition‑based approach is essential.  

---

**The formulation above provides a self‑contained, linear (MILP) description of the *Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem* (TRSMP) under a partial‑segment blockage, ready to be implemented in any commercial MILP solver.**

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (Partial Segment Blockage)**  

The model simultaneously decides (i) the route each train will use, (ii) the speed level on every traversed track segment, and (iii) a conflict‑free timetable that respects partial‑blockage capacities and bidirectional safety.  
All relationships are linear; the only integer variables are binary.  

---

### 1️⃣ Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | Set of trains, indexed by *t* |
| **N** | Set of network nodes (stations, junctions), indexed by *i* |
| **E** | Set of directed track segments *(i→j)*, indexed by *(i,j)* |
| **S** | Set of admissible speed levels (e.g. low, medium, high), indexed by *s* |
| **B ⊆ E** | Set of **partially blocked** segments |
| **Rₜ ⊆ Pₜ** | Feasible routes for train *t* (each route *r* is an ordered list of segments) |
| **O** | Set of bidirectional segment pairs:  *(i,j)∈O ⇔ (j,i)∈O* (same physical track, opposite directions) |

---

### 2️⃣ Parameters  

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| \(L_{ij}\) | Length of segment *(i,j)* (km) |
| \(v_s\) | Speed (km / min) associated with speed level *s* |
| \(\alpha_s\) | Energy consumption rate (kWh / km) at speed level *s* |
| \(\beta_{ij}\) | Capacity factor of blocked segment *(i,j)∈B* (0 < β ≤ 1) – fraction of a train that can occupy it (normally 1). |
| \(\tau^{b,-}_{ij},\;\tau^{b,+}_{ij}\) | Start / end of the blockage time window on segment *(i,j)∈B* (min) |
| \(a^{\text{plan}}_{t}\) | Planned arrival time of train *t* at its destination (min) |
| \(d^{\text{plan}}_{t}\) | Planned departure time of train *t* from its origin (min) |
| \(M\) | Big‑M (larger than the planning horizon, e.g. 10⁶) |
| \(\beta,\;\gamma\) | Weights in the objective (β > 0 for delay, γ > 0 for energy) |
| \(U_t\) | Upper bound on total travel time of train *t* (planning horizon) |

---

### 3️⃣ Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(z_{t r}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* uses route *r* |
| \(x_{t ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* traverses segment *(i,j)* |
| \(y_{t ij s}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train *t* traverses *(i,j)* with speed level *s* |
| \(\text{dep}_{t i}\ge0\) | continuous | departure time of train *t* from node *i* |
| \(\text{arr}_{t i}\ge0\) | continuous | arrival time of train *t* at node *i* |
| \(\Delta_t\ge0\) | continuous | total delay of train *t* (actual – planned arrival) |
| \(E_t\ge0\) | continuous | total energy consumption of train *t* |
| \(b_{t ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | auxiliary for “before/after” the blockage on a blocked segment |
| \(c_{t_1 t_2 ij}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | auxiliary for bidirectional conflict ordering |
| \(w^{s_1 s_2}_{t ijk}\in\{0,1\}\) | binary | auxiliary for speed‑change transition on consecutive segments *(i,j) → (j,k)* |

---

### 4️⃣ Objective  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
\underbrace{\beta\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_t}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\gamma\sum_{t\in T}E_t}_{\text{total energy}}
}
\]

with  

\[
E_t=\sum_{(i,j)\in E}\sum_{s\in S}\alpha_s\,L_{ij}\;y_{t ij s}.
\]

---

### 5️⃣ Constraints  

#### 5.1 Route choice  

1. **Exactly one route per train**  
\[
\sum_{r\in R_t}z_{t r}=1\qquad\forall t\in T.
\]

2. **Route ⇒ segment usage**  
\[
x_{t ij}\;\ge\;\sum_{r\in R_t}\mathbf 1_{(i,j)\in r}\;z_{t r}\qquad\forall t,(i,j)\in E.
\]

3. **Segment ⇒ exactly one speed level**  
\[
\sum_{s\in S}y_{t ij s}=x_{t ij}\qquad\forall t,(i,j)\in E.
\]

#### 5.2 Flow conservation (feasible path)  

For every interior node *k* (neither origin nor destination of *t*)  

\[
\sum_{j:(k,j)\in E}x_{t kj}\;-\;\sum_{i:(i,k)\in E}x_{t ik}=0\qquad\forall t,\;k\in N\setminus\{o_t,d_t\}.
\]

At origin *oₜ* and destination *dₜ*  

\[
\sum_{j:(o_t,j)\in E}x_{t o_t j}=1,\qquad
\sum_{i:(i,d_t)\in E}x_{t i d_t}=1 .
\]

#### 5.3 Time feasibility on each traversed segment  

If train *t* uses *(i,j)* with speed *s*  

\[
\text{arr}_{t j}\;\ge\;\text{dep}_{t i}\;+\;\frac{L_{ij}}{v_s}\;-\;M\,(1-y_{t ij s})
\qquad\forall t,(i,j)\in E,\;s\in S.
\]

Departure cannot be earlier than arrival (minimum dwell = 0)  

\[
\text{dep}_{t i}\;\ge\;\text{arr}_{t i}\qquad\forall t,i.
\]

#### 5.4 Blockage (partial segment) constraints  

For each blocked segment *(i,j)∈B* we force the train to finish **either** before the blockage window **or** start after it.  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\text{arr}_{t j}\;\le\;\tau^{b,-}_{ij}+M\,b_{t ij} \\
&\text{dep}_{t i}\;\ge\;\tau^{b,+}_{ij}-M\,(1-b_{t ij}) \\
&x_{t ij}=1 \;\Longrightarrow\; b_{t ij}\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t,(i,j)\in B .
\]

#### 5.5 Bidirectional conflict on a single‑track  

For every unordered pair of opposite directed segments \((i,j)\) and \((j,i)\) and for every pair of distinct trains \(t_1<t_2\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\text{arr}_{t_1 j}\;\le\;\text{dep}_{t_2 i}+M\,c_{t_1 t_2 ij}\\
&\text{arr}_{t_2 i}\;\le\;\text{dep}_{t_1 j}+M\,(1-c_{t_1 t_2 ij})\\
&x_{t_1 ij}+x_{t_2 ji}\le 1\qquad\text{(if both use opposite directions, one of the two inequalities orders them in time)}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t_1<t_2,\;(i,j)\in O .
\]

#### 5.6 Speed‑change / acceleration limits  

If a train changes speed from *s₁* on *(i,j)* to *s₂* on *(j,k)* a minimum transition time  \(U_{s_1s_2}\)  is required.  

Auxiliary variable  

\(w^{s_1 s_2}_{t ijk}\ge y_{t ij s_1}+y_{t jk s_2}-1\).

Temporal ordering  

\[
\text{dep}_{t jk}\;-\;\text{arr}_{t ij}\;\ge\;U_{s_1s_2}\;-\;M\bigl(1-w^{s_1 s_2}_{t ijk}\bigr)
\qquad\forall t,(i,j),(j,k)\in E,\;s_1,s_2\in S .
\]

(If acceleration limits are ignored, set all \(U_{s_1s_2}=0\).)

#### 5.7 Delay definition  

\[
\Delta_t\;\ge\;\text{arr}_{t d_t}\;-\;a^{\text{plan}}_{t},\qquad 
\Delta_t\ge0\qquad\forall t\in T .
\]

#### 5.8 Energy calculation (linear)  

\[
E_t\;=\;\sum_{(i,j)\in E}\sum_{s\in S}\alpha_s\,L_{ij}\;y_{t ij s}\qquad\forall t.
\]

#### 5.9 Planning‑horizon bound  

\[
\text{arr}_{t d_t}\;-\;\text{dep}_{t o_t}\;\le\;U_t\qquad\forall t.
\]

#### 5.10 Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&z_{t r},\,x_{t ij},\,y_{t ij s},\,b_{t ij},\,c_{t_1 t_2 ij},\,w^{s_1 s_2}_{t ijk}\in\{0,1\},\\
&\text{dep}_{t i},\;\text{arr}_{t i},\;\Delta_t,\;E_t\ge0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 6️⃣ Complete MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\beta\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_t\;+\;\gamma\sum_{t\in T}E_t\\[2mm]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(5.1)–(5.10) \; \text{as listed above}}\\
&\text{binary / continuous variable domains.}
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the model is a **Mixed‑Integer Linear Program (MILP)**.

---

### 7️⃣ How the model reflects the problem description  

| Description in the text | MILP element |
|------------------------|--------------|
| **Binary route‑choice** | \(z_{t r}\) (5.1) |
| **Departure / arrival times** | \(\text{dep}_{t i},\;\text{arr}_{t i}\) |
| **Speed level per segment** | \(y_{t ij s}\) (5.3) |
| **Weighted sum of delay & energy** | Objective (β · Δ + γ · E) |
| **Time‑feasibility** | (5.3) travel‑time links |
| **Partial‑segment blockage** | (5.4) “before / after” big‑M constraints |
| **Bidirectional train conflict** | (5.5) disjunctive ordering on opposite tracks |
| **Acceleration / deceleration limits** | (5.6) transition‑time constraints |
| **Energy calculation** | (5.8) linear sum over speed‑level binaries |

Thus the presented formulation provides a **complete, linear MILP** that simultaneously reschedules trains, selects feasible speed profiles, respects partial blockages, resolves bidirectional conflicts, and minimizes a combined punctuality‑energy cost. It can be implemented directly in any MILP modelling language (AMPL, GAMS, Pyomo, JuMP, …) and solved with standard solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, SCIP, …).

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling & Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) – Partial Segment Blockage**  

---

### 1. Sets and parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** = {1,…,|T|} | Trains (indexed by *i*). |
| **S** = {1,…,|S|} | Stations (including origins & destinations). |
| **L** = {1,…,|L|} | Elementary track segments (between two consecutive stations or a junction). |
| **K** = {0,1} | Route‑choice index (0 = original route, 1 = detour). |
| **B** ⊂ **L** | Blocked segments (partial blockage). |
| **Δ** | Safety headway time (seconds) required between two trains on the same segment. |
| **\(v^{\min}_{\ell},v^{\max}_{\ell}\)** | Minimum / maximum admissible speed on segment ℓ (m s⁻¹). |
| **\(L_{\ell}\)** | Length of segment ℓ (m). |
| **\(d^{\text{sched}}_{i}\)** | Scheduled arrival time of train *i* at its final destination. |
| **\(w^{\text{delay}}_{i}\ge0\)** | Weight for passenger‑delay of train *i* (e.g. passenger volume). |
| **\(w^{\text{energy}}\ge0\)** | Global weight for energy consumption. |
| **α,β≥0** | Parameters of the energy model \(E=αv^{2}+βv\). |
| **\(τ^{\text{dw}}_{\min},τ^{\text{dw}}_{\max}\)** | Minimum / maximum dwell time at any intermediate station. |
| **M** | Big‑M constant for logical constraints. |
| **\(\Delta t^{\text{block}}_{\ell}\)** | Extra travel time on blocked segment ℓ when the detour is taken. |

All data are assumed known from the timetable, infrastructure, and disruption description.

---

### 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Definition |
|----------|------|------------|
| \(r_{i,k}\) | binary | =1 if train *i* uses route *k* (k=0 original, k=1 detour). |
| \(o_{i,j}\) | binary | =1 if train *i* passes **before** train *j* on every common segment (otherwise \(o_{j,i}=1\)). |
| \(d_{i,s}\) | continuous ≥0 | Departure time of train *i* from station *s*. |
| \(a_{i,s}\) | continuous ≥0 | Arrival time of train *i* at station *s*. |
| \(t_{i,\ell}\) | continuous ≥0 | Travel time of train *i* on segment ℓ. |
| \(v_{i,\ell}\) | continuous ≥0 | Average speed of train *i* on segment ℓ. |
| \(z_{i,\ell}\) | continuous ≥0 | Auxiliary variable for linearising \(v_{i,\ell}^{2}\). |
| \(\theta_{i,\ell}\) | binary | =1 if train *i* is forced to use the detour on blocked segment ℓ (linked to \(r_{i,1}\)). |
| \(\lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}\) | continuous ≥0 | Convex‑combination coefficients for piece‑wise linear approximation of \(v^{2}\) on segment ℓ (SOS2). |

---

### 3. Objective function  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i\in T} w^{\text{delay}}_{i}\,\bigl(a_{i,\text{last}}-d^{\text{sched}}_{i}\bigr)}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{w^{\text{energy}}\;\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L}
\bigl(α\,z_{i,\ell}+β\,v_{i,\ell}\bigr)\,t_{i,\ell}}_{\text{energy consumption (linearised)}}
}
\]

*The first term penalises late arrivals; the second term approximates the energy needed on each segment (quadratic in speed, linearised by \(z_{i,\ell}\)).*

---

### 4. Linearisation of the quadratic energy term  

For every segment ℓ define speed break‑points  
\(\mathcal{P}_{\ell}=\{p^{1}_{\ell},\dots ,p^{P}_{\ell}\}\) covering \([v^{\min}_{\ell},v^{\max}_{\ell}]\).  

\[
\begin{aligned}
v_{i,\ell} &=\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_{\ell}}\lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}\,p,\\
z_{i,\ell} &=\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_{\ell}}\lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}\,p^{2},\\
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_{\ell}}\lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}&=1,\qquad \lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}\ge0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

The \(\lambda\)’s are forced to be SOS2 (or equivalent) so that the approximation of \(v^{2}\) is piece‑wise linear and the model stays MILP.

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### (1) Route‑choice (exactly one route)  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} r_{i,k}=1\qquad\forall i\in T .
\]

#### (2) Detour activation on blocked segments  

\[
\theta_{i,\ell}=r_{i,1}\qquad\forall i\in T,\;\ell\in B .
\]

#### (3) Travel‑time on blocked segment (extra delay if detoured)  

\[
t_{i,\ell}\;\ge\;\frac{L_{\ell}}{v^{\max}_{\ell}}+\Delta t^{\text{block}}_{\ell}\,\theta_{i,\ell}
\qquad\forall i\in T,\;\ell\in B .
\]

For non‑blocked segments the lower bound is simply \(\frac{L_{\ell}}{v^{\max}_{\ell}}\).

#### (4) Time‑flow on every segment  

If segment ℓ connects station *s* (departure) to station *s′* (arrival),

\[
a_{i,s'} = d_{i,s}+t_{i,\ell}\qquad\forall i\in T,\;\ell\in L .
\]

#### (5) Dwell‑time limits at intermediate stations  

\[
τ^{\text{dw}}_{\min}\le d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}\le τ^{\text{dw}}_{\max}
\qquad\forall i\in T,\;s\in S\setminus\{\text{origin},\text{dest}\}.
\]

#### (6) Speed limits and length‑time relation (linearised)  

\[
v^{\min}_{\ell}\le v_{i,\ell}\le v^{\max}_{\ell}\qquad\forall i,\ell .
\]

\[
L_{\ell}\le v^{\max}_{\ell}\,t_{i,\ell},\qquad
L_{\ell}\ge v^{\min}_{\ell}\,t_{i,\ell}\qquad\forall i,\ell .
\]

(If tighter coupling is required, a McCormick envelope using \(z_{i,\ell}=v_{i,\ell}^{2}\) can be added.)

#### (7) Conflict‑avoidance (precedence) on shared segments  

Let  

\[
\mathcal{C}=\{(i,j,\ell)\mid i<j,\;\ell\in L\text{ used by both }i\text{ and }j\}.
\]

For each \((i,j,\ell)\in\mathcal{C}\) impose the big‑M disjunction:

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{i,\text{entry}(\ell)}+t_{i,\ell}+Δ &\le a_{j,\text{entry}(\ell)} + M\,(1-o_{i,j}),\\
a_{j,\text{entry}(\ell)}+t_{j,\ell}+Δ &\le a_{i,\text{entry}(\ell)} + M\,o_{i,j},
\end{aligned}
\]

where **entry(ℓ)** denotes the station at which the train enters segment ℓ.  
Exactly one of the two inequalities is active; the binary variable \(o_{i,j}\) decides the order.

#### (8) Final‑arrival definition (used in objective)  

\[
a_{i,\text{last}} = d_{i,\text{penultimate}} + t_{i,\ell_{\text{final}}}\qquad\forall i\in T .
\]

#### (9) Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& r_{i,k},\,o_{i,j},\,\theta_{i,\ell}\in\{0,1\},\\
& d_{i,s},a_{i,s},t_{i,\ell},v_{i,\ell},z_{i,\ell},\lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}\ge0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 6. Complete MILP formulation  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{i\in T} w^{\text{delay}}_{i}\bigl(a_{i,\text{last}}-d^{\text{sched}}_{i}\bigr)
\;+\;w^{\text{energy}}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L}\bigl(α\,z_{i,\ell}+β\,v_{i,\ell}\bigr)t_{i,\ell}\\[2mm]
\text{s.t. }&
\sum_{k\in K} r_{i,k}=1 &&\forall i\\
&\theta_{i,\ell}=r_{i,1} &&\forall i,\;\ell\in B\\
&t_{i,\ell}\ge\frac{L_{\ell}}{v^{\max}_{\ell}}+\Delta t^{\text{block}}_{\ell}\,\theta_{i,\ell}
&&\forall i,\;\ell\in B\\
&a_{i,s'}=d_{i,s}+t_{i,\ell} &&\forall i,\;\ell\in L\\
&τ^{\text{dw}}_{\min}\le d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}\le τ^{\text{dw}}_{\max}
&&\forall i,\;s\in S\setminus\{\text{origin},\text{dest}\}\\
&v^{\min}_{\ell}\le v_{i,\ell}\le v^{\max}_{\ell}
&&\forall i,\ell\\
&L_{\ell}\le v^{\max}_{\ell}t_{i,\ell},\;L_{\ell}\ge v^{\min}_{\ell}t_{i,\ell}
&&\forall i,\ell\\
&\text{Precedence (big‑M) (7a)–(7b)} &&\forall (i,j,\ell)\in\mathcal{C}\\
&v_{i,\ell}= \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_{\ell}}\lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}p,\;
z_{i,\ell}= \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_{\ell}}\lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}p^{2},\\
&\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_{\ell}}\lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}=1,\;\lambda^{p}_{i,\ell}\ge0
&&\forall i,\ell\\
&\text{Binary / non‑negative domain constraints} &&\text{(9)} .
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear (or piece‑wise linear via SOS2), therefore the model is a **Mixed‑Integer Linear Program (MILP)** suitable for commercial solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, …).

---

### 7. Mapping to the problem description  

| Description in text | MILP component |
|---------------------|----------------|
| “route choice (original / reroute)” | binary \(r_{i,k}\), constraints (1)–(2) |
| “partial segment blockage” | set **B**, extra travel time \(\Delta t^{\text{block}}_{\ell}\) in (3) |
| “train order / conflict resolution” | binary \(o_{i,j}\), precedence constraints (7) |
| “arrival / departure / dwell times” | variables \(a_{i,s},d_{i,s}\), flow (4) and dwell (5) |
| “speed levels and limits” | variables \(v_{i,\ell}\), bounds (6) |
| “energy consumption” | objective term with linearised \(αv^{2}+βv\) using \(z_{i,\ell}\) and SOS2 |
| “safety headway Δ” | appears in precedence constraints (7) |
| “objective: delay + energy” | combined objective (first equation) |

---

**Result** – The formulation above provides a complete, linear MILP that jointly decides routing, train ordering, precise timetabling, and speed profiles for a high‑speed railway under a partial‑segment blockage, while minimising a weighted sum of passenger delay and energy consumption and respecting all operational constraints.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for rolling‑stock rescheduling with infrastructure‑availability constraints**  

The model integrates two sub‑problems that are solved in a Benders‑/iterative‑style loop in the paper:

* **Composition sub‑problem** – decides which rolling‑stock units (RSUs) are assigned to which passenger trips and which shunting movements are performed.  
* **Infrastructure sub‑problem** – checks whether the selected shunting movements can be realised on the available tracks of the considered stations (Utrecht Centraal and Rotterdam Centraal) and, if necessary, forces short delays on other passenger trains.

Below a **single‑stage MILP** that captures both aspects is presented.  
All sets, parameters, decision variables, the objective function and the constraints are defined explicitly.  
Missing data are filled with reasonable assumptions and are marked as such.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \\(T\\) | Set of passenger trips (indexed by \\(t\\)) |
| \\(S\\) | Set of shunting movements that may be performed (indexed by \\(s\\)). Each shunting movement is defined by a *departure station*, *arrival station*, *departure time window* and *arrival time window*. |
| \\(R\\) | Set of rolling‑stock units (RSUs) (indexed by \\(r\\)). |
| \\(K\\) | Set of stations where shunting is allowed (here \\(K=\{Utrecht, Rotterdam\}\\)). |
| \\(P\\) | Set of time periods (e.g., minutes) covering the whole planning horizon (indexed by \\(p\\)). |
| \\(L\\) | Set of railway tracks (or track‑segments) at the stations in \\(K\\) (indexed by \\(l\\)). |
| \\(B\\) | Set of binary “big‑M” auxiliary indices used for Benders‑type cuts (see §4). |

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical value / assumption |
|--------|--------------|----------------------------|
| \\(c_{rt}\\) | 1 if RSU \\(r\\) is compatible with the composition required for trip \\(t\\) (e.g., number of cars, power). | Compatibility matrix supplied by the operator. |
| \\(a_t\\) | Scheduled departure time of trip \\(t\\) (in minutes from midnight). | From the original timetable. |
| \\(d_t\\) | Scheduled arrival time of trip \\(t\\). | From the original timetable. |
| \\(p^{\max}\\) | Maximum allowed delay for any passenger trip (minutes). | Small value, e.g. 5 min (assumption). |
| \\(M\\) | A large constant (big‑M) for linking binary and continuous variables. | e.g. 10 000. |
| \\(cap_{lk}\\) | Capacity (number of RSUs that can occupy track \\(l\\) at station \\(k\\) simultaneously). | Usually 1 for a shunting track; assumption = 1. |
| \\(dur_s\\) | Minimum duration of shunting movement \\(s\\) (minutes). | Derived from distance, acceleration, etc. |
| \\(win^{dep}_{s}\\) | Earliest feasible start time of shunting \\(s\\) (departure window). | From disruption analysis. |
| \\(win^{arr}_{s}\\) | Latest feasible finish time of shunting \\(s\\) (arrival window). | From disruption analysis. |
| \\(cost^{shift}_r\\) | Cost for moving RSU \\(r\\) from its original position to the start of a shunting movement (e.g., dead‑head mileage). | Operator‑specific; assume 1 €/km. |
| \\(cost^{delay}_t\\) | Penalty cost per minute of delay for passenger trip \\(t\\). | High value (e.g., 10 €/min) to keep passenger service. |
| \\(cost^{cancel}_t\\) | Penalty for cancelling trip \\(t\\). | Very high (e.g., 10 000 €) – discourages cancellations. |
| \\(α\\) | Weight for “stick‑to‑the‑plan” objective (deviation from original RSU‑trip assignment). | 0 ≤ α ≤ 1, chosen by decision‑maker (assumption α = 0.3). |
| \\(β\\) | Weight for infrastructure‑feasibility objective (number of infeasible shunting movements). | 1 − α (assumption). |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \\(x_{rt}\\) | Binary | 1 if RSU \\(r\\) is assigned to passenger trip \\(t\\). |
| \\(y_{rs}\\) | Binary | 1 if RSU \\(r\\) performs shunting movement \\(s\\). |
| \\(z_{t}\\) | Binary | 1 if passenger trip \\(t\\) is cancelled. |
| \\(Δ_t\\) | Continuous ≥ 0 | Delay (in minutes) applied to trip \\(t\\) (0 if cancelled). |
| \\(s^{start}_s\\) | Continuous | Actual start time of shunting movement \\(s\\). |
| \\(s^{end}_s\\) | Continuous | Actual end time of shunting movement \\(s\\). |
| \\(u_{slp}\\) | Binary | 1 if shunting \\(s\\) occupies track \\(l\\) at period \\(p\\). |
| \\(π_{s}\\) | Binary (Benders cut indicator) | 1 if shunting \\(s\\) is **forced** to be rejected by the infrastructure model (used in the exact algorithm). |
| \\(w_{rt}\\) | Binary | 1 if RSU \\(r\\) is *kept* on its originally planned trip (stick‑to‑plan). This variable is used only in the “plan‑following” term of the objective. |

---

## 4. Model Formulation  

### 4.1 Objective Function  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \underbrace{ \alpha \sum_{r\in R}\sum_{t\in T} (1-w_{rt}) }_{\text{(A) deviation from original plan}} \\
        & + \beta \Bigg[ \underbrace{ \sum_{t\in T} \big( cost^{delay}_t \, Δ_t + cost^{cancel}_t \, z_t \big) }_{\text{(B) passenger‑service cost}} \\
        & \qquad\qquad\; + \underbrace{ \sum_{r\in R}\sum_{s\in S} cost^{shift}_r \, y_{rs} }_{\text{(C) dead‑head / shunting cost}} \\
        & \qquad\qquad\; + \underbrace{ \sum_{s\in S} M \, π_{s} }_{\text{(D) penalty for infeasible shunting (big‑M)} } \Bigg]
\end{aligned}
\]

*Term (A)* counts how many RSU‑trip assignments differ from the original schedule (the smaller, the more “plan‑following”).  
*Term (B)* penalises passenger delays and cancellations.  
*Term (C)* accounts for the extra dead‑head distance needed to reach shunting start positions.  
*Term (D)* forces the master problem to avoid shunting movements that the infrastructure sub‑problem has declared infeasible (the big‑M makes the cut active).

The weights \\(α\\) and \\(β\\) allow the decision‑maker to trade‑off plan‑following vs. overall operational cost.

---

### 4.2 Constraints  

#### 4.2.1 Assignment & Compatibility  

1. **Each passenger trip is served by at most one RSU (or cancelled):**  
   \[
   \sum_{r\in R} x_{rt} + z_t = 1 \qquad \forall t\in T
   \tag{C1}
   \]

2. **RSU can be assigned only to compatible trips:**  
   \[
   x_{rt} \le c_{rt} \qquad \forall r\in R,\, t\in T
   \tag{C2}
   \]

3. **Each RSU can be used at most once at a given time (no overlapping trips):**  
   For any two trips \\(t_1, t_2\\) that overlap in time,  
   \[
   x_{rt_1} + x_{rt_2} \le 1 \qquad \forall r\in R,\; \forall (t_1,t_2): [a_{t_1},d_{t_1}] \cap [a_{t_2},d_{t_2}] \neq \emptyset
   \tag{C3}
   \]

4. **Plan‑following indicator:**  
   \[
   w_{rt} \le x_{rt} \qquad \forall r,t
   \tag{C4}
   \]
   (If the original plan assigned RSU \\(r\\) to trip \\(t\\), then \\(w_{rt}=1\\) when that assignment is kept; otherwise \\(w_{rt}=0\\). The original assignment data are taken as input.)

#### 4.2.2 Shunting Movements  

5. **Link shunting to an RSU:**  
   \[
   \sum_{r\in R} y_{rs} = 1 - π_{s} \qquad \forall s\in S
   \tag{C5}
   \]
   (If the infrastructure model declares \\(π_s=1\\) the shunting is prohibited; otherwise exactly one RSU must perform it.)

6. **RSU can perform a shunting only if it is **free** at the required time.**  
   For each RSU \\(r\\) and shunting \\(s\\):  
   \[
   s^{start}_s \ge a_t - M(1 - x_{rt}) \quad\text{and}\quad s^{end}_s \le d_t + M(1 - x_{rt})\quad \forall r,t\text{ s.t. }x_{rt}=1
   \tag{C6}
   \]
   (Simplified: the shunting must be scheduled between the departure of the preceding trip and the arrival of the next trip of the same RSU.)

7. **Shunting time window:**  
   \[
   win^{dep}_{s} \le s^{start}_s \le s^{end}_s - dur_s \le win^{arr}_{s} \qquad \forall s\in S
   \tag{C7}
   \]

8. **Track capacity (only one shunting on a track at a time):**  
   For each track \\(l\\) and period \\(p\\):  
   \[
   \sum_{s\in S} u_{slp} \le cap_{lk} \qquad \forall l\in L,\, p\in P
   \tag{C8}
   \]

9. **Link binary occupancy to the continuous start/end times:**  
   \[
   u_{slp} = 1 \;\Longrightarrow\; s^{start}_s \le p \le s^{end}_s \qquad \forall s,l,p
   \tag{C9}
   \]
   (Implemented with big‑M linearisation:  
   \(p - s^{start}_s \ge -M(1-u_{slp})\) and \(s^{end}_s - p \ge -M(1-u_{slp})\).)

#### 4.2.3 Passenger‑Trip Delays  

10. **Delay limits:**  
    \[
    0 \le Δ_t \le p^{\max} (1 - z_t) \qquad \forall t\in T
    \tag{C10}
    \]

11. **If a trip is delayed, its actual departure/arrival must respect the original schedule plus the delay:**  
    \[
    a_t + Δ_t \le \text{actual departure time of }t \le a_t + Δ_t + p^{\max}
    \tag{C11}
    \]
    (In a compact model we keep only the delay variable and use it in the objective; feasibility with respect to RSU availability is already enforced by (C3).)

#### 4.2.4 Benders / Iterative Cuts  

12. **Cut generated by the infrastructure model:**  
    When the infrastructure check finds that a set \\(S' \subseteq S\\) of shunting movements cannot be performed simultaneously (because of track conflicts), a cut of the form  

    \[
    \sum_{s\in S'} π_{s} \ge 1
    \tag{C12}
    \]

    is added to the master problem. This forces at least one shunting in the infeasible set to be rejected (i.e., \\(π_s=1\\)).  

    In the **iterative heuristic** the cuts are added one‑by‑one after each feasibility test, i.e. each time a shunting is found infeasible the corresponding binary \\(π_s\\) is fixed to 1.

#### 4.2.5 Variable Domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& x_{rt}, y_{rs}, z_t, π_s, w_{rt}, u_{slp} \in \{0,1\} \\
& Δ_t, s^{start}_s, s^{end}_s \ge 0
\end{aligned}
\tag{C13}
\]

---

## 5. Remarks & Assumptions  

| # | Assumption | Reason / Comment |
|---|------------|-------------------|
| A1 | **Compatibility matrix** \\(c_{rt}\\) is known from the rolling‑stock composition model (Fioole et al., 2006). | If not available, set all entries to 1 (any RSU can serve any trip). |
| A2 | **Maximum passenger delay** \\(p^{\max}\\) is small (≤ 5 min) because the timetable already contains buffer times. | Larger values would increase the feasible region but also the passenger‑service cost. |
| A3 | **Track capacity** at each station’s shunting tracks is 1 (no parallel shunting). | Real stations often have a single dedicated shunting track; the model can be extended to >1. |
| A4 | **Big‑M** value is set to 10 000, which is larger than any possible time (e.g., horizon ≤ 1440 min). | Guarantees correct logical implication without numerical instability. |
| A5 | **Cost coefficients** are linear and additive. | In practice, some economies of scale (e.g., grouping dead‑heads) could be modelled, but linearity keeps the problem MILP. |
| A6 | **Original plan data** (which RSU was assigned to which trip) are known; they are used only in the “plan‑following” term \\(w_{rt}\\). | If not available, set \\(α=0\\) and drop term (A). |
| A7 | **Shunting start/end times** are continuous (minute resolution). | Integer time could be used; continuous simplifies the model. |
| A8 | **Iterative heuristic**: after each shunting is accepted by the infrastructure model, it is fixed (\\(y_{rs}=1\\)) and the next shunting is examined. The master problem is re‑solved with the new \\(π_s\\) cut(s). | Mimics the real interaction between rolling‑stock and infrastructure dispatchers. |
| A9 | **Exact algorithm**: the master problem (variables \\(x, y, z, Δ, π\\)) is solved, the infrastructure sub‑problem checks feasibility of the selected shunting set, and generates Benders cuts (C12) until no infeasibility remains. | Guarantees optimality but may be slower. |

---

## 6. How the Model Is Used  

1. **Initialize** the master MILP (objective + constraints C1‑C13) with no Benders cuts.  
2. **Solve** the master problem (any MILP solver).  
3. **Pass** the selected shunting set \\(\{s \mid y_{rs}=1\}\\) to the **infrastructure model** (a separate timetable‑adjustment MILP similar to Van Aken et al., 2017).  
   *If the infrastructure model reports infeasibility,* it returns a minimal infeasible subset \\(S'\\) and a cut (C12).  
4. **Add** the cut to the master problem and go to step 2 (exact approach).  
   *If the heuristic is used,* the infeasible shunting is simply fixed to \\(π_s=1\\) (i.e., rejected) and the master is re‑solved.  
5. **Iterate** until the infrastructure model declares the whole set feasible.  
6. **Output** the final values of \\(x_{rt}\\) (rolling‑stock assignment), \\(y_{rs}\\) (accepted shunting movements), \\(Δ_t\\) (delays) and \\(z_t\\) (cancellations).  

The resulting schedule respects **all railway‑infrastructure availability constraints**, **limits passenger delays**, **minimises dead‑head shunting mileage**, and **stays as close as possible to the original rolling‑stock plan** – exactly the objectives described in the paper.

Text:
**Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (Partial‑Segment Blockage)**  

---

### 1. Sets, indices and parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | Set of trains, indexed by *t* |
| **S** | Set of directed track segments, indexed by *s = (i,j)* (i → j) |
| **Rₜ** | Feasible routes for train *t* (each route *r* is an ordered list of segments) |
| **L** | Set of admissible speed levels, indexed by *ℓ* (ℓ = 1 … L, ℓ = 1 = lowest speed, L = highest) |
| **B ⊆ S** | Sub‑set of segments that are **partially blocked** |
| **Kₛ** | Maximum number of trains that can occupy segment *s* simultaneously (normally 1, >1 for double‑track) |
| **Δtₛ^ℓ** | Travel time on segment *s* when speed level ℓ is used (pre‑computed from length / speed) |
| **eₛ^ℓ** | Energy consumption (kWh) of a train traversing *s* at speed level ℓ |
| **w_d , w_e** | Positive weights for delay and energy in the objective |
| **dₜ⁰** | Planned (baseline) departure time of train *t* from its origin node |
| **aₜ⁰(i)** | Planned arrival time of train *t* at node *i* under the original schedule |
| **γₛ** | Usable fraction of segment *s* during a blockage (0 < γₛ ≤ 1; γₛ = 1 if unblocked) |
| **H** | Planning horizon (minutes) |
| **M** | Large constant (big‑M) larger than any feasible time (e.g. 10⁶) |
| **A_max** | Maximum admissible change in speed‑level index between consecutive segments (derived from acceleration limits) |
| **dᵈᵉˡˡᵢₜ(i)** | Minimum dwell time of train *t* at node *i* |
| **h_head** | Minimum headway between two trains departing the same station |

---

### 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **xₜᵣ** | binary | =1 if train *t* follows route *r* (exactly one route per train) |
| **βₜₛ** | binary | =1 if train *t* actually uses segment *s* (derived from *xₜᵣ*) |
| **αₜₛℓ** | binary | =1 if train *t* traverses segment *s* with speed level ℓ |
| **τₜᵢ** | continuous ≥0 | Actual departure time of train *t* from node *i* |
| **zₜₛ** | continuous ≥0 | Start time of train *t* on segment *s* (leaves upstream node) |
| **yₜₛ** | continuous ≥0 | End time of train *t* on segment *s* (arrives at downstream node) |
| **δₜᵢ** | continuous ≥0 | Delay of train *t* at node *i*: δₜᵢ = τₜᵢ – aₜ⁰(i) |
| **ρₜₜ′ₛ** | binary | Ordering variable: ρₜₜ′ₛ =1 ⇒ train *t* finishes *s* before train *t′* starts *s* |
| **θₜₜ′ₒ** | binary | Ordering of departures from the same origin *o* (headway) |

---

### 3. Objective function  

\[
\min\;
\underbrace{w_d\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in N}\delta_{t,i}}_{\text{total passenger delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{w_e\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{\ell\in L} e_{s}^{\ell}\,\alpha_{t,s,\ell}}_{\text{total energy consumption}}
\]

Both terms are linear in the decision variables.

---

### 4. Constraints  

#### 4.1 Route‑choice  

1. **Exactly one route per train**  
\[
\sum_{r\in R_t} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T
\]

2. **Link route choice to segment usage**  
\[
\beta_{t,s}= \sum_{r\in R_t}\mathbf{1}_{\{s\in r\}}\,x_{t,r}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S
\]

#### 4.2 Speed‑level selection  

3. **One speed level per used segment**  
\[
\sum_{\ell\in L}\alpha_{t,s,\ell}= \beta_{t,s}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S
\]

#### 4.3 Time propagation along a route  

For each segment *s = (i,j)*  

4. **Start cannot be earlier than departure from upstream node**  
\[
z_{t,s}\ge \tau_{t,i}-M\,(1-\beta_{t,s})\qquad\forall t,\;s=(i,j)
\]

5. **End equals start plus travel time of selected speed level**  
\[
y_{t,s}=z_{t,s}+ \sum_{\ell\in L}\Delta t_{s}^{\ell}\,\alpha_{t,s,\ell}\qquad\forall t,\;s
\]

6. **Down‑stream departure ≥ arrival from upstream segment**  
\[
\tau_{t,j}\ge y_{t,s}-M\,(1-\beta_{t,s})\qquad\forall t,\;s=(i,j)
\]

7. **Delay definition**  
\[
\delta_{t,i}= \tau_{t,i}-a_{t}^{0}(i)\qquad\forall t,\;i\in N
\]

#### 4.4 Blockage (partial capacity)  

8. **Total occupied time on a blocked segment cannot exceed usable fraction**  
\[
\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(y_{t,s}-z_{t,s}\bigr)\le \gamma_{s}\,H\qquad\forall s\in B
\]

9. **Pairwise ordering to avoid overlap (single‑track case, Kₛ=1)**  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&z_{t',s}\ge y_{t,s}-M\,(1-\rho_{t,t',s}) &&\forall s\in S,\;t\neq t'\\
&z_{t,s}\ge y_{t',s}-M\,\rho_{t,t',s} &&\forall s\in S,\;t\neq t'\\
&\rho_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\} &&\forall s\in S,\;t<t'
\end{aligned}
\]

If a segment has capacity *Kₛ>1* the above can be replaced by a cumulative‑capacity formulation (omitted for brevity).

#### 4.5 Speed‑profile feasibility  

10. **Bound on speed‑level change between consecutive used segments**  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{\ell}\ell\,\alpha_{t,s,\ell}-\sum_{\ell}\ell\,\alpha_{t,s',\ell}\le A_{\max}\\
&\sum_{\ell}\ell\,\alpha_{t,s',\ell}-\sum_{\ell}\ell\,\alpha_{t,s,\ell}\le A_{\max}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall t,\;s=(i,j),\;s'=(j,k),\;\beta_{t,s}=\beta_{t,s'}=1
\]

#### 4.6 Dwell‑time and headway  

11. **Minimum dwell time at stations**  

\[
\tau_{t,i}\ge y_{t,s_{\text{in}}}+d^{\text{dwell}}_{t,i}\qquad\forall t,\;i\in N,\;s_{\text{in}}=(\text{prev}(i),i)
\]

12. **Headway between two trains departing the same origin**  

\[
\tau_{t',o}\ge \tau_{t,o}+h_{\text{head}}-M\,(1-\theta_{t,t',o})\qquad\forall t\neq t',\;o\in\text{origins}
\]

#### 4.7 Logical linking of binaries  

13. **If a segment is not used, all associated variables are zero**  

\[
z_{t,s}\le M\,\beta_{t,s},\; y_{t,s}\le M\,\beta_{t,s},\;
\alpha_{t,s,\ell}\le \beta_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,s,\ell
\]

---

### 5. Complete MILP formulation  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& w_d\sum_{t,i}\delta_{t,i}+w_e\sum_{t,s,\ell}e_s^{\ell}\alpha_{t,s,\ell}\\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\sum_{r\in R_t}x_{t,r}=1 &&\forall t\\
&\beta_{t,s}= \sum_{r\in R_t}\mathbf{1}_{\{s\in r\}}x_{t,r} &&\forall t,s\\
&\sum_{\ell}\alpha_{t,s,\ell}= \beta_{t,s} &&\forall t,s\\
&z_{t,s}\ge \tau_{t,i}-M(1-\beta_{t,s}) &&\forall t,\;s=(i,j)\\
&y_{t,s}=z_{t,s}+ \sum_{\ell}\Delta t_{s}^{\ell}\alpha_{t,s,\ell} &&\forall t,s\\
&\tau_{t,j}\ge y_{t,s}-M(1-\beta_{t,s}) &&\forall t,\;s=(i,j)\\
&\delta_{t,i}= \tau_{t,i}-a_{t}^{0}(i) &&\forall t,i\\
&\sum_{t}(y_{t,s}-z_{t,s})\le \gamma_{s}H &&\forall s\in B\\
&z_{t',s}\ge y_{t,s}-M(1-\rho_{t,t',s}) &&\forall s,\;t\neq t'\\
&z_{t,s}\ge y_{t',s}-M\rho_{t,t',s} &&\forall s,\;t\neq t'\\
&\rho_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\} &&\forall s,\;t<t'\\
&\bigl|\sum_{\ell}\ell\alpha_{t,s,\ell}-\sum_{\ell}\ell\alpha_{t,s',\ell}\bigr|\le A_{\max}
&&\forall t,\;s=(i,j),\;s'=(j,k),\;\beta_{t,s}=\beta_{t,s'}=1\\
&\tau_{t,i}\ge y_{t,s_{\text{in}}}+d^{\text{dwell}}_{t,i} &&\forall t,i\\
&\tau_{t',o}\ge \tau_{t,o}+h_{\text{head}}-M(1-\theta_{t,t',o}) &&\forall t\neq t',\;o\\
&z_{t,s},y_{t,s}\le M\beta_{t,s},\;
\alpha_{t,s,\ell}\le \beta_{t,s} &&\forall t,s,\ell\\
&x_{t,r},\beta_{t,s},\alpha_{t,s,\ell},\rho_{t,t',s},\theta_{t,t',o}\in\{0,1\}\\
&\tau_{t,i},z_{t,s},y_{t,s},\delta_{t,i}\ge 0
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only non‑continuous variables are binaries, so the model belongs to the class of **Mixed‑Integer Linear Programs (MILP)**. It can be solved directly with any commercial or open‑source MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, SCIP, …).  

The formulation captures:

* **Route choice** (binary *xₜᵣ*),  
* **Departure/arrival times** (*τ, z, y*),  
* **Speed‑level selection** (*α*),  
* **Partial‑segment blockage** (usable‑fraction constraint and capacity ordering),  
* **Bidirectional conflict avoidance** (pairwise ordering *ρ*),  
* **Acceleration limits** (speed‑level change constraint),  
* **Delay and energy objectives** (weighted linear sum).  

Thus the model provides a complete, linear MILP description of the integrated train‑rescheduling and speed‑management problem under partial segment blockages.

Text:
**Variables**

* \( y_{i,s}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(i\) uses side (track) \(s\in\{0,1\}\) (0 = normal side, 1 = opposite side).  
* \( x_{i,j}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(i\) precedes train \(j\) on any segment that they share (ordering variable).  
* \( d_i\ge 0\) – departure time of train \(i\) from its origin.  
* \( a_i\ge a_i^{0}\) – arrival time of train \(i\) at its final destination (scheduled arrival \(a_i^{0}\)).  
* \( t_{i,k}\ge 0\) – travel time of train \(i\) on segment \(k\in K\).  
* \( v_{i,k,\ell}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(i\) runs on segment \(k\) with speed level \(\ell\in L\) (different speed profiles).  

**Parameters**

* \(a_i^{0}\) – scheduled arrival time (without disruption).  
* \(\underline{d}_i,\ \overline d_i\) – minimum / maximum dwell time at the terminal.  
* \(L_k\) – physical length of segment \(k\).  
* \(s_{\ell}\) – speed (km h\(^{-1}\)) associated with level \(\ell\).  
* \(e_{k,\ell}\) – energy consumption (kWh) when segment \(k\) is traversed with level \(\ell\).  
* \(\beta_{s,k}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if side \(s\) on segment \(k\) is blocked during the disruption (otherwise 0).  
* \(M\) – a sufficiently large constant (Big‑M).  
* \(w_{\text{delay}},w_{\text{energy}}\) – weights in the objective.  

**Objective**

\[
\min\;
\underbrace{w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(a_i-a_i^{0}\bigr)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{\ell\in L}
e_{k,\ell}\,v_{i,k,\ell}}_{\text{total energy consumption}} .
\]

**Constraints**

1. **Side‑choice (routing)**
   \[
   \sum_{s\in S} y_{i,s}=1 \qquad\forall i\in I .
   \]

2. **Flow conservation (departure → travel → arrival)**
   \[
   d_i+\sum_{k\in K} t_{i,k}+ \underline d_i \;=\; a_i \qquad\forall i\in I .
   \]

3. **Travel time – speed‑profile linkage**
   \[
   t_{i,k}= \sum_{\ell\in L}\frac{L_k}{s_{\ell}}\;v_{i,k,\ell} \qquad\forall i\in I,\;k\in K .
   \]

4. **Exactly one speed level per train‑segment**
   \[
   \sum_{\ell\in L} v_{i,k,\ell}=1 \qquad\forall i\in I,\;k\in K .
   \]

5. **Blocked side prohibition**
   \[
   y_{i,s}\le 1-\beta_{s,k}\qquad\forall i\in I,\;s\in S,\;k\in K .
   \]

6. **Dwell‑time limits**
   \[
   \underline d_i\le a_i-d_i-\sum_{k\in K} t_{i,k}\le \overline d_i \qquad\forall i\in I .
   \]

7. **Capacity (no two trains on the same segment simultaneously).**  
   Let the cumulative start instant of train \(i\) on segment \(k\) be  
   \[
   \sigma_{i,k}=d_i+\sum_{q\in K,\;q<k} t_{i,q}.
   \]
   Then for every unordered pair \((i,j)\) and every segment \(k\):
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
   \sigma_{i,k}+t_{i,k}&\le \sigma_{j,k}+M\,(1-x_{i,j}) ,\\
   \sigma_{j,k}+t_{j,k}&\le \sigma_{i,k}+M\,x_{i,j} ,\\
   x_{i,j}+x_{j,i}&=1 \qquad (i\neq j).
   \end{aligned}
   \]

8. **Variable domains**
   \[
   y_{i,s},\,x_{i,j},\,v_{i,k,\ell}\in\{0,1\},
   \qquad
   d_i\ge0,\; a_i\ge a_i^{0},\; t_{i,k}\ge0 .
   \]

---

### Assumptions (explicit)

* Each train uses a single side for the whole journey (the model can be extended with segment‑specific side variables if needed).  
* Dwell time is modeled as a single term at the final station; additional intermediate dwell constraints can be added analogously.  
* Energy consumption is linear in the binary speed‑profile variables; more detailed nonlinear energy models would require linearisation.  
* The big‑M constant is chosen larger than the maximum possible time difference between any two trains on any segment.  

The set of equations above constitutes a complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment‑blockage disruptions.

**Passenger‑oriented Real‑time Train‑Scheduling MILP (MPC‑based)**  
The formulation below follows the description in the prompt and adds the missing pieces (sets, parameters, decision variables, objective, and constraints).  All symbols are defined in the tables that follow.  Wherever information is not given in the text, a *reasonable assumption* is explicitly marked.

---

## 1. Sets, Indices and Time Discretisation  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \( \mathcal{L} \) | Set of rail lines (for a single‑line case \( |\mathcal{L}|=1\)). |
| \( \mathcal{S} =\{1,\dots,S\} \) | Ordered set of stations on a line (index \(s\)). |
| \( \mathcal{T} =\{1,\dots,T\} \) | Set of discrete **prediction‑horizon** time steps (MPC horizon).  Length of each step = \(\Delta t\) minutes (assumed constant). |
| \( \mathcal{K} =\{1,\dots,K\} \) | Set of admissible train‑type (composition) options (e.g., 2‑car, 4‑car, 6‑car). |
| \( \mathcal{P} =\{1,\dots,P\} \) | Set of demand scenarios (used for robustness – optional, can be set to 1). |
| \( \mathcal{R} =\{1,\dots,R\} \) | Set of rolling‑stock units (individual trainsets) available for circulation. |

*Assumption 1*: The horizon is divided into equal‑length intervals so that passenger demand can be treated as piece‑wise constant on each interval \(\tau\in\mathcal{T}\).

---

## 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical Unit / Value |
|--------|-------------|----------------------|
| \(C_k\) | Capacity (seats) of train type \(k\) (passengers per train). | e.g. 300, 600, 900 |
| \(c_k^{\text{op}}\) | Operating cost per departure of type \(k\) (fuel/energy + crew). | €/departure |
| \(c_k^{\text{fix}}\) | Fixed cost for using a rolling‑stock unit of type \(k\) (maintenance, depreciation). | €/hour |
| \(d_{s,s'}\) | Running time (minutes) from station \(s\) to \(s'\) (adjacent stations). | from timetable or track data |
| \(h_{\min},h_{\max}\) | Minimum / maximum admissible headway between consecutive departures (minutes). | 2 – 10 |
| \(w_{s,\tau}\) | Expected passenger arrival rate at station \(s\) during interval \(\tau\) (passengers/min). *Assumption 2*: Obtained from historical data and forecast (piece‑wise constant). |
| \(B_{s,\tau}\) | Number of passengers already waiting at the beginning of interval \(\tau\) (state variable fed to MPC). |
| \(M\) | A large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints (e.g., \(M=10^5\)). |
| \(\alpha\) | Weight for passenger waiting time in the objective (dimensionless). |
| \(\beta\) | Weight for timetable deviation (e.g., from a nominal timetable) (dimensionless). |
| \(\gamma\) | Weight for energy/operating cost (dimensionless). |
| \( \overline{N}_r\) | Maximum number of trips a rolling‑stock unit \(r\) can perform within the horizon (due to crew shift, maintenance). |
| \( \theta_{s}^{\text{dwell}}\) | Minimum dwell time at station \(s\) (seconds). |
| \( \theta_{s}^{\text{max}}\) | Maximum allowed dwell time at station \(s\) (seconds). |
| \( \delta_{s}^{\text{stop}}\in\{0,1\}\) | Binary indicating whether station \(s\) may be skipped by any train (stop‑skipping option). *Assumption 3*: All stations are stop‑allowed (\(\delta_s^{\text{stop}}=1\)). |

---

## 3. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(x_{r,k,\tau} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if rolling‑stock unit \(r\) starts a **departure** of train type \(k\) at the first station at the beginning of interval \(\tau\). |
| \(y_{r,\tau} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if rolling‑stock unit \(r\) is **in service** (i.e., has left the depot) during interval \(\tau\). |
| \(a_{s,\tau} \ge 0\) | Continuous | **Arrival time** (in minutes from horizon start) of the *next* train at station \(s\) during interval \(\tau\). |
| \(d_{s,\tau} \ge 0\) | Continuous | **Departure time** of the *next* train from station \(s\) during interval \(\tau\). |
| \(h_{\tau} \ge 0\) | Continuous | Headway (time between two consecutive departures from the first station) for interval \(\tau\). |
| \(p_{s,\tau} \ge 0\) | Continuous | Number of **passengers on board** when the train departs station \(s\) in interval \(\tau\). |
| \(w_{s,\tau}^{\text{wait}} \ge 0\) | Continuous | Number of passengers **still waiting** at station \(s\) at the end of interval \(\tau\). |
| \(z_{s,\tau} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if a train **stops** at station \(s\) during interval \(\tau\) (stop‑skipping decision). |
| \(u_{r,\tau} \in \{0,1\}\) | Binary | 1 if rolling‑stock unit \(r\) **returns to depot** (ends service) at the end of interval \(\tau\). |

*Assumption 4*: Only one departure can be scheduled per interval per line (the model can be easily extended to multiple parallel departures by indexing with a departure index).  

*Assumption 5*: The integer variables concerning rolling‑stock circulation (\(x_{r,k,\tau}, y_{r,\tau}, u_{r,\tau}\)) are the ones that will be supplied by the LSTM‑based predictor after the presolve step; the remaining variables are continuous and solved by a linear program.

---

## 4. Model Equations  

### 4.1. Headway and Departure‑time coupling  

\[
\begin{aligned}
h_{\tau} &= \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \frac{x_{r,k,\tau}}{\Delta t} \qquad &&\text{(binary departure ⇒ headway contribution)}\\
h_{\min} \le h_{\tau} \le h_{\max} &&&&\forall \tau\in\mathcal{T}
\end{aligned}
\]

*(If multiple departures per interval are allowed, replace the RHS by the number of departures in \(\tau\).)*  

### 4.2. Train‑type selection (linking \(x\) and train capacity)  

\[
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} x_{r,k,\tau} \le y_{r,\tau} \qquad \forall r,\tau
\]

If a unit is in service (\(y_{r,\tau}=1\)), it may start at most one departure of a chosen type.

### 4.3. Rolling‑stock circulation limits  

\[
\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} x_{r,k,\tau} \le \overline{N}_r \qquad \forall r,k
\]

\[
y_{r,\tau+1}= y_{r,\tau}+x_{r,k,\tau} - u_{r,\tau} \qquad \forall r,\tau\in\mathcal{T}\setminus\{T\}
\]

\(u_{r,\tau}\) forces the unit to leave service when needed.

### 4.4. Time‑propagation along the line  

For each station \(s=1,\dots,S\) (except the first) and each interval \(\tau\):

\[
a_{s,\tau}= d_{s-1,\tau}+ d_{s-1,s} \qquad \forall s>1,\tau
\]

\[
d_{s,\tau}= a_{s,\tau}+ \theta_{s}^{\text{dwell}}\,z_{s,\tau} \qquad \forall s,\tau
\]

The dwell time is applied only if the train stops (\(z_{s,\tau}=1\)).  

### 4.5. Capacity and passenger‑flow balance  

Boarding at station \(s\) during interval \(\tau\):

\[
\text{Board}_{s,\tau}= \min\Big\{ C_{k}\,z_{s,\tau} - p_{s-1,\tau},\; w_{s,\tau}+B_{s,\tau}\Big\}
\]

Because the model is linear, we linearise the min‑operator with a big‑M formulation:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Board}_{s,\tau} &\le C_{k}\,z_{s,\tau} - p_{s-1,\tau} \\
\text{Board}_{s,\tau} &\le w_{s,\tau}+B_{s,\tau} \\
\text{Board}_{s,\tau} &\ge 0
\end{aligned}
\]

Update on‑board passengers:

\[
p_{s,\tau}= p_{s-1,\tau}+ \text{Board}_{s,\tau} - \text{Alight}_{s,\tau}
\]

Alighting is assumed to be a known proportion of the on‑board load; for linearity we use a fixed fraction \(\lambda_{s}\) (e.g., 0.2) :

\[
\text{Alight}_{s,\tau}= \lambda_{s}\,p_{s-1,\tau}
\]

Waiting‑passenger balance at each station:

\[
w_{s,\tau+1}= w_{s,\tau}+ w_{s,\tau}^{\text{arr}} - \text{Board}_{s,\tau}
\]

where \(w_{s,\tau}^{\text{arr}} = w_{s,\tau}\,\Delta t\) is the number of new arrivals during the interval (derived from the demand rate \(w_{s,\tau}\)).  

### 4.6. Service‑level (waiting‑time) constraints  

A service‑level target can be imposed, e.g.:

\[
w_{s,\tau}^{\text{wait}} \le \overline{W}_{s}\qquad \forall s,\tau
\]

where \(\overline{W}_{s}\) is a maximum allowable number of waiting passengers (or equivalently a maximum waiting time).

### 4.7. Stop‑skipping feasibility  

\[
z_{s,\tau} \le \delta_{s}^{\text{stop}} \qquad \forall s,\tau
\]

If \(\delta_{s}^{\text{stop}}=0\) the station cannot be served in that interval.

---

## 5. Objective Function  

The MPC‑based MILP minimizes a weighted sum of three key performance indicators:

1. **Passenger waiting time** (total number of passengers left waiting at the end of each interval).  
2. **Timetable deviation** (difference between the generated departure times and a nominal timetable \(d^{\text{nom}}_{s,\tau}\)).  
3. **Operating cost** (cost of dispatching trains of different compositions and rolling‑stock usage).  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \alpha \underbrace{\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} w_{s,\tau}^{\text{wait}}}_{\text{Passenger waiting}} \\
& + \beta \underbrace{\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} \bigl| d_{s,\tau}- d^{\text{nom}}_{s,\tau}\bigr|}_{\text{Timetable deviation}} \\
& + \gamma \underbrace{\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}}\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} \bigl(c_k^{\text{op}}+c_k^{\text{fix}}\bigr) x_{r,k,\tau}}_{\text{Operating cost}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

The absolute value in the second term can be linearised with the usual pair of auxiliary variables:

\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{s,\tau}- d^{\text{nom}}_{s,\tau} &\le \zeta_{s,\tau} \\
-(d_{s,\tau}- d^{\text{nom}}_{s,\tau}) &\le \zeta_{s,\tau} \\
\zeta_{s,\tau} &\ge 0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

The objective is therefore purely linear once \(\zeta_{s,\tau}\) are introduced.

---

## 6. Complete MILP Statement  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{min } & \; \alpha\sum_{s,\tau} w_{s,\tau}^{\text{wait}} 
               + \beta\sum_{s,\tau}\zeta_{s,\tau}
               + \gamma\sum_{r,k,\tau} (c_k^{\text{op}}+c_k^{\text{fix}})x_{r,k,\tau} \\
\text{s.t. } &
   \text{(4.1)–(4.7) constraints listed above} \\
   & x_{r,k,\tau},y_{r,\tau},z_{s,\tau},u_{r,\tau}\in\{0,1\} \\
   & a_{s,\tau},d_{s,\tau},h_{\tau},p_{s,\tau},w_{s,\tau}^{\text{wait}},\zeta_{s,\tau}\ge 0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear (big‑M linearisation is used for logical relations).  

---

## 7. MPC Implementation  

At each control step \(t\) (real time):

1. **State update** – obtain the current waiting‑passenger vector \(B_{s,\tau}\) and the set of rolling‑stock units that are already in service (\(y_{r,\tau}\)).  
2. **Demand forecast** – use historical data to build the piece‑wise‑constant demand rates \(w_{s,\tau}\) for the next \(T\) intervals.  
3. **Presolve** – apply the four presolve techniques (e.g., eliminate train‑type options that cannot satisfy the demand, prune rolling‑stock units that are already scheduled for return, fix stop‑skipping decisions for stations with mandatory service, bound headways).  
4. **Learning step** – an LSTM network, trained offline on solved instances, predicts the binary variables \((x_{r,k,\tau}, y_{r,\tau})\) that survive the presolve reduction.  
5. **Optimization step** – with the predicted binary variables fixed, solve the remaining linear program (continuous variables only) to obtain the exact timetable \((a_{s,\tau},d_{s,\tau})\) and passenger flows.  
6. **Apply first‑step control** – implement the departure decision for the current interval; shift the horizon forward and repeat.

Because the integer part is supplied by the neural network, the online MILP reduces to a **linear program**, guaranteeing real‑time feasibility while still respecting all hard constraints.

---

## 8. Remarks & Extensions  

* **Robustness** – Scenario index \(p\in\mathcal{P}\) can be added to the demand parameters \(w_{s,\tau}^p\) and the objective can be a worst‑case or expected value over scenarios.  
* **Energy consumption** – If a more detailed energy model is desired, a linear approximation of energy as a function of speed profile (derived from running times \(d_{s,s'}\)) can be added with extra continuous variables.  
* **Multiple lines / junctions** – The index set \(\mathcal{L}\) can be introduced; coupling constraints would then enforce track‑capacity at shared sections.  
* **Rolling‑stock circulation** – The model already tracks each unit; a separate “circulation cost” (e.g., dead‑head trips to depot) can be added linearly.

---

**The formulation above is a complete, linear (MILP) model that captures**  

* time‑varying passenger demand,  
* flexible train composition (capacity \(C_k\)),  
* rolling‑stock circulation (binary variables \(x_{r,k,\tau}, y_{r,\tau}, u_{r,\tau}\)),  
* headway and dwell‑time constraints,  
* passenger‑waiting‑time service level, and  
* an objective that balances passenger satisfaction and operating cost.  

All missing data have been supplied by reasonable assumptions, which are clearly indicated. This model can be embedded directly into the MPC loop described in Section 7 and solved efficiently in real time when the integer part is supplied by a learning‑based predictor.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling & Speed‑Management MILP (Partial‑Segment Blockage)**  

The model below captures every element described in the prompt: binary route‑choice, arrival/departure times, speed‑level decisions on each traversed segment, a weighted objective that balances total delay and energy consumption, and all necessary feasibility, blockage‑avoidance and bidirectional‑conflict constraints.  All constraints are linear; the only non‑continuous variables are binaries, so the formulation is a **mixed‑integer linear program (MILP)** ready for CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP, …  

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(T=\{1,\dots ,|T|\}\) | Trains (indexed by \(t\)). |
| \(S=\{1,\dots ,|S|\}\) | Discrete speed levels (e.g. low, medium, high). |
| \(E\subseteq N\times N\) | Directed track **segments** (arcs) \((i,j)\) from node \(i\) to node \(j\). |
| \(R_t\) | Feasible **routes** for train \(t\); a route \(r\in R_t\) is an ordered list of arcs. |
| \(B\subseteq E\) | Set of arcs belonging to the **partially blocked segment**. |
| \(C\subseteq E\) | Set of arcs that are **bidirectional** (two opposite arcs share the same physical track). |

For each arc \((i,j)\in E\) we know:

* \(L_{ij}\) – length (km).  
* \(d_{ij}^s\) – travel time (h) when speed level \(s\) is used (pre‑computed from \(L_{ij}\) and speed \(v_s\)).  
* \(e_{ij}^s\) – energy consumption (kWh) for speed level \(s\).  

---

### 2. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,r}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) follows route \(r\in R_t\). |
| \(z_{t,ij}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses arc \((i,j)\) (any speed). |
| \(y_{t,ij}^s\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses arc \((i,j)\) **with speed level** \(s\). |
| \(a_{t,i}\) | \(\ge0\) | Arrival time of train \(t\) at node \(i\). |
| \(d_{t,i}\) | \(\ge0\) | Departure time of train \(t\) from node \(i\). |
| \(\theta_{t,ij}\) | \(\ge0\) | Travel time of train \(t\) on arc \((i,j)\) (selected from \(d_{ij}^s\)). |
| \(\varepsilon_{t,ij}\) | \(\ge0\) | Energy spent by train \(t\) on arc \((i,j)\) (selected from \(e_{ij}^s\)). |
| \(\Delta_t\) | \(\ge0\) | Total delay of train \(t\) w.r.t. its scheduled arrival at its destination. |
| \(E_t\) | \(\ge0\) | Total energy consumption of train \(t\). |
| \(w_{tt',ij}\) | binary | Ordering on a **blocked** arc \((i,j)\in B\): 1 if train \(t\) passes before train \(t'\). |
| \(u_{tt',ij}\) | binary | Ordering on a **bidirectional** arc \((i,j)\in C\): 1 if train \(t\) passes before train \(t'\). |

---

### 3. Parameters  

* \(\alpha>0\) – weight of total delay in the objective.  
* \(\beta>0\) – weight of total energy in the objective.  
* \(\bar a_{t}^{\text{dest}}\) – scheduled (baseline) arrival time of train \(t\) at its destination node.  
* \(M\) – a sufficiently large constant (e.g. horizon length, 24 h).  

---

### 4. Objective  

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle 
\min\; \alpha\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_t \;+\; \beta\sum_{t\in T}E_t }
\]

The planner can tune \(\alpha,\beta\) to emphasise punctuality or energy efficiency.

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Route choice & speed‑level linking  

1. **Exactly one route per train**  
\[
\sum_{r\in R_t} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T \tag{R1}
\]

2. **Arc usage from route choice**  
\[
z_{t,ij}= \sum_{r\in R_t:\;(i,j)\in r} x_{t,r}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in E \tag{R2}
\]

3. **Exactly one speed level on a used arc**  
\[
\sum_{s\in S} y_{t,ij}^s = z_{t,ij}
\qquad\forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in E \tag{R3}
\]

#### 5.2 Travel‑time & energy selection  

4. **Travel‑time definition**  
\[
\theta_{t,ij}= \sum_{s\in S} d_{ij}^s\, y_{t,ij}^s
\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j) \tag{T1}
\]

5. **Energy definition**  
\[
\varepsilon_{t,ij}= \sum_{s\in S} e_{ij}^s\, y_{t,ij}^s
\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j) \tag{T2}
\]

#### 5.3 Temporal continuity along a route  

6. **Flow of time** (departure from tail + travel = arrival at head)  
\[
a_{t,j} \ge d_{t,i} + \theta_{t,ij} - M\,(1-z_{t,ij})
\qquad\forall t,\;(i,j)\in E \tag{T3}
\]

7. **Minimum dwell at stations** (if node \(i\) is a station, \(\tau_i^{\min}\) is the required stop)  
\[
d_{t,i} \ge a_{t,i} + \tau_i^{\min}\,z_{t,ij}
\qquad\forall t,\;i\in N_{\text{st}},\;(i,j)\in E \tag{T4}
\]

#### 5.4 Delay and energy aggregation  

8. **Delay at destination**  
\[
\Delta_t \ge a_{t,\text{dest}(t)} - \bar a_{t}^{\text{dest}}
\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{D1}
\]

9. **Total energy per train**  
\[
E_t = \sum_{(i,j)\in E}\varepsilon_{t,ij}
\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{E1}
\]

#### 5.5 Partial‑segment blockage (no overlap)  

For every blocked arc \((i,j)\in B\) and every unordered pair of trains \(t<t'\):

10. **Ordering on blocked arc**  
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{t',i} &\ge d_{t,i} + \theta_{t,ij} - M\,(1-w_{tt',ij})\\
a_{t,i}   &\ge d_{t',i} + \theta_{t',ij} - M\,w_{tt',ij}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall (i,j)\in B,\; t<t' \tag{B1}
\]

The constraints are active only when both trains actually use the arc; this is enforced by  

\[
w_{tt',ij}\le z_{t,ij},\qquad w_{tt',ij}\le 1- z_{t',ij}
\qquad\forall (i,j)\in B,\; t<t' \tag{B2}
\]

(If a train does not traverse the blocked arc, the corresponding \(z\) is 0 and the big‑M term relaxes the constraint.)

#### 5.6 Bidirectional conflict (head‑on avoidance)  

For each pair of opposite arcs \((i,j)\) and \((j,i)\) belonging to the same physical track (\((i,j)\in C\)) and each unordered pair of trains \(t<t'\):

11. **Ordering on bidirectional track**  
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{t',j} &\ge d_{t,i} + \theta_{t,ij} - M\,(1-u_{tt',ij})\\
a_{t,i}   &\ge d_{t',j} + \theta_{t',ji} - M\,u_{tt',ij}
\end{aligned}
\qquad\forall (i,j)\in C,\; t<t' \tag{H1}
\]

Again, the ordering variable is only relevant when both directed arcs are used:

\[
u_{tt',ij}\le z_{t,ij},\qquad u_{tt',ij}\le 1- z_{t',ij}
\qquad\forall (i,j)\in C,\; t<t' \tag{H2}
\]

#### 5.7 Logical consistency  

12. **Departure cannot precede arrival**  
\[
d_{t,i}\ge a_{t,i}\qquad\forall t,\;i\in N \tag{L1}
\]

13. **Variable domains**  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,r},\,z_{t,ij},\,y_{t,ij}^s,\,w_{tt',ij},\,u_{tt',ij}\in\{0,1\}\\
&a_{t,i},\,d_{t,i},\,\theta_{t,ij},\,\varepsilon_{t,ij},\,\Delta_t,\,E_t\ge 0
\end{aligned}
\tag{V}
\]

---

### 6. Full MILP Statement  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \alpha\sum_{t\in T}\Delta_t \;+\; \beta\sum_{t\in T}E_t \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(R1)–(R3)} &&\text{route choice \& speed‑level linking}\\
&\text{(T1)–(T4)} &&\text{travel‑time, energy, and temporal flow}\\
&\text{(D1)} &&\text{delay definition}\\
&\text{(E1)} &&\text{energy aggregation}\\
&\text{(B1)–(B2)} &&\text{no‑overlap on blocked arcs}\\
&\text{(H1)–(H2)} &&\text{head‑on avoidance on bidirectional tracks}\\
&\text{(L1)} &&\text{basic time ordering}\\
&\text{(V)} &&\text{binary / non‑negative domains.}
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only non‑continuous variables are binaries that encode route selection, speed‑level choice, and the ordering decisions required for conflict resolution.  Consequently the formulation is a **mixed‑integer linear program**.

---

### 7. How to Use the Model  

1. **Data preparation** – compute \(d_{ij}^s\) and \(e_{ij}^s\) for every arc and speed level; list all feasible routes \(R_t\) for each train; provide the baseline arrival times \(\bar a_{t}^{\text{dest}}\) and minimum dwell times \(\tau_i^{\min}\).  
2. **Set weights** – choose \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) to reflect the operator’s trade‑off between punctuality and energy consumption.  
3. **Solve** – feed the MILP to any modern MILP solver.  The optimal solution yields:  

   * the selected route for each train (\(x_{t,r}=1\)),  
   * the exact arrival/departure schedule (\(a_{t,i},d_{t,i}\)),  
   * the speed level on each traversed segment (\(y_{t,ij}^s=1\)),  
   * the total delay \(\Delta_t\) and energy \(E_t\).  

4. **Interpret ordering variables** – \(w_{tt',ij}\) tells which train should be given priority on a blocked segment, while \(u_{tt',ij}\) resolves head‑on conflicts on bidirectional tracks, providing concrete dispatching rules for the controller.

---

**The model above is a complete, linear MILP that simultaneously reschedules trains, selects executable speed profiles, respects partial‑segment blockages, resolves bidirectional conflicts, and minimises a weighted sum of delay and energy consumption.**
