Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockages**

---

### 1. Sets, indices and parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** = {1,…,|T|} | set of trains (index *i*) |
| **S** = {1,…,|S|} | set of track segments (index *s*) |
| **K** = {1,…,K} | set of discrete speed levels (index *k*) |
| **τ** = {1,…,τmax} | set of time‑interval indices for a segment (index *τ*) |
| **B** ⊆ S | segments that are **blocked** during a known window \([t^{blk}_{start},t^{blk}_{end}]\) |
| **O** ⊆ S | segments that are the **opposite track** (available only when the original is blocked) |
| **N_i** | ordered list of segments of the **original route** of train *i* |
| **N_i^{opp}** | ordered list of segments of the **detour route** (opposite track) of train *i* |
| **d_s** | length of segment *s* (km) |
| **v_k** | speed associated with level *k* (km h⁻¹) |
| **e_k** | energy coefficient of level *k* (kWh per km) |
| **Δt** | length of a discretisation interval (minutes) |
| **v_max , v_min** | global speed limits (km h⁻¹) |
| **a_max , a_min** | max acceleration / deceleration (km h⁻²) |
| **h** | safety headway (minutes) |
| **\underline w_i** | minimum dwell time of train *i* at any station (minutes) |
| **α_i** | weight of train *i* in the delay part of the objective |
| **β** | weight of the energy‑consumption part of the objective |
| **\hat t_i^{arr}(s)** | nominal (undelayed) arrival time of train *i* at the upstream end of segment *s* |
| **M** | big‑M constant (≥ any feasible time, e.g. 10⁶) |

---

### 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **x_i ∈ {0,1}** | binary | route choice of train *i*: 0 = original route, 1 = opposite‑track detour |
| **y_{i,s,τ,k} ∈ {0,1}** | binary | speed‑level selection: 1 if train *i* traverses segment *s* in interval *τ* with speed level *k* |
| **u_{i,s,τ} ∈ {0,1}** | binary | occupancy of train *i* on segment *s* during interval *τ* ( \(u_{i,s,τ}=∑_k y_{i,s,τ,k}\) ) |
| **a_{i,s} ≥ 0** | continuous | arrival time of train *i* at the upstream end of segment *s* |
| **d_{i,s} ≥ 0** | continuous | departure time of train *i* from the downstream end of segment *s* |
| **z_{i,j,s} ∈ {0,1}** | binary | ordering on shared segment *s*: 1 if train *i* passes *s* before train *j* |
| **E ≥ 0** | continuous | total energy consumption (kWh) |

---

### 3. Model constraints  

#### 3.1. Exactly one speed level per occupied interval  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} y_{i,s,τ,k}=u_{i,s,τ}\qquad\forall i\in T,\;s\in S,\;τ\in τ .
\tag{1}
\]

\[
\sum_{k\in K} y_{i,s,τ,k}\le 1\qquad\forall i,s,τ .
\tag{2}
\]

#### 3.2. Travel time on a segment  

\[
d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}=Δt\sum_{τ\in τ} u_{i,s,τ}\qquad\forall i,s .
\tag{3}
\]

#### 3.3. Speed‑limit and acceleration (piece‑wise linear)  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} v_k\,y_{i,s,τ,k} - \sum_{k\in K} v_k\,y_{i,s,τ-1,k}
\le a_{\max}Δt\qquad\forall i,s,τ>1 .
\tag{4}
\]

\[
\sum_{k\in K} v_k\,y_{i,s,τ-1,k} - \sum_{k\in K} v_k\,y_{i,s,τ,k}
\le |a_{\min}|Δt\qquad\forall i,s,τ>1 .
\tag{5}
\]

(If a simpler model is sufficient, constraints (4)–(5) can be omitted and only (3) together with the bounds (6) below are kept.)

\[
Δt\sum_{τ}u_{i,s,τ}\ge \frac{d_s}{v_{\max}},\qquad
Δt\sum_{τ}u_{i,s,τ}\le \frac{d_s}{v_{\min}}
\qquad\forall i,s .
\tag{6}
\]

#### 3.4. Route‑choice and blockage window  

For every blocked segment \(b\in B\):

\[
a_{i,b}\ge t^{blk}_{start}-M(1-x_i),\qquad
a_{i,b}\le t^{blk}_{end}+Mx_i\qquad\forall i .
\tag{7}
\]

Thus, if \(x_i=0\) the train may enter the blocked segment only **outside** the disruption window; if \(x_i=1\) it must use the opposite‑track route.

#### 3.5. Temporal flow (continuity) on the selected route  

For any consecutive pair \((s,s')\) on the **original** route \(N_i\):

\[
a_{i,s'}\ge d_{i,s}+ \underline w_i - Mx_i,\qquad
a_{i,s'}\le d_{i,s}+ \underline w_i + Mx_i .
\tag{8a}
\]

For any consecutive pair on the **detour** route \(N_i^{opp}\):

\[
a_{i,s'}\ge d_{i,s}+ \underline w_i - M(1-x_i),\qquad
a_{i,s'}\le d_{i,s}+ \underline w_i + M(1-x_i) .
\tag{8b}
\]

Only the constraints belonging to the chosen route are active.

#### 3.6. Safety headway on a shared segment  

For every unordered pair \((i,j)\) that may use the same segment *s*:

\[
a_{j,s}\ge d_{i,s}+h-M(1-z_{i,j,s}),\qquad
a_{i,s}\ge d_{j,s}+h-Mz_{i,j,s},
\tag{9}
\]

\[
z_{i,j,s}+z_{j,i,s}=1\qquad\forall i<j,\;s\text{ shared}.
\tag{10}
\]

#### 3.7. Capacity of the opposite track (single‑track)  

\[
\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{k\in K} y_{i,s,τ,k}\le 1\qquad\forall s\in O,\;τ\in τ .
\tag{11}
\]

(If the original track is also single‑track when not blocked, the same constraint is added for \(s\notin B\).)

#### 3.8. Energy consumption  

\[
E=\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{τ\in τ}\sum_{k\in K}
e_k\,d_s\,y_{i,s,τ,k}.
\tag{12}
\]

#### 3.9. Delay definition (used in the objective)  

Let \(s_i^{last}\) be the last segment of train *i* (according to the selected route).  

\[
\text{delay}_i = a_{i,s_i^{last}}-\hat t_i^{arr}(s_i^{last})\qquad\forall i .
\tag{13}
\]

---

### 4. Objective function  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i\in T}\alpha_i\,
\bigl(a_{i,s_i^{last}}-\hat t_i^{arr}(s_i^{last})\bigr)}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\beta\,E}_{\text{total energy cost}}
}
\tag{14}
\]

Both terms are linear in the decision variables.

---

### 5. Complete MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \sum_{i\in T}\alpha_i\bigl(a_{i,s_i^{last}}-\hat t_i^{arr}(s_i^{last})\bigr)
      +\beta\sum_{i,s,τ,k} e_k d_s\,y_{i,s,τ,k} \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(1)–(13)   (all constraints listed above)} \\[2pt]
& x_i\in\{0,1\},\; y_{i,s,τ,k}\in\{0,1\},\; u_{i,s,τ}\in\{0,1\},\\
& z_{i,j,s}\in\{0,1\},\; a_{i,s}\ge0,\; d_{i,s}\ge0,\; E\ge0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 6. Remarks & modelling assumptions  

* **Discretisation** – Δt (e.g., 1 min) and the number of speed levels K (e.g., 3–5) determine model size; the formulation remains linear for any choice.  
* **Big‑M** – M must be larger than the planning horizon (e.g., 24 h expressed in minutes). Tightening M improves solver performance.  
* **Energy linearisation** – Energy is approximated by a constant coefficient per speed level; this yields a linear term while still capturing the trade‑off between fast (high‑energy) and slow (low‑energy) operation.  
* **Bidirectional conflict** – The ordering variables \(z_{i,j,s}\) together with the headway constraint (9) guarantee a conflict‑free timetable on the shared track, even when trains travel in opposite directions on the opposite track.  
* **Scalability** – The model can be solved directly with commercial MILP solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) for medium‑size instances; for larger instances a decomposition (IP master + train‑plan sub‑problems) can be applied, as described in the source paper.  

---

**The formulation above provides a complete, linear MILP that simultaneously decides (i) which route each train should take around a blocked segment, (ii) the order of trains on the shared track, (iii) the exact arrival/departure times, and (iv) the discrete speed level for every train‑segment‑interval, while minimising a weighted sum of total passenger delay and energy consumption and respecting all operational constraints of high‑speed railway operations.**

Text:
**Variables**

- \(x_{i,r}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(i\in I\) uses feasible route \(r\in R_i\); each train chooses exactly one route.  
- \(y_{i,s,t}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(i\) occupies track segment \(s\in S\) during discrete time period \(t\in T\).  
- \(v_{i,s,t}\ge 0\) – speed of train \(i\) on segment \(s\) at time \(t\) (km / min).  
- \(z_{i,s,t}\ge 0\) – linearisation of \(v_{i,s,t}^{2}\) (used for energy).  
- \(a_i\ge 0\) – arrival time of train \(i\) at its terminal station.  
- \(d_i\ge 0\) – departure time from the terminal ( \(d_i=a_i+\text{dwell}\) ).  
- \(e_i\ge 0\) – total energy consumption of train \(i\).

**Parameters**

- \(\hat a_i\) – scheduled arrival time of train \(i\).  
- \(\ell_s\) – length of segment \(s\) (km).  
- \(v^{\min},\,v^{\max}\) – lower/upper speed limits (km / min).  
- \(\text{dwell}\) – required dwell time at the terminal (minutes).  
- \(\mathcal B_s\subseteq T\) – set of time periods in which segment \(s\) is blocked (cannot be occupied).  
- \(\text{cap}_s\) – capacity of segment \(s\) (1 for a single‑track line).  
- \(\alpha\) – energy coefficient (kWh per \((\text{km/min})^{2}\)·min).  
- \(w^{\text{delay}}, w^{\text{energy}}\) – weights in the objective.

**Objective**

\[
\min\;
w^{\text{delay}}\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(a_i-\hat a_i\bigr)
\;+\;
w^{\text{energy}}\sum_{i\in I} e_i
\tag{OBJ}
\]

**Constraints**

1. **Route choice** (one route per train)  
   \[
   \sum_{r\in R_i} x_{i,r}=1 \qquad\forall i\in I
   \tag{C1}
   \]

2. **Occupancy only on the selected route**  
   \[
   y_{i,s,t}\le \Bigl(\sum_{r\in R_i:\,s\in r} x_{i,r}\Bigr) \qquad\forall i\in I,\;s\in S,\;t\in T
   \tag{C2}
   \]

3. **Blockage windows**  
   \[
   y_{i,s,t}=0 \qquad\forall i\in I,\;s\in S,\;t\in\mathcal B_s
   \tag{C3}
   \]

4. **Capacity / conflict avoidance** (single‑track)  
   \[
   \sum_{i\in I} y_{i,s,t}\le \text{cap}_s \qquad\forall s\in S,\;t\in T
   \tag{C4}
   \]

5. **One segment at a time per train**  
   \[
   \sum_{s\in S} y_{i,s,t}\le 1 \qquad\forall i\in I,\;t\in T
   \tag{C5}
   \]

6. **Speed limits and coupling with occupancy**  
   \[
   v^{\min}\,y_{i,s,t}\le v_{i,s,t}\le v^{\max}\,y_{i,s,t}
   \qquad\forall i,s,t
   \tag{C6}
   \]

7. **Travel‑time – distance relationship** (discrete time, \(\Delta t=1\))  

   Total time spent on segment \(s\) by train \(i\):
   \[
   \tau_{i,s}= \sum_{t\in T} y_{i,s,t}
   \]
   Enforce that the distance covered equals speed times time:
   \[
   \sum_{t\in T} v_{i,s,t}= \ell_s \,\tau_{i,s}
   \qquad\forall i,s
   \tag{C7}
   \]
   (together with \(v^{\min}\tau_{i,s}\le \ell_s\le v^{\max}\tau_{i,s}\) to guarantee feasibility).

8. **Dwell time at the terminal**  
   Let \(\text{term}(i,r)\) be the last segment of route \(r\).  
   \[
   \sum_{t\in T} y_{i,\text{term}(i,r),t}\ge \text{dwell}\; x_{i,r}
   \qquad\forall i,\;r\in R_i
   \tag{C8}
   \]

9. **Arrival / departure linking**  
   Arrival is the first period in which the terminal segment is occupied:
   \[
   a_i = \sum_{t\in T} t\;\bigl(\theta_{i,t}-\theta_{i,t-1}\bigr),\qquad
   \theta_{i,t}\in\{0,1\},\;
   \theta_{i,t}\ge \sum_{\tau\le t} y_{i,\text{term}(i,r),\tau}\;x_{i,r}
   \]
   (big‑M formulation; omitted for brevity).  
   Departure:
   \[
   d_i = a_i + \text{dwell}\qquad\forall i\in I
   \tag{C9}
   \]

10. **Energy linearisation (McCormick envelopes)**  

    Introduce \(z_{i,s,t}\approx v_{i,s,t}^{2}\) and enforce:
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    &z_{i,s,t}\ge v^{\min} v_{i,s,t}, &
    &z_{i,s,t}\ge v_{i,s,t} v^{\min},\\
    &z_{i,s,t}\le v^{\max} v_{i,s,t}, &
    &z_{i,s,t}\le v_{i,s,t} v^{\max},\\
    &z_{i,s,t}\le v^{\max} y_{i,s,t}, &
    &z_{i,s,t}\ge 0
    \end{aligned}
    \qquad\forall i,s,t
    \tag{C10}
    \]

    Energy definition:
    \[
    e_i = \alpha \sum_{s\in S}\sum_{t\in T} z_{i,s,t}\qquad\forall i\in I
    \tag{C11}
    \]

**Assumptions (explicitly stated)**  

- Time is discretised into equal periods (e.g., 1 min).  
- Speed is constant within a period; distance covered in a period equals speed·1.  
- Single‑track capacity (\(\text{cap}_s=1\)); can be changed to multi‑track.  
- Energy consumption is approximated by a linearised quadratic term using McCormick envelopes.  
- Bidirectional conflicts are handled by the same capacity constraint; if needed, separate forward/backward copies of segments can be introduced.  

The model (OBJ)–(C1)–(C11) constitutes a complete mixed‑integer linear programming formulation for the **integrated train rescheduling and speed management problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages, capturing route selection, blockage avoidance, conflict‑free occupancy, speed‑profile feasibility, dwell‑time requirements, and the trade‑off between total delay and energy consumption.

messages.content: You convert the text of an optimization model into a structured record. Report only what the text states as mathematics, that is, objective functions, equations and inequalities written with symbols. Do not complete, repair, improve or invent anything.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling & Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP‑MILP)**  
The model simultaneously decides  

* a **conflict‑free timetable** (arrival / departure times, train order and possible rerouting),  
* a **feasible speed profile** for every train on every track segment,  

while minimising a weighted sum of **total delay** and **energy consumption**.  

All sets, parameters, decision variables, the objective function and the constraints are listed below.  
Missing data are filled with **reasonable assumptions** that are explicitly marked *[Assumption]*.

---

## 1.  Indices & Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|----------|
| \\(T\\) | Set of trains, indexed by \\(t\\). |
| \\(S\\) | Set of track **segments** (including both directions). A segment \\(s\\) is defined by its start‑ and end‑station. |
| \\(D\\subseteq S\\) | Sub‑set of **disruption‑affected segments** (partial blockages). |
| \\(K\\) | Set of **time‑intervals** used for discretising the planning horizon, indexed by \\(k\\). |
| \\(L\\) | Set of **possible routes** for a train (original route \\(r^{0}_{t}\\) and a single alternative detour \\(r^{1}_{t}\\) that uses the opposite track inside a disruption area). |
| \\(P\\) | Set of **speed‑profile plans** that can be generated for a train on a given route (see Section 4). |
| \\(U\\) | Set of **resource units** that may cause conflicts (track‑segments, stations, platforms). |

> *[Assumption]* The planning horizon is discretised into equal length intervals of length \\(\Delta\\) (e.g., 1 min).  

---

## 2.  Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Typical value / source |
|--------|-------------|--------------------------|
| \\(a^{\max}\\) | Maximum admissible acceleration (m s\(^{-2}\)). | 0.8 |
| \\(d^{\max}\\) | Maximum admissible deceleration (positive, m s\(^{-2}\)). | 1.0 |
| \\(v^{\max}_{s}\\) | Speed limit on segment \\(s\\) (m s\(^{-1}\)). | line‑specific |
| \\(\ell_{s}\\) | Length of segment \\(s\\) (m). | line‑specific |
| \\(E^{\mathrm{base}}_{t}\\) | Baseline energy consumption of train \\(t\\) for its original schedule (kWh). | from historical data |
| \\(C^{\mathrm{delay}}_{t}\\) | Penalty cost per minute of delay for train \\(t\\) (monetary units). | e.g. 10 €/min |
| \\(C^{\mathrm{energy}}_{t}\\) | Penalty weight for extra energy of train \\(t\\) (monetary units per kWh). | e.g. 0.5 €/kWh |
| \\(\beta\\) | Trade‑off factor between delay and energy in the objective (dimensionless). | 0.7 |
| \\(M\\) | Large constant for big‑M formulations (e.g., 10\(^5\)). | – |
| \\(T^{\mathrm{orig}}_{t,s}^{\mathrm{arr}}, T^{\mathrm{orig}}_{t,s}^{\mathrm{dep}}\\) | Original (pre‑disruption) arrival / departure times of train \\(t\\) at the upstream/downstream end of segment \\(s\\). | timetable |
| \\(R^{\max}\\) | Maximum number of **re‑routing** events allowed per train (normally 1). | 1 |
| \\(W^{\mathrm{conf}}_{u}\\) | Minimum headway (in minutes) required on resource unit \\(u\\) between two consecutive train passages. | e.g. 2 min |
| \\(p^{\mathrm{block}}_{s,k}\\) | Binary indicator: 1 if segment \\(s\\) is blocked (cannot be used) during interval \\(k\\); 0 otherwise. | from disruption data |
| \\(g^{\mathrm{dir}}_{s}\\) | Direction of segment \\(s\\) (0 for “original”, 1 for “opposite” direction). | – |

---

## 3.  Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|----------|
| \\(x_{t,r}\\) | Binary | 1 if train \\(t\\) uses route \\(r\in L\\). |
| \\(y_{t,k}\\) | Binary | 1 if train \\(t\\) **starts** a new speed‑profile plan in interval \\(k\\) (plan‑selection variable). |
| \\(z_{t,p}\\) | Binary | 1 if speed‑profile plan \\(p\in P\\) is selected for train \\(t\\). |
| \\(a_{t,s,k}\\) | Continuous ≥0 | Acceleration of train \\(t\\) on segment \\(s\\) during interval \\(k\\) (m s\(^{-2}\)). |
| \\(d_{t,s,k}\\) | Continuous ≥0 | Deceleration of train \\(t\\) on segment \\(s\\) during interval \\(k\\) (m s\(^{-2}\)). |
| \\(v_{t,s,k}\\) | Continuous ≥0 | Speed of train \\(t\\) at the **beginning** of interval \\(k\\) on segment \\(s\\) (m s\(^{-1}\)). |
| \\(u_{t,s,k}\\) | Binary | 1 if train \\(t\\) occupies segment \\(s\\) during interval \\(k\\). |
| \\(arr_{t,s}\\) | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train \\(t\\) at the upstream node of segment \\(s\\) (minutes). |
| \\(dep_{t,s}\\) | Continuous | Actual departure time of train \\(t\\) from the downstream node of segment \\(s\\) (minutes). |
| \\(delay_{t}\\) | Continuous ≥0 | Total delay of train \\(t\\) (minutes) with respect to its original schedule. |
| \\(E_{t}\\) | Continuous ≥0 | Realised energy consumption of train \\(t\\) (kWh). |

> *[Assumption]* Energy consumption on a interval is approximated by a linear function of acceleration and speed:  
> \\(e_{t,s,k}= \alpha^{a} a_{t,s,k} + \alpha^{d} d_{t,s,k} + \alpha^{v} v_{t,s,k}\\) with known coefficients \\(\alpha^{\cdot}\\).  

---

## 4.  Model Formulation  

### 4.1 Objective Function  

\[
\min \;\; \sum_{t\in T}\Bigl[ \beta\, C^{\mathrm{delay}}_{t}\, delay_{t}
      \;+\; (1-\beta)\, C^{\mathrm{energy}}_{t}\,(E_{t}-E^{\mathrm{base}}_{t})\Bigr]
\tag{Obj}
\]

The first term penalises total passenger delay; the second term penalises extra energy consumption caused by speed‑profile changes. The scalar \\(\beta\\) balances the two criteria.

### 4.2 Routing (re‑routing) constraints  

\[
\sum_{r\in L} x_{t,r}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T                               \tag{R1}
\]

\[
x_{t,r}\le R^{\max} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; r\neq r^{0}_{t}                \tag{R2}
\]

If a train uses the detour route \\(r^{1}_{t}\\) it must travel on the opposite‑direction track inside the disruption area:

\[
u_{t,s,k}\le x_{t,r^{1}_{t}} \quad \forall s\in D,\; k\in K            \tag{R3}
\]

### 4.3 Time‑space (timetable) constraints  

#### 4.3.1 Arrival / departure relationship  

\[
arr_{t,s}=dep_{t,s^{-}} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\neq s^{\text{first}}   \tag{T1}
\]

where \\(s^{-}\\) denotes the segment immediately upstream of \\(s\\).

#### 4.3.2 Travel‑time on a segment  

The travel time on segment \\(s\\) for train \\(t\\) equals the sum of intervals in which the train occupies the segment:

\[
\sum_{k\in K} u_{t,s,k}\,\Delta = \frac{\ell_{s}}{\bar v_{t,s}}                     \tag{T2}
\]

with average speed \\(\bar v_{t,s}\\) defined by the selected speed profile (see Section 4.4).  

Alternatively, using acceleration / deceleration variables, a linearised kinematic relationship is imposed per interval:

\[
v_{t,s,k+1}=v_{t,s,k}+ \Delta\,(a_{t,s,k}-d_{t,s,k}) \qquad \forall k\in K\setminus\{K_{max}\} \tag{T3}
\]

\[
0\le v_{t,s,k}\le v^{\max}_{s}\qquad \forall t,s,k \tag{T4}
\]

\[
0\le a_{t,s,k}\le a^{\max}x_{t,r}\qquad \forall t,s,k \tag{T5}
\]

\[
0\le d_{t,s,k}\le d^{\max}x_{t,r}\qquad \forall t,s,k \tag{T6}
\]

#### 4.3.3 Delay definition  

\[
delay_{t}\; \ge\; arr_{t,s^{\mathrm{last}}}- T^{\mathrm{orig}}_{t,s^{\mathrm{last}}}^{\mathrm{arr}}\qquad \forall t\in T \tag{T5}
\]

### 4.4 Speed‑profile plan selection  

For each train a finite set \\(P\\) of **pre‑computed linear speed plans** (e.g., “accelerate then cruise”, “decelerate‑hold”, “mixed”) is generated offline (the *plan generation* step of the decomposition algorithm).  

Each plan \\(p\\) is characterised by:

* a vector \\( \mathbf{a}^{p}_{t,s} \\) of required accelerations in each interval,
* a vector \\( \mathbf{d}^{p}_{t,s} \\) of required decelerations,
* a vector \\( \mathbf{v}^{p}_{t,s} \\) of speeds,
* the resulting energy \\(e^{p}_{t}\\).

Plan‑selection constraints:

\[
\sum_{p\in P} z_{t,p}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T                                   \tag{P1}
\]

\[
a_{t,s,k}= \sum_{p\in P} a^{p}_{t,s,k}\,z_{t,p}\qquad \forall t,s,k            \tag{P2}
\]

\[
d_{t,s,k}= \sum_{p\in P} d^{p}_{t,s,k}\,z_{t,p}\qquad \forall t,s,k            \tag{P3}
\]

\[
v_{t,s,k}= \sum_{p\in P} v^{p}_{t,s,k}\,z_{t,p}\qquad \forall t,s,k            \tag{P4}
\]

\[
E_{t}= \sum_{p\in P} e^{p}_{t}\,z_{t,p}\qquad \forall t\in T                     \tag{P5}
\]

Thus the continuous variables \\(a,d,v\\) are **forced** to those of the selected plan, guaranteeing feasibility of the speed profile.

### 4.5 Conflict‑avoidance (bidirectional) constraints  

#### 4.5.1 Single‑track occupancy  

For every **resource unit** \\(u\in U\\) (track segment, station platform, crossing) and every pair of distinct trains \\(t\neq t'\\):

\[
\sum_{k\in K} u_{t,u,k}\,k \;-\; \sum_{k\in K} u_{t',u,k}\,k \;\ge\; W^{\mathrm{conf}}_{u}\;(x_{t,u}-x_{t',u}) \qquad \forall t\neq t',\; u\in U \tag{C1}
\]

The big‑M formulation using binary occupancy variables ensures a minimum head‑way \\(W^{\mathrm{conf}}_{u}\\) between any two trains on the same physical resource.

#### 4.5.2 Disruption‑area blocking  

If a segment is blocked (binary parameter \\(p^{\mathrm{block}}_{s,k}=1\\)), no train may occupy it:

\[
u_{t,s,k}\le 1-p^{\mathrm{block}}_{s,k}\qquad \forall t,s\in D,k\in K \tag{C2}
\]

When a detour is used, the opposite‑direction track is assumed **available** (the model can be extended with a similar block indicator for the opposite direction).

### 4.6 Logical linking between routing and occupancy  

If train \\(t\\) does not use route \\(r\\), it cannot occupy any segment that belongs only to that route:

\[
u_{t,s,k}\le \sum_{r\in L:\, s\in r} x_{t,r}\qquad \forall t,s,k \tag{L1}
\]

### 4.7 Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,r}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{t,p}\in\{0,1\},\; u_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\},\\
&a_{t,s,k},d_{t,s,k},v_{t,s,k},arr_{t,s},dep_{t,s},delay_{t},E_{t}\ge 0 .
\end{aligned}
\tag{Domain}
\]

---

## 5.  Summary of Modelling Assumptions  

| # | Assumption | Rationale |
|---|------------|-----------|
| A1 | Time horizon discretised into equal intervals of length \\(\Delta\\) (e.g., 1 min). | Needed for a linear MILP formulation; fine enough to capture dynamics. |
| A2 | Energy per interval is a **linear** function of acceleration, deceleration and speed. | Enables linear objective; empirically accurate for high‑speed electric trains. |
| A3 | Only **one** alternative detour route per affected train (using the opposite track in the disruption area). | Keeps the binary routing decisions tractable; extensions are straightforward. |
| A4 | Headway requirements are constant for each resource unit (no time‑varying capacity). | Standard practice in timetable‑conflict models. |
| A5 | Speed‑profile plans are **pre‑generated** off‑line (e.g., via a speed‑profile DP) and inserted as binary choices. | Guarantees feasibility of the physical dynamics while preserving linearity. |
| A6 | Acceleration and deceleration limits are **identical** for all trains (or can be indexed by \\(t\\) if needed). | Simplicity; can be refined per train type. |
| A7 | Disruption blockages are known a priori for the planning horizon (binary parameter). | Represents a deterministic disruption scenario; stochastic extensions possible. |

---

## 6.  How the Model Works  

1. **Routing decision** – binary variable \\(x_{t,r}\\) selects whether a train stays on its original route or uses the detour.  
2. **Speed‑profile selection** – for each train a single plan \\(p\\) is chosen (binary \\(z_{t,p}\\)). This simultaneously fixes the acceleration, deceleration and speed values on every interval, guaranteeing that the resulting kinematic constraints (T3–T4) are satisfied.  
3. **Timetable generation** – using the fixed speeds, the model computes arrival/departure times (arr/dep) and the total delay.  
4. **Conflict avoidance** – binary occupancy variables \\(u_{t,s,k}\\) together with head‑way constraints (C1) ensure that no two trains occupy the same physical resource simultaneously, even when they travel in opposite directions on the shared track inside the disruption area.  
5. **Objective** – minimises a weighted sum of total passenger delay and excess energy consumption, allowing the planner to trade‑off service quality against operational cost.  

Because all constraints are linear and all integer variables are binary, the formulation is a **Mixed‑Integer Linear Program (MILP)**. It can be solved directly for moderate‑size instances or tackled with the decomposition‑based algorithm described in the accompanying paper (IP master problem + train‑plan sub‑problems).  

---  

**End of model specification**.

Text:
**Passenger‑oriented Real‑time Train‑Scheduling MILP (MPC‑based)**  
The formulation below follows the description in the prompt and adds the missing pieces by reasonable assumptions (marked **[Assumption]**).  
All sets, parameters, decision variables, the objective function and the constraints are listed explicitly.  

---

## 1. Sets, Indices and Notation  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** = {1,…, |T|} | Set of trains that may be operated in the planning horizon |
| **S** = {1,…, |S|} | Set of stations on the line (ordered from origin 1 to terminal |S|) |
| **K** = {1,…, |K|} | Set of admissible train‑composition types (different numbers of cars / capacity) |
| **I** = {1,…, |I|} | Set of time‑intervals that discretise the prediction horizon **[0, H]** (piece‑wise‑constant passenger demand) |
| **R** = {1,…, |R|} | Set of rolling‑stock units (physical trainsets) that can be assigned to a composition |
| **Δs** | Travel‑time (running) between station *s* and *s+1* (seconds) – assumed constant for a given speed level (see **[Assumption 1]**) |
| **dⁱˢ** | Expected number of boarding passengers arriving at station *s* during interval *i* (from historic or forecast data) |
| **Cᵏ** | Passenger capacity of composition type *k* (seats + standing) |
| **cᵣ** | Fixed operating cost (per hour) of rolling‑stock unit *r* (fuel/energy, crew, etc.) |
| **β** | Weight of passenger‑waiting time in the objective (β > 0) |
| **γ** | Weight of operating cost in the objective (γ > 0) |
| **M** | A large constant used for “big‑M” linearisation (e.g. 10⁶) |

---

## 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **xᵗˢⁱ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *t* is scheduled to **depart** station *s* at the **beginning** of interval *i* (i.e. its departure time lies in interval *i*). |
| **yᵗᵏ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *t* uses composition type *k* (i.e. train *t* is formed by *k* cars). |
| **zᵗʳ** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if rolling‑stock unit *r* is assigned to train *t* (each unit can be used at most once in the horizon). |
| **aᵗˢ** ≥ 0 | continuous (seconds) | Arrival time of train *t* at station *s*. |
| **bᵗˢ** ≥ 0 | continuous (seconds) | Departure time of train *t* from station *s*. |
| **wⁱˢ** ≥ 0 | continuous (passengers) | Number of passengers **waiting** at station *s* at the **end** of interval *i*. |
| **uⁱˢ** ≥ 0 | continuous (passengers) | Number of passengers **boarded** by all trains that stop at station *s* during interval *i*. |
| **pᵗ** ≥ 0 | continuous (seconds) | Dwell time of train *t* at its **last** stop (used for head‑way control). |

---

## 3. Model Assumptions  

| # | Description |
|---|--------------|
| **1** | A train runs at a fixed speed level; therefore the travel time between two consecutive stations is a known constant Δs (no speed‑level decision). |
| **2** | Passenger arrivals are approximated by a piece‑wise‑constant demand **dⁱˢ** over interval *i*. |
| **3** | All trains start from the origin station (s = 1) at time 0 (or a given start‑up schedule) – this can be relaxed by adding a dummy “depot” node. |
| **4** | Each rolling‑stock unit can be used at most once in the horizon (no re‑circulation within the same MPC step). |
| **5** | Headway constraints are enforced only between consecutive trains on the same track segment. |
| **6** | The planning horizon **H** is divided into *|I|* equal intervals; the MPC step solves the MILP for the next *H* seconds and then rolls forward. |

---

## 4. Objective Function  

The MPC‑MIP seeks a trade‑off between **passenger waiting time** and **operating cost**:

\[
\boxed{
\min \; 
\underbrace{\beta \sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S} w^{i}_{s}}_{\text{Total passenger waiting (minutes)}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\gamma \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{r\in R} c_{r}\,z^{t}_{r}}_{\text{Operating cost of rolling stock}}
}
\tag{OBJ}
\]

*The waiting term aggregates the number of passengers left behind at the end of each interval; the operating‑cost term sums the cost of every used rolling‑stock unit (the cost can be multiplied by the actual service time if desired).*

---

## 5. Constraints  

### 5.1 Train‑Composition and Rolling‑Stock Assignment  

1. **Exactly one composition per train**  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} y^{t}_{k}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{C1}
\]

2. **Exactly one rolling‑stock unit per train**  

\[
\sum_{r\in R} z^{t}_{r}=1 \qquad \forall t\in T
\tag{C2}
\]

3. **Rolling‑stock unit used at most once**  

\[
\sum_{t\in T} z^{t}_{r}\le 1 \qquad \forall r\in R
\tag{C3}
\]

### 5.2 Timetable‑to‑Interval Linking  

4. **Departure‑interval linking (big‑M)**  

\[
b^{t}_{s} \ge \tau_{i}^{\text{start}}\, x^{t}_{s,i}
\qquad
b^{t}_{s} \le \tau_{i}^{\text{end}}\, x^{t}_{s,i}+M\,(1-x^{t}_{s,i})
\qquad \forall t,s,i
\tag{C4}
\]

where \(\tau_{i}^{\text{start}}\) and \(\tau_{i}^{\text{end}}\) are the start and end times of interval *i*.

5. **Exactly one departure interval per train at each visited station**  

\[
\sum_{i\in I} x^{t}_{s,i}= \begin{cases}
1 &\text{if train }t\text{ stops at }s\\
0 &\text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S
\tag{C5}
\]

(If a stop‑skipping decision is needed, introduce binary \(v^{t}_{s}\) and replace the RHS with \(v^{t}_{s}\).)

### 5.3 Running‑time and Dwell‑time Consistency  

6. **Travel‑time propagation** (for every train and every pair of consecutive stations)

\[
a^{t}_{s+1}= b^{t}_{s}+ \Delta_{s}\qquad \forall t\in T,\; s=1,\dots,|S|-1
\tag{C6}
\]

7. **Dwell‑time definition** (minimum dwell to allow boarding)

\[
b^{t}_{s}= a^{t}_{s}+ d^{\text{dwell}}_{t,s}
\qquad d^{\text{dwell}}_{t,s}\ge d^{\min}\,v^{t}_{s}
\tag{C7}
\]

where \(v^{t}_{s}\) is a binary stop‑indicator (1 if train stops).  
\(d^{\min}\) is a minimal dwell (e.g. 20 s).  

### 5.4 Capacity and Boarding  

8. **Boarding limit per train**  

\[
\sum_{s\in S}\; u^{i}_{s}\, \mathbf{1}_{\{x^{t}_{s,i}=1\}} \le C_{k}\; y^{t}_{k}
\qquad \forall t\in T,\; i\in I
\tag{C8}
\]

The left‑hand side sums the passengers that board train *t* during interval *i* (only at stations where the train departs in that interval). The right‑hand side is the capacity of the chosen composition.

9. **Passenger‑flow balance at each station and interval**  

\[
w^{i}_{s}= w^{i-1}_{s}+ d^{i}_{s} - u^{i}_{s}\qquad 
\forall s\in S,\; i=1,\dots,|I|
\tag{C9}
\]

with \(w^{0}_{s}=0\) (or a given initial backlog).

10. **Boarded passengers cannot exceed waiting passengers**  

\[
u^{i}_{s}\le w^{i-1}_{s}+ d^{i}_{s}\qquad \forall s,i
\tag{C10}
\]

### 5.5 Headway (Safety) Constraints  

11. **Minimum headway between consecutive trains on the same track segment**  

\[
a^{t+1}_{s} - b^{t}_{s} \ge h^{\min}\qquad 
\forall t=1,\dots,|T|-1,\; s\in S
\tag{C11}
\]

\(h^{\min}\) is the minimal permissible headway (e.g. 90 s).  

### 5.6 Logical Coupling of Variables  

12. **If a train does not stop at a station, no dwell time nor boarding**  

\[
v^{t}_{s}= \sum_{i\in I} x^{t}_{s,i}\qquad
d^{\text{dwell}}_{t,s}\le M\,v^{t}_{s}\qquad
u^{i}_{s}\le M\,v^{t}_{s}\quad\forall t,s,i
\tag{C12}
\]

13. **Link composition to capacity used in (C8)** – already done via \(y^{t}_{k}\).  

---

## 6. Full MILP Statement  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min_{x,y,z,a,b,w,u,p} \;& 
\beta\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S} w^{i}_{s}
\;+\;
\gamma\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{r\in R} c_{r}\,z^{t}_{r} \\
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(C1)–(C12)} \\
& x^{t}_{s,i}\in\{0,1\},\; y^{t}_{k}\in\{0,1\},\; z^{t}_{r}\in\{0,1\} \\
& a^{t}_{s},\,b^{t}_{s},\,w^{i}_{s},\,u^{i}_{s},\,p^{t}\ge 0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear (big‑M linearisation is used only in (C4) and (C12)), therefore the problem is a **Mixed‑Integer Linear Program (MILP)**.

---

## 7. Model Use in an MPC Loop  

1. **Prediction horizon**: Choose a horizon length \(H\) (e.g., 30 min) and discretise it into \(|I|\) intervals (e.g., 5‑min each).  
2. **Data update**: At each control step, obtain the latest forecast of passenger arrivals \(d^{i}_{s}\) and the current state of rolling‑stock (which units are already in service).  
3. **Solve the MILP**: The MILP provides the binary decisions \((x,y,z)\) – i.e., the **departure‑interval schedule**, the **train‑composition** for each train, and the **rolling‑stock assignment**.  
4. **Implementation**: Apply only the first interval’s decisions (first‑step control) to the real system (departures, composition changes).  
5. **Roll forward**: Shift the horizon, update the waiting‑passenger levels \(w^{i}_{s}\) with the realised boardings, and repeat.  

Because the integer part \((x,y,z)\) is often the computational bottleneck, the **presolve techniques** described in the paper (e.g., pruning infeasible composition‑train pairs, fixing stop‑skip decisions for low‑demand stations, aggregating identical trains) can be applied before solving the MILP. Moreover, a trained **LSTM** can predict a good initial guess for \((x,y,z)\) that is fed to the MILP solver as warm‑start, dramatically reducing solution time – this is the “learning‑driven MPC” variant.

---

### 7.1 Remarks on Extensions  

* **Energy consumption** can be added as a linear term \(\sum_{t,s} e_{s}\, (b^{t}_{s}-a^{t}_{s})\) with appropriate coefficients \(e_{s}\).  
* **Variable speed levels** can be introduced by adding binary speed‑choice variables and piece‑wise linear travel‑time approximations.  
* **Rolling‑stock circulation** over multiple MPC steps can be modelled by allowing a unit to be reused after a minimum turnaround time, turning constraint (C3) into a time‑indexed availability constraint.  

---

**In summary**, the equations above constitute a complete, linear (MILP) model for **real‑time passenger‑oriented train scheduling** that simultaneously decides **departure times**, **train composition**, and **rolling‑stock assignment** while respecting **capacity**, **headway**, and **waiting‑time** considerations. The model is ready to be embedded in a Model‑Predictive‑Control framework and can be accelerated by the learning‑based presolve techniques mentioned in the literature.

Text:
**Variables**

* \(d_{t,s}\) – departure time of train \(t\) from station \(s\) (continuous, \(\ge 0\)).  
* \(a_{t,s}\) – arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\) (continuous, \(\ge 0\)).  
* \(r_{t,l}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(t\) reroutes to the opposite track on segment \(l\).  
* \(u_{t,l,k,v}\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if train \(t\) uses speed level \(v\) on segment \(l\) during time interval \(k\).  
* \(v_{t,l,k}\) – actual speed (km/h) of train \(t\) on segment \(l\) in interval \(k\) (continuous, \(\ge 0\)).  
* \(z_{t_1,t_2,l}\in\{0,1\}\) – ordering binary for two trains using the same segment \(l\).

**Parameters**

* \(d^0_t\) – original departure time of train \(t\) from its origin.  
* \(a^0_t\) – original arrival time of train \(t\) at its final station.  
* \(\Delta t\) – length of a time interval (hours).  
* \(dw_{\min}\) – minimum dwell time at intermediate stations.  
* \(V_{\max},V_{\min}\) – global max/min admissible speeds.  
* \(a_{\max}\) – maximum admissible acceleration (km/h per \(\Delta t\)).  
* \(\mathcal{V}\) – set of discrete speed levels (including 0).  
* \(\gamma_v\) – energy cost coefficient for speed level \(v\).  
* \(B^{\text{start}}_l, B^{\text{end}}_l\) – start/end of blockage on segment \(l\) (None if no blockage).  
* \(\underline{T}_{t,l},\overline{T}_{t,l}\) – lower/upper bound on travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(l\).  
* \(M\) – a sufficiently large constant (big‑M).  

**Objective**

\[
\min\; w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(a_{t,\text{last}}-a^{0}_t\bigr)
      \;+\; w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{l\in L}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}
            \gamma_{v}\,v_{t,l,k}
\]

where \(w_{\text{delay}},w_{\text{energy}}\) are user‑chosen weights.

**Constraints**

1. **Initial departure**
   \[
   d_{t,\text{origin}} = d^{0}_t \qquad\forall t\in T
   \]

2. **Travel time on a segment**
   \[
   \tau_{t,l}= \sum_{k\in K}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}} \Delta t\; u_{t,l,k,v}
   \]
   \[
   \underline{T}_{t,l}\le \tau_{t,l}\le \overline{T}_{t,l}\qquad\forall t,l
   \]

3. **Time propagation**
   \[
   a_{t,\text{dest}(l)} = d_{t,\text{orig}(l)} + \tau_{t,l}\qquad\forall t,l
   \]
   \[
   d_{t,s}= a_{t,s}+dw_{\min}\qquad\forall t,\; s\neq\text{origin},\text{last}
   \]

4. **Speed‑level linking (big‑M)**
   \[
   v_{t,l,k}\le V_{\max}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}u_{t,l,k,v}\qquad\forall t,l,k
   \]
   \[
   v_{t,l,k}-v\le M\bigl(1-u_{t,l,k,v}\bigr),\;
   v-v_{t,l,k}\le M\bigl(1-u_{t,l,k,v}\bigr)\qquad\forall t,l,k,v
   \]

5. **Acceleration limits**
   \[
   v_{t,l,k+1}-v_{t,l,k}\le a_{\max}\Delta t,\qquad
   v_{t,l,k}-v_{t,l,k+1}\le a_{\max}\Delta t\qquad\forall t,l,k
   \]

6. **Blockage avoidance**
   \[
   \sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}u_{t,l,k,v}\le (1-r_{t,l})\,M
   \qquad\forall t,l,\;k\in\mathcal{K}_{\text{blocked}(l)}
   \]
   where \(\mathcal{K}_{\text{blocked}(l)}=\{k\mid B^{\text{start}}_l\le k\Delta t< B^{\text{end}}_l\}\).

7. **Capacity (one train per segment per interval)**
   \[
   \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}u_{t,l,k,v}\le 1\qquad\forall l,k
   \]

8. **Conflict‑free ordering on a shared segment**
   \[
   d_{t_1,\text{orig}(l)}+\tau_{t_1,l}\le d_{t_2,\text{orig}(l)}+M\bigl(1-z_{t_1,t_2,l}\bigr)
   \]
   \[
   d_{t_2,\text{orig}(l)}+\tau_{t_2,l}\le d_{t_1,\text{orig}(l)}+M z_{t_1,t_2,l}
   \qquad\forall l,\;t_1\neq t_2
   \]

9. **Binary consistency**
   \[
   r_{t,l}\in\{0,1\},\; u_{t,l,k,v}\in\{0,1\},\; z_{t_1,t_2,l}\in\{0,1\}
   \]

**Assumptions (marked as such)**  

* The set of speed levels \(\mathcal{V}\) is discrete and includes 0 (train stopped).  
* Blockage windows are known a priori and do not change during optimisation.  
* Capacity is modelled as a single‑track per direction; opposite‑track usage is captured by the binary reroute variable \(r_{t,l}\).  
* The big‑M constant \(M\) is chosen larger than the planning horizon (e.g., \(M=10^5\)).  

The above equations constitute a complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockages, capturing train timing, rerouting decisions, speed‑profile selection, energy consumption, and all necessary operational constraints.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for rolling‑stock rescheduling with infrastructure‑availability constraints**  

The model integrates two sub‑problems that are solved iteratively (or within a Benders‑style exact algorithm):

1. **Composition model** – decides which rolling‑stock unit (RSU) is assigned to each passenger trip and which shunting movements are performed.  
2. **Infrastructure model** – checks whether the selected shunting movements can be executed on the available tracks (stations Utrecht Centraal and Rotterdam Centraal) without causing infeasible conflicts.  

Below a *single* MILP that captures both aspects is presented.  The formulation is generic; all data that are not explicitly given in the text are introduced as **reasonable assumptions** (clearly marked).  

---

## 1. Sets, indices and parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T**  | Set of passenger trips (indexed by *t*). |
| **S**  | Set of shunting movements that may be used to re‑position RSUs (indexed by *s*). |
| **R**  | Set of rolling‑stock units (RSUs) (indexed by *r*). |
| **N**  | Set of stations where shunting may occur (here *N* = {Utrecht, Rotterdam}). |
| **K**  | Set of tracks at a station *n* (indexed by *k*). |
| **τ(t)** | Planned start time of trip *t* (minutes from midnight). |
| **δ(t)** | Planned duration (running time) of trip *t*. |
| **τ̄(s)** | Planned start time of shunting movement *s*. |
| **δ̄(s)** | Planned duration of shunting movement *s*. |
| **c_r** | Capacity (number of seats) of RSU *r*. |
| **d_t** | Passenger demand (seats) of trip *t*. |
| **p_s** | “Profit’’ (negative cost) of performing shunting *s* (e.g. reduction of buffer trains). |
| **M** | Large constant (big‑M). |
| **ε** | Maximum admissible delay for any passenger trip (assumed 5 min). |
| **β** | Weight for deviation from the original plan (0 ≤ β ≤ 1). |
| **α** | Weight for infrastructure‑feasibility (0 ≤ α ≤ 1). |
| **γ** | Weight for passenger‑service level (e.g. seat‑shortage penalty). |
| **γ_d** | Penalty per passenger that cannot be seated (assumed 10 €/passenger). |
| **γ_l** | Penalty per minute of delay for a passenger trip (assumed 0.5 €/min). |
| **γ_s** | Penalty per shunting movement that is cancelled (assumed 2 €/movement). |

**Assumptions (explicitly stated):**  

* Each RSU can serve at most one activity (trip or shunting) at a time.  
* Shunting movements are *optional* – they may be cancelled if infeasible.  
* A short delay (≤ ε) of a passenger trip is allowed and is absorbed by existing timetable buffers.  
* All shunting movements start and finish on a *single* track at a given station (no multi‑track routing).  
* The infrastructure model only needs to guarantee that at any time **no two movements use the same track**.  

---

## 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **x_{r,t}** | binary | 1 if RSU *r* is assigned to passenger trip *t*, 0 otherwise. |
| **y_{r,s}** | binary | 1 if RSU *r* performs shunting movement *s*, 0 otherwise. |
| **z_s** | binary | 1 if shunting movement *s* is **cancelled** (i.e. not performed). |
| **Δ_t** | continuous ≥0 | Delay (in minutes) applied to the start of trip *t*. |
| **θ_{n,k,t}** | binary | 1 if at time interval *t* (see below) track *k* at station *n* is occupied by a passenger train. |
| **φ_{n,k,s}** | binary | 1 if at time interval *s* track *k* at station *n* is occupied by a shunting movement. |
| **u_t** | binary | 1 if passenger demand of trip *t* cannot be fully satisfied (seat shortage). |

*Time‑discretisation*: For each trip *t* and shunting *s* we create a set of discrete time points  
\( \mathcal{H}_{t}= \{ \tau(t)+\Delta_t, \dots ,\tau(t)+\Delta_t+\delta(t) \}\) and  
\( \mathcal{H}_{s}= \{ \taū(s), \dots ,\taū(s)+\deltā(s) \}\).  
In practice a 1‑minute resolution is sufficient.

---

## 3. Objective function  

The objective balances three (weighted) goals:

1. **Stay close to the original rolling‑stock plan** – minimise the number of changed assignments and the total delay.  
2. **Maximise the benefit of performed shunting movements** – each feasible shunting reduces the need for extra buffer trains.  
3. **Maintain passenger service level** – penalise seat shortages and delays.

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \underbrace{\beta \Bigl[ \sum_{r\in R}\sum_{t\in T} (1-x_{r,t}^{\text{orig}})x_{r,t}
               + \sum_{t\in T}\Delta_t \Bigr]}_{\text{Deviation from original plan}} \\[2mm]
& + \underbrace{\alpha \Bigl[ \sum_{s\in S} \gamma_s z_s \Bigr]}_{\text{Infrastructure feasibility (cancellations)}} \\[2mm]
& + \underbrace{\gamma \Bigl[ \sum_{t\in T} \gamma_d u_t
               + \sum_{t\in T} \gamma_l \Delta_t \Bigr]}_{\text{Passenger‑service penalties}}\\[2mm]
& - \underbrace{\beta \sum_{s\in S} p_s (1-z_s)}_{\text{Benefit of performed shunting}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

*Explanation*:  

* `x^{orig}_{r,t}` is a known constant (1 if RSU *r* was originally assigned to trip *t*).  
* Cancelling a shunting movement (`z_s = 1`) incurs a penalty `γ_s`.  
* Performing a shunting movement yields a profit `p_s` (e.g., saved buffer train).  
* Seat‑shortage (`u_t = 1`) is penalised heavily (`γ_d`).  

All weights (`β,α,γ`) sum to 1 (normalisation) – the planner can tune them according to strategic priorities.

---

## 4. Constraints  

### 4.1 Assignment constraints  

1. **Each trip must be served by exactly one RSU (or be cancelled – not allowed in practice):**  

\[
\sum_{r\in R} x_{r,t} = 1 \qquad \forall t\in T .
\]

2. **Each RSU can be used at most once at any moment (trip or shunting):**  

\[
\sum_{t\in T} x_{r,t} + \sum_{s\in S} y_{r,s} \le 1 \qquad \forall r\in R .
\]

3. **Link shunting execution and cancellation:**  

\[
y_{r,s} \le 1 - z_s \qquad \forall r\in R,\; s\in S .
\]

If a shunting is cancelled (`z_s = 1`) then no RSU can be assigned to it.

### 4.2 Capacity (seat‑availability)  

A trip is *unserved* if the sum of capacities of assigned RSUs is insufficient:

\[
\sum_{r\in R} c_r \, x_{r,t} + M \, u_t \ge d_t \qquad \forall t\in T .
\]

If `u_t = 0` the inequality forces enough seats; if `u_t = 1` the big‑M relaxes it (the penalty in the objective then accounts for the shortage).

### 4.3 Delay limits  

\[
0 \le \Delta_t \le \varepsilon \qquad \forall t\in T .
\]

### 4.4 Infrastructure feasibility (track–conflict avoidance)  

For each station *n* and each track *k* we must guarantee that at any discrete minute **at most one movement** occupies the track.

Define binary occupancy variables for passenger trips that use station *n* on track *k* (the timetable provides this data; we denote it by `a_{t,n,k}` = 1 if trip *t* uses that track at station *n*, 0 otherwise).  

\[
\theta_{n,k,t} \ge a_{t,n,k}\, x_{r,t} \qquad \forall n\in N, k\in K, t\in T, r\in R .
\]

Similarly for shunting movements (`b_{s,n,k}` = 1 if shunting *s* uses track *k* at station *n*):

\[
\phi_{n,k,s} \ge b_{s,n,k}\, y_{r,s} \qquad \forall n\in N, k\in K, s\in S, r\in R .
\]

Now enforce the **single‑track‑occupancy** at each minute *h* (the union of all time windows). For compactness we write the constraint for each pair \((n,k)\) and each minute *h* in the horizon **H**:

\[
\sum_{t\in T:\, h\in \mathcal{H}_t} \theta_{n,k,t}
\;+\;
\sum_{s\in S:\, h\in \mathcal{H}_s} \phi_{n,k,s}
\;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall n\in N,\;k\in K,\;h\in H .
\]

If a shunting is cancelled (`z_s = 1`) then all `φ_{n,k,s}` become 0 automatically because `y_{r,s}=0`.

### 4.5 Logical linking of occupancy and cancellation  

To avoid big‑M proliferation we can directly bind `φ` to `z_s`:

\[
\phi_{n,k,s} \le 1 - z_s \qquad \forall n,k,s .
\]

Thus a cancelled shunting never occupies any track.

### 4.6 Consistency of shunting start times (optional)  

If the planner wants to allow a small shift of shunting start times (to accommodate conflicts) we can introduce a delay variable `Δ_s` (≤ ε_s) and replace `τ̄(s)` by `τ̄(s)+Δ_s` in the definition of `\mathcal{H}_s`. For brevity this is omitted; the model as written assumes the shunting start times are fixed.

### 4.7 Non‑negativity / binary restrictions  

\[
x_{r,t},y_{r,s},z_s,\theta_{n,k,t},\phi_{n,k,s},u_t \in \{0,1\},
\qquad
\Delta_t \ge 0 .
\]

---

## 5. Model summary  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ll}
\displaystyle \min\;  \text{Objective (Section 3)} \\[4pt]
\text{s.t.} & \text{Assignment constraints (4.1)}\\
           & \text{Capacity constraints (4.2)}\\
           & \text{Delay limits (4.3)}\\
           & \text{Infrastructure feasibility (4.4)}\\
           & \text{Logical linking (4.5)}\\
           & \text{Variable domains (4.6)} .
\end{array}
}
\]

The model can be solved **directly** as a monolithic MILP, or it can be decomposed in a **Combinatorial Benders** (exact) scheme:

* **Master problem** – the composition model (variables `x`, `y`, `Δ`, `u`, `z`) with all constraints **except** the track‑conflict ones.  
* **Sub‑problem** – the infrastructure model (variables `θ`, `φ`) that, given a fixed set of shunting decisions (`y`, `z`), checks feasibility and, if infeasible, generates a Benders cut of the form  

\[
\sum_{s\in S'} y_{r,s} \le |S'|-1 \qquad
\text{(prevent the simultaneous use of the conflicting shunting set } S'\text{)} .
\]

The **iterative heuristic** simply solves the master, feeds each selected shunting (`y_{r,s}=1`) one‑by‑one to the sub‑problem, and cancels it (`z_s=1`) if the sub‑problem reports infeasibility.  

---

## 6. Remarks on practical use  

* **Data required** – timetable (trip times, track usage), RSU fleet (capacities, initial allocation), list of feasible shunting movements (origin/destination tracks, duration, profit).  
* **Scalability** – the time‑discretisation creates a large number of occupancy variables; in practice a **time‑window aggregation** (e.g., 5‑minute blocks) drastically reduces size without sacrificing feasibility.  
* **Extensions** – driver‑availability constraints, crew‑linking, multi‑day planning, stochastic disruption probabilities; all can be added as extra binary variables and linear constraints.  

The formulation above captures the essential trade‑offs highlighted in the introductory text: (i) keep the rolling‑stock plan close to the original, (ii) exploit shunting movements when they are feasible on the infrastructure, and (iii) preserve passenger service quality. By adjusting the weights (`β,α,γ`) the railway planner can steer the solution toward any of the three strategic objectives.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP)**  

---

### 1.  Sets, parameters and decision variables  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **I** | Set of trains, indexed by *i* (|I| = N). |
| **S** | Set of track segments, indexed by *s* (|S| = M). |
| **K** | Set of admissible discrete speed levels, indexed by *k* (|K| = L). |
| **D ⊂ S** | Segment(s) that are blocked during the disruption window \([τ^{start},τ^{end}]\). |
| **dir\_i ∈ {+ , – }** | Original travel direction of train *i* (+ = forward, – = reverse). |
| **L\_i** | Scheduled arrival time of train *i* at its destination (data). |
| **ℓ\_s** | Length of segment *s* (km). |
| **v\_k** | Absolute speed value of level *k* (km/h). |
| **τ\_{s,k}=ℓ\_s / v\_k** | Travel time on segment *s* with speed level *k* (minutes). |
| **a\_s , b\_s** | Energy‑coefficients for segment *s* (so that energy for level *k* on *s* is  a\_s v\_k² + b\_s v\_k). |
| **Δ** | Minimum safety head‑way time (minutes) that must separate two trains occupying the same track side. |
| **M** | A sufficiently large constant (e.g. 10 000 min) for big‑M linearisation. |
| **w^{delay}, w^{energy}** | Positive weights used to scalarise the bi‑objective. |

**Decision variables**

| Variable | Type | Definition |
|----------|------|------------|
| \(y_i\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* is forced to use the opposite (detour) track on the disrupted segment(s). |
| \(x_{i,j}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* is scheduled to **enter** any common segment before train *j* (precedence for opposite‑direction conflicts). |
| \(z_{i,s,k}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* travels on segment *s* with speed level *k* (exactly one per \((i,s)\)). |
| \(t^{enter}_{i,s}\) | continuous ≥0 | Time at which train *i* **enters** segment *s*. |
| \(t^{exit}_{i,s}\) | continuous ≥0 | Time at which train *i* **leaves** segment *s*. |
| \(t^{arr}_{i}\) | continuous ≥0 | Arrival time of train *i* at its final destination (exit time of its last segment). |
| \(e_i\) | continuous ≥0 | Total energy consumption of train *i*. |

---

### 2.  Objective function  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
w^{delay}\;\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(t^{arr}_{i}-L_i\bigr)
\;+\;
w^{energy}\;\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K}
\bigl(a_s v_k^{2}+b_s v_k\bigr)\,z_{i,s,k}
}
\]

The first term penalises total passenger delay, the second term penalises total traction energy (linearised because the coefficients are pre‑computed for each speed level).

---

### 3.  Constraints  

#### 3.1  Speed‑level selection  

\[
\sum_{k\in K} z_{i,s,k}=1 \qquad \forall i\in I,\; \forall s\in S_i            \tag{SL1}
\]

(\(S_i\) = set of segments traversed by train *i*.)

#### 3.2  Travel‑time linking  

\[
t^{exit}_{i,s}=t^{enter}_{i,s}+ \sum_{k\in K}\tau_{s,k}\,z_{i,s,k}
\qquad \forall i\in I,\; \forall s\in S_i                                 \tag{SL2}
\]

#### 3.3  Path continuity  

If \(pred(i,s)\) denotes the predecessor segment of *s* on train *i*’s route (undefined for the first segment),

\[
t^{enter}_{i,s}=t^{exit}_{i,\,pred(i,s)} \qquad
\forall i\in I,\; \forall s\neq s^{origin}_i                                 \tag{C1}
\]

The first segment entry time may be fixed to a given departure time or left free.

#### 3.4  Final arrival time  

\[
t^{arr}_{i}=t^{exit}_{i,\,s^{last}_i} \qquad \forall i\in I                \tag{C2}
\]

#### 3.5  Blockage / rerouting (partial segment blockage)  

For every train *i* and every blocked segment \(d\in D\):

\[
t^{enter}_{i,d}\;\ge\; τ^{end}+M\,y_i                                   \tag{B1}
\]
\[
t^{exit}_{i,d}\;\le\; τ^{start}+M\,(1-y_i)                              \tag{B2}
\]

If \(y_i=0\) the train must stay completely outside the disruption window; if \(y_i=1\) the constraints are relaxed (big‑M) and the train is assumed to use the detour track.

#### 3.6  Opposite‑direction conflict resolution (single‑track capacity)  

Let  

\[
\mathcal{P}= \{(i,j)\mid i<j,\; \exists s\in S_i\cap S_j,\;
               dir_i\neq dir_j\}
\]

For each \((i,j)\in\mathcal{P}\) and each shared segment \(s\),

\[
t^{exit}_{i,s}+Δ \le t^{enter}_{j,s}+ M\,(1-x_{i,j})                 \tag{O1}
\]
\[
t^{exit}_{j,s}+Δ \le t^{enter}_{i,s}+ M\,x_{i,j}                     \tag{O2}
\]

Exactly one of the two inequalities is active; the binary \(x_{i,j}\) decides which train passes first.  
(For trains travelling in the same direction the same formulation can be used with \(\Delta=0\) if desired.)

#### 3.7  Energy definition (linear)  

\[
e_i=\sum_{s\in S_i}\sum_{k\in K}\bigl(a_s v_k^{2}+b_s v_k\bigr)\,z_{i,s,k}
\qquad \forall i\in I                                                     \tag{E}
\]

#### 3.8  Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& y_i \in\{0,1\} &&\forall i\in I\\
& x_{i,j} \in\{0,1\} &&\forall (i,j)\in\mathcal{P}\\
& z_{i,s,k} \in\{0,1\} &&\forall i,s,k\\
& t^{enter}_{i,s},\,t^{exit}_{i,s},\,t^{arr}_{i},\,e_i \ge 0 &&\forall i,s
\end{aligned}
\tag{D}
\]

---

### 4.  Full MILP (compact form)

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& w^{delay}\sum_{i}(t^{arr}_{i}-L_i)
      + w^{energy}\sum_{i}\sum_{s}\sum_{k}(a_s v_k^{2}+b_s v_k)z_{i,s,k}\\
\text{s.t. }&
\sum_{k}z_{i,s,k}=1 &&\forall i,s\\
&t^{exit}_{i,s}=t^{enter}_{i,s}+ \sum_{k}\tau_{s,k}z_{i,s,k} &&\forall i,s\\
&t^{enter}_{i,s}=t^{exit}_{i,\,pred(i,s)} &&\forall i,s\neq s^{origin}_i\\
&t^{arr}_{i}=t^{exit}_{i,\,s^{last}_i} &&\forall i\\
&t^{enter}_{i,d}\ge τ^{end}+M y_i &&\forall i,d\in D\\
&t^{exit}_{i,d}\le τ^{start}+M(1-y_i) &&\forall i,d\in D\\
&t^{exit}_{i,s}+Δ\le t^{enter}_{j,s}+M(1-x_{i,j}) &&\forall (i,j)\in\mathcal{P},\,s\in S_i\cap S_j\\
&t^{exit}_{j,s}+Δ\le t^{enter}_{i,s}+M x_{i,j} &&\forall (i,j)\in\mathcal{P},\,s\in S_i\cap S_j\\
&e_i=\sum_{s}\sum_{k}(a_s v_k^{2}+b_s v_k)z_{i,s,k} &&\forall i\\
&\text{binary / non‑negative domain constraints (D).}
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 5.  How to use the model  

1. **Data preparation** – build the train routes, compute \(\tau_{s,k}\) and the energy coefficients for each speed level, identify the disrupted segment(s) and the time window \([τ^{start},τ^{end}]\).  
2. **Implementation** – code the formulation in a MILP modelling language (Pyomo, GAMS, AMPL, JuMP, …).  
3. **Solve** – with any commercial/open‑source MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP). The model size is roughly \(|I|\times|S|\times|K|\) binary variables plus \(|\mathcal{P}|\) precedence binaries, which is tractable for realistic high‑speed networks.  
4. **Output** – the optimal schedule \((t^{enter},t^{exit})\), the rerouting decisions \(y_i\), the selected speed levels \(z_{i,s,k}\), and the resulting delays and energy consumptions.

---

**This MILP contains all required variables, a linear objective, and every physical constraint (time feasibility, speed‑level selection, blockage‑induced rerouting, head‑way safety, and energy linearisation) and is ready for direct implementation.**

Text:
**Variables**

*Continuous variables*  

\(A_{t,s}\) – arrival time of train \(t\) at the beginning of segment \(s\) (min)  

\(D_{t,s}\) – departure time of train \(t\) from the end of segment \(s\) (min)

*Binary variables*  

\(x_{t,s,k}\) – 1 if train \(t\) uses speed level \(k\in K\) on segment \(s\) (otherwise 0)  

\(y_{t,s}\) – 1 if train \(t\) is rerouted to the opposite track on the blocked segment \(s\) (otherwise 0)  

\(z_{t_1,t_2,s}\) – 1 if train \(t_1\) passes segment \(s\) before train \(t_2\) (otherwise 0)  

\(c_t\) – 1 if train \(t\) is cancelled (otherwise 0)

**Parameters (illustrative, to be filled with real data)**  

\(a^{0}_{t,s}\) – original scheduled arrival of train \(t\) at segment \(s\)  

\(d^{0}_{t,s}\) – original scheduled departure of train \(t\) from segment \(s\)  

\(\text{dwell}_{t,s}\) – minimum dwell time of train \(t\) at segment \(s\)  

\(L_{t,s},U_{t,s}\) – lower/upper bounds on travel time of train \(t\) on segment \(s\)  

\(t_k\) – travel time associated with speed level \(k\) on a normal track  

\(t^{\text{alt}}_k\) – travel time associated with speed level \(k\) when using the opposite track (rerouting)  

\(e_{t,s,k}\) – energy consumption of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) when speed level \(k\) is used  

\(M\) – a sufficiently large constant (big‑M)  

\(s^{\text{blk}}\) – the segment that is partially blocked  

\([\tau^{\text{start}},\tau^{\text{end}}]\) – disruption time window on the blocked segment  

\(w^{\text{delay}},w^{\text{energy}}\) – weighting coefficients in the objective

**Objective function**

\[
\min\; 
w^{\text{delay}}\;\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(A_{t,s^{\text{last}}}-a^{0}_{t,s^{\text{last}}}\bigr)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
w^{\text{energy}}\;\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} e_{t,s,k}\,x_{t,s,k}}_{\text{total energy}}
\]

where \(s^{\text{last}}\) denotes the last segment of the route.

**Constraints**

1. **Time propagation (arrival → dwell → departure → travel)**  

   \[
   D_{t,s}=A_{t,s}+ \text{dwell}_{t,s}+M\,c_t \qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S
   \]

   For every non‑last segment \(s\) (let \(s'\) be its successor):

   \[
   A_{t,s'} = D_{t,s}
   +\bigl(1-y_{t,s}\bigr)\sum_{k\in K} t_k\,x_{t,s,k}
   +y_{t,s}\sum_{k\in K} t^{\text{alt}}_k\,x_{t,s,k}
   +M\,c_t
   \qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\neq s^{\text{last}}
   \]

2. **Exactly one speed level per train‑segment**  

   \[
   \sum_{k\in K} x_{t,s,k}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S
   \]

3. **Travel‑time bounds**  

   \[
   L_{t,s}\le \sum_{k\in K} t_k\,x_{t,s,k}\le U_{t,s}
   \qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S
   \]

4. **Rerouting only on the blocked segment**  

   \[
   y_{t,s}=0 \qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\neq s^{\text{blk}}
   \]

   (If the disruption window is modelled explicitly, an additional constraint
   \(y_{t,s^{\text{blk}}}\le 1\) is sufficient; the binary nature already limits it.)

5. **Conflict avoidance on a shared track**  

   For every unordered pair of trains \((t_1,t_2)\) on the same segment \(s\):

   *Exactly one order*  

   \[
   z_{t_1,t_2,s}+z_{t_2,t_1,s}\ge 1-c_{t_1}-c_{t_2},
   \qquad
   z_{t_1,t_2,s}+z_{t_2,t_1,s}\le 1
   \]

   *Big‑M linking order to times*  

   \[
   A_{t_2,s}\ge D_{t_1,s}-M\bigl(1-z_{t_1,t_2,s}\bigr)-M\bigl(c_{t_1}+c_{t_2}\bigr)
   \]

   \[
   A_{t_1,s}\ge D_{t_2,s}-M\bigl(1-z_{t_2,t_1,s}\bigr)-M\bigl(c_{t_1}+c_{t_2}\bigr)
   \qquad\forall t_1\neq t_2,\;s\in S
   \]

6. **Cancellation handling**  

   \[
   A_{t,s}\le M\,(1-c_t),\qquad
   D_{t,s}\le M\,(1-c_t)\qquad\forall t\in T,\;s\in S
   \]

   (If \(c_t=1\), the times are forced to a large value so the train never interferes.)

7. **Variable domains**  

   \[
   A_{t,s},D_{t,s}\ge 0,\qquad
   x_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\},\;
   y_{t,s}\in\{0,1\},\;
   z_{t_1,t_2,s}\in\{0,1\},\;
   c_t\in\{0,1\}
   \]

**Assumptions (explicitly stated)**  

* The set of speed levels \(K\) and their associated travel times are the same for all trains; they can be made train‑/segment‑specific if required.  
* Dwell times are given and must be respected; they are independent of speed choice.  
* The disruption affects only one segment \(s^{\text{blk}}\) and a known time window; trains may be rerouted on that segment (binary \(y_{t,s^{\text{blk}}}\)).  
* Energy consumption is linear in the chosen speed level (parameter \(e_{t,s,k}\)).  
* Big‑M \(M\) is chosen larger than any feasible arrival/departure time in the planning horizon.  
* Cancellation is allowed; cancelled trains do not contribute to delay or energy and are excluded from conflict constraints via the \(c_t\) terms.  

The model above fully captures the integrated train‑rescheduling and speed‑management problem under a partial‑segment blockage, including bidirectional conflict resolution, speed‑level selection, rerouting decisions, delay minimisation, and energy‑efficiency.

Text:
**Mixed‑Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial‑segment blockages**

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(\mathcal I\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(i\). |
| \(\mathcal R_i\) | Feasible routes for train \(i\); a route \(r\in\mathcal R_i\) is an ordered list of track segments. |
| \(\mathcal S\) | Set of all track segments, indexed by \(s\). |
| \(\mathcal S_{i,r}\) | Segments belonging to route \(r\) of train \(i\). |
| \(\mathcal K\) | Set of admissible speed levels, indexed by \(k\) (e.g. slow / normal / fast). |
| \(\mathcal T\) | Discrete time intervals of the planning horizon, indexed by \(\tau\). |
| \(\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal S\) | Segments that are partially blocked; for each \(s\in\mathcal B\) a blockage window \([B^{\text{start}}_s,\;B^{\text{end}}_s]\) is known. |
| \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal S\) | Set of stations (segments where a train may dwell). |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(L_s\) | Length of segment \(s\) (km). |
| \(v_k\) | Nominal speed for level \(k\) (km/h). |
| \(e_k\) | Energy consumption (or cost) per km when travelling at speed level \(k\). |
| \(\hat d_i,\;\hat a_i\) | Scheduled departure / arrival times of train \(i\) (baseline timetable). |
| \(D^{\max}_i\) | Maximum permissible delay for train \(i\) (optional). |
| \(C_s\) | Capacity of segment \(s\) (max number of trains occupying it simultaneously). |
| \(\delta_{i,p}\) | Minimum dwell time required for train \(i\) at station \(p\). |
| \(M\) | Large constant for big‑M linearisation. |
| \(\Delta\tau\) | Length of a time interval \(\tau\). |
| \(\alpha,\;\beta\ge 0\) | Weights for delay and energy in the objective. |
| \(T^{\text{horizon}}\) | Length of the planning horizon (same unit as times). |

---

### 3. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| \(y_{i,r}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train \(i\) uses route \(r\in\mathcal R_i\). |
| \(d_i\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Actual departure time of train \(i\). |
| \(a_i\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Actual arrival time of train \(i\). |
| \(t_{i,s}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | Travel time of train \(i\) on segment \(s\) (0 if segment not used). |
| \(v_{i,s,k}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ on segment \(s\) train \(i\) travels with speed level \(k\). |
| \(z_{i,\tau}^{(s)}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train \(i\) occupies segment \(s\) during interval \(\tau\). |
| \(o_{i,j,s}\) | binary | Ordering: 1 ⇔ train \(i\) passes segment \(s\) **before** train \(j\). |
| \(w_{i,p}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train \(i\) stops (dwells) at station \(p\). |

---

### 4. Objective function  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
\alpha\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\bigl(a_i-\hat a_i\bigr)
\;+\;
\beta\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}
e_k\,L_s\,v_{i,s,k}
}
\tag{Obj}
\]

*First term = total passenger delay, second term = total energy consumption (linear because \(v_{i,s,k}\) are binary).*

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Route‑selection  
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_i} y_{i,r}=1 \qquad\forall i\in\mathcal I \tag{R1}
\]

#### 5.2 Exactly one speed level on each used segment  
\[
\sum_{k\in\mathcal K} v_{i,s,k}= 
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_i}\mathbf{1}_{\{s\in\mathcal S_{i,r}\}}\,y_{i,r}
\qquad\forall i\in\mathcal I,\; \forall s\in\mathcal S \tag{R2}
\]

#### 5.3 Travel time as a function of speed level  
\[
t_{i,s}= \sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\frac{L_s}{v_k}\;v_{i,s,k}
\qquad\forall i,s \tag{R3}
\]

#### 5.4 Time‑flow (departure → arrival)  
\[
a_i = d_i + \sum_{s\in\mathcal S} t_{i,s}
\qquad\forall i\in\mathcal I \tag{R4}
\]

#### 5.5 Minimum dwell time at stations  
For every station \(p\) that train \(i\) must serve (set \(P_i\)):
\[
t_{i,p}= \delta_{i,p}\, w_{i,p}
\qquad\forall i,\; \forall p\in P_i \tag{R5}
\]
(where segment \(p\) represents the dwell portion of the station).

#### 5.6 Occupancy–capacity coupling  

*Link travel time to interval occupancy (a linear over‑approximation):*
\[
\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\Delta\tau\,z_{i,\tau}^{(s)}\;\ge\; t_{i,s}
\qquad\forall i,s \tag{R6a}
\]

*Capacity of each segment in each interval:*
\[
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I} z_{i,\tau}^{(s)}\;\le\; C_s
\qquad\forall s,\;\forall \tau\in\mathcal T \tag{R6b}
\]

#### 5.7 Blockage enforcement  

If segment \(s\in\mathcal B\) is blocked in interval \(\tau\subseteq[B^{\text{start}}_s,B^{\text{end}}_s]\):
\[
z_{i,\tau}^{(s)} = 0 \qquad\forall i,\; \forall s\in\mathcal B,\; \forall \tau\in\mathcal T\text{ with }\tau\subseteq[B^{\text{start}}_s,B^{\text{end}}_s] \tag{R7}
\]

(Consequently a train can only traverse a blocked segment if it selects a route that does not contain it – already enforced by (R2).)

#### 5.8 Conflict‑avoidance ordering on a shared segment  

For every unordered pair of trains \((i,j)\) that may use the same segment \(s\) (i.e. there exist routes where \(s\in\mathcal S_{i,r}\) and \(s\in\mathcal S_{j,r'}\)):

\[
\begin{aligned}
& d_i + \sum_{s'\in\text{pre}_{i}(s)} t_{i,s'} + t_{i,s}
\;\le\;
d_j + \sum_{s'\in\text{pre}_{j}(s)} t_{j,s'} \;+\; M\bigl(1-o_{i,j,s}\bigr)
\qquad\forall i<j,\; \forall s \tag{R8a}\\
& o_{i,j,s}+o_{j,i,s}=1 \qquad\forall i<j,\; \forall s \text{ used by both }i\text{ and }j \tag{R8b}
\end{aligned}
\]

\(\text{pre}_{i}(s)\) denotes the set of segments that train \(i\) traverses **before** reaching segment \(s\) on its selected route.  
Big‑M de‑activates the inequality when the corresponding ordering is not chosen; (R8b) forces a strict order.

#### 5.9 Maximum admissible delay (optional)  
\[
a_i - \hat a_i \le D^{\max}_i \qquad\forall i\in\mathcal I \tag{R9}
\]

#### 5.10 Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& y_{i,r}\in\{0,1\}, \quad v_{i,s,k}\in\{0,1\}, \quad
z_{i,\tau}^{(s)}\in\{0,1\}, \quad
o_{i,j,s}\in\{0,1\}, \quad
w_{i,p}\in\{0,1\} \\
& d_i,\; a_i,\; t_{i,s}\ge 0 \qquad\forall i,s .
\end{aligned}
\tag{R10}
\]

---

### 6. Model summary  

- **Decision space**: binary route choice, binary speed‑level per segment, binary occupancy/ordering variables, and continuous departure/arrival/travel times.  
- **Objective**: minimise a weighted sum of total passenger delay and total energy consumption.  
- **Core feasibility**: each train selects exactly one route and one speed level per travelled segment, respects dwell‑time requirements, never exceeds segment capacity, and never occupies a partially blocked segment during its blockage window.  
- **Bidirectional conflict resolution**: ordering variables plus big‑M constraints guarantee a conflict‑free passage on any shared segment.  
- **Linear**: all expressions are linear in the decision variables; therefore the model can be solved directly by any MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, SCIP, …).

The formulation captures the intertwined nature of **train rescheduling** (route, departure/arrival times) and **speed management** (speed‑level selection), while explicitly modelling the disruptive partial‑segment blockages that induce rerouting and bidirectional track‑sharing conflicts. Adjusting \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) lets planners balance punctuality against energy efficiency.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management Problem (TRSMP) – MILP formulation**

---

### 1. Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(I\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(i\). |
| \(S_i\) | Ordered list of stations (or way‑points) that train \(i\) must visit on any feasible route. |
| \(U\) | Set of track nodes (stations, junctions, …). |
| \(E\subseteq U\times U\) | Set of directed track segments \((u,v)\). |
| \(E^{\text{blk}}\subseteq E\) | Segments that are partially blocked during the disruption window \([T^{\text{start}},T^{\text{end}}]\). |
| \(R_i=\{0,1\}\) | Two possible routes for train \(i\): 0 = original, 1 = rerouted. |
| \(P_i^r\subseteq E\) | Set of directed segments belonging to route \(r\) of train \(i\). |
| \(C\) | Set of conflict triples \((i,j,uv)\) where trains \(i\) and \(j\) may occupy the same segment \((u,v)\) (including opposite directions). |
| \(A\) | Set of acceleration‑decision arcs (identical to \(E\)). |

---

### 2. Parameters  

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| \(L_{uv}\) | Length of segment \((u,v)\). | km |
| \(v^{\max}_{uv}\) | Speed limit on \((u,v)\). | km/h |
| \(\underline v_{uv},\overline v_{uv}\) | Minimum / maximum feasible average speed on \((u,v)\) (for linearisation). | km/h |
| \(\alpha_{uv},\beta_{uv}\) | Energy‑consumption coefficients: \(e_{i,uv}= \alpha_{uv}t_{i,uv}+ \beta_{uv}a^{\text{acc}}_{i,uv}\). | kWh/h, kWh |
| \(dw_{i,s}\) | Mandatory dwell time of train \(i\) at station \(s\). | min |
| \(M\) | Big‑M constant larger than any feasible time (e.g. 10 000 min). | min |
| \(w_i\) | Weight of train‑\(i\) delay in the objective. | – |
| \(\lambda\) | Weight of total energy consumption in the objective. | – |
| \(T^{\text{start}},T^{\text{end}}\) | Beginning and end of the disruption (blocked) interval. | min |
| \(p_i\) | Planned arrival time of train \(i\) at its final destination (baseline). | min |

*All parameters are assumed known.*

---

### 3. Decision Variables  

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(x_i^{r}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train \(i\) uses route \(r\) (0 = original, 1 = rerouted). |
| \(a_{i,s}\) | continuous \(\ge0\) | Arrival time of train \(i\) at station \(s\in S_i\). |
| \(d_{i,s}\) | continuous \(\ge0\) | Departure time of train \(i\) from station \(s\in S_i\). |
| \(t_{i,uv}\) | continuous \(\ge0\) | Travel time of train \(i\) on segment \((u,v)\). |
| \(e_{i,uv}\) | continuous \(\ge0\) | Energy consumed by train \(i\) on segment \((u,v)\). |
| \(a^{\text{acc}}_{i,uv}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train \(i\) uses the “accelerated’’ speed profile on \((u,v)\). |
| \(y_{ij,uv}\) | binary | Ordering variable for conflict pair \((i,j,uv)\): 1 ⇔ train \(i\) passes before train \(j\). |
| \(\delta_{i,uv}\) | binary | 1 ⇔ train \(i\) actually traverses segment \((u,v)\) (links travel‑time to the chosen route). |

---

### 4. Objective  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I} w_i\bigl(a_{i,\text{dest}(i)}-p_i\bigr)}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\lambda\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{(u,v)\in E} e_{i,uv}}_{\text{total weighted energy}}
}
\]

The first term penalises the deviation of the actual arrival time at the final destination from the planned schedule; the second term aggregates linearised energy consumption.

---

### 5. Constraints  

#### 5.1 Route choice (exactly one route per train)  
\[
\sum_{r\in\{0,1\}} x_i^{r}=1 \qquad\forall i\in I \tag{R1}
\]

#### 5.2 Link segment usage to the chosen route  

\[
\delta_{i,uv}\le \sum_{r\in\{0,1\}} \mathbf 1_{\{(u,v)\in P_i^{r}\}}\,x_i^{r}
\qquad\forall i\in I,\;(u,v)\in E \tag{R2}
\]

If a segment belongs to a route, the corresponding \(\delta_{i,uv}\) must be 1 when that route is selected (the converse follows from the binary nature of \(\delta\)).

#### 5.3 Time flow along the selected route  

\[
a_{i,v}\;\ge\; d_{i,u}+t_{i,uv}-M\,(1-\delta_{i,uv})
\qquad\forall i\in I,\;(u,v)\in E \tag{F1}
\]

When \(\delta_{i,uv}=0\) the big‑M term deactivates the constraint; otherwise it enforces the travel‑time relationship.

#### 5.4 Mandatory dwell time at stations  

\[
d_{i,s}=a_{i,s}+dw_{i,s}\qquad\forall i\in I,\;s\in S_i \tag{D1}
\]

#### 5.5 Linear speed‑profile envelope  

\[
t_{i,uv}\;\ge\; \frac{L_{uv}}{v^{\max}_{uv}}
      -a^{\text{acc}}_{i,uv}\Bigl(\frac{L_{uv}}{v^{\max}_{uv}}-\frac{L_{uv}}{\overline v_{uv}}\Bigr)
\qquad\forall i,\;(u,v)\in E \tag{S1}
\]

\[
t_{i,uv}\;\le\; \frac{L_{uv}}{\underline v_{uv}}
\qquad\forall i,\;(u,v)\in E \tag{S2}
\]

The binary \(a^{\text{acc}}_{i,uv}\) selects the lower bound (fast profile) or the higher bound (conservative profile).

#### 5.6 Energy linearisation  

\[
e_{i,uv}= \alpha_{uv}\,t_{i,uv}+ \beta_{uv}\,a^{\text{acc}}_{i,uv}
\qquad\forall i,\;(u,v)\in E \tag{E1}
\]

#### 5.7 Link travel‑time / energy to segment usage  

\[
t_{i,uv}\le M\,\delta_{i,uv}\qquad\forall i,\;(u,v)\in E \tag{L1}
\]

\[
e_{i,uv}\le M\,\delta_{i,uv}\qquad\forall i,\;(u,v)\in E \tag{L2}
\]

If a segment is not traversed (\(\delta_{i,uv}=0\)) both travel time and energy are forced to zero.

#### 5.8 Conflict‑avoidance on shared segments  

For each \((i,j,uv)\in C\):

\[
a_{i,v}\;\ge\; d_{j,u}-M\,(1-y_{ij,uv}) \tag{C1}
\]

\[
a_{j,v}\;\ge\; d_{i,u}-M\,y_{ij,uv} \tag{C2}
\]

If \(y_{ij,uv}=1\) train \(i\) must start after train \(j\) leaves; otherwise the opposite ordering holds.

#### 5.9 Disruption (blocked‑segment) constraints  

For every blocked segment \((b_1,b_2)\in E^{\text{blk}}\):

\[
a_{i,b_2}\;\ge\; T^{\text{end}}-M\,(1-x_i^{0}) \qquad\forall i\in I \tag{B1}
\]

\[
d_{i,b_1}\;\le\; T^{\text{start}}+M\,(1-x_i^{0}) \qquad\forall i\in I \tag{B2}
\]

If the original route is kept (\(x_i^{0}=1\)), the train must finish the blocked segment after the disruption window (or finish before it starts). When rerouted (\(x_i^{0}=0\)) the big‑M relaxes the constraints.

#### 5.10 Variable domains  

\[
x_i^{r},\;\delta_{i,uv},\;a^{\text{acc}}_{i,uv},\;y_{ij,uv}\in\{0,1\}
\qquad\forall i,r,uv,ij
\]

\[
a_{i,s},d_{i,s},t_{i,uv},e_{i,uv}\ge 0
\qquad\forall i,s,uv
\]

---

### 6. Complete Model  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{i\in I} w_i\bigl(a_{i,\text{dest}(i)}-p_i\bigr)
      +\lambda\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{(u,v)\in E} e_{i,uv} \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(R1)–(R2)} && \text{route selection and segment activation}\\
&\text{(F1)} && \text{time flow on chosen segments}\\
&\text{(D1)} && \text{mandatory dwell times}\\
&\text{(S1)–(S2)} && \text{linear speed‑profile envelope}\\
&\text{(E1)} && \text{energy linearisation}\\
&\text{(L1)–(L2)} && \text{link travel‑time/energy to usage}\\
&\text{(C1)–(C2)} && \text{conflict ordering on shared tracks}\\
&\text{(B1)–(B2)} && \text{blocked‑segment disruption window}\\
&\text{binary / non‑negativity constraints.}
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 7. Remarks & Assumptions  

1. **Big‑M** must be larger than the total planning horizon (e.g., 10 000 min).  
2. The speed‑profile envelope (S1‑S2) can be refined with additional break‑points for higher fidelity.  
3. Energy model (E1) is linear; quadratic terms can be linearised with extra binaries if needed.  
4. The disruption constraints force trains staying on the original route to wait until the blockage clears; alternative policies can be modelled by swapping the two inequalities.  
5. The formulation already captures the core TRSMP under partial segment blockages: route choice, timetable adjustment, speed‑profile selection, conflict resolution, delay minimisation and energy efficiency. Additional operational constraints (platform capacity, crew, rolling‑stock) can be added analogously.  

This MILP can be directly supplied to any commercial (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress) or open‑source (CBC, SCIP) solver to obtain an optimal integrated schedule and speed plan for the disrupted high‑speed railway network.
