Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP)  
Partial‑Segment‑Blockage Disruption Scenario**  

---

### 1.  Index Sets, Parameters and Assumptions  

| Symbol | Meaning | Remarks / Assumptions |
|--------|---------|-----------------------|
| **\(T\)** | Set of trains, \(|T|=N_T\) | All trains that are scheduled to run during the disruption horizon. |
| **\(S\)** | Set of stations (including the two end‑stations of every line). |
| **\(L\)** | Set of line‑segments (track sections) between two consecutive stations. |
| **\(B\subseteq L\)** | Set of *blocked* segments (the disruption area). |
| **\(K\)** | Set of discrete *speed‑profile* plans that can be assigned to a train on a given segment.  (Plans are generated a‑priori by a lower‑level speed‑profile generator; each plan is feasible w.r.t. train dynamics, acceleration/deceleration limits, and energy consumption.) |
| **\(P_{t,\ell}\subseteq K\)** | Feasible speed‑plan indices for train \(t\) on segment \(\ell\). |
| **\(d_{t,s}\)** | Original (pre‑disruption) scheduled departure time of train \(t\) from station \(s\). |
| **\(a_{t,s}\)** | Original scheduled arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\). |
| **\(\underline{t}^{\text{run}}_{\ell}\), \(\overline{t}^{\text{run}}_{\ell}\)** | Minimum / maximum admissible running time on segment \(\ell\) (derived from physical limits). |
| **\(\underline{t}^{\text{dwell}}_{t,s}\), \(\overline{t}^{\text{dwell}}_{t,s}\)** | Minimum / maximum dwell time for train \(t\) at station \(s\) (including passenger boarding/alighting). |
| **\(M\)** | A “big‑M’’ constant larger than any feasible time value (e.g. 10 000 s). |
| **\(E_{k}\)** | Energy consumption (kWh) of speed‑plan \(k\) on the corresponding segment (pre‑computed). |
| **\(C^{\text{delay}}_{t,s}\)** | Penalty cost (e.g. €) for a unit of delay of train \(t\) at station \(s\). |
| **\(C^{\text{cancel}}_{t}\)** | Fixed cost for cancelling train \(t\). |
| **\(C^{\text{reroute}}_{t}\)** | Fixed cost for using the opposite track (i.e., rerouting) for train \(t\) on a blocked segment. |
| **\(T^{\text{horizon}}\)** | Planning horizon (e.g., the last scheduled departure time). |

**Assumptions (explicitly stated)**  

1. **Deterministic disruption window** – each blocked segment \(\ell\in B\) is unavailable for the whole interval \([T^{\text{start}}_{\ell},T^{\text{end}}_{\ell}]\).  
2. **Binary routing decision** – a train can either use the original (unidirectional) track or the opposite track on a blocked segment; the opposite track is assumed to be free of other scheduled traffic except the trains that we also decide to reroute.  
3. **Pre‑generated speed‑plans** – for each train‑segment pair a finite set of feasible speed‑profiles (indexed by \(k\)) is known; the MILP only selects one of them.  
4. **No overtaking** – trains keep their order on a given track direction; overtaking is prohibited (common for high‑speed lines).  
5. **Energy is additive** – total energy consumption is the sum of the selected plan energies.  
6. **All time variables are continuous (seconds).**  

---

### 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,\ell,k}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) traverses segment \(\ell\) using speed‑plan \(k\in P_{t,\ell}\); 0 otherwise. |
| \(r_{t,\ell}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) **reroutes** (uses opposite track) on blocked segment \(\ell\in B\); 0 otherwise. |
| \(c_t\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) is **cancelled**; 0 otherwise. |
| \(a_{t,s}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Actual arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(s\). |
| \(d_{t,s}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Actual departure time of train \(t\) from station \(s\). |
| \(z_{t,\ell}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Actual running time of train \(t\) on segment \(\ell\). |
| \(\delta_{t,s}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Delay of train \(t\) at station \(s\) w.r.t. the original schedule, i.e. \(\delta_{t,s}=a_{t,s}-a_{t,s}^{\text{orig}}\). |
| \(\theta_{t,\ell}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) occupies segment \(\ell\) (any direction) at any time (used for conflict constraints). |
| \(\phi_{t,\ell}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) occupies segment \(\ell\) **in the original direction**; 0 if opposite direction (only relevant for \(\ell\in B\)). |

---

### 3.  Objective Function  

We minimise a weighted sum of (i) total passenger‑delay cost, (ii) energy consumption, (iii) cancellation cost and (iv) rerouting cost.

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & 
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} C^{\text{delay}}_{t,s}\,\delta_{t,s}}_{\text{Delay penalty}} 
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L}\sum_{k\in P_{t,\ell}} E_k\,x_{t,\ell,k}}_{\text{Energy consumption}}\\[2mm]
&\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} C^{\text{cancel}}_{t}\,c_t}_{\text{Cancellation cost}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell\in B} C^{\text{reroute}}_{t}\,r_{t,\ell}}_{\text{Rerouting cost}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

All coefficients are non‑negative; the model can be easily adapted to a **lexicographic** (multi‑objective) approach by assigning very large weights to higher‑priority terms (e.g., cancellations).

---

### 4.  Core Constraints  

#### 4.1  Train‑cancellation coupling  

\[
\begin{aligned}
& a_{t,s} \le M\,(1-c_t) \qquad &&\forall t\in T,\; \forall s\in S,\\
& d_{t,s} \le M\,(1-c_t) \qquad &&\forall t\in T,\; \forall s\in S,\\
& x_{t,\ell,k} \le 1-c_t \qquad &&\forall t,\ell,k,\\
& r_{t,\ell} \le 1-c_t \qquad &&\forall t,\ell\in B .
\end{aligned}
\]

If a train is cancelled (\(c_t=1\)), all timing and routing variables are forced to zero.

#### 4.2  Selection of exactly one speed‑plan per traversed segment  

\[
\sum_{k\in P_{t,\ell}} x_{t,\ell,k}= \theta_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;\forall \ell\in L .
\]

\[
\theta_{t,\ell}\in\{0,1\}.
\]

If a train does not travel on segment \(\ell\) (\(\theta_{t,\ell}=0\)), no plan is selected.

#### 4.3  Rerouting logic on blocked segments  

\[
r_{t,\ell}\le \theta_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;\forall \ell\in B .
\]

\[
\phi_{t,\ell}= \theta_{t,\ell} - r_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;\forall \ell\in B .
\]

Thus \(\phi_{t,\ell}=1\) if the train uses the original direction, \(\phi_{t,\ell}=0\) if it uses the opposite direction.

#### 4.4  Running‑time definition from selected speed‑plan  

Each plan \(k\) carries a deterministic running time \(\tau_{t,\ell,k}\) (pre‑computed from the speed profile).  

\[
z_{t,\ell}= \sum_{k\in P_{t,\ell}} \tau_{t,\ell,k}\,x_{t,\ell,k}\qquad\forall t,\ell .
\]

Running time must respect physical bounds (redundant but useful for model robustness):

\[
\underline{t}^{\text{run}}_{\ell}\,\theta_{t,\ell}\le z_{t,\ell}\le\overline{t}^{\text{run}}_{\ell}\,\theta_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t,\ell .
\]

#### 4.5  Temporal linking between stations and segments  

For every train \(t\) and every pair of consecutive stations \((s,s')\) connected by segment \(\ell\):

\[
a_{t,s'} = d_{t,s} + z_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;\forall \ell=(s,s')\in L .
\]

#### 4.6  Dwell‑time limits  

\[
\underline{t}^{\text{dwell}}_{t,s}\,\theta_{t,\ell_{in}(s)} \le d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \le \overline{t}^{\text{dwell}}_{t,s}\,\theta_{t,\ell_{in}(s)}\qquad\forall t,\; \forall s\in S .
\]

\(\ell_{in}(s)\) denotes the segment arriving at station \(s\) (or a dummy “zero‑length’’ segment for the first station).

#### 4.7  Delay definition  

\[
\delta_{t,s}= a_{t,s} - a^{\text{orig}}_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,\; \forall s\in S .
\]

\(\delta_{t,s}\ge 0\) is enforced implicitly by the objective (penalising negative values would be meaningless, thus we also add a non‑negativity constraint if desired).

#### 4.8  Conflict‑avoidance on **any** track direction  

Two trains that occupy the same physical segment (regardless of direction) must not overlap in time.  
Let  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Enter}_{t,\ell}= d_{t,s_{\text{tail}}(\ell)} \quad (\text{departure from the upstream station}),\\
&\text{Exit}_{t,\ell}= a_{t,s_{\text{head}}(\ell)} \quad (\text{arrival at the downstream station}).
\end{aligned}
\]

Introduce binary ordering variables for each unordered pair of trains \((t,t')\) on segment \(\ell\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\beta_{t,t',\ell}\in\{0,1\}\qquad\forall t<t',\;\forall \ell\in L .
\end{aligned}
\]

Conflict‑free constraints (big‑M formulation):

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Enter}_{t,\ell} \ge \text{Exit}_{t',\ell} - M\,(1-\beta_{t,t',\ell}) \qquad\forall t<t',\;\forall \ell,\\
&\text{Enter}_{t',\ell} \ge \text{Exit}_{t,\ell} - M\,\beta_{t,t',\ell} \qquad\forall t<t',\;\forall \ell,\\
&\beta_{t,t',\ell} \le \theta_{t,\ell} \quad,\quad \beta_{t,t',\ell} \le \theta_{t',\ell} \qquad\forall t<t',\;\forall \ell .
\end{aligned}
\]

If either train does not use the segment (\(\theta=0\)), the ordering variable is forced to 0 and the constraints become non‑binding.

#### 4.9  Bidirectional‑track capacity on blocked segments  

When a blocked segment is used in the opposite direction, the capacity of that track is reduced because the original direction trains may still occupy it. We enforce that at any time **at most one** train (in any direction) can be on the opposite track:

\[
\sum_{t\in T} r_{t,\ell} \le 1 \qquad\forall \ell\in B .
\]

(If the opposite track can host multiple trains, replace “1’’ by the known capacity.)

#### 4.10  Logical coupling between routing and plan selection on blocked segments  

A train that reroutes must use a speed‑plan that is feasible on the opposite track. This is captured by defining a separate set of feasible plans \(P^{\text{opp}}_{t,\ell}\) for the opposite direction and adding:

\[
\sum_{k\in P^{\text{opp}}_{t,\ell}} x_{t,\ell,k} \ge r_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t,\;\forall \ell\in B .
\]

Similarly, if the train stays on the original direction:

\[
\sum_{k\in P^{\text{orig}}_{t,\ell}} x_{t,\ell,k} \ge \phi_{t,\ell}\qquad\forall t,\;\forall \ell\in B .
\]

---

### 5.  Complete MILP Formulation  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ll}
\displaystyle \min\limits_{x,r,c,a,d,z,\delta,\theta,\phi,\beta} &
\displaystyle \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} C^{\text{delay}}_{t,s}\,\delta_{t,s}
      +\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L}\sum_{k\in P_{t,\ell}} E_k\,x_{t,\ell,k}
      +\sum_{t\in T} C^{\text{cancel}}_{t}\,c_t
      +\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell\in B} C^{\text{reroute}}_{t}\,r_{t,\ell} \\[4mm]
\text{s.t.} &
\text{(4.1)–(4.10) listed above} \\[2mm]
& x_{t,\ell,k}\in\{0,1\},\; r_{t,\ell}\in\{0,1\},\; c_t\in\{0,1\},\;
   \beta_{t,t',\ell}\in\{0,1\},\\
& \theta_{t,\ell},\phi_{t,\ell}\in\{0,1\},\\
& a_{t,s},d_{t,s},z_{t,\ell},\delta_{t,s}\ge 0\qquad\forall t,\ell,s .
\end{array}
}
\]

---

### 6.  Discussion of Model Features  

| Feature | How it is captured in the MILP |
|---------|--------------------------------|
| **Partial‑segment blockage** | Set \(B\) marks blocked segments; binary variables \(r_{t,\ell}\) allow a train to switch to the opposite track only on those segments. |
| **Rerouting cost & capacity** | Term \(C^{\text{reroute}}_{t} r_{t,\ell}\) in the objective; constraint \(\sum_t r_{t,\ell}\le 1\) (or a capacity parameter) limits simultaneous opposite‑track usage. |
| **Integrated speed‑profile selection** | Variables \(x_{t,\ell,k}\) choose exactly one pre‑computed speed plan per traversed segment; the selected plan supplies the running time \(\tau_{t,\ell,k}\) and energy \(E_k\). |
| **Delay & energy co‑optimisation** | Delay penalties appear in the objective via \(\delta_{t,s}\); energy appears via the sum of selected plan energies. |
| **Cancellation** | Binary \(c_t\) deactivates all timing, routing and speed‑plan variables for a cancelled train, incurring a fixed penalty. |
| **Conflict‑free operation** | Big‑M ordering variables \(\beta_{t,t',\ell}\) enforce that any two trains using the same physical segment do not overlap in time, irrespective of direction. |
| **Bidirectional conflict on blocked segments** | The opposite‑track capacity constraint together with the ordering constraints guarantee that a train using the opposite direction does not clash with any train still on the original direction. |
| **Physical feasibility** | Minimum/maximum running‑time and dwell‑time bounds, as well as the pre‑computed feasible speed‑plan sets, guarantee that any feasible solution respects train dynamics and operational rules. |

---

### 7.  Remarks on Solving the MILP  

* The model is **mixed‑integer linear** because all non‑linearities have been linearised (e.g., the product of binary and continuous variables appears only in big‑M constraints).  
* The number of binary variables grows with \(|T|\times|L|\times|K|\) (speed‑plan selection) and with \(|T|^2\times|L|\) (conflict ordering). In practice, the **decomposition** described in the source paper (IP for train interactions + single‑train speed‑plan sub‑problems) can be reproduced by:  
  1. Solving a master IP that decides \(\theta_{t,\ell}, r_{t,\ell}, c_t\) and the ordering \(\beta\).  
  2. For each train, generating the set of feasible plans \(P_{t,\ell}\) consistent with the master decisions (this is a **plan‑selection** problem, linear because the master fixes which direction the train must use).  
  3. Adding Benders‑type cuts or column‑generation constraints to the master to eliminate infeasible plan combinations.  
* The **adaptive iterative algorithm** (plan‑granularity refinement) can be implemented by initially limiting \(K\) to a coarse set (e.g., only “slow”, “nominal”, “fast” profiles) and enriching the set locally around the current solution.  
* Commercial solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress) handle the presented MILP up to medium‑size networks (≈ 50 – 100 trains, 30 – 40 segments) within minutes; for larger instances the decomposition is essential.  

---

**End of formulation**. The model above is self‑contained, linear, and ready to be encoded in any MILP modelling language (AMPL, GAMS, Pyomo, JuMP, …). All missing data (e.g., exact running times \(\tau_{t,\ell,k}\), energy values \(E_k\), big‑M constant) are indicated as parameters that must be supplied from the railway’s operational database or from a lower‑level speed‑profile generator.

Now write the filled-in form for the text above as one JSON object, without code fences and without repeating the template.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling & Speed‑Management MILP (Partial‑Segment Blockage)**  

---

### 1️⃣ Sets  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** = {1,…,|T|} | Trains to be scheduled |
| **N** = {1,…,|N|} | Network nodes (stations, junctions) |
| **A** ⊆ N×N | Directed arcs (track sections) |
| **B** ⊂ A | Arcs that are **partially blocked** (only part of the cross‑section usable) |
| **U\_{ij}** | Set of **sub‑segments** of arc (i,j):  *approach*, *blocked part*, *exit* (or a bypass side‑track). For an unblocked arc |U\_{ij}| = {0}. |
| **S** = {1,…,|S|} | Discrete **speed levels** (ordered, e.g. 30, 60, 90 km/h) |
| **K** = {0,…,K\_max} | Discrete time slots (e.g. 1‑min slots) |
| **P** ⊆ A | Set of **bidirectional arc pairs** (i,j) and (j,i) that share the same physical track |

---

### 2️⃣ Parameters  

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| τ\_i | Scheduled departure time of train *i* (baseline) |
| π\_i | Scheduled arrival time of train *i* at its final destination |
| L\_{ij}^u | Length of sub‑segment *u* of arc (i,j) |
| d\_{ij}^{s} = L\_{ij}^u / v^{s} | **Travel time** of sub‑segment *u* when speed level *s* is used |
| e\_{ij}^{s} = c^{s}·L\_{ij}^u | **Energy** consumption of sub‑segment *u* at speed level *s* (c^{s}: energy coefficient) |
| α, β | Positive weights for total delay and total energy in the objective |
| Δ\_b | Capacity of a blocked sub‑segment (usually 1 train) |
| U\_min , U\_max | Minimum / maximum dwell time at a scheduled stop |
| a\_i^{max}, a\_i^{min} | Max / min admissible **acceleration** (expressed as change of speed‑level index per time slot) |
| M | Big‑M constant (larger than the planning horizon) |
| T\_max | Upper bound on the planning horizon (e.g. 1440 min for a day) |
| t^{open}\_{ij}, t^{close}\_{ij} | Earliest and latest time the blocked part of arc (i,j) can be occupied |

---

### 3️⃣ Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **x\_{i,k}** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* departs its origin at the beginning of time slot *k* |
| **y\_{i,ij}^{k,s}** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* traverses sub‑segment *u* of arc (i,j) **starting** in slot *k* with speed level *s* |
| **t\_{i,n}** ≥ 0 | continuous | Arrival time of train *i* at node *n* |
| **δ\_{i,n}** ≥ 0 | continuous | Dwell time of train *i* at node *n* (only for scheduled stops) |
| **p\_{i,k}** ≥ 0 | continuous | **Speed‑level index** of train *i* in slot *k* (used to enforce acceleration limits) |
| **z\_{i,k}** ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* occupies any blocked sub‑segment in slot *k* (derived from y) |

---

### 4️⃣ Objective  

\[
\min \; 
\underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i\in T}\bigl(t_{i,\text{dest}}-\pi_i\bigr)}_{\text{Total delay (min)}}
\;+\; 
\underbrace{\beta \sum_{(i,j)\in A}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} e_{ij}^{s}\; y_{i,ij}^{k,s}}_{\text{Total energy (kWh)}}
\]

*The first term penalises passenger delay; the second term penalises energy use. The weights α, β are chosen by the planner.*

---

### 5️⃣ Constraints  

#### 5.1 Departure – schedule coupling  
\[
\sum_{k\in K} k\,x_{i,k}\;\ge\;\tau_i \qquad\forall i\in T     \tag{C1}
\]

\[
t_{i,\text{origin}} = \sum_{k\in K} k\,x_{i,k}\qquad\forall i\in T     \tag{C2}
\]

#### 5.2 Flow (route continuity) – each train must select exactly one sub‑segment for every arc it traverses  

For every train *i* and arc (m,n) belonging to its planned node sequence **P\_i**:

\[
\sum_{u\in U_{mn}}\;\sum_{k\in K}\;\sum_{s\in S} y_{i,mn}^{k,s}=1\qquad\forall i,\;(m,n)\in P_i   \tag{C3}
\]

(The binary y forces exactly one sub‑segment, one start‑time, and one speed level.)

#### 5.3 Time feasibility on a traversed sub‑segment  

If train *i* starts sub‑segment *u* of arc (m,n) in slot *k* with speed *s* then the arrival at node *n* must respect the travel time:

\[
t_{i,n}\;\ge\; t_{i,m}+d_{mn}^{s}\;-\;M\bigl(1-y_{i,mn}^{k,s}\bigr)
\qquad\forall i,m,n,u,k,s   \tag{C4}
\]

\[
t_{i,m}\;\le\; k\;+\;M\bigl(1-y_{i,mn}^{k,s}\bigr)
\qquad\forall i,m,n,u,k,s   \tag{C5}
\]

#### 5.4 Dwell‑time limits at scheduled stations  

\[
U_{\min}\;\le\;\delta_{i,n}\;\le\;U_{\max}
\qquad\forall i,\;n\in\text{stop\_nodes}_i   \tag{C6}
\]

\[
t_{i,n}^{\text{depart}} = t_{i,n}^{\text{arr}} + \delta_{i,n}
\qquad\forall i,\;n\in\text{stop\_nodes}_i   \tag{C7}
\]

(In the model the departure time is simply the arrival time of the next traversed arc; the above relation is enforced through (C4)–(C5).)

#### 5.5 Partial‑blockage capacity  

Only Δ\_b trains may occupy a blocked sub‑segment *b* simultaneously:

\[
\sum_{i\in T}\;\sum_{s\in S}\;\sum_{k\in K} y_{i,b}^{k,s}\;\le\;\Delta_{b}
\qquad\forall b\in B,\;\forall k\in K   \tag{C8}
\]

#### 5.6 Blockage‑time window  

A blocked sub‑segment can be used only inside its allowed interval:

\[
t^{open}_{ij}\;\le\; t_{i,m}+d_{ij}^{s}
\;+\;M\bigl(1-y_{i,ij}^{k,s}\bigr)
\qquad\forall i,(i,j)\in B,\;k,s   \tag{C9}
\]

\[
t_{i,m}+d_{ij}^{s}\;\le\; t^{close}_{ij}
\;+\;M\bigl(1-y_{i,ij}^{k,s}\bigr)
\qquad\forall i,(i,j)\in B,\;k,s   \tag{C10}
\]

#### 5.7 Bidirectional conflict (head‑on avoidance)  

For every pair of opposite arcs (i,j) and (j,i) that share the same physical track:

\[
\sum_{s\in S}\;y_{i,ij}^{k,s}
\;+\;
\sum_{s\in S}\;y_{i,ji}^{k,s}
\;\le\;1
\qquad\forall k\in K,\;(i,j)\in P   \tag{C11}
\]

If the line is double‑track but one lane is blocked, the RHS becomes the number of still‑available lanes (typically 1).

#### 5.8 Speed‑level index and acceleration limits  

Introduce a continuous index **p\_{i,k}** that equals the chosen speed‑level number (1 = slowest, |S| = fastest). The binary y forces p to match the selected level:

\[
p_{i,k}\;\ge\; s\;-\;M\bigl(1-y_{i,ij}^{k,s}\bigr)
\qquad\forall i,(i,j),k,s   \tag{C12a}
\]

\[
p_{i,k}\;\le\; s\;+\;M\bigl(1-y_{i,ij}^{k,s}\bigr)
\qquad\forall i,(i,j),k,s   \tag{C12b}
\]

Acceleration (or deceleration) limits between two consecutive slots:

\[
a_i^{\min}\;\le\; p_{i,k+1}-p_{i,k}\;\le\;a_i^{\max}
\qquad\forall i,\;k=0,\dots,K-1   \tag{C13}
\]

(The bounds are expressed in “speed‑level change per slot”; they can be calibrated from physical a\_i^{max/min}.)

#### 5.9 Upper bound on all times  

\[
0\;\le\; t_{i,n}\;\le\;T_{\max}\qquad\forall i,n   \tag{C14}
\]

---

### 6️⃣ Model Summary  

* **Decision variables** – binary route‑choice & start‑time variables `y`, departure‑time binaries `x`, continuous arrival times `t`, dwell times `δ`, speed‑level index `p`.  
* **Objective** – weighted sum of total passenger delay and total energy consumption.  
* **Constraints** – enforce (i) schedule feasibility, (ii) flow continuity, (iii) dwell‑time limits, (iv) capacity of the partially blocked segment, (v) admissible time window for the blocked part, (vi) head‑on avoidance on bidirectional track, (vii) linear acceleration limits via the speed‑level index, (viii) big‑M linking of binaries to continuous quantities.  

All constraints are **linear**, and the only integer decisions are the binaries `x` and `y`. Hence the formulation is a **mixed‑integer linear program (MILP)** that can be handed directly to any MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, CBC, …).  

The optimal solution provides, for each train:  

* exact departure time from the origin,  
* the chosen sub‑segment (bypass or blocked lane) for every possibly‑blocked arc,  
* the exact start‑time and speed level on each traversed sub‑segment (hence a feasible speed profile),  
* the induced dwell times,  
* the resulting total delay and energy consumption.  

This model captures the integrated nature of the **train‑rescheduling‑and‑speed‑management problem (TRSMP)** under partial‑segment blockages, resolves bidirectional conflicts, respects physical acceleration limits, and simultaneously optimises punctuality and energy efficiency.

Text:
**Variables**

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| \(x_{t,n}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | arrival time of train \(t\) at station \(n\) (minutes) |
| \(y_{t,n}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | departure time of train \(t\) from station \(n\) (minutes) |
| \(z_{t,s}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) uses segment \(s\) (original or opposite track) |
| \(v_{t,s,\tau}\) | binary | 1 if train \(t\) occupies segment \(s\) during time period \(\tau\) |
| \(p_{t,s,\tau}\) | continuous, \(\ge 0\) | speed of train \(t\) on segment \(s\) during period \(\tau\) (km/h) |

**Parameters (assumed known)**  

- \(a^{0}_{t,n}\) – original scheduled arrival of train \(t\) at station \(n\).  
- \(d^{0}_{t,n}\) – original scheduled departure of train \(t\) from station \(n\).  
- \(\text{dwell}_{t,n}\) – mandatory dwell time at station \(n\) for train \(t\).  
- \(\Delta\tau\) – length of one discretised time period (minutes).  
- \(\mathcal{T}\) – set of time periods \(\tau\).  
- \(\mathcal{S}\) – set of track segments (including opposite‑track alternatives).  
- \(\mathcal{R}_{t,n}\subseteq\mathcal{S}\) – ordered list of segments that constitute the path from station \(n\) to \(n+1\) for train \(t\).  
- \(\mathcal{G}_{t,g}\subseteq\mathcal{S}\) – set of alternative segments (original vs opposite) belonging to routing group \(g\) for train \(t\).  
- \(\text{cap}_s\) – maximum number of trains that can occupy segment \(s\) simultaneously.  
- \(\text{minTravel}_{t,s}\) – minimum feasible travel time on segment \(s\) for train \(t\) (minutes).  
- \(e_{t,s}\) – energy coefficient (energy per km/h) for train \(t\) on segment \(s\).  
- \(B_s\in\{0,1\}\) – 1 if segment \(s\) is blocked (partial blockage).  
- \(v^{\max}_s, v^{\min}_s\) – speed limits on segment \(s\).  
- \([ \tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}} ]\) – disruption time window (same for all blocked segments; can be made segment‑specific).  

**Objective function**

\[
\min \; 
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{n\in\mathcal{N}}\bigl(x_{t,n}-a^{0}_{t,n}\bigr)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} e_{t,s}\,p_{t,s,\tau}\,\Delta\tau}_{\text{total energy consumption}}
\]

(Weights can be introduced if desired.)

**Constraints**

1. **Dwell‑time consistency**  
   \[
   y_{t,n}=x_{t,n}+\text{dwell}_{t,n}\qquad\forall t,\; n
   \]

2. **Travel‑time linking between successive stations**  
   For every train \(t\) and station \(n\) (except the last):
   \[
   x_{t,n+1}\;\ge\; y_{t,n}
   +\sum_{s\in\mathcal{R}_{t,n}}\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} v_{t,s,\tau}\,\Delta\tau
   \]

3. **Minimum travel time on a chosen segment**  
   \[
   \sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} v_{t,s,\tau}\,\Delta\tau\;\ge\;\text{minTravel}_{t,s}\;z_{t,s}
   \qquad\forall t,\; s
   \]

4. **Segment capacity per time period**  
   \[
   \sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} v_{t,s,\tau}\;\le\;\text{cap}_s\qquad\forall s,\; \tau\in\mathcal{T}
   \]

5. **Blockage (no occupation during disruption)**  
   \[
   v_{t,s,\tau}=0\qquad\forall t,\; s\text{ with }B_s=1,\;
   \tau^{\text{start}}\le\tau\le\tau^{\text{end}}
   \]

6. **Rerouting – exactly one alternative segment per routing group**  
   \[
   \sum_{s\in\mathcal{G}_{t,g}} z_{t,s}=1\qquad\forall t,\; g
   \]

7. **Linking occupancy and route choice**  
   \[
   v_{t,s,\tau}\le z_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,\; s,\; \tau\in\mathcal{T}
   \]

8. **Speed limits (speed defined only when the train is on the segment)**  
   \[
   p_{t,s,\tau}\le v^{\max}_s\,v_{t,s,\tau}\qquad\forall t,\; s,\; \tau
   \]
   \[
   p_{t,s,\tau}\ge v^{\min}_s\,v_{t,s,\tau}\qquad\forall t,\; s,\; \tau
   \]

9. **Variable domains**  
   \[
   x_{t,n},y_{t,n}\ge0,\quad
   p_{t,s,\tau}\ge0,\quad
   z_{t,s}\in\{0,1\},\quad
   v_{t,s,\tau}\in\{0,1\}
   \]

**Assumptions (explicitly stated)**  

- Time is discretised into equal periods of length \(\Delta\tau\).  
- Dwell times at stations are known and fixed.  
- Speed–energy relationship is linear (energy coefficient \(e_{t,s}\)).  
- Each train follows a predetermined ordered list of segments between consecutive stations; rerouting is modelled by binary choice among alternative segments in each routing group.  
- Blockage affects only the specified segments during the given disruption window; opposite‑track segments are assumed unblocked unless otherwise indicated.  
- Minimum travel time on a segment enforces a lower bound on the sum of occupied periods, approximating the physical speed limit.  

The model above constitutes a complete mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the integrated **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages, capturing bidirectional conflict resolution, routing decisions, timetable adjustments, and energy‑efficient speed profiling.

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP‑MILP)**  
The model below captures, in a single mixed‑integer linear program, the three‑fold decision problem that arises when a partial‑track blockage forces a set of high‑speed trains to be (i) **re‑timed**, (ii) **re‑ordered**, (iii) **re‑routed** (use the opposite track) and (iv) **driven with feasible speed profiles**.  

The formulation follows the narrative of the introduction and adds the missing quantitative details. Wherever data are not supplied in the text, reasonable assumptions are explicitly stated (marked **[Assumption]**).

---

## 1. Sets, Indices and Parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | Set of trains, indexed by *t* (|T| = *N*). |
| **S** | Set of stations (including the origin *0* and the final destination *L*), indexed by *s*. |
| **E** | Set of track **segments** (directed edges) between consecutive stations, indexed by *e = (s, s′)*. |
| **B ⊆ E** | Subset of **blocked segments** (the disruption area). |
| **K** | Set of **speed‑profile discretisation intervals** (e.g., 5‑second slots) used to linearise the speed‑energy relationship, indexed by *k*. |
| **P** | Set of **possible routes** for each train (normally two: normal direction on the “right” track, and detour on the opposite track). For train *t*, the admissible routes are *P_t ⊆ P*. |
| **Δ** | Length of a discretisation interval (seconds). |
| **L_e** | Physical length of segment *e* (km). |
| **v_max** | Maximum admissible speed on any segment (km/h). |
| **a_max**, **d_max** | Maximum acceleration / deceleration (km/h²). |
| **E_k** | Energy consumption (kWh) associated with travelling one kilometre at speed level *k* (linearised, see below). |
| **τ_s^dw** | Minimum dwell time required at station *s* (seconds). |
| **M** | A large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints. |
| **T_start**, **T_end** | Planning horizon (seconds from the start of the day). |

**[Assumption]** – All trains have the same technical characteristics (v_max, a_max, d_max). If heterogeneous fleets exist, the parameters can be indexed by *t*.

---

## 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| **x_{t,s}** | Continuous, ≥0 | **Arrival time** of train *t* at station *s* (seconds). |
| **y_{t,s}** | Continuous, ≥0 | **Departure time** of train *t* from station *s* (seconds). |
| **z_{t,e}** | Binary | **Route‑choice**: 1 if train *t* traverses segment *e* on its **primary** track, 0 if it uses the **opposite** track (only defined for *e ∈ B*). For non‑blocked segments, *z_{t,e}=1* is forced. |
| **r_{t,p}** | Binary | **Route‑selection**: 1 if train *t* follows pre‑defined route *p ∈ P_t*, 0 otherwise. |
| **u_{t,e,k}** | Binary | **Speed‑level selection**: 1 if train *t* travels segment *e* with speed level *k* (i.e., average speed in interval *k*), 0 otherwise. |
| **δ_{t,e}** | Continuous, ≥0 | **Travel time** of train *t* on segment *e* (seconds). |
| **e_{t}** | Continuous, ≥0 | **Energy consumption** of train *t* over the whole horizon (kWh). |
| **c_{t,t',e}** | Binary | **Conflict indicator**: 1 if trains *t* and *t′* occupy the same **track direction** on segment *e* at overlapping times (used to enforce conflict‑free operation). |

---

## 3. Linearised Speed–Energy Relationship  

The continuous speed *v* on a segment is approximated by a set of *K* discrete speed levels *v_k* (e.g., 0–50 km/h, 50–100 km/h, …, v_max). For each level we pre‑compute the **energy per kilometre** *E_k* (including traction and regenerative braking).  

For every train *t* and segment *e* :

\[
\sum_{k\in K} u_{t,e,k}=1 \qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\in E \tag{1}
\]

The travel time on a segment is linked to the selected speed level:

\[
\delta_{t,e}= \frac{L_e}{v_k}\,\Delta \; u_{t,e,k}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\in E,\;k\in K \tag{2}
\]

Because (2) is bilinear, we linearise it by pre‑computing the **time coefficient**  

\[
\theta_{e,k}= \frac{L_e}{v_k}\,\Delta \quad (\text{seconds})
\]

and writing

\[
\delta_{t,e}= \sum_{k\in K}\theta_{e,k}\,u_{t,e,k}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\in E \tag{3}
\]

Energy of train *t* is the sum of segment‑wise energy:

\[
e_{t}= \sum_{e\in E}\sum_{k\in K} E_k\,L_e\,u_{t,e,k}\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{4}
\]

---

## 4. Temporal Consistency (Timetable)  

For each train *t* and consecutive stations *(s, s′)* that define segment *e=(s,s′)* :

\[
y_{t,s}+ \delta_{t,e}= x_{t,s′}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e=(s,s′)\in E \tag{5}
\]

Minimum dwell time at stations:

\[
y_{t,s} \ge x_{t,s}+ \tau_s^{dw}\qquad\forall t\in T,\; s\in S\setminus\{0\} \tag{6}
\]

First‑departure and last‑arrival must stay inside the planning horizon:

\[
T_{\text{start}}\le x_{t,0}\le T_{\text{end}},\qquad
T_{\text{start}}\le y_{t,L}\le T_{\text{end}}\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{7}
\]

---

## 5. Route‑Selection (Rerouting)  

Each train chooses exactly one admissible route:

\[
\sum_{p\in P_t} r_{t,p}=1\qquad\forall t\in T \tag{8}
\]

A route *p* is defined by a binary incidence vector *α_{p,e}* (1 if route *p* uses segment *e* on the primary track, 0 otherwise). For blocked segments *e∈B* the opposite‑track usage is expressed by *z_{t,e}* :

\[
z_{t,e}= \sum_{p\in P_t} \bigl(1-α_{p,e}\bigr)\, r_{t,p}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\in B \tag{9}
\]

For non‑blocked segments we force the primary track:

\[
z_{t,e}=1\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\notin B \tag{10}
\]

The **effective travel time** on a blocked segment depends on whether the train uses the opposite track (which may have a different speed limit *v^{opp}_max*). This is captured by using two sets of speed‑level coefficients:

\[
\theta^{\text{prim}}_{e,k},\;\theta^{\text{opp}}_{e,k}
\]

and writing

\[
\delta_{t,e}= \sum_{k\in K}\Bigl[\,z_{t,e}\,\theta^{\text{prim}}_{e,k}+(1-z_{t,e})\,\theta^{\text{opp}}_{e,k}\Bigr]u_{t,e,k}\qquad\forall t\in T,\;e\in B \tag{11}
\]

---

## 6. Conflict‑Free Operation (Bidirectional Track Sharing)  

When two trains travel on the **same physical track** (i.e., same direction on the same side) their occupancy intervals must not overlap. Let  

\[
\Omega_{t,e}= \bigl[x_{t,s},\; y_{t,s}+ \delta_{t,e}\bigr] \quad\text{(time window of train }t\text{ on segment }e)
\]

We linearise the “no‑overlap” condition using binary variables *c_{t,t',e}* :

\[
x_{t,s}+ \delta_{t,e} \le x_{t',s}+ M\;c_{t,t',e}\qquad\forall t<t',\;e\in E \tag{12a}
\]
\[
x_{t',s}+ \delta_{t',e} \le x_{t,s}+ M\;(1-c_{t,t',e})\qquad\forall t<t',\;e\in E \tag{12b}
\]

If *c_{t,t',e}=1* the first inequality is enforced, otherwise the second. The pair of constraints guarantees that at most one ordering holds, i.e. the two intervals are disjoint.  

**Bidirectional conflict** (trains travelling in opposite directions on the same physical track) is avoided by the **track‑choice** variable *z_{t,e}*. For a blocked segment *e∈B* the opposite track can be used by at most one direction at a time:

\[
\sum_{t\in T} (1-z_{t,e}) \le 1 \qquad\forall e\in B \tag{13}
\]

---

## 7. Acceleration / Deceleration Feasibility  

The selected speed level on consecutive segments must be reachable given the train’s acceleration/deceleration limits. Let *v_k* be the representative speed of level *k*. For each train *t* and two consecutive segments *e=(s,s′)* and *e′=(s′,s″)* :

\[
v_{k'} - v_{k} \le a_{\max}\,\Delta \quad\text{if } v_{k'}\ge v_{k} \tag{14a}
\]
\[
v_{k} - v_{k'} \le d_{\max}\,\Delta \quad\text{if } v_{k'}< v_{k} \tag{14b}
\]

These are linearised with big‑M and the binary selectors *u_{t,e,k}* :

\[
\sum_{k} v_k u_{t,e,k} - \sum_{k'} v_{k'} u_{t,e',k'} \le a_{\max}\,\Delta + M\bigl(1-\sum_{k,k'}u_{t,e,k}u_{t,e',k'}\bigr) \tag{14}
\]

In practice, a **pairwise** formulation is used (only the active speed levels appear), which remains linear because the product of binaries is replaced by an auxiliary binary and a big‑M.

---

## 8. Objective Function  

The integrated problem has two natural, possibly conflicting goals:

1. **Minimise total delay** with respect to the original (pre‑disruption) timetable.  
   Let *\(\hat{x}_{t,s}\)* be the scheduled arrival time (data). The delay of train *t* at its final destination is  

   \[
   d_t = x_{t,L} - \hat{x}_{t,L}\quad (\ge 0)
   \]

2. **Minimise total energy consumption** (kWh).  

A weighted sum is used (weights can be tuned by the railway operator):

\[
\min\; \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{t\in T} d_t}_{\text{Delay term}} \;+\; \underbrace{\beta \sum_{t\in T} e_t}_{\text{Energy term}} \tag{OBJ}
\]

where **α** (€/s) reflects the economic cost of passenger delay and **β** (€/kWh) reflects the energy price (or a carbon‑emission penalty).  

**[Assumption]** – No train cancellations are allowed in this baseline model. If cancellations are permitted, a binary *canc_t* can be introduced with a large penalty term *γ·canc_t* in the objective.

---

## 9. Complete MILP Formulation  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& \alpha\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(x_{t,L}-\hat{x}_{t,L}\bigr) \;+\; \beta\sum_{t\in T} e_t \\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
\text{(1)–(14)   (linear constraints listed above)}\\
& x_{t,s},y_{t,s},\delta_{t,e},e_t \ge 0 \\
& u_{t,e,k},z_{t,e},r_{t,p},c_{t,t',e}\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only non‑linearities that could appear (products of binaries) are eliminated by standard big‑M linearisation, yielding a **pure MILP**.

---

## 10. Summary of Modelling Assumptions  

| # | Assumption | Reason / Typical Value |
|---|------------|-----------------------|
| A1 | All trains share the same technical limits (*v_max*, *a_max*, *d_max*). | Simplifies the model; heterogeneous fleets can be handled by indexing parameters by *t*. |
| A2 | Speed on a segment is approximated by a small set *K* of discrete levels (e.g., 5‑km/h steps). | Provides a linear relationship between speed, travel time, and energy. |
| A3 | Energy per kilometre for each speed level is known (from a calibrated train‑energy model). | Allows linear expression (4). |
| A4 | Blocked segment *e∈B* can be traversed on the opposite track, but only one train may use the opposite track at a time (13). | Reflects the physical limitation of a single‑track detour. |
| A5 | No train cancellations; every train must be served (if cancellations are allowed, add binary *canc_t*). | Keeps the baseline model tractable. |
| A6 | Minimum dwell time *τ_s^dw* is the same for all trains at a given station. | Standard practice; can be made train‑specific if needed. |
| A7 | Big‑M values are chosen large enough to deactivate constraints but not too large to cause numerical instability (e.g., *M = 10⁶* seconds). | Standard MILP practice. |
| A8 | The planning horizon *[T_start, T_end]* comfortably contains all feasible arrivals/departures (e.g., a 24‑hour window). | Guarantees feasibility of time‑window constraints. |

---

## 11. Remarks for Implementation  

* **Decomposition** – The model can be decomposed exactly as described in the paper (IP for interaction + train‑plan generation). The MILP above is the *master* formulation; the decomposition replaces the huge set of *u_{t,e,k}* variables by a pre‑computed **plan library** for each train.  
* **Scalability** – The number of binary variables grows with *|T|·|E|·|K|*. In practice, *K* is kept small (5‑10 levels) and the time‑discretisation *Δ* is chosen to balance accuracy and size.  
* **Solver** – Any modern MILP solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress) can handle instances up to a few hundred trains and a few hundred segments when the plan‑generation step is used.  
* **Extensions** – The model can be enriched with (i) train‑cancellation binaries, (ii) passenger‑connection constraints, (iii) stochastic disruption durations (scenario‑based robust MILP), or (iv) a multi‑objective Pareto front (ε‑constraint method).

---

**The formulation above provides a complete, linear (MILP) description of the integrated train‑rescheduling and speed‑management problem under partial‑track blockages, ready for computational testing and further methodological extensions.**

Sets and Indices | Symbol | Meaning | |--------|---------| | \(T=\{1,\dots ,|T|\}\) | Set of trains scheduled for the planning horizon | | \(S=\{1,\dots ,|S|\}\) | Set of stations (including start‑ and end‑nodes) | | \(L=\{(i,j)\mid i,j\in S, i• running time \(\tau^{p}_{ij}\) (h)
• energy consumption \(\eta^{p}_{ij}\) (kWh) | | \(M\) | Large constant (big‑M) for logical constraints | | \(\alpha,\beta\) | Weight coefficients in the objective (energy vs. delay) | | \(\Gamma_{t}\) | Set of passengers on train \(t\) (used only for scaling delay, optional) | | \(R_{t}\in\{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(t\) is *allowed* to be rerouted (i.e. \(t\in\mathcal{R}\)), 0 otherwise | | \(t^{\text{blk}}_{ij},t^{\text{end}}_{ij}\) | Start / end of the blockage on segment \((i,j)\) (h) | | \(U\) | Upper bound on the number of trains that may simultaneously occupy a blocked segment (normally 1). | | \(w_{t,i}\) | Passenger‑weight of train \(t\) at station \(i\) (e.g., number of on‑board passengers, used for delay‑penalty). | -------------------------------------------------------------------- ### 4. Modeling Assumptions (explicit) 1. **Deterministic disruption** – the blockage interval \([t^{\text{blk}}_{ij},t^{\text{end}}_{ij}]\) is known in advance. 2. **Single‑track operation on blocked segments** – at any instant at most one train (irrespective of direction) may occupy the physical block. 3. **No overtaking** – trains keep their order on each *directional* track; ordering can change only by feasible **reordering** decisions (captured by binary \(x\) and \(y\)). 4. **Rerouting only to the opposite track** – a train may be forced to travel on the opposite directional track of a blocked segment (binary variable \(y\)). 5. **Speed plans are pre‑computed** – for each segment a finite set \(\mathcal{P}_{ij}\) of feasible average‑speed / acceleration‑deceleration patterns is generated (e.g., by a lower‑level optimal control problem). The MILP only selects among them. 6. **Energy is a linear function of the selected plan** – the energy consumption \(\eta^{p}_{ij}\) of plan \(p\) is treated as a parameter; the model does not need to linearise the physics. 7. **Passengers experience delay only through arrival‑time deviation** – the passenger‑delay cost for train \(t\) is proportional to the sum of absolute deviations of arrival times from the original schedule (or weighted by passenger‑load). 8. **Dwell‑time bounds are respected** – for each stop the departure‑time minus arrival‑time lies within \([\underline d_i,\overline d_i]\). If a station is passed (\(\pi_{t,i}=0\)) then \(\underline d_i=0\). 9. **Train‑specific feasibility** – each train has its own maximal acceleration / deceleration capabilities, already embedded in the admissible speed‑plans. -------------------------------------------------------------------- ### 5. Objective Function \[ \min\; \underbrace{\alpha\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in S}\, w_{t,i}\,\bigl|a_{t,i}-a^{0}_{t,i}\bigr|}_{\text{Weighted passenger delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\beta\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in L}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_{ij}} \eta^{p}_{ij}\,z^{p}_{t,ij}}_{\text{Total traction energy}} \tag{OBJ} \] *The absolute deviation can be linearised with auxiliary variables \(u_{t,i}\ge0\):* \[ u_{t,i} \ge a_{t,i}-a^{0}_{t,i},\qquad u_{t,i} \ge a^{0}_{t,i}-a_{t,i}, \] and the delay term becomes \(\alpha\sum_{t,i} w_{t,i} u_{t,i}\). -------------------------------------------------------------------- ### 6. Core Constraints #### 6.1 Routing / Direction‑Choice For every train‑segment pair that belongs to the original route: \[ x_{t,ij}+y_{t,ij}=1\quad \forall t\in T,\;(i,j)\in K_{ij} \tag{R1} \] *If a train is not allowed to reroute:* \[ y_{t,ij}\le R_{t}\qquad \forall t,i,j . \tag{R2} \] #### 6.2 Selection of a Speed Plan Exactly one speed plan must be chosen **if** the segment is traversed: \[ \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_{ij}} z^{p}_{t,ij}=x_{t,ij}+y_{t,ij}\qquad \forall t,(i,j)\in L. \tag{SP1} \] Running time on the segment is linked to the selected plan: \[ \delta_{t,ij}= \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_{ij}} \tau^{p}_{ij}\,z^{p}_{t,ij}\qquad \forall t,(i,j)\in L. \tag{SP2} \] #### 6.3 Temporal Consistency (timetable feasibility) **Travel‑time linking arrival/departure and running time** \[ a_{t,j}= d_{t,i}+ \delta_{t,ij}\qquad \forall t,(i,j)\in L. \tag{TT1} \] **Dwell‑time limits** \[ \underline d_i\,\pi_{t,i}\le d_{t,i}-a_{t,i}\le \overline d_i\,\pi_{t,i}\qquad\forall t,i. \tag{TT2} \] If a station is passed (\(\pi_{t,i}=0\)) the equality forces \(d_{t,i}=a_{t,i}\). **Departure cannot precede original schedule (optional)** \[ d_{t,i}\ge d^{0}_{t,i}\qquad\forall t,i. \tag{TT3} \] #### 6.4 Single‑Track Conflict on Blocked Segments A train *passes* the blocked interval on segment \((i,j)\) iff its **entry** time onto the segment lies before the end of the blockage **and** its **exit** time lies after the start of the blockage: \[ c_{t,ij}\ge \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } d_{t,i}< t^{\text{end}}_{ij}\ \text{and}\ a_{t,j}>t^{\text{blk}}_{ij}\\[2mm] 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \] Linearised with big‑M: \[ \begin{aligned} d_{t,i} &\le t^{\text{end}}_{ij}+M\,(1-c_{t,ij})\\ a_{t,j} &\ge t^{\text{blk}}_{ij}-M\,(1-c_{t,ij})\\ c_{t,ij} &\in\{0,1\} \end{aligned}\tag{BLK1} \] **Capacity of the blocked block** (only one train, irrespective of direction, may be present): \[ \sum_{t\in T} c_{t,ij}\le 1\qquad \forall (i,j)\in\mathcal{B}. \tag{BLK2} \] If a train is **rerouted** onto the opposite track, the same constraint still applies because the two opposite tracks share the same physical block. #### 6.5 Train‑Ordering (Reordering) on the Same Direction For any two trains \(t_1,t_2\) that use the *same* direction on segment \((i,j)\) (i.e. \(x_{t_1,ij}=x_{t_2,ij}=1\) or \(y_{t_1,ij}=y_{t_2,ij}=1\)), introduce binary \(\theta_{t_1t_2,ij}\) = 1 if \(t_1\) precedes \(t_2\) on that segment. \[ \begin{aligned} d_{t_1,i}+ \delta_{t_1,ij} &\le a_{t_2,j}+ M\,(1-\theta_{t_1t_2,ij})\\ d_{t_2,i}+ \delta_{t_2,ij} &\le a_{t_1,j}+ M\,\theta_{t_1t_2,ij}\\ \theta_{t_1t_2,ij} &\in\{0,1\} \end{aligned}\qquad\forall t_1

Text:
**Integrated Train‑Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) for Partial Segment Blockage**

---

### 1. Sets, indices and parameters  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **I** | Set of trains, *i* ∈ I |
| **S** = {1,2} | Parallel track sides (1 = normal, 2 = detour) |
| **K** | Set of line segments, *k* ∈ K |
| **K_i** ⊆ K | Segments that train *i* must travel |
| **pred(k)** | Predecessor segment of *k* (∅ for first) |
| **succ(k)** | Successor segment of *k* (∅ for last) |
| **L_k** | Length of segment *k* (km) |
| **v_i^min , v_i^max** | Speed limits for train *i* (km h⁻¹) |
| **a_i^max** | Max acceleration/deceleration for train *i* (km h⁻²) |
| **τ_i^dwell** | Minimum dwell time at stations (min) |
| **sched_arr_i** | Scheduled arrival time of train *i* (min) |
| **w_i^delay , w_i^energy** | Weights in the objective |
| **c₁ , c₂** | Energy‑cost coefficients |
| **B_{k,s} = [T^{start}_{k,s}, T^{end}_{k,s}]** | Blockage interval of segment *k* on side *s* (empty if no blockage) |
| **M** | Big‑M constant (≥ planning horizon) |
| **Δt** | Planning horizon (large enough) |

---

### 2. Decision variables  

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| **r_{i,s}** | binary | 1 ⇔ train *i* uses side *s* |
| **o_{i,j,s}** | binary | 1 ⇔ on side *s* train *i* departs before train *j* (conflict‑avoidance) |
| **w_{i,j,s}** | binary | = r_{i,s}·r_{j,s} (linearised) |
| **d_i** | continuous ≥0 | Departure time of train *i* from origin |
| **a_i** | continuous ≥0 | Arrival time of train *i* at final destination |
| **t_{i,k}** | continuous ≥0 | Travel time of train *i* on segment *k* |
| **v_{i,k}** | continuous ≥0 | Average speed of train *i* on segment *k* |
| **e_{i,k}** | continuous ≥0 | Linearisation of \(v_{i,k}^{2}\) |
| **q_{i,k}** | continuous ≥0 | Linearisation of \((v_{i,k}-v_{i, pred(k)})^{2}\) |
| **y_{i,k}^{p}** | binary | SOS2 variable for speed‑time linearisation (p = 1,…,P) |
| **b_{i,k,s}** | binary | Block‑avoidance indicator (see (B2)) |

---

### 3. Linearisation of quadratic energy terms  

For each *i,k* let \(v_i^{min} \le v_{i,k} \le v_i^{max}\).

**McCormick envelope for \(v_{i,k}^{2}\):**  

\[
\begin{aligned}
e_{i,k} &\ge 2v_i^{min}v_{i,k} - (v_i^{min})^{2},\\
e_{i,k} &\ge 2v_i^{max}v_{i,k} - (v_i^{max})^{2},\\
e_{i,k} &\le v_i^{max}v_{i,k} + v_i^{min}v_{i,k} - v_i^{min}v_i^{max},\\
e_{i,k} &\le v_i^{min}v_{i,k} + v_i^{max}v_{i,k} - v_i^{min}v_i^{max}.
\end{aligned}
\]

**Speed‑difference linearisation:**  

Introduce \(\Delta v_{i,k}=v_{i,k}-v_{i, pred(k)}\) (continuous).  
Apply the same McCormick envelope to \(\Delta v_{i,k}^{2}\) using bounds \(\pm \Delta v_i^{max}\) (derived from \(a_i^{max}\) and segment length). The resulting linear variable is **q_{i,k}**.

---

### 4. Objective function  

\[
\boxed{
\min\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I} w_i^{delay}\,\bigl(a_i-\text{sched\_arr}_i\bigr)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K_i}
w_i^{energy}\,\bigl(c_1 e_{i,k}+c_2 q_{i,k}\bigr)}_{\text{energy consumption}}
}
\]

---

### 5. Model constraints  

#### 5.1 Side‑choice  
\[
\sum_{s\in S} r_{i,s}=1 \qquad\forall i\in I \tag{R1}
\]

#### 5.2 Blockage avoidance (for every *i, k∈K_i, s∈S*)  

\[
\begin{aligned}
d_i+\!\!\sum_{h\in pred(k)}\! t_{i,h} &\ge T^{end}_{k,s}-M\bigl(1-b_{i,k,s}\bigr),\\
d_i+\!\!\sum_{h\in pred(k)}\! t_{i,h} &\le T^{start}_{k,s}+M\,b_{i,k,s},\\
b_{i,k,s} &\le r_{i,s},\qquad b_{i,k,s}\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{B2}
\]

If side *s* is not chosen, the constraints are relaxed.

#### 5.3 Travel‑time – speed relationship (SOS2)  

Choose a set of speed breakpoints \(\{\hat v^{p}\}_{p=1}^{P}\).  

\[
\begin{aligned}
v_{i,k}&=\sum_{p=1}^{P}\hat v^{p}\,y_{i,k}^{p},\\
t_{i,k}&=\sum_{p=1}^{P}\frac{60L_k}{\hat v^{p}}\,y_{i,k}^{p},\\
\sum_{p=1}^{P} y_{i,k}^{p}&=1,\qquad y_{i,k}^{p}\in\{0,1\},
\end{aligned}
\tag{T2}
\]

with SOS2 ordering on the \(y\)’s (at most two consecutive non‑zero).

#### 5.4 Speed limits  

\[
v_i^{min}\le v_{i,k}\le v_i^{max}\qquad\forall i,k\in K_i. \tag{S1}
\]

#### 5.5 Acceleration limits (for every interior segment)  

\[
\begin{aligned}
v_{i,k}-v_{i, pred(k)} &\le a_i^{max}\,\frac{t_{i, pred(k)}}{60},\\
v_{i, pred(k)}-v_{i,k} &\le a_i^{max}\,\frac{t_{i, pred(k)}}{60}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{A2}
\]

#### 5.6 Minimum dwell time (stations)  

If segment *k* is a station for train *i*:  

\[
t_{i,k}\ge \tau_i^{dwell}. \tag{D1}
\]

#### 5.7 Temporal linking  

\[
a_i = d_i + \sum_{k\in K_i} t_{i,k}\qquad\forall i\in I. \tag{F3}
\]

#### 5.8 Sequencing (conflict‑avoidance)  

Define \(w_{i,j,s}\) to linearise the product \(r_{i,s}r_{j,s}\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{i,j,s}&\le r_{i,s},\; w_{i,j,s}\le r_{j,s},\\
w_{i,j,s}&\ge r_{i,s}+r_{j,s}-1,\\
o_{i,j,s}+o_{j,i,s}&= w_{i,j,s},\qquad o_{i,j,s},o_{j,i,s}\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{SEQ‑lin}
\]

For every unordered pair \((i,j)\) that share at least one segment \(C_{i,j}\neq\emptyset\) and for each side *s*:

\[
\begin{aligned}
d_i+\!\!\sum_{h\in pred(k)}\! t_{i,h} &\ge d_j+\!\!\sum_{h\in pred(k)}\! t_{j,h}+t_{j,k}-M\bigl(1-o_{i,j,s}\bigr) \\
&\qquad\forall k\in C_{i,j},\\
d_j+\!\!\sum_{h\in pred(k)}\! t_{j,h} &\ge d_i+\!\!\sum_{h\in pred(k)}\! t_{i,h}+t_{i,k}-M\bigl(o_{i,j,s}\bigr) \\
&\qquad\forall k\in C_{i,j}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{SEQ}
\]

If \(w_{i,j,s}=0\) (trains on different sides) the constraints are inactive.

#### 5.9 Variable domains  

\[
\begin{aligned}
&r_{i,s},o_{i,j,s},w_{i,j,s},b_{i,k,s},y_{i,k}^{p}\in\{0,1\},\\
&d_i,a_i,t_{i,k},v_{i,k},e_{i,k},q_{i,k}\ge 0.
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 6. Complete MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{i\in I} w_i^{delay}\bigl(a_i-\text{sched\_arr}_i\bigr)
      +\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K_i}
        w_i^{energy}\bigl(c_1 e_{i,k}+c_2 q_{i,k}\bigr)\\
\text{s.t. }&
\text{(R1)}\;\; \sum_{s} r_{i,s}=1 &&\forall i\\
&\text{(B2)}\;\; \text{block‑avoidance constraints} &&\forall i,k,s\\
&\text{(T2)}\;\; \text{SOS2 speed–time linearisation} &&\forall i,k\\
&\text{(S1)}\;\; v_i^{min}\le v_{i,k}\le v_i^{max} &&\forall i,k\\
&\text{(A2)}\;\; \text{acceleration limits} &&\forall i,k\neq first\\
&\text{(D1)}\;\; t_{i,k}\ge \tau_i^{dwell} &&\forall (i,k)\in\text{stations}\\
&\text{(F3)}\;\; a_i = d_i+\sum_{k\in K_i} t_{i,k} &&\forall i\\
&\text{(SEQ‑lin)}\;\; w_{i,j,s}\text{ linearisation} &&\forall i<j,s\\
&\text{(SEQ)}\;\; \text{ordering constraints} &&\forall i<j,s\\
&\text{(Energy‑lin)}\;\; \text{McCormick envelopes for }e_{i,k},q_{i,k}\\
&\text{binary / continuous domain restrictions.}
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; quadratic energy terms are replaced by the auxiliary variables **e** and **q** with their linear envelopes, keeping the model within the MILP class.

---

### 7. Remarks  

* **Partial blockage** is modeled by the interval \([T^{start}_{k,s},T^{end}_{k,s}]\); the binary \(b_{i,k,s}\) forces each train to be completely before or after the blocked period on the chosen side.  
* **Side‑choice** variables allow detouring to the opposite track when the normal side is blocked.  
* **Sequencing binaries** guarantee conflict‑free use of shared segments on the same side.  
* **Energy linearisation** captures both aerodynamic drag (\(v^{2}\)) and the cost of speed changes, enabling a true co‑optimisation of delay and energy.  
* The model can be extended with additional operational constraints (crew limits, platform capacity, overtaking, etc.) without breaking linearity.

Solving this MILP with a modern MIP solver yields a feasible, conflict‑free timetable together with executable speed profiles that minimise total delay and energy consumption under the given disruption.

Text:
**Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed‑Management MILP (TRSMP) – Partial Segment Blockage**  

---

### 1. Sets and Indices  

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **T** | Set of trains, indexed by *t* (|T| = N). |
| **S** | Set of track segments, indexed by *s* (|S| = M). |
| **K** | Set of admissible discrete speed levels, indexed by *k* (|K| = L). |
| **B ⊆ S** | Sub‑set of *blocked* segments (partial blockage). |
| **R ⊆ T** | Trains that may be rerouted (their original path contains a blocked segment). |
| **\(P_t\)** | Ordered list of segments of the *original* path of train *t*: \(P_t=(s_{t,1},…,s_{t,|P_t|})\). |
| **\(P^{\text{alt}}_t\)** | Ordered list of segments of an *alternative* path for train *t* (pre‑computed for all \(t∈R\)). |
| **\(W_t\)** | Weight of train *t* in the objective (e.g. passenger importance). |
| **\(c_k\)** | Energy cost (per km) associated with speed level *k* (higher speed ⇒ higher energy). |
| **\(v_k\)** | Physical speed (km h⁻¹) belonging to level *k*. |
| **\(L_s\)** | Length (km) of segment *s*. |
| **\(U_s\)** | Maximum number of trains that may occupy segment *s* simultaneously (normally 1). |
| **\(T^{\text{block}}_s=[\tau^{\text{start}}_s,\tau^{\text{end}}_s]\)** | Time window during which segment *s∈B* is blocked. |
| **\(a^{\max}_t,\;d^{\max}_t\)** | Latest permissible arrival / departure times (hard deadline). |
| **\(a^{\min}_t,\;d^{\min}_t\)** | Earliest permissible arrival / departure times (safety limits). |
| **\(\Delta^{\text{acc}}_{k,k'}\)** | Minimum dwell time needed to change speed from level *k* to *k′* (acceleration/deceleration limit). |

---

### 2. Decision Variables  

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| **\(x_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\}\)** | binary | 1 if train *t* traverses segment *s* with speed level *k*. |
| **\(y_t\in\{0,1\}\)** | binary | 1 if train *t* is **rerouted** (uses \(P^{\text{alt}}_t\)); defined only for \(t∈R\). |
| **\(a_{t,s}\ge0\)** | continuous | Actual arrival time of train *t* at the *up‑stream* end of segment *s*. |
| **\(d_{t,s}\ge0\)** | continuous | Actual departure time of train *t* from the *down‑stream* end of segment *s*. |
| **\(z_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\)** | binary | 1 if train *t* occupies segment *s* (i.e. any speed level is chosen). |
| **\(c_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}\)** | binary | Ordering variable for two trains on a single‑track segment (conflict‑avoidance). |
| **\(w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\in\{0,1\}\)** | binary | 1 if train *t* uses speed *k* on segment *i* and speed *k′* on segment *i+1*. |

---

### 3. Objective Function  

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min\; &\underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} W_t\Bigl(a_{t,s^{\text{last}}}-\hat a_{t,s^{\text{last}}}\Bigr)}_{\text{Total weighted delay}} \\
&\;+\;\underbrace{\lambda\;\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in P_t\cup P^{\text{alt}}_t}\sum_{k\in K} c_k\,L_s\,x_{t,s,k}}_{\text{Total energy consumption}}
\end{aligned}}
\]

* \(\hat a_{t,s^{\text{last}}}\) = scheduled arrival of train *t* at its final station.  
* \(\lambda\ge0\) balances delay vs. energy (larger λ → more emphasis on energy).

---

### 4. Constraints  

#### 4.1  Speed‑choice ↔ occupancy  

\[
z_{t,s}= \sum_{k\in K} x_{t,s,k}\qquad\forall t,s
\]
\[
\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,s,k}\le 1\qquad\forall t,s
\]

#### 4.2  Travel time on a segment  

\[
d_{t,s}-a_{t,s}= \sum_{k\in K}\frac{L_s}{v_k}\;x_{t,s,k}\qquad\forall t,s
\]

#### 4.3  Flow of times along the chosen path  

For every consecutive pair \((s_i,s_{i+1})\) on the **selected** path (original or alternative):

\[
a_{t,s_{i+1}} = d_{t,s_i}+ \Delta^{\text{stop}}_{t,s_i}\qquad\forall t,\;i
\]

(\(\Delta^{\text{stop}}_{t,s_i}\) is a known dwell time, set to 0 if the train does not stop.)

#### 4.4  Blockage avoidance  

\[
a_{t,s}\ge\tau^{\text{end}}_s\,z_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,\;s\in B
\]
\[
d_{t,s}\le\tau^{\text{start}}_s\,(1-z_{t,s})\qquad\forall t,\;s\in B
\]

These force \(z_{t,s}=0\) (no occupancy) unless the whole traversal lies **after** the blockage.

#### 4.5  Rerouting logic (only for \(t∈R\))

\[
\sum_{s\in B\cap P_t} z_{t,s}\le |B\cap P_t|\;(1-y_t)\qquad\forall t∈R
\]

If \(y_t=1\) (reroute) the left‑hand side must be zero – the train cannot use any originally blocked segment.

Force the train to stay on the chosen path:

\[
z_{t,s}\le 1-y_t\qquad\forall t∈R,\;s\in P_t\setminus P^{\text{alt}}_t
\]
\[
z_{t,s}\ge y_t\qquad\forall t∈R,\;s\in P^{\text{alt}}_t\setminus P_t
\]

#### 4.6  Capacity / bidirectional conflict on a single‑track segment  

For every unordered pair of distinct trains \((t,t')\) and every segment *s* with capacity \(U_s=1\):

\[
a_{t',s}\ge d_{t,s}-M\,c_{t,t',s}
\]
\[
a_{t,s}\ge d_{t',s}-M\,(1-c_{t,t',s})
\]
\[
c_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}
\]

\(M\) is a sufficiently large constant (e.g., the planning horizon). The constraints guarantee that on a single‑track segment the two trains are ordered in time, thus conflict‑free.

#### 4.7  Acceleration / deceleration limits  

Introduce auxiliary variables \(w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\) linking speed choices on consecutive segments:

\[
w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\le x_{t,s_i,k},\qquad
w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\le x_{t,s_{i+1},k'},\qquad
w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\ge x_{t,s_i,k}+x_{t,s_{i+1},k'}-1
\]

Then enforce a minimum transition time:

\[
a_{t,s_{i+1}}-d_{t,s_i}\ge \Delta^{\text{acc}}_{k,k'}\,w^{k,k'}_{t,i}
\qquad\forall t,i,\;k,k'\in K
\]

If acceleration limits are to be ignored set all \(\Delta^{\text{acc}}_{k,k'}=0\).

#### 4.8  Time‑window (hard) bounds  

\[
a^{\min}_t\le a_{t,s}\le a^{\max}_t,\qquad
d^{\min}_t\le d_{t,s}\le d^{\max}_t\qquad\forall t,s
\]

#### 4.9  Variable domains  

\[
x_{t,s,k},\,y_t,\,z_{t,s},\,c_{t,t',s},\,w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\in\{0,1\},
\qquad
a_{t,s},d_{t,s}\ge0.
\]

---

### 5. Complete MILP  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\sum_{t\in T} W_t\bigl(a_{t,s^{\text{last}}}-\hat a_{t,s^{\text{last}}}\bigr)
      +\lambda\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s}\sum_{k\in K}c_k L_s x_{t,s,k}\\[4pt]
\text{s.t. } &
z_{t,s}= \sum_{k}x_{t,s,k} &&\forall t,s\\
&\sum_{k}x_{t,s,k}\le 1 &&\forall t,s\\
&d_{t,s}-a_{t,s}= \sum_{k}\frac{L_s}{v_k}x_{t,s,k} &&\forall t,s\\
&a_{t,s_{i+1}} = d_{t,s_i}+ \Delta^{\text{stop}}_{t,s_i} &&\forall t,i\\
&a_{t,s}\ge\tau^{\text{end}}_s z_{t,s},\;
d_{t,s}\le\tau^{\text{start}}_s (1-z_{t,s}) &&\forall t,s\in B\\
&\sum_{s\in B\cap P_t}z_{t,s}\le |B\cap P_t|(1-y_t) &&\forall t∈R\\
&z_{t,s}\le 1-y_t &&\forall t∈R,\;s∈P_t\setminus P^{\text{alt}}_t\\
&z_{t,s}\ge y_t &&\forall t∈R,\;s∈P^{\text{alt}}_t\setminus P_t\\
&a_{t',s}\ge d_{t,s}-M c_{t,t',s}\\
&a_{t,s}\ge d_{t',s}-M(1-c_{t,t',s}) &&\forall t\neq t',\;s\\
&c_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}\\
&w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\le x_{t,s_i,k},\;
w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\le x_{t,s_{i+1},k'},\;
w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\ge x_{t,s_i,k}+x_{t,s_{i+1},k'}-1\\
&a_{t,s_{i+1}}-d_{t,s_i}\ge \Delta^{\text{acc}}_{k,k'} w^{k,k'}_{t,i}
&&\forall t,i,k,k'\\
&a^{\min}_t\le a_{t,s}\le a^{\max}_t,\;
d^{\min}_t\le d_{t,s}\le d^{\max}_t &&\forall t,s\\
&x_{t,s,k},y_t,z_{t,s},c_{t,t',s},w^{k,k'}_{t,i}\in\{0,1\}\\
&a_{t,s},d_{t,s}\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\]

All constraints are linear; the only non‑continuous variables are binaries, therefore the formulation is a **Mixed‑Integer Linear Program (MILP)**.

---

### 6. How to Use  

1. **Data preparation** – supply the sets, segment lengths, speed levels, blockage windows, and for every train the original and alternative paths.  
2. **Parameter tuning** – choose the trade‑off weight \(\lambda\) and train‑specific importance \(W_t\).  
3. **Solve** – feed the model to any MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, SCIP, CBC, …).  
4. **Result interpretation** –  
   * \(y_t=1\) → train *t* is rerouted (uses \(P^{\text{alt}}_t\)).  
   * \(x_{t,s,k}=1\) → speed level *k* on segment *s* (defines the executable speed profile).  
   * \(a_{t,s},d_{t,s}\) give the conflict‑free rescheduled timetable.  

The model simultaneously decides **where to reroute, when to run each train, and at which speed**, while guaranteeing **no occupation of blocked segments, conflict‑free use of single‑track sections, and compliance with acceleration limits**. It therefore provides a complete linear MILP representation of the integrated train rescheduling and speed‑management problem under partial segment blockages.
